signals.title: Unconditional model injection in `get_deployment_credentials_with_provider` loses alias identity when model groups share a `litellm_params.model`
signals.text: Since #24548, `get_deployment_credentials_with_provider` always sets `credentials["model"] = deployment.litellm_params.model`, and endpoints that merge these credentials into the request body (batches, files, vector stores) overwrite the caller's router alias with the underlying provider model before dispatch. In the common case the router recovers via the `_get_deployment_by_litellm_model` fallback in `_common_checks_available_deployment`. But when two model groups point at the same underlying `litellm_params.model` with different access groups, team scoping, or per-group settings (fallbacks, rate limits, tags), the alias identity is gone by the time the router resolves the deployment, so the request can be served under the wrong group, bypassing per-group access restrictions and misattributing spend and logs. The tenant-guard test changes in #24548 show the overwrite reaching dispatch. Possible directions: keep the requested alias in `data["model"]` and carry the underlying model separately, or make the injection opt-in per call site (as in the now-closed #36047).

signals.title: [Feature]: Adaptive similarity threshold for the valkey-semantic cache backend
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature The `valkey-semantic` cache backend uses a single static `similarity_threshold` (default 0.8) to decide cache hits. This proposes an optional adaptive mode where the threshold moves with observed LLM latency: accept fuzzier cache hits when the upstream model is slow, and demand higher similarity when it is fast. Config would stay backward compatible. The static threshold remains the default; adaptive mode is opt-in: ```yaml litellm_settings: cache: True cache_params: type: valkey-semantic host: os.environ/VALKEY_HOST port: os.environ/VALKEY_PORT valkey_semantic_cache_embedding_model: openai-embedding similarity_threshold: 0.8 # still supported, still the default # New, optional: adaptive_threshold: True adaptive_min_threshold: 0.72 # floor: never accept below this adaptive_max_threshold: 0.88 # ceiling: never demand above this adaptive_low_latency_ms: 500 # p95 at or below this -> max threshold adaptive_high_latency_ms: 3000 # p95 at or above this -> min threshold adaptive_latency_window: 50 # rolling sample size ``` Behavior when `adaptive_threshold: True`: - LiteLLM already measures the upstream call duration on a cache miss. Feed that into a rolling window (per cache scope). - Compute the effective threshold by linear interpolation over the window's p95: - p95 at or below `adaptive_low_latency_ms` -> `adaptive_max_threshold` (model is fast, prefer quality) - p95 at or above `adaptive_high_latency_ms` -> `adaptive_min_threshold` (model is slow, prefer a hit) - between the two -> linear interpolation - Cold start: until the window has a few samples, use `similarity_threshold` as the default. Everything stays within the existing backend. No new dependency, no Valkey server changes. The threshold decision that already happens at lookup time reads from the rolling window instead of a constant. ### Motivation, pitch Bringing part of a [conversation in valkey-search](https://github.com/valkey-io/valkey-search/issues/1188) here The static threshold forces a fixed trade-off that the runtime cannot revisit. When an upstream model degrades from 500ms to 3s, the cost of a cache miss triples, and a slightly-less-similar cached answer becomes the better call. A static 0.8 cannot express that. The result is either a threshold set too high (missing cheap hits exactly when the model is slow and hits matter most) or too low (serving loose matches even when the model is fast and quality is cheap). Tying the threshold to observed latency lets the cache spend its "fuzziness budget" when it is worth the most. LiteLLM is uniquely well placed to do this because it already sees every upstream call's latency at the proxy. Nothing else in the stack has that signal in one place. This is opt-in and additive. Existing configs behave exactly as they do today. Teams that want the adaptive behavior turn it on and set the bounds; everyone else is unaffected. I have a working reference for the interpolation logic and am happy to open a PR against the `valkey-semantic` backend if this direction makes sense. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No ### Twitter / LinkedIn details linkedin.com/in/pnigelbrown

signals.title: [Bug]: DB proxy routes all GET /v1/batches through managed files, provider filter 500s and Vertex provider-side listing is unreachable
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? On a proxy with a database attached, `GET /v1/batches` is unconditionally routed through the enterprise managed-files hook before any provider routing runs (`litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py:684-694` at 1bafdb3c93). The hook rejects any `provider` filter with a bare `Exception` (`enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py:346-349`), and `handle_exception_on_proxy` turns that into an opaque HTTP 500 Two consequences: - `GET /v1/batches?provider=...` and the `GET /{provider}/v1/batches` route (the path param binds to the same `provider` argument, `endpoints.py:614-632`) return a 500 `internal_server_error` for what is really an unsupported-parameter condition, indistinguishable from a gateway crash - The endpoint's own provider fallback (SCENARIO 3, `endpoints.py:737-756`), which supports `vertex_ai` via `litellm.alist_batches` (`litellm/types/utils.py:3715`), is unreachable on these deployments. No proxy route reaches `VertexAIBatchPrediction.list_batches`, so provider-side Vertex batches (anything created outside this proxy) cannot be listed at all Found while QA'ing #35141 (see "What the QA also turned up" there): the list-path error handling that PR touches could not be exercised end to end because the route dies before reaching the handler ### User Flow Today the walk dead-ends at step 2: 1. Create a Vertex batch through the proxy, `POST /v1/batches` with `"custom_llm_provider": "vertex_ai"`, and get back a unified batch id 2. `GET /v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai` to see that batch alongside everything else Vertex has, and get `500` with `{"error":{"message":"Filtering by 'provider' is not supported when using managed batches.","type":"internal_server_error","param":"None","code":"500"}}` 3. Retry as `GET /vertex_ai/v1/batches`, and get the same 500, since the path param feeds the same argument 4. Read `internal_server_error` as a gateway outage and retry or escalate, when nothing is down and the request was simply carrying an unsupported filter 5. Drop the filter, `GET /v1/batches`, and get only rows this proxy created. Batch prediction jobs created from the console, gsutil, or another gateway never appear, and no other proxy route reaches Vertex's list API After a fix, the same walk succeeds at step 2: 1. Create a Vertex batch through the proxy the same way 2. `GET /v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai` returns 200 with the provider-side listing from `litellm.alist_batches`, and the job created in step 1 is in it under its provider-side id 3. `GET /v1/batches` with no filter keeps returning the managed view, unchanged ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run the proxy with `DATABASE_URL` set (the managed-files hook registers automatically, `litellm/proxy/hooks/__init__.py` merges `ENTERPRISE_PROXY_HOOKS`) 2. `curl -sS -i "http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` 3. Observe HTTP 500 instead of a listing or a 4xx ### Relevant log output ```shell $ curl -sS -i "http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error {"error":{"message":"Filtering by 'provider' is not supported when using managed batches.","type":"internal_server_error","param":"None","code":"500"}} ``` Reproduced at both `0acca3e86a` (base of #35141) and that PR's head, litellm 1.97.0 ### What a fix PR should look like Scope it as endpoint routing, not as adding provider metadata to the managed-objects table (that larger design is sketched in the comment at `managed_files.py:343-345` and can stay future work) - `litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py`: gate the managed-files branch in `list_batches` on having no `provider` and no `target_model_names` (the hook rejects both identically, `managed_files.py:354-357`), so filtered requests fall through to the existing SCENARIO 2-alt and SCENARIO 3 handling. Roughly a one-condition change around line 685 - `enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py`: keep both guards as defense in depth, but raise `HTTPException(status_code=400, ...)` instead of bare `Exception`, so any remaining direct caller gets a 4xx rather than a 500 - Tests: adjust `tests/enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/test_managed_files.py::test_list_batches_from_managed_objects_table_provider_filter_raises_exception` and its `target_model_names` twin to expect the `HTTPException`; add an endpoint-level test that a provider-filtered list on a DB proxy routes to `litellm.alist_batches` rather than the hook. The `managed_filter_unsupported` carve-out in `tests/e2e/batches/test_batches_e2e.py:299-319` can then be simplified since the filtered list stops erroring - Behavior note for the PR body: SCENARIO 3 returns raw provider batch ids without unified-id encoding, matching what DB-less proxies do today, and unfiltered listing must not change - QA proof: on a DB proxy with Vertex credentials, `GET /v1/batches?provider=vertex_ai` returns 200 and reaches `VertexAIBatchPrediction.list_batches`, which also finally exercises the list-path error handling touched by #35141 end to end. `GET /v1/batches` unfiltered still returns the managed view ### What version of LiteLLM are you on? 1.97.0 (litellm_internal_staging, 1bafdb3c93)

signals.title: [Bug]: Bedrock-managed batch file uploads always report bytes: 0 in the returned FileObject
signals.text: ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When uploading a batch input file via `POST /v1/files` for a Bedrock managed-batch model, the file is uploaded to S3 correctly, but the `FileObject` returned to the client always reports `bytes: 0`, regardless of the actual size of the uploaded file. signals.title: [Bug]: Named MCP authorization-server issuer mismatches protected-resource metadata
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? For a named OAuth2 MCP server, LiteLLM's protected-resource metadata advertises a scoped authorization-server identifier: ```json { "authorization_servers": [ "https://proxy.example.com/example-server" ] } ``` However, the corresponding authorization-server metadata returns the bare proxy origin: ``` { "issuer": "https://proxy.example.com" } ``` RFC 8414 requires the returned issuer to exactly match the authorization-server identifier represented by that metadata. OAuth clients that validate issuer matching therefore reject discovery before authorization can begin. Expected behavior: ``` { "issuer": "https://proxy.example.com/example-server" } ``` The issuer should match authorization_servers[0] from the protected-resource metadata. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure an OAuth2 MCP server named `example-server` behind LiteLLM Proxy. 2. Request its protected-resource metadata: ```bash curl https://proxy.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/example-server 3. Observe that the response advertises the scoped authorization-server identifier: ``` { "authorization_servers": [ "https://proxy.example.com/example-server" ] } ``` 4. Request the corresponding authorization-server metadata: `curl https://proxy.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/example-server` 5. Observe that its issuer is the unscoped proxy origin: ``` { "issuer": "https://proxy.example.com" } ``` 6. Compare the values and observe that issuer does not equal authorization_servers[0]. An OAuth client that enforces RFC 8414 issuer validation rejects discovery before authorization begins. ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Feature]: Lakera v2 guardrail: advisory mode (inject_system_message) instead of block/monitor on flagged content
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Add a third `on_flagged` action to the Lakera v2 guardrail (`litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/lakera_ai_v2.py`): `inject_system_message`. On a flag, instead of raising HTTP 400 (`block`) or silently allowing the request (`monitor`), this mode appends an advisory system message describing why the request was flagged and lets the real LLM call proceed. The LLM itself then decides whether to respond helpfully or decline, based on the flagged reason and its own judgment of the actual request. The message-injection mechanism itself should be a shared, guardrail-agnostic helper on `CustomGuardrail` (not Lakera-only code), living next to the existing `raise_passthrough_exception` helper, since both represent generic strategies for handling a flagged request. `raise_passthrough_exception` short-circuits the LLM call entirely and returns a canned message; the new helper does the opposite: it lets the request through with an added note, and never blocks the LLM from seeing the underlying content. ### Motivation, pitch Lakera today only supports `on_flagged: block` (hard fail every flagged request) or `monitor` (log only, no user-visible effect at all). Neither option fits a common need: a false-positive-prone detector such as prompt-injection heuristics that can trip on legitimate instructional language (for example, a support agent prompt that says "ignore the customer's previous request and start a new ticket"). With `block`, that legitimate request fails outright. With `monitor`, a genuinely malicious request sails through with no signal reaching the model at all. An advisory mode gives a middle ground: the request proceeds, but the LLM is told the request was flagged and why, and can use its own judgment, similar to how a human reviewer would weigh a flagged item rather than auto-rejecting or ignoring the flag. This is especially useful for guardrails with a nonzero false-positive rate, where blocking outright causes real user friction but staying silent forfeits the LLM's ability to react to a real threat. This does not overlap with the existing `passthrough` mechanism (`raise_passthrough_exception`, used by several other guardrails via their own `on_flagged_action` field), which short-circuits the LLM call entirely and returns a canned response without ever showing the model the actual request. The proposal here is the opposite: the model sees the full, unmodified request plus an advisory note, and decides how to proceed. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No

signals.title: [Bug]: GET /health returns extra_headers and aws_session_token in plaintext
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related, not a duplicate: #18818 fixed masking of `extra_headers` on `/model/info`. `GET /health` is a different sanitizer. It still returns those values in full. `api_key` is stripped (CVE-2025-11203 class). `extra_headers` and `aws_session_token` were never added to that strip list. ### What happened? LiteLLM 1.96.2. No master key. A deployment in `config.yaml` has `extra_headers` (Azure `api-key`, Google `x-goog-api-key`, a Bearer token) and `aws_session_token`. `GET /health` returns those values in plaintext on the healthy (or unhealthy) row. `api_key` is absent. `api_base` is absent for a non-admin caller. The extra headers stay. This was reproduced with fake `CANARY_*` strings, not real provider keys. A live proxy with a normal `api_key: os.environ/...` and no `extra_headers` does not echo the resolved key on `/model/info` (`api_key` is popped). The hole is specifically fields that are not `api_key`. Expected: `/health` should omit or mask `extra_headers`, `headers`, and `aws_session_token` the same way it already omits `api_key`. ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a tenant who can call `/health` can read the admin's upstream credentials out of the JSON. 1. The proxy admin puts provider auth in `litellm_params.extra_headers` (and optionally `aws_session_token`) in `config.yaml`, then starts the proxy on `http://127.0.0.1:4000`. 2. Any caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health` with no `Authorization` header (default install, no master key). 3. HTTP 200. The `healthy_endpoints` (or `unhealthy_endpoints`) row contains `extra_headers.Authorization`, `extra_headers.x-goog-api-key`, `extra_headers.api-key`, and `aws_session_token` in full. 4. That caller can take those values and call the provider directly, bypassing the proxy. After a (hypothetical) fix: the same `/health` call still reports healthy/unhealthy, but those secret fields are gone or masked. 1. The proxy admin uses the same `config.yaml` and starts the same proxy. 2. The same caller sends `GET http://127.0.0.1:4000/health`. 3. HTTP 200. The row still has `model` and health status. It does not contain the `extra_headers` values or `aws_session_token`. 4. That caller cannot recover the admin's upstream credentials from `/health`. ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: mock litellm_params: model: openai/mockmodel api_base: http://127.0.0.1:9996/v1 api_key: sk-x-CANARY_DEPLOYMENT_API_KEY extra_headers: Authorization: Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE ``` The backend at `127.0.0.1:9996` is a local OpenAI-compatible stub that returns HTTP 200 so the row lands in `healthy_endpoints`. The leak is the proxy copying `litellm_params` into the `/health` body. It does not depend on a real provider key. You can drop the stub: point `api_base` at `http://127.0.0.1:1`. The health check fails, and the same fields still appear under `unhealthy_endpoints`. No API key required. Version or commit: LiteLLM **1.96.2** Commands and their full output: ``` curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health ``` ```json { "healthy_endpoints": [ { "model": "openai/mockmodel", "extra_headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION", "x-goog-api-key": "CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE", "api-key": "CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY" }, "aws_session_token": "CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE" } ], "unhealthy_endpoints": [], "healthy_count": 1, "unhealthy_count": 0 } ``` `api_key` is not in that object. `GET /v1/models` and `GET /health/liveliness` do not contain the canaries. Copy-paste repro, no keys, no stub: ```yaml # leak.yaml model_list: - model_name: demo litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_base: http://127.0.0.1:1 api_key: sk-not-a-real-key extra_headers: x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE ``` ``` litellm --config leak.yaml --port 4000 --host 127.0.0.1 curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4000/health ``` The canaries show up on the unhealthy row. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.96.2

signals.title: [Bug]: service_tier=priority silently billed at default rate for gpt-4o/gpt-4.1 family (missing pricing keys on dated-snapshot model entries)
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? ## Actual behaviour For `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, and `gpt-4.1-mini`, sending `service_tier="priority"` is accepted by OpenAI (the response correctly echoes back `response.service_tier == "priority"`), but the cost LiteLLM computes (`x-litellm-response-cost` header / spend logs) is identical to the **default**-tier cost, not the priority-tier cost. By contrast, the same test against `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-5.4-mini` correctly applies priority/flex pricing. ## Live verification (thunk-prod proxy, tiny `max_tokens=5` calls) | model | tier | prompt/completion tokens | reported cost | expected cost (priority rate) | |---|---|---|---|---| | gpt-4o-mini | priority | 9 / 2 | 2.55e-06 | 4.25e-06 | | gpt-4o | priority | 9 / 1 | 3.25e-05 | 5.525e-05 | | gpt-4.1 | priority | 9 / 1 | 2.6e-05 | 4.55e-05 | | gpt-4.1-mini | priority | 9 / 1 | 5.2e-06 | 9.1e-06 | In every case the "reported cost" exactly matches what default-tier pricing would produce for the same token counts, confirming priority pricing was silently not applied. ## Root cause `model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` defines `input_cost_per_token_priority` / `output_cost_per_token_priority` on the **alias** entries (`gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, `gpt-4.1-mini`) but **not** on the **dated-snapshot** entries that OpenAI actually echoes back in `response.model` (`gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, `gpt-4o-2024-11-20`, `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`, `gpt-4.1-2025-04-14`, `gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14`): ``` gpt-4o priority_in=4.25e-06 priority_out=1.7e-05 gpt-4o-2024-08-06 priority_in=None priority_out=None gpt-4o-2024-11-20 priority_in=None priority_out=None gpt-4o-mini priority_in=2.5e-07 priority_out=1e-06 gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 priority_in=None priority_out=None gpt-4.1 priority_in=3.5e-06 priority_out=1.4e-05 gpt-4.1-2025-04-14 priority_in=None priority_out=None gpt-4.1-mini priority_in=7e-07 priority_out=2.8e-06 gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14 priority_in=None priority_out=None ``` `cost_calculator.py`'s model-name resolution (`_select_model_name_for_cost_calc` / `potential_model_names`, around lines 688-692 and 1115-1131) prefers the dated snapshot name echoed by OpenAI over the caller-supplied alias when looking up pricing. `litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/utils.py`'s `_get_cost_per_unit` (~lines 349-388) then silently falls back to base (non-priority) pricing when the `_priority` key is absent on the resolved (dated-snapshot) model_info entry — no error or warning is raised. For `gpt-5`/`gpt-5-mini`, both the alias **and** the dated-snapshot entry (`gpt-5-2025-08-07`, `gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07`) carry `_priority` keys, so the same lookup path resolves correctly there — confirming this is a pricing-data completeness gap, not a code-path difference between model families. ## Expected behaviour Priority-tier cost should be applied whenever the model actually served the request at `priority` tier, regardless of whether the model resolves via alias or dated-snapshot name. Either: 1. Add `input_cost_per_token_priority`/`output_cost_per_token_priority` (and `_flex` where applicable) to the dated-snapshot JSON entries for these models, or 2. Make the cost-key fallback in `llm_cost_calc/utils.py` fall back from a dated-snapshot entry to its alias entry (not straight to base pricing) when a tier-specific key is missing. ## Impact Any proxy user billing `service_tier=priority` traffic on `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4.1`, or `gpt-4.1-mini` is under-reporting spend — potentially significantly, since priority pricing is ~1.7-2x the default rate on these models while actual OpenAI billing is presumably at the priority rate. ### Relevant log output _N/A — reproducible via `x-litellm-response-cost` response header, see table above._ ### Are you a ML Ops Team? - [ ] Yes ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? Reproduced against a production proxy; latest `main` as of 2026-08-15 has the same gap in `model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json`. ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: LiteLLM proxy silently returns understated token counts when Bedrock CountTokens is unsupported for a model
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? `bedrock-runtime`'s `CountTokens` API does not support most current Anthropic models — including **Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5** (full matrix below; of the current line-up only Sonnet 4.6 works). When it rejects a model, the proxy logs a warning and falls through to its local tokenizer. For these models the local tokenizer is badly miscalibrated, so `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` returns a **confidently wrong, much lower number** with a `200 OK` and no indication to the caller that the value is an estimate. Clients that use `count_tokens` for context management (Claude Code / Claude Desktop do) therefore believe they have far more headroom than they do, keep growing the conversation, and eventually get a hard `400 prompt is too long` from the provider — long after any context-compaction threshold should have fired. ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer running Claude Code against the proxy is told their conversation is ~675K tokens when the model actually measures it at ~1.19M, so their client never trims it and the next turn is rejected outright.** 1. They export `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://litellm-domain` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5`, then start a long refactoring session in Claude Code. 2. As the conversation grows, their client sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages/count_tokens` with `{"model": "claude-opus-5", "messages": [...the whole conversation...]}`. 3. It comes back `200 OK` with `{"input_tokens": 675431}` — a plain number, with nothing marking it as an estimate rather than a figure the model itself confirmed. 4. Their client compares 675,431 against the 1,000,000-token window Opus 5 advertises, concludes it is at ~68% capacity, and does not summarise or trim anything. 5. They send the next turn: `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with `{"model": "claude-opus-5", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [...the same conversation...]}`. 6. It comes back **`400`** with `{"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error", "message":"...prompt is too long: 1227544 tokens > 1000000 maximum"}}` — the model counted the identical conversation as **1,227,544** tokens, roughly 1.8× the number they were given in step 3. 7. Every retry fails the same way. Nothing they can request from the proxy reports a number anywhere near 1.2M, so from their seat the rejection has no visible cause. 8. If the proxy has `fallbacks` configured, they never see the 400 at all: the turn returns `200` and at `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` that request is listed against **`claude-sonnet-4-6`**, not the `claude-opus-5` they asked for — with the whole conversation re-charged as fresh input, so its cost on that page is roughly 9× the neighbouring turns. **After a (hypothetical) fix: the same call reports a count the model agrees with, so their client trims in time and the turn succeeds on the model they asked for.** 1. They export `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://litellm-domain` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5`, then start a long refactoring session in Claude Code. 2. As the conversation grows, their client sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages/count_tokens` with `{"model": "claude-opus-5", "messages": [...the whole conversation...]}`. 3. It comes back `200 OK` with `{"input_tokens": 1227544}` — matching what the model itself counts. (Equally acceptable from the user's seat: a `4xx` saying the count is unavailable for this model, which at least tells their client not to trust a guess.) 4. Their client compares 1,227,544 against the 1,000,000-token window, sees it is over capacity, and summarises the earlier part of the conversation before sending anything. 5. They send the next turn: `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with `{"model": "claude-opus-5", "max_tokens": 4096, "messages": [...the trimmed conversation...]}`. 6. It comes back **`200 OK`** with `"model": "claude-opus-5"` and a normal `usage` block. 7. The session continues. Trimming happens whenever the reported count approaches the window, so the wall is never hit. 8. At `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` every turn is listed against `claude-opus-5`, at costs consistent with its neighbours. ### Proof the bug occurs ## Steps to reproduce 1. Configure any model whose Bedrock `CountTokens` support is absent — e.g. ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-opus-5 litellm_params: model: bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-opus-5 aws_region_name: us-east-1 ``` 2. `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` with `{"model": "claude-opus-5", "messages": [...]}` 3. Observe `200 OK` with an `input_tokens` value, and in the proxy log: ``` LiteLLM:ERROR: handler.py:123 - HTTP error in CountTokens handler: Client error '400 Bad Request' for url 'https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/model/anthropic.claude-opus-5/count-tokens' LiteLLM:WARNING: bedrock_token_counter.py:91 - Bedrock CountTokens API error: status=400, message={"message":"The provided model doesn't support counting tokens."} LiteLLM Proxy:WARNING: proxy_server.py:8772 - Provider token counting failed (400): {"message":"The provided model doesn't support counting tokens."}. Falling back to local tokenizer. ``` ## Scope: this affects every current-generation Claude model on Bedrock This is not one edge-case model. Probed directly against `bedrock-runtime` in `us-east-1` (`aws bedrock-runtime count-tokens --model-id <id> --input '{"invokeModel":{"body":"…"}}'`, body containing a valid Anthropic Messages payload with `max_tokens`): | Model ID | Bedrock `CountTokens` | |---|---| | `anthropic.claude-opus-5` | ❌ `ValidationException: The provided model doesn't support counting tokens.` | | `anthropic.claude-opus-4-8` | ❌ same | | `anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` | ❌ same | | `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0` | ❌ same | | `anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5` | ❌ `The provided model identifier is invalid.` | | **`anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`** | ✅ **works** — returns `{"inputTokens": 26}` | | `global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` | ❌ unsupported — **the geo prefix alone breaks a model that works bare** | So of the current Claude line-up, **only Sonnet 4.6 can be counted on `bedrock-runtime`.** Every other model — including Opus 5 and Sonnet 5, the current defaults — takes the local-tokenizer path on every `count_tokens` call. Two diagnostic notes for whoever picks this up: - A **different** error message (`max_tokens: Field required`) means the model *is* supported and only the request body was wrong. `"doesn't support counting tokens"` is the real rejection, and is what should gate any retry logic. - The proxy already strips the geo/global prefix when building the CountTokens URL (the logged URL is `/model/anthropic.claude-opus-5/count-tokens` for a model configured as `bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-opus-5`), which is correct — passing the prefixed ID through would fail even for Sonnet 4.6. Worth preserving if this code is touched. ## Measured error Identical text throughout. `claude-sonnet-4-6` *is* supported by Bedrock CountTokens, so it gives an authoritative reference count; the target model's true count comes from the provider's own rejection message, which states both the count and the limit. **Tokenizer ratio** — same text, two models: | source | tokens | |---|---| | `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` via Bedrock `CountTokens` (authoritative) | 745,753 | | `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5` — from `ValidationException: prompt is too long: 1227544 tokens > 1000000 maximum` | **1,227,544** | | ratio | **1.646×** | **What the proxy reports** — same 400-paragraph sample: | source | tokens | |---|---| | Bedrock `CountTokens` for `claude-sonnet-4-6` (authoritative) | 12,025 | | proxy `count_tokens` for `claude-sonnet-4-6` | 12,025 ✅ exact (provider path used) | | proxy `count_tokens` for `claude-opus-5` | **11,208** ⬅ local tokenizer, 0.93× the sonnet count | | `claude-opus-5` real count (0.93 → 1.646 correction) | **~19,793** | **The proxy understates this model by ~1.77×.** Note the local tokenizer returns *slightly fewer* tokens than the older model's tokenizer, while the target model's real tokenizer produces considerably more — the two errors compound. ## Impact With a 1,000,000-token model limit, the effective ceiling expressed in numbers the proxy reports is about **565K**. A client that compacts at, say, 80% of the advertised window would trigger at 800K reported — i.e. **~1.41M real, which is past the hard limit.** The safety mechanism is unreachable: the request fails before the threshold is ever approached. Observed in production: a long agentic session ran to ~1.19–1.22M real tokens while the client believed it was around 675K, then failed with `prompt is too long`. Requests below the boundary succeeded normally, so the failure is purely a function of size. Two secondary effects worth noting: 1. **Cost.** If `litellm_settings.fallbacks` is configured, the resulting 400 is silently retried on the fallback model. Prompt caches are per-model, so the fallback runs cold and re-reads the entire context at full price. In our case the per-request cost rose roughly 9×, with no error surfaced to the client and — see below — nothing in the logs. 2. **CPU.** Local tokenization of very large contexts is expensive. Repeated `count_tokens` calls over ~150K-token conversations saturated one of two vCPUs on the proxy host, causing an outage: the app stayed internally healthy while throughput collapsed and health checks timed out. ## Reproduction helper Deliberately overshooting is free — a rejected request is not billed, and the error names both the real token count and the limit, which is the only way we found to obtain a ground-truth count for a model Bedrock will not count: ```python import json, boto3 br = boto3.client("bedrock-runtime", region_name="us-east-1") br.invoke_model(modelId="global.anthropic.claude-opus-5", body=json.dumps({ "anthropic_version": "bedrock-2023-05-31", "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<oversized text>"}]})) # botocore.errorfactory.ValidationException: # prompt is too long: 1227544 tokens > 1000000 maximum ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.96.2 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_
signals.author: ravinder79

signals.title: [Bug]: Admin-only route denials return 401 instead of 403, and are recorded in Prometheus with exception_status="None"
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a non-admin user calls an admin-only management route, the proxy correctly refuses the request but reports the refusal incorrectly in two ways. **Problem 1 — the client receives 401 instead of 403.** Authentication succeeded: the proxy identifies the caller well enough to name their role and user ID in the error message, and other requests in the same session succeed with the same key. The request is refused purely on authorization, so the correct status is **403 Forbidden**. Returning **401** is misleading. It tells the client its credentials are invalid, when in fact the key is valid, retrying with it is correct, and re-authenticating will not help. The proxy already returns 403 for comparable permission denials elsewhere. **Problem 2 — the failure is recorded in Prometheus with `exception_status="None"`.** The denial carries no status code at the point metrics are recorded; the HTTP status is only decided later, when the error is turned into the client response. Prometheus therefore records: ``` litellm_proxy_failed_requests_metric_total{exception_class="Exception", exception_status="None", route="/key/aliases"} ``` This is not limited to one endpoint. In our deployment the same label pair is produced by at least ten admin-only routes, all triggered by non-admin users loading Admin UI pages: `/key/aliases`, `/organization/list`, `/team/list`, `/tag/list`, `/policies/list`, `/prompts/list`, `/user/available_roles`, `/search_tools/list`, `/search_tools/ui/available_providers`, `/in_product_nudges`. These denials are indistinguishable by label from real infrastructure failures, which also appear as `exception_class="Exception"`, `exception_status="None"` — database-connectivity failures during auth, for example. There is no label that separates a routine permission denial from an outage, so they cannot be excluded from a proxy error-rate alert. **What I expected:** a 403 response, recorded with a matching `exception_status="403"` so that routine authorization denials can be told apart from proxy failures. ### User Flow The flow fails at step 3: the viewer is told their credentials are invalid, when in fact their credentials are fine and they simply lack permission. 1. A teammate with the `internal_user_viewer` role signs in to the Admin UI at `http://localhost:4000/ui` using their virtual key. 2. They open the Virtual Keys page. The page loads and lists the keys they are allowed to see, confirming their key is accepted. 3. The page requests `GET /key/aliases`. The response is **401 Unauthorized**, with body text beginning `Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/key/aliases. Your role=internal_user_viewer`. 4. The viewer reads "Authentication Error" and "401", concludes their key has expired or been revoked, and asks an admin to reissue it. The new key behaves identically. 5. Meanwhile `GET /organization/list` with the same key returns **200 OK**, so the key is demonstrably valid — the two responses contradict each other. 6. On the operations side, the 401 from step 3 is counted as a proxy failure with no status attached. It cannot be told apart from a database outage, so the error-rate alert fires and pages the on-call for what was only a viewer opening a page. Authorization consequence: no user gains access they should not have — the route is correctly refused. The cost is that a legitimate viewer is told their identity is invalid, and an operator cannot distinguish routine denials from real failures. ### Proof the bug occurs ```yaml router_settings: redis_host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST redis_port: os.environ/REDIS_PORT redis_password: os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD litellm_settings: cache: True cache_params: type: redis host: os.environ/REDIS_HOST port: os.environ/REDIS_PORT password: os.environ/REDIS_PASSWORD supported_call_types: [] callbacks: ["prometheus"] service_callback: ["prometheus_system"] prometheus_metrics_config: - group: "traffic_total_requests" metrics: - "litellm_proxy_total_requests_metric" include_labels: - "status_code" - "requested_model" - "route" - group: "traffic_failed_requests" metrics: - "litellm_proxy_failed_requests_metric" include_labels: - "exception_status" - "exception_class" - "requested_model" - "route" ``` Version: v1.81.3-stable **Problem 1 — 401 returned for an authorization failure** Preceding request in the same session, same virtual key — succeeds, confirming the caller is authenticated: ``` INFO: 10.x.x.x:<> - "GET /organization/list HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` Seconds later, the same session requests an admin-only route. **Client response: 401 Unauthorized** (expected: 403 Forbidden): ``` LiteLLM Proxy:ERROR: auth_exception_handler.py:78 - litellm.proxy.proxy_server.user_api_key_auth(): Exception occured - Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/key/aliases. Your role=internal_user_viewer. Your user_id=<> Requester IP Address: 10.x.x.x Traceback (most recent call last): File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py", line 1154, in _user_api_key_auth_builder _ = await common_checks( ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ...<11 lines>... ) ^ File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py", line 285, in common_checks _is_route_allowed = _is_allowed_route( route=route, ...<4 lines>... valid_token=valid_token, ) File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py", line 407, in _is_allowed_route return _is_api_route_allowed( route=route, ...<3 lines>... user_obj=user_obj, ) File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py", line 362, in _is_api_route_allowed RouteChecks.non_proxy_admin_allowed_routes_check( ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^ user_obj=user_obj, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ...<4 lines>... valid_token=valid_token, ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ) ^ File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/route_checks.py", line 252, in non_proxy_admin_allowed_routes_check RouteChecks._raise_admin_only_route_exception( ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^ user_obj=user_obj, route=route ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ ) ^ File "/usr/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/route_checks.py", line 143, in _raise_admin_only_route_exception raise Exception( f"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route={route}. Your role={user_role}. Your user_id={masked_user_id}" ) Exception: Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/key/aliases. Your role=internal_user_viewer. Your user_id=<> ``` **Problem 2 — the denial is recorded with `exception_status="None"`** ```promql sum by (exception_class, exception_status, route) ( increase(litellm_proxy_failed_requests_metric_total{exception_class="Exception"}[5m]) ) ``` Ten admin-only routes, all recorded as `exception_status="None"`: The proxy is explicitly configured to emit `exception_status` for this metric (see `include_labels` above) — the label is requested and populated, and its value is the literal string `"None"` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.81.3-stable ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: Bedrock OpenAI GPT-5.6 (us.openai.*) — Responses routing hang + missing chat/stream transforms
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related (not duplicates — different symptoms / code paths): - #36922 — FastAPI `get_flat_dependant` startup crash (same root as Bug 1 below) - #36016 — `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*` metadata `mode: responses` (related to Bug 2 fuzzy match / routing) This issue covers end-to-end failures when calling **Bedrock Invoke** models via `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}` (Chat Completions / Anthropic Messages proxy), which are not covered by the above. --- ### What happened? On **litellm 1.97.0** with FastAPI **0.141.1**, proxying AWS Bedrock OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (`bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol|terra|luna` in `us-east-1`) fails in four stacked ways: 1. **Proxy may not start** with recent FastAPI (`ImportError: cannot import name 'get_flat_dependant'`). 2. **Requests hang forever** unless the model is forced to chat mode — routing incorrectly treats these as Responses API models (fuzzy match against `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*` with `mode: responses`), leading to an infinite completion ↔ responses bridge loop. 3. **Non-streaming** returns `BadRequestError` / `'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` when parsing the Bedrock OpenAI Chat Completions JSON (no OpenAI provider branch in the Invoke response transform; falls through to Titan `results[0].outputText`). 4. **Streaming** returns valid SSE / event structure but **empty text** on every delta (no OpenAI `choices[].delta.content` branch in the event-stream chunk parser). **Expected:** `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-*` work as chat models for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` (stream + non-stream), same as other Bedrock chat providers. **Workaround that unblocks after local patches:** set `model_info.mode: chat` on each model, plus add OpenAI cases to Invoke `transform_response` and stream `_chunk_parser` (see Technical notes). --- ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix:** a developer who configured Bedrock GPT-5.6 on the proxy never gets usable completions (hang, parse error, or empty stream). 1. They add `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` to the proxy `model_list` and start the proxy (or hit startup ImportError on FastAPI ≥0.115). 2. They send `POST /v1/chat/completions` (or `/v1/messages`) with a short user message to that model alias. 3. Without `model_info.mode: chat`, the request never returns (proxy hangs / retries forever). 4. With `mode: chat` forced, non-stream returns HTTP 400-class LiteLLM error mentioning BedrockException / `'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` while the raw body still contains OpenAI-shaped `choices[].message.content`. 5. With non-stream patched locally, stream returns SSE / Anthropic event frames but every `content_block_delta` / delta has empty text — client UI shows a finished stream with no tokens. **After a (hypothetical) fix:** the same Bedrock GPT-5.6 alias works for chat and messages, stream and non-stream, without hanging or empty deltas. 1. Admin configures `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` (no special `mode` workaround required). 2. Developer sends the same `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages`. 3. Non-stream returns assistant text + usage in the normal OpenAI / Anthropic response shape. 4. Stream returns incremental text deltas with a normal finish reason. --- ### Proof the bug occurs **Config / setup the proxy ran with:** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-sol-bedrock # Without this, requests hang (Bug 2). With it, Bugs 3–4 still reproduce. model_info: mode: chat litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol aws_profile_name: your-profile aws_region_name: us-east-1 drop_params: true general_settings: master_key: "sk-litellm-local" ``` Same pattern for `us.openai.gpt-5.6-terra` and `us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna`. **Version or commit:** litellm **1.97.0**, FastAPI **0.141.1**, Python **3.11**, macOS aarch64, AWS region **us-east-1**. **Observed errors / symptoms:** Bug 1 — startup: ```text ImportError: cannot import name 'get_flat_dependant' from 'fastapi.dependencies.utils' ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'proxy_server' ``` Bug 2 — without `model_info.mode: chat`: request hangs indefinitely; debug shows recursive `acompletion` via Responses bridge after fuzzy-matching `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol` (`mode: responses`). Bug 3 — non-streaming (with `mode: chat`): ```text litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - Error processing={"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"annotations":[],"content":"ok","role":"assistant"}}],...}, Received error='NoneType' object is not subscriptable ``` (Note: payload already contains valid OpenAI `choices[].message.content` — parse path is wrong.) Bug 4 — streaming (after Bug 3 fixed locally): SSE / `/v1/messages` event stream structure is valid, but all content deltas are empty strings. Non-stream works; stream does not (separate code path). **Models tested:** `us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, `us.openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, `us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna`. --- ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy (Also reproducible via SDK completion paths that use Bedrock Invoke transforms.) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_ --- ### Technical notes (for maintainers) **Bug 1** — `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/common.py` still imports `get_flat_dependant` (removed FastAPI 0.115+). See also #36922. **Bug 2** — Built-in `model_cost` has `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*` with `mode: responses`. Resolving `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` fuzzy-matches that entry → `responses_api_bridge` → infinite loop. Prefer `mode: chat` (+ keep `/v1/responses` in endpoints if needed) **or** stop cross-matching `bedrock/us.openai.*` → `bedrock_mantle/openai.*`. Overlaps #36016 metadata discussion; hang is the user-visible failure here. **Bug 3** — `litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/invoke_transformations/base_invoke_transformation.py`: `transform_request` already has an `openai` branch; `transform_response` does not — falls through to Titan `results[0]`. Suggested: handle `provider == "openai"` via `choices[0].message.content` + usage; also strip Anthropic-only optional params before Invoke for OpenAI models. **Bug 4** — `litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/invoke_handler.py` `AWSEventStreamDecoder._chunk_parser`: add branch for OpenAI stream chunks `choices[0].delta.content` / `finish_reason`. Happy to open a PR with the local patches if useful.

signals.title: [Bug]: chat->responses bridge emits output_text input items without required 'annotations' field (strict providers like Azure reject with 400)
signals.text: ### What happened? When a `/chat/completions` request for a gpt-5.x model contains **both `tools` and `reasoning_effort`**, LiteLLM correctly bridges the request to the Responses API (the upstream chat endpoint rejects that combination with *"Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported ... Please use /v1/responses instead"*). However, the bridge converts assistant **history** messages into `output_text` content blocks **without the `annotations` field**: ```python # litellm/completion_extras/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py def _convert_content_str_to_input_text(self, content: str, role: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: if role == "user" or role == "system" or role == "tool": return {"type": "input_text", "text": content} else: return {"type": "output_text", "text": content} # <-- no "annotations" ``` Per the OpenAI spec, `annotations` is **required** on `output_text` items passed as input. See the official openai-python SDK type ([response_output_text_param.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response_output_text_param.py)): ```python class ResponseOutputTextParam(TypedDict, total=False): annotations: Required[Iterable[Annotation]] # Required text: Required[str] type: Required[Literal["output_text"]] ``` OpenAI's own endpoint is lenient about the missing field, but stricter spec-conformant providers (e.g. **Azure AI Foundry `/openai/v1`**) reject the bridged request with 400: ```json { "error": { "code": "invalid_payload", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations", "type": "invalid_request_error" } } ``` Every odd `input[N]` index in the error corresponds to an assistant history message, so any multi-turn conversation (2nd request onward) fails. First requests succeed because there is no assistant history yet. This breaks agentic clients (OpenCode, etc.) that always send `tools` + `reasoning_effort`. ### Reproduction Proxy config: `openai/gpt-5.x` model with `api_base` pointing to an Azure AI Foundry v1 endpoint (`https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<proj>/openai/v1`). ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.x-deployment", "reasoning_effort": "medium", "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_time","description":"get time","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{}}}}], "messages": [ {"role":"user","content":"say ok"}, {"role":"assistant","content":"ok"}, {"role":"user","content":"again"} ] }' ``` Matrix (all against the same deployment): | payload | result | |---|---| | multi-turn only | 200 OK (no bridge) | | multi-turn + `reasoning_effort` | 200 OK (no bridge) | | multi-turn + `tools` | 200 OK (no bridge) | | multi-turn + `tools` + `reasoning_effort` | **400 annotations error** (bridged) | The value of `reasoning_effort` doesn't matter (`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high` all fail). ### Proposed fix One line — always emit the field, empty array when there are no annotations: ```python return {"type": "output_text", "text": content, "annotations": []} ``` (The list-content path `_convert_content_to_responses_format` should likewise preserve/emit `annotations` on `output_text` items.) Related (opposite direction, already fixed): #18378 / #18754 handled responses→chat annotation preservation; this issue is about the chat→responses **request** direction. ### Relevant log output ``` litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - { "error": { "code": "invalid_payload", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations", "type": "invalid_request_error", "details": [ {"code": "ValidationError", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations", "type": "error"}, {"code": "ValidationError", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[3].content[0].annotations", "type": "error"} ] } } ``` ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.88.1

signals.title: [Bug]: Proxy shutdown always fails with AttributeError when Redis cluster mode is enabled (async_redis_conn_pool is None)
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? With Redis **cluster mode** enabled, every proxy shutdown ends in an unhandled `AttributeError`, and uvicorn reports `Application shutdown failed. Exiting.` ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'disconnect' File "litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 1232, in <lifespan> await proxy_shutdown_event() File "litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 843, in proxy_shutdown_event await litellm.cache.disconnect() File "litellm/caching/caching.py", line 913, in disconnect await self.cache.disconnect() File "litellm/caching/redis_cache.py", line 1356, in disconnect await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True) ``` This is deterministic, not intermittent — it fires on every shutdown. ### User Flow ### Suggested fix Two parts: 1. Guard the base class — `redis_cache.py`: ```python async def disconnect(self): if self.async_redis_conn_pool is not None: await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True) ``` 2. Give `RedisClusterCache` a real teardown, since the guard alone leaks the cluster client: ```python async def disconnect(self): if self.redis_async_redis_cluster_client is not None: await self.redis_async_redis_cluster_client.aclose() await super().disconnect() ``` `aclose()` is already the primitive used in `test_connection()` in that same file. Wrapping the `litellm.cache.disconnect()` call in `proxy_shutdown_event()` in a try/except would also stop one cache failure from aborting the rest of shutdown, independent of this bug. ### Proof the bug occurs ### Root cause `get_redis_connection_pool()` returns `None` by design in cluster mode, because a `RedisCluster` builds its own per-node pools rather than taking a shared `BlockingConnectionPool` — `litellm/_redis.py:691-692`: ```python if "startup_nodes" in redis_kwargs: return None ``` `RedisCache.__init__` stores that `None` unconditionally (`redis_cache.py:309`), and `RedisCache.disconnect()` then dereferences it with no guard (`redis_cache.py:1355-1356`): ```python async def disconnect(self): await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True) ``` `RedisClusterCache` overrides `init_async_client`, the two mget paths and `test_connection` — but **not** `disconnect()` — so the base-class dereference is always reached. ### Impact The exception propagates out of `proxy_shutdown_event()`, so everything ordered after `litellm.cache.disconnect()` is skipped: | line | step | outcome | |---|---|---| | 838-840 | `flush_gateway_requests()`, `prisma_client.disconnect()` | ✅ run before the crash | | 843 | `litellm.cache.disconnect()` | 💥 raises | | 845 | `jwt_handler.close()` | ❌ skipped | | 848 | `db_writer_client.close()` | ❌ skipped | | 852 | `shutdown_billing_metrics_recorder()` | ❌ skipped | | 856 | langfuse flush | ❌ skipped | | 868 | `cleanup_router_config_variables()` | ❌ skipped | Prisma closing first bounds the damage, but the skipped billing flush is data loss by your own comment at `proxy_server.py:851-852`: *"final flush of billable-request counts: without it, up to one export interval of enterprise billing data is dropped on every restart."* Anyone running cluster mode with enterprise billing or langfuse loses that on every restart. ### Reproduce 1. Point the proxy at any cluster-mode Redis (e.g. ElastiCache Serverless, which is always cluster-mode) and set `REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES`. 2. Start the proxy, then send SIGTERM. 3. Shutdown raises instead of completing. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.97.0 (also reproduces on 1.96.2 — same code, only a Final annotation differs) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signals.title: [Bug]: Non-streaming requests never cancel upstream work when the client disconnects
signals.text: # [Bug]: Non-streaming requests never cancel upstream work when the client disconnects ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related but distinct: - #30244 / #30245 — fixed the **streaming** `/chat/completions` path (confirmed working, see below). - #36123 — streaming `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` still leak. Open. - #3341 — the original feature request for this behaviour. Closed as "done" in 2024, then reverted. Details below. This report is about the **non-streaming** path, which none of the above covers. ### What happened? When a client disconnects from a non-streaming request, the proxy never tells the upstream provider to stop. The backend keeps generating to completion, holding GPU memory and a scheduler slot for a response nobody will read. If the user retries after their own timeout, the orphaned work stacks up. ### History `check_request_disconnection()` was added for #3341 and wired into the `chat_completion` and `completion` routes. It was then removed in [`498bfa9`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/498bfa9a4cc7eeb00eec31af8be50689a68b4835) ("fix - revert check_request_disconnection"). A user asked on #3341 why the revert happened and never received an answer. On `v1.89.5` the function definition survives at `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:1936` with **zero call sites** anywhere in the package. On current `main` the function is gone entirely, and `proxy_server.py` contains no `is_disconnected` reference at all. So the streaming path was repaired by #30245 while the non-streaming path has been without cancellation since 2024. ### Reproduction Backend: a local OpenAI-compatible server that *does* implement disconnect cancellation (polls `Request.is_disconnected()` and aborts the generation task), so the backend is not the variable here. **Through the proxy, non-streaming** — client killed at 20 s: ``` 08:52:35 client disconnects 08:53:55 backend log: Chat completion: 1 tokens in 87.06s, prompt: 11213 ``` The backend ran for a further 67 s after the client was gone. **Direct to the same backend, non-streaming** — client killed at 15 s: ``` backend log: Request b6b64dc4-... cancelled, aborting ``` Cancelled immediately. **Through the proxy, streaming** — client killed at 18 s: ``` 09:00:36 client disconnects 09:00:36 backend log: Aborting request dba57122-... ``` Cancelled in the same second — #30245 works. The only variable across the three runs is proxy-vs-direct and stream-vs-non-stream. ### Expected A client disconnect on a non-streaming request should cancel the upstream call, the same way it now does for streaming `/chat/completions`. ### Questions 1. Was the 2024 revert of `check_request_disconnection` due to a specific problem (false positives from `is_disconnected()`, interaction with spend logging, event-loop cost of the polling task)? #3341 never got an answer, and knowing the reason would shape any fix. 2. Is a `poll`-based approach still the intended design, or should non-streaming reuse the response-closing mechanism that #30245 introduced for streaming? ### Relevant log output See reproduction section above. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.89.5 (behaviour also expected on `main`, where the function no longer exists at all)

signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? # Bug: LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend remains 0 while SpendLogs accumulates spend ## Summary We've identified an inconsistency between `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` and `LiteLLM_VerificationToken`. For at least one API key, LiteLLM successfully: - accepts requests - records token usage - calculates request cost - writes non-zero spend into `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` However, the corresponding record in `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` still shows: ```text spend = 0 ``` This causes the UI to display zero spend for the key even though billable traffic exists. --- ## Environment - LiteLLM Proxy - PostgreSQL backend - Model: `<MODEL_NAME>` --- ### User Flow ## Evidence ### VerificationToken record ```sql SELECT key_alias, spend, team_id, max_budget FROM "LiteLLM_VerificationToken" WHERE token='<API_KEY_1>'; ``` Result: ```text key_alias : <KEY_ALIAS> team_id : <TEAM_ID> max_budget: 833 spend : 0 ``` ### SpendLogs for the same key ```sql SELECT COUNT(*) AS*requests, SUM(total_tokens) AS*total_tokens, SUM(spend) AS to*al_spend FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" *HERE api_key='<API_KEY_1>'; ``* *esult: ```text requests = 45*80 total_tokens = 3309020890 tota*_spend* = 123.02 *`* This shows the key has generated*significant billable traffic and s*end is being calculated correctly.* ### Proof the bug occurs ## Evidence ### VerificationToken record ```sql SELECT key_alias, spend, team_id, max_budget FROM "LiteLLM_VerificationToken" WHERE token='<API_KEY_1>'; ``` Result: ```text key_alias : <KEY_ALIAS> team_id : <TEAM_ID> max_budget: 833 spend : 0 ``` ### SpendLogs for the same key ```sql SELECT COUNT(*) AS*requests, SUM(total_tokens) AS*total_tokens, SUM(spend) AS to*al_spend FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" *HERE api_key='<API_KEY_1>'; ``* *esult: ```text requests = 45*80 total_tokens = 3309020890 tota*_spend* = 123.02 *`* This shows the key has generated*significant billable traffic and s*end is being calculated correctly.* ### Example successful request `*`sql SELECT model, *status, total_tokens, spen*, *metadata*FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" WHERE api*key='<API_KEY_1>' AND spend > 0 *IMIT 1; ``` Relevant metadata: `*`json { "cost_breakdown": { *"input_cost": 0.000008, "outpu*_cost": 0.000296, *"*otal_cost": 0.000304 }, "model*map_information": { "model_map*key": "<MODEL_NAME>", * "model_map_value": { "key*: "custom_openai/<MODEL_NAME>" * *} } } *`` The request is successful and *ost calculation is working correct*y. --- ## Expected Behavior `Li*eLLM_VerificationToken.spend` shou*d reflect the accumulated spend fo* the key. Expected: ```text Lite*LM_VerificationToken.spend ≈ 123.0* ``` --- ## Actual Behavior ```*ext LiteLLM_SpendLogs.total_spend * 123.02 LiteLLM_VerificationToken.*pend = 0 ``` Spend logging works *orrectly, but the spend value trac*ed on the API key record never upd*tes. --- ## Additional Observati*n We found another API key: ```t*xt <API_KEY_2> ``` For this key: *```text VerificationToken.spend = * SpendLogs.total_spend = 0 ``` Su*cessful requests showed: ```json*{ "cost_breakdown": null, *"*odel_map_information": { "mode*_map_key": "<MODEL_NAME>", * *"model_map_value": null *} } *`` This appears to be a separate *odel-mapping issue. The primary b*g reported here is that even when *pend is successfully calculated an* written to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`, t*e corresponding `LiteLLM_Verificat*onToken.spend` field remains `0`. *--- ## Questions 1. Is `LiteLLM_*erificationToken.spend` expected t* be updated in current LiteLLM ver*ions? 2. If yes, what component, *ob, or process is responsible for *pdating this field? 3. Under what*conditions can `LiteLLM_SpendLogs`*continue accumulating spend while *LiteLLM_VerificationToken.spend` r*mains 0? ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? signals.title: [Bug]: GET /v1/batches returns 200 for ?limit=0, -1, 101 and 1000; limit=0 returns 20 records
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [X] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? `GET /v1/batches?limit=` returns HTTP 200 for values outside 1..100. On an account holding 99 batches: | `limit` | Records returned | `has_more` | | --- | --- | --- | | 0 | 20 | true | | -1 | 0 | false | | 1 | 1 | true | | 2 | 2 | true | | 5 | 5 | true | | 101 | 97 | false | | 1000 | 97 | false | OpenAI returns HTTP 400 for values outside 1..100: ```json { "error": { "message": "Invalid 'limit': integer above maximum value. Expected a value <= 100, but got 101 instead.", "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": "limit", "code": "integer_above_max_value" } } ``` ### Code as it stands at v1.94.3 `litellm/proxy/batches_endpoints/endpoints.py:574`: ```python async def list_batches( request: Request, fastapi_response: Response, provider: Optional[str] = None, limit: Optional[int] = None, after: Optional[str] = None, user_api_key_dict: UserAPIKeyAuth = Depends(user_api_key_auth), target_model_names: Optional[str] = None, ): ``` No `Query(...)` constraint is attached to `limit`. --- ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix: a script paginating batch history computes a page size of 0 and receives 20 records** 1. The script sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=100` and processes the returned page 2. Its remaining-count arithmetic yields `0` on the final iteration 3. It sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=0` 4. The response is `200` carrying 20 records, so the script processes 20 records it did not request 5. A separate call with `?limit=101` returns `200` carrying 97 records 6. A call with `?limit=-1` returns `200` carrying 0 records **After a (hypothetical) fix: values outside 1..100 return 400** 1. The script sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=100` and processes the returned page 2. Its remaining-count arithmetic yields `0` on the final iteration 3. It sends `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=0` 4. The response is `400` with `"Invalid 'limit'"` and `"param": "limit"` 5. `?limit=101` returns `400` 6. `?limit=-1` returns `400` --- ### Proof the bug occurs **Version**: `litellm 1.94.3`, image digest `sha256:b7d979bac2a9e8fbb7d55272ef5f1f4a08ab365de8f78b1800834ca718d4c941`. The account held 99 batches. No provider call is made on this path. **Config the proxy ran with** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5-batch litellm_params: model: azure/gpt-5-batch-2025-08-07 api_base: os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` **Commands and their full output** ``` $ for L in 0 -1 1 2 5 101 1000; do N=$(curl -s "http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?limit=$L" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(len(d.get("data",[])), "has_more=",d.get("has_more"))') printf 'limit=%-6s -> %s\n' "$L" "$N" done limit=0 -> 20 has_more= True limit=-1 -> 0 has_more= False limit=1 -> 1 has_more= True limit=2 -> 2 has_more= True limit=5 -> 5 has_more= True limit=101 -> 97 has_more= False limit=1000 -> 97 has_more= False ``` Status code for one of them: ``` $ curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'HTTP %{http_code}\n' 'http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?limit=0' \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" HTTP 200 ``` The total returned by a single in-range request: ``` $ curl -s 'http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?limit=100' -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("total:", len(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]))' total: 99 ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.94.3

signals.title: [Bug]: GET /v1/batches with after= does not advance: 99 batches walked in pages of 10 returned 16 distinct rows and has_more stayed true
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [X] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? On an account holding 99 managed batches, walking `GET /v1/batches?limit=10` and passing the `id` of each page's last item as `after` on the next request: - 15 pages returned 10 rows each, 150 rows total - 16 of those rows were distinct - 83 of the 99 batches did not appear in any page - `has_more` was `true` on every page, including page 15 Two consecutive pages at `limit=3` shared 2 of 3 rows. ### Code as it stands at v1.94.3 `litellm_enterprise/proxy/hooks/managed_files.py:318`: ```python if after: where_clause["id"] = {"gt": after} fetch_limit = limit or 20 if target_model_names: # Oversample so post-fetch model-name filtering still has enough rows. fetch_limit = max(fetch_limit * 3, 100) batches = await self.prisma_client.db.litellm_managedobjecttable.find_many( where=where_clause, take=fetch_limit, order={"created_at": "desc"}, ) ``` `:341`, inside the loop over `batches`: ```python batch_obj = LiteLLMBatch(**batch_data) batch_obj.id = batch.unified_object_id batch_objects.append(batch_obj) ``` `:354`: ```python return build_list_page( batch_objects, has_more=len(batch_objects) == (limit or 20) ) ``` `batch_objects` excludes rows dropped earlier in the same loop when `file_object` fails to parse, and rows excluded by `build_owner_filter`. The two columns involved hold different value shapes: ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -t -c \ "SELECT id, unified_object_id FROM \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" WHERE file_purpose='batch' ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 3;" d11caa62-27a6-4279-adb2-e70b7f4aa1fe | bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDo0ZDhhNWVmMGY2Y2M5OTZkMmEwYzlmYmEzYTMxMzQ5Mjg0OTYxNWNhM2E2YmJjNGRjOTcyMDQ0Mjg4MTBmMjk0O2xsbV9iYXRjaF9pZDpiYXRjaF8yMDI2MDgxNy0wNTU4LjMyMA d0fc3f0d-4edd-458a-bfe6-601f98a816f6 | bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDo0ZDhhNWVmMGY2Y2M5OTZkMmEwYzlmYmEzYTMxMzQ5Mjg0OTYxNWNhM2E2YmJjNGRjOTcyMDQ0Mjg4MTBmMjk0O2xsbV9iYXRjaF9pZDpiYXRjaF8yMDI2MDgxNy0wNTU3LjAxOQ 32e97180-688a-4e74-a757-bcf9924915af | bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTttb2RlbF9pZDo2MzA0N2NjOGU1MzU3MWJmMDRiY2E4ODZiYjhiNzljNjg5MmQ5OWIwMjEwZGIzMTdhM2Y3MTVmM2EzZjYyMDQ0O2xsbV9iYXRjaF9pZDpiYXRjaF8yMDI2MDgxMy0xMDMxLjMzNA ``` `id` holds a UUID. `unified_object_id`, the value returned to the caller as `id`, holds a base64 string. The `{"gt": after}` filter is applied to `id`. --- ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix: an analyst exporting a quarter of batch jobs receives repeated rows and a loop that does not end** 1. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=10` and receive 10 batches 2. They take the `id` of the last item and send `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=10&after=<that id>` 3. The second page returns 10 batches, of which 8 appeared on page 1 4. Every page reports `"has_more": true`, so their loop continues requesting pages 5. They stop it after 15 pages. It has collected 150 rows containing 16 distinct batches, and 83 of the account's 99 batches appear on no page 6. Every call in the sequence returned `200` **After a (hypothetical) fix: each page continues from the previous one and the loop ends** 1. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=10` and receive 10 batches 2. They take the `id` of the last item and send `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches?limit=10&after=<that id>` 3. The second page returns 10 batches, none of which appeared on page 1 4. On the tenth page `"has_more"` is `false`, so their loop exits 5. The 10 pages together contain all 99 batches, each once 6. Every call in the sequence returned `200` --- ### Proof the bug occurs **Version**: `litellm 1.94.3`, image digest `sha256:b7d979bac2a9e8fbb7d55272ef5f1f4a08ab365de8f78b1800834ca718d4c941`. No provider call is made on this path. **Config the proxy ran with** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5-batch litellm_params: model: azure/gpt-5-batch-2025-08-07 api_base: os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` **Commands and their full output** Total from a single request: ``` $ curl -s 'http://localhost:4000/v1/batches?limit=100' -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("total:", len(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]))' total: 99 ``` Walk at `limit=10`, passing the previous page's last `id` as `after`, capped at 15 pages: ``` === paginated walk, limit=10, following the id the API returns === page 1: returned=10 has_more=True page 2: returned=10 has_more=True page 3: returned=10 has_more=True page 4: returned=10 has_more=True page 5: returned=10 has_more=True page 6: returned=10 has_more=True page 7: returned=10 has_more=True page 8: returned=10 has_more=True page 9: returned=10 has_more=True page 10: returned=10 has_more=True page 11: returned=10 has_more=True page 12: returned=10 has_more=True page 13: returned=10 has_more=True page 14: returned=10 has_more=True page 15: returned=10 has_more=True true total (single page): 99 rows returned by walk: 150 distinct rows in walk: 16 DUPLICATES: 134 NEVER SEEN by the walk: 83 ``` Two consecutive pages at `limit=3`: ``` page1 ids (first 20 chars): ['bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTtt', 'bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTtt', 'bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTtt'] cursor sent as after= bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTtt (len 166) page2 ids (first 20 chars): ['bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTtt', 'bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTtt', 'bGl0ZWxsbV9wcm94eTtt'] page2 identical to page1? False overlap count: 2 of 3 ``` The `id` values returned to the caller are 166-character base64 strings. The `id` column the `after` filter compares against holds UUIDs, per the psql output above. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.94.3
