signals.title: [Bug]: CheckBatchCost stale sweep excludes completed statuses that its own job selection includes, so a completed unprocessed row is never swept and is polled indefinitely
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [X] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? A managed batch row with `status='completed'` and `batch_processed=false` is not marked `stale_expired` by `_cleanup_stale_managed_objects` regardless of age, while the poller's own job-selection query continues to return it on every cycle. Observed on two rows seeded 30 days old (`MANAGED_OBJECT_STALENESS_CUTOFF_DAYS=7`), identical except for `status`: | row | status before | status after sweep | batch_processed | still selected by poller | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `u02-inprogress` | `in_progress` | `stale_expired` | false | no | | `u02-completed` | `completed` | `completed` | false | yes | The sweep reported `marked 1 stale managed objects`, not 2. ### Code as it stands at v1.94.3 `enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py:64`, the sweep: ```python async def _cleanup_stale_managed_objects(self) -> None: """ Mark managed objects older than MANAGED_OBJECT_STALENESS_CUTOFF_DAYS days in non-terminal states as 'stale_expired'. These will never complete and should not be polled. """ cutoff = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(days=MANAGED_OBJECT_STALENESS_CUTOFF_DAYS) result = await self.prisma_client.db.litellm_managedobjecttable.update_many( where={ "file_purpose": "batch", "status": {"not_in": ["completed", "complete", "failed", "expired", "cancelled", "stale_expired"]}, "created_at": {"lt": cutoff}, }, data={"status": "stale_expired"}, ) ``` `:527`, the job selection in the same class, run immediately after the sweep in `check_batch_cost()`: ```python if self._has_batch_processed_column: try: # Include "complete"/"completed" batches: the retrieve_batch # endpoint may transition a batch to "complete" before # CheckBatchCost runs. The batch_processed=False filter # already prevents reprocessing finished batches. jobs = await self.prisma_client.db.litellm_managedobjecttable.find_many( where={ "file_purpose": "batch", "batch_processed": False, "status": { "not_in": [ "failed", "expired", "cancelled", "stale_expired", ] }, }, take=MAX_OBJECTS_PER_POLL_CYCLE, order={"created_at": "asc"}, ) ``` The sweep's `not_in` list contains `completed` and `complete`; the selection's `not_in` list does not. --- ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix: an operator reviewing the batch backlog finds rows that neither clear nor age out** 1. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and see batch activity recorded normally for recent jobs 2. Reviewing older batch records, they find entries that reached a completed state weeks ago but are still listed as awaiting cost reconciliation 3. They wait past the documented staleness window and check again; the same entries are still listed as awaiting reconciliation, unchanged 4. Entries in a non-completed state from the same period are no longer listed, having been aged out 5. The entries remain in that state indefinitely, and each occupies one of the fixed number of slots the background reconciliation reads per cycle, so newer batches queue behind them 6. No API call fails and nothing is logged as an error at any point **After a (hypothetical) fix: the same rows either reconcile or age out, and the backlog drains** 1. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and see batch activity recorded normally for recent jobs 2. Reviewing older batch records, they find entries that reached a completed state weeks ago but are still listed as awaiting cost reconciliation 3. They wait past the documented staleness window and check again; those entries have left the awaiting state 4. Entries in a non-completed state from the same period have also aged out 5. No entry occupies a reconciliation slot indefinitely, so newer batches are read on the following cycle 6. No API call fails and nothing is logged as an error at any point --- ### Proof the bug occurs **Version**: `litellm 1.94.3`, image digest `sha256:b7d979bac2a9e8fbb7d55272ef5f1f4a08ab365de8f78b1800834ca718d4c941`. Constants in effect on the running proxy: `MANAGED_OBJECT_STALENESS_CUTOFF_DAYS = 7`, `MAX_OBJECTS_PER_POLL_CYCLE = 50`. This path is entirely internal to the proxy and its database; no provider call is involved in the sweep. **Config the proxy ran with** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5-batch litellm_params: model: azure/gpt-5-batch-2025-08-07 api_base: os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Proxy started with `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=10` so cycles are observable. **Commands and their full output** Seed two rows 30 days old, both unprocessed, differing only in `status`: ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c " INSERT INTO \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" (id, unified_object_id, model_object_id, file_object, file_purpose, created_at, updated_at, status, batch_processed, created_by) VALUES ('u02-completed', 'u02-uoid-completed', 'u02-moid-completed', '{}'::jsonb, 'batch', NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days', NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days', 'completed', false, 'u02-test'), ('u02-inprogress', 'u02-uoid-inprogress', 'u02-moid-inprogress', '{}'::jsonb, 'batch', NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days', NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days', 'in_progress', false, 'u02-test'); SELECT id, status, batch_processed FROM \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" WHERE created_by='u02-test' ORDER BY id;" INSERT 0 2 id | status | batch_processed ----------------+-------------+----------------- u02-completed | completed | f u02-inprogress | in_progress | f (2 rows) ``` Wait one poll cycle and read the sweep's own log line: ``` $ docker logs --since 60s <proxy> 2>&1 | grep -o "CheckBatchCost: marked .* as stale_expired" CheckBatchCost: marked 1 stale managed objects (older than 7 days) as stale_expired ``` Row state after the sweep: ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c \ "SELECT id, status, batch_processed FROM \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" WHERE created_by='u02-test' ORDER BY id;" id | status | batch_processed ----------------+---------------+----------------- u02-completed | completed | f u02-inprogress | stale_expired | f (2 rows) ``` The two `where` clauses from the source above, run against the same rows. Sweep clause (`:71-76`): ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c " SELECT id, status FROM \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" WHERE file_purpose='batch' AND status NOT IN ('completed','complete','failed','expired','cancelled','stale_expired') AND created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days' AND created_by='u02-test';" id | status ----+-------- (0 rows) ``` Job-selection clause (`:533-546`): ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c " SELECT id, status FROM \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" WHERE file_purpose='batch' AND batch_processed = false AND status NOT IN ('failed','expired','cancelled','stale_expired') AND created_by='u02-test' ORDER BY created_at ASC;" id | status ---------------+----------- u02-completed | completed (1 row) ``` The `completed` row is matched by the selection clause and not by the sweep clause. The `in_progress` control row, seeded at the same age in the same statement, was swept. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.94.3

signals.title: [Bug]: CheckBatchCost marks an expired batch processed without billing it, even when the provider reports an output file
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [X] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? When a provider reports a batch as `expired` while `output_file_id` is populated, `CheckBatchCost` sets `batch_processed=true` and writes no spend row. The output file is never fetched, so no cost is calculated for the request lines that completed before expiry. Observed on one batch driven through both states, provider `output_file_id` identical in each case: | provider status | output_file_id | output file fetched | poller spend row | row after poll | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `expired` | populated | no | none | `expired`, `batch_processed=true` | | `completed` | populated | yes | `spend=0.07125`, 9 prompt / 12 completion tokens | `complete`, `batch_processed=true` | `batch_processed=true` is the poller's re-pickup gate, so the row is not selected again on later cycles. OpenAI's batch documentation states that a batch expires when it does not finish inside its completion window, and that output for the requests that did complete remains available; `request_counts` on an expired batch reports `completed` and `failed` separately. ### Code as it stands at v1.94.3 `enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py:587`: ```python ## RETRIEVE THE BATCH JOB OUTPUT FILE if ( response.status == "completed" and response.output_file_id is not None ): try: tracked = await self._track_completed_batch_cost( job=job, response=response, model_id=model_id, batch_id=batch_id, prom_logger=prom_logger, ) ``` `:630`, the next branch: ```python elif response.status in ("failed", "expired", "cancelled"): try: update_data = { "status": response.status, "file_object": response.model_dump_json(), } if self._has_batch_processed_column: update_data["batch_processed"] = True await self.prisma_client.db.litellm_managedobjecttable.update( where={"id": job.id}, data=update_data, ) ``` The first branch requires `status == "completed"`. `expired` therefore reaches the second branch regardless of `output_file_id`, and the second branch contains no call to `_track_completed_batch_cost`. --- ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix: a team whose overnight batch does not finish inside its window is not charged for the requests that did complete** 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and their JSONL, and receive a file ID 2. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches` with that `input_file_id`, `"endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions"` and `"completion_window": "24h"`, and receive a batch ID 3. The batch does not finish inside the window. `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}` reports `"status": "expired"`, a populated `output_file_id`, and `"request_counts"` showing some requests completed 4. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and receive output lines for the completed requests, each carrying real token usage 5. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and find no spend recorded against that batch, and their key's spend total is unchanged 6. The provider bills the account for the completed requests, so the gateway's spend total is lower than the provider invoice, and a key with a hard budget was not charged for work it consumed **After a (hypothetical) fix: the completed portion of an expired batch is charged** 1. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and their JSONL, and receive a file ID 2. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches` with that `input_file_id`, `"endpoint": "/v1/chat/completions"` and `"completion_window": "24h"`, and receive a batch ID 3. The batch does not finish inside the window. `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}` reports `"status": "expired"`, a populated `output_file_id`, and `"request_counts"` showing some requests completed 4. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and receive output lines for the completed requests, each carrying real token usage 5. They open `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` and find spend recorded against that batch matching the tokens in the output file, and their key's spend total has increased by that amount 6. The gateway's spend total reconciles against the provider invoice, and the key's budget reflects the work consumed --- ### Proof the bug occurs **Version**: `litellm 1.94.3`, image digest `sha256:b7d979bac2a9e8fbb7d55272ef5f1f4a08ab365de8f78b1800834ca718d4c941`, no proxy-side patches. Proxy started with `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=10` so cycles are observable. The same batch is driven through both provider states so that everything except `status` is held constant: same batch id, same `output_file_id`, same output-file contents, same deployment, same poller. **Config the proxy ran with** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5-batch litellm_params: model: azure/gpt-5-batch-2025-08-07 api_base: os.environ/AZURE_API_BASE api_key: os.environ/AZURE_API_KEY api_version: 2025-03-01-preview custom_llm_provider: azure base_model: azure/gpt-5 model_info: mode: batch input_cost_per_token_batches: 0.00125 output_cost_per_token_batches: 0.005 general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` **Commands and their full output** Upload and create, then let the batch finish: ``` $ printf '%s\n' '{"custom_id":"u01-1","method":"POST","url":"/v1/chat/completions","body":{"model":"gpt-5-batch","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"u01 expired-with-output"}]}}' > u01.jsonl $ FILE_ID=$(curl -s http://localhost:4001/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ -F purpose=batch -F 'target_model_names=gpt-5-batch' -F file=@u01.jsonl \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])') $ BATCH_ID=$(curl -s http://localhost:4001/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $LITELLM_KEY" \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"input_file_id\":\"$FILE_ID\",\"endpoint\":\"/v1/chat/completions\",\"completion_window\":\"24h\"}" \ | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["id"])') ``` The provider reports the batch completed with an output file: ``` status: completed | output_file_id: batch_20260817-0849.737-output-file-1 ``` ### Run 1: provider reports expired, output file present Provider state, output file unchanged: ``` status: expired | output_file_id: batch_20260817-0849.737-output-file-1 | expired_at: 1786956606 ``` Reset the row to its pre-poll state and record the baseline: ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c \ "UPDATE \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" SET status='completed', batch_processed=false WHERE unified_object_id='$BATCH_ID' RETURNING status, batch_processed;" status | batch_processed -----------+----------------- completed | f (1 row) $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -t -c \ "SELECT count(*), coalesce(sum(spend),0) FROM \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" WHERE request_id='$BATCH_ID';" 1 | 0 ``` After the poll cycles: ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c \ "SELECT status, batch_processed FROM \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" WHERE unified_object_id='$BATCH_ID';" status | batch_processed ---------+----------------- expired | t (1 row) $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c \ "SELECT call_type, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens FROM \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" WHERE request_id='$BATCH_ID';" call_type | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens ---------------+-------+---------------+------------------- acreate_batch | 0 | 0 | 0 (1 row) $ docker logs --since 60s <proxy> 2>&1 | grep -c "output-file-1" 0 ``` The row is retired, the only spend row is the pre-existing $0 create row, and the output file was never requested. ### Run 2: same batch, provider reports completed Only `status` changes; `output_file_id` and its contents are identical: ``` status: completed | output_file_id: batch_20260817-0849.737-output-file-1 ``` Row reset the same way, then after the poll cycles: ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c \ "SELECT status, batch_processed FROM \"LiteLLM_ManagedObjectTable\" WHERE unified_object_id='$BATCH_ID';" status | batch_processed ----------+----------------- complete | t (1 row) ``` A poller spend row is written, which did not appear during run 1: ``` $ psql -U llmproxy -d litellm -c \ "SELECT to_char(\"startTime\",'HH24:MI:SS') AS t, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens FROM \"LiteLLM_SpendLogs\" WHERE call_type='aretrieve_batch' AND \"startTime\" > '2026-08-17 08:49:00' ORDER BY \"startTime\";" t | spend | prompt_tokens | completion_tokens ----------+---------+---------------+------------------- 08:51:21 | 0.07125 | 9 | 12 (1 row) ``` Run 1 covered roughly 08:50 and run 2 roughly 08:51. Across the window spanning both runs there is exactly one poller spend row, written during run 2. ### Note on the harness The provider in this capture is a local server standing in for Azure OpenAI batch, driven to report `expired` with a populated `output_file_id`. The proxy, the poller, the database and the HTTP path between them are unmodified; the branch under test is reached over HTTP in the normal way. A real provider produces the same pair of fields when a batch expires after some request lines have completed. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.94.3

signals.title: ResponsesAPIResponse.created_at should be Optional[int] - Azure returns null for in-progress/queued responses
signals.text:
## Description

`ResponsesAPIResponse` in `litellm/types/llms/openai.py` declares `created_at: int` as a required field. However, Azure OpenAI's GET /v1/responses/{id} returns `created_at: null` when the response is still in_progress or queued.

This causes a `pydantic.ValidationError` in `transform_get_response_api_response` → wrapped as `APIConnectionError` → HTTP 500 returned to the caller, defeating Azure's intended polling semantics (which should return HTTP 200 with an in-progress object).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Submit a response creation request to Azure OpenAI (e.g. model `gpt-5.1`)
2. Immediately poll GET /v1/responses/{id}
3. Azure returns: `{"id": "...", "created_at": null, "output": null, "status": "queued"}`
4. `ResponsesAPIResponse(**payload)` raises ValidationError

## Expected behavior

`created_at` should be `Optional[int] = None` (similar to `model`, `status`, and other fields), or `transform_get_response_api_response` should normalize null values before constructing the model.

## Context

We're running LiteLLM v1.92.0 proxying Azure OpenAI. When polling queued/in-progress responses, Azure returns `created_at: null` along with other nullable fields (`id`, `output`). We've patched two of those fields but `created_at` still causes failures.

Related upstream issue for nullable fields in streaming: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/20570

## Observed error

```
pydantic.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ResponsesAPIResponse
created_at
 Input should be a valid integer [type=int_type, input_value=None, input_type=NoneType]
```
signals.author: LaPetiteSouris

Related upstream issue for nullable fields in streaming: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/20570 ## Observed error ``` pydantic.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ResponsesAPIResponse created_at Input should be a valid integer [type=int_type, input_value=None, input_type=NoneType] ```

signals.title: bug: Anthropic /v1/messages -> Responses API adapter drops required `detail` field on images and mislabels `thinking` as `output_text`
signals.text: Related to #23841 (same file, different specific bugs). **Environment:** litellm `main-stable`, target backend: self-hosted vLLM 0.27.1 (OpenAI-compatible `/v1/responses`), via `/v1/messages` -> `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/responses_adapters/transformation.py`. ## Bug 1: `input_image` missing required `detail` field -> 400 `translate_messages_to_responses_input`, `btype == "image"` branch: ```python user_parts.append({"type": "input_image", "image_url": url}) ``` The Responses API's `ResponseInputImageParam` requires `detail: "low"|"high"|"auto"|"original"`. Without it the backend rejects the request with a large Pydantic union-validation error, which litellm's own `MaskedHTTPStatusError` then hides -- confirmed by reproducing the identical error directly against vLLM with the same field missing, and confirmed fixed by adding it. **Repro:** send any image content block (e.g. a PDF page rendered by Claude Code's `Read` tool) through `/v1/messages` to an OpenAI-Responses-API-compatible backend. **Fix:** ```diff - user_parts.append({"type": "input_image", "image_url": url}) + user_parts.append({"type": "input_image", "image_url": url, "detail": "auto"}) ``` ## Bug 2: assistant `thinking` blocks mislabeled as `output_text` Same function, `btype == "thinking"` branch: ```python asst_parts.append({"type": "output_text", "text": thinking_text}) ``` Prior reasoning content gets folded into the message's regular visible text instead of a proper `reasoning` item, so on multi-turn replay the model can no longer distinguish its own prior thinking from prior final answers. The response-side translation in this same file already builds real `reasoning`/`ResponseReasoningItem` items -- this is only the request-side/history-replay path. **Fix:** ```diff - asst_parts.append({"type": "output_text", "text": thinking_text}) + input_items.append({"type": "reasoning", "id": block.get("signature") or f"reasoning_{len(input_items)}", "summary": [{"type": "summary_text", "text": thinking_text}]}) ``` Happy to open a PR with both fixes if useful.

signals.title: [Feature]: add async_post_call_failure_deployment_hook to complete the deployment lifecycle hook triplet
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [X] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### The Feature Add `async_post_call_failure_deployment_hook(request_data, exception, call_type, fallback_depth=None)` to `CustomLogger`. It is an async, no-op-by-default method that fires once per real deployment attempt (attempt 1, every retry, every fallback hop), completing the deployment-attempt lifecycle triplet alongside the existing `async_pre_call_deployment_hook` (fires before every real provider call) and `async_post_call_success_deployment_hook` (fires after every successful one). Includes an optional best-effort `fallback_depth: int | None` reflecting how many fallback hops deep the current failure is (`None` on the original attempt, `1`, `2`, and so on per hop), read from Router's own internal bookkeeping. Implemented in #36657. ### User Flow Before this feature (today): a developer wiring pre-call and post-success deployment hooks has no equivalent hook for the failure case, so their integration covers two-thirds of a lifecycle and has no symmetric way to observe a failed attempt 1. They override `async_pre_call_deployment_hook` and `async_post_call_success_deployment_hook` on a `CustomLogger` and register it via `litellm.callbacks` 2. They look for a matching failure-side method to complete the same per-attempt lifecycle and find none; `CustomLogger` has no method that pairs with the two they already have After this feature (ideal user flow): the same developer gets a third, symmetric hook 1. They also override `async_post_call_failure_deployment_hook` 2. It fires once for every failed deployment attempt (attempt 1, each retry, each fallback hop), receiving that attempt's own `request_data`, the exception, and `fallback_depth` 3. Their integration now has a complete pre-call, success, and failure lifecycle for a single deployment attempt, all three hooks with the same shape and semantics ### How far you got Confirmed by reading `litellm/integrations/custom_logger.py` and `litellm/utils.py` (`wrapper_async`, the `client` decorator) that `async_pre_call_deployment_hook` and `async_post_call_success_deployment_hook` are the only deployment-attempt-level hooks that exist today, both dispatched from `wrapper_async`. Config / setup the proxy ran with: `litellm.Router` (SDK, not proxy) with three deployments of `openai/gpt-4o-mini`, each given a deliberately invalid API key so the failures are real `AuthenticationError`s from OpenAI's own API, not mocked, and `fallbacks=[{"group-a": ["group-b", "group-c"]}]`, `num_retries=0`. Version or commit: `litellm_internal_staging` HEAD, same branch point as #36657. Commands and output, up to the step that dead-ends: ```python from litellm.integrations.custom_logger import CustomLogger class Probe(CustomLogger): pass # no async_post_call_failure_deployment_hook to override; the method does not exist print(hasattr(Probe, "async_post_call_failure_deployment_hook")) # False, before this feature ``` What stopped me there: there is no method on `CustomLogger` that a callback can override to receive one call per failed deployment attempt with attempt-scoped `request_data`, symmetric with the pre-call and post-success hooks that already exist and need no dedup coordination of their own. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? SDK (litellm Python package) ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No

signals.title: CustomStreamWrapper erases the remembered model when an Azure chunk carries model=None
signals.text: ## Summary In `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py`, the Azure branch of `chunk_creator` does: ```python if isinstance(chunk, BaseModel) and hasattr(chunk, "model"): # for azure, we need to pass the model from the original chunk self.model = getattr(chunk, "model", self.model) ``` The `getattr` default only applies when the attribute is **missing**. When the attribute exists and is `None` — which is what the Responses-API bridge produces — `self.model` is overwritten with `None`, discarding the request model the wrapper stored at construction. The comment states the intent is to *pass along* the model; the effect is to erase it. ## Impact Every downstream consumer that reads the model from the stream loses it. In our case (Google ADK + LiteLLM against Azure OpenAI), `LlmResponse.model_version` became `None`, the field was dropped by `exclude_none` when the SSE event was serialized, and 100% of token usage in our evaluation runs was recorded as unattributed — so per-model cost and attribution silently stopped working. Nothing errors; the numbers just quietly lose their label. ## Reproduction Any deployment routed through the Responses bridge shows it. With LiteLLM 1.84.x: ```python import asyncio from litellm import acompletion async def main(): stream = await acompletion( model="azure/<a gpt-5.6 deployment>", api_key=..., api_base=..., api_version="<a Responses-capable version>", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with OK."}], # tools + reasoning_effort together are what select the Responses bridge tools=[{"type": "function", "function": { "name": "unused", "description": "unused", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}], reasoning_effort="medium", stream=True, stream_options={"include_usage": True}, ) async for chunk in stream: print(repr(getattr(chunk, "model", "<ABSENT>"))) asyncio.run(main()) ``` Observed: every chunk prints `None`. The equivalent non-streaming call returns a populated `model`, because the non-streaming Responses transformer sets it from the request. ## Suggested fix Guard on truthiness rather than attribute presence, so a null chunk model leaves the remembered request model intact: ```python chunk_model = getattr(chunk, "model", None) if chunk_model: self.model = chunk_model ``` Alternatively (or additionally), have the Responses→chat translator propagate the request/response model onto every `ModelResponseStream` it emits. The guard above is the smaller and more general correction, since it also protects any other provider path that emits a null model on a chunk. ## Environment - litellm 1.84.x (pinned range `>=1.84.0,<1.85.0`) - Provider: Azure OpenAI, `azure/` prefix, Responses-API bridge selected by tools + `reasoning_effort` - Consumer: google-adk 1.33.0 (`LiteLlm.generate_content_async`, streaming branch)

signals.title: [Bug]: POST /reload/model_cost_map is not reliably propagated to all proxy replicas
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? `POST /reload/model_cost_map` does not reliably propagate a refreshed model-cost map to every LiteLLM Proxy replica. In a three-replica deployment, calling **Reload Price Data** through the load-balanced Admin UI caused `/model/info` to alternate between old and new metadata. Twenty identical requests returned the stale value 17 times and the refreshed value 3 times. This can make model capability metadata, token limits, and pricing depend on which replica serves a request. Clients that cache `/model/info` can then retain stale capabilities after hitting an outdated replica. The implementation appears to use a lossy shared boolean as an event: 1. The endpoint refreshes the serving process's `litellm.model_cost` and writes `force_reload: true` to `model_cost_map_reload_config`. 2. Background polling processes observe that flag. 3. The first process that consumes it reloads its local map and writes `force_reload: false`. 4. Replicas that poll afterward see `false` and remain stale. If DB model synchronization is disabled, the other replicas do not consume the flag at all. Redis does not distribute `litellm.model_cost`; the map remains process-local. Expected behavior: after a successful manual reload, every running proxy replica should converge on the same model-cost-map generation. This is separate from the custom-pricing defects tracked in #30081, although its production report independently notes the same multi-replica behavior: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/30081#issuecomment-5030843840 The multi-pod reload feature was introduced by #13470: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/13470 A durable implementation could store a monotonically increasing reload generation in shared storage. Each process would retain its last applied generation and reload whenever the shared generation is newer, without any process clearing the event for the others. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Run LiteLLM Proxy with at least three replicas sharing the same database and with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=True`. 2. Set `LITELLM_MODEL_COST_MAP_URL` to a controllable valid model-cost-map URL and start all replicas with version A of that map. 3. Publish version B at the same URL with a recognizable metadata change. 4. Call `POST /reload/model_cost_map` once through the load-balanced Service, or use **Reload Price Data** in the Admin UI. 5. Wait longer than the background polling interval. 6. Query each pod directly using `/public/litellm_model_cost_map` or authenticated `/model/info`. 7. Observe that only the serving pod and, depending on polling order, at most one additional pod has version B. At least one replica can remain on version A. The same problem is even more direct with `STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=False`: only the serving process reloads. ### Relevant log output ```shell requests 1-17: supports_reasoning = null request 18: supports_reasoning = true request 19: supports_reasoning = null request 20: supports_reasoning = true ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.95.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details No response

signals.title: Bridge envelope admission returns a bare 401 where the gateway session path returns an invalid_token challenge
signals.text: ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## What happened? `MCPRequestHandler` has two admission arms for a cryptographically valid credential that can no longer be admitted, for example because it has expired. They handle the same condition differently. `_admit_gateway_session` fails closed with an RFC 9728 challenge via `_gateway_dcr_challenge`, including RFC 6750 `error="invalid_token"` when a bearer was presented. Its own comment explains why: > A cryptographically valid bearer whose referenced user is now missing or SCIM-deactivated is an invalid_token at the requested scope: relay the RFC 9728 challenge so the DCR client re-authorizes, matching the SessionBearerInvalid arm, instead of a bare 401 with no WWW-Authenticate. `_admit_dcr_bridge_delegate`, in the same class, raises `HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid or expired credential")` on its `BridgeEnvelopeInvalid() | NotBridgeEnvelope()` arm. No `WWW-Authenticate` header, so it never reaches the challenge helper that the sibling arm uses. Without a challenge a client has no machine-readable signal telling it where to re-authorize, so recovery has to be driven by hand even though the client is capable of re-running the flow. This also seems inconsistent with the mode's own intent. For `is_oauth_delegate` servers, `mcp_server_manager` already relays an upstream 401 as `MCPUpstreamAuthError` specifically so callers can turn it into a 401 with the upstream's `WWW-Authenticate` and re-run the OAuth flow, and `server.py` converts that to a 401 preserving the challenge. So challenge-driven re-authorization is the intended recovery path for this mode. The envelope admission arm is the one place in that chain that drops it. Three merged PRs have closed the same kind of gap in neighboring paths: #30124 (surface upstream challenges for delegated OAuth), #31921 (surface `tools/list` auth failures as a 401 challenge on single-server routes), and #32741 (surface rejected delegate-auth upstream tokens as a connect-time 401, whose verification output shows the `error="invalid_token"` challenge being relayed). The bridge envelope arm arrived with #32824 and did not get the same treatment, so this looks like an oversight rather than a deliberate exception. Related but distinct: #36358 reports a different defect in the same bridge mode, where the injected upstream credential is discarded on tool calls. That one is about egress after a successful admission. This one is about the response when admission fails. ## User Flow Before: - Someone uses an MCP client that connects through the proxy. Their credential eventually reaches its expiry. - The next request fails with a 401 that carries no challenge, so the client has no way to discover where to re-authorize. It surfaces a generic failure instead. - The person has to work out for themselves that re-authorization is what is needed, then re-run the login by hand. After: - The 401 carries a challenge, so the client discovers the authorization server and re-runs the flow. - The person either keeps working or is prompted once by their client, rather than diagnosing an opaque error. ## Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml mcp_servers: example_server: url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp transport: http auth_type: oauth_delegate dcr_bridge: true ``` Version or commit: 1.97.0 Commands and their full output: 1. Configure an MCP server in `dcr_bridge` + `oauth_delegate` mode and complete the DCR flow so the client holds an access envelope. 2. Wait for the envelope to pass its `exp`, or tamper with it. 3. Send any request to the server's MCP route with that envelope as the bearer. Observed: `401` with body `{"detail":"Invalid or expired credential"}` and no `WWW-Authenticate` response header. Expected: `401` carrying a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, as the gateway session path returns for the equivalent condition. Concretely, `_admit_dcr_bridge_delegate` would emit an `invalid_token` challenge on an expired or otherwise unusable envelope, matching `_admit_gateway_session`. Scope note: this would fix the REST and connect-time paths. It would not by itself help a tool call that fails mid-session, because as `server.py` notes, the MCP session manager serializes handler exceptions as JSON-RPC errors, so a mid-session tool call cannot emit a raw 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header and degrades to an `isError` result instead. That looks like a separate limitation rather than part of this inconsistency. Happy to send a PR if the direction is agreeable. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.97.0
signals.author: chris-smith-zocdoc

signals.title: No renewal path when an upstream grant has neither expires_in nor refresh_token
signals.text: ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## The Feature When an upstream token response carries neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`: - the access envelope gets `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` (3600), since `_envelope_ttl_seconds(None)` returns the cap, and - no refresh envelope is minted, because `discoverable_endpoints.py` skips that step when the response has no `refresh_token`. The result is that the client has no renewal path at all. Recovery is a full interactive `authorization_code` flow, roughly every hour, for the lifetime of the integration. Some providers issue access tokens that do not expire, and signal that by omitting `expires_in`. Nothing on the wire distinguishes this from "expires, lifetime unstated", so the gateway assumes the latter. We are not asking it to assume otherwise. The problem is what happens next: for this shape of grant there is no bounded renewal mechanism, only re-authorization. Two mechanisms already exist and neither reaches this case. **The upstream 401 relay.** For `is_oauth_delegate` servers, `mcp_server_manager` relays an upstream 401 as `MCPUpstreamAuthError` so callers turn it into a 401 with the upstream's own `WWW-Authenticate` and re-run the OAuth flow. The comment states the intent: only a 401 is a re-auth signal, and it is the caller's to resolve. That is the right design, but the access envelope's own `exp` fires first, so the upstream is never asked and the relay never runs. The gateway's locally chosen expiry pre-empts the provider's own answer. **The refresh envelope.** #32980 added refresh envelopes and scoped them to grants returning a `refresh_token`: > A new refresh envelope is re-issued only when the upstream returns a new refresh token, so the design mirrors the upstream authorization server's own rotation policy rather than reinventing it: against a rotating upstream the client rotates and the upstream detects reuse of a retired token; against a non-rotating upstream the original refresh envelope stands until its bounded TTL. That covers a non-rotating upstream, which keeps its refresh envelope for the 14-day bound. It does not cover an upstream that returns no refresh token at all, which gets no envelope and therefore no bound other than the 1h access cap. We are not asking for the access cap to be raised or removed. The constant's own docstring anticipates that argument and rejects it: > Hard ceiling on ACCESS envelope lifetime [...] matching the 1h lifetime of the > BYOK session bearer this module's signing approach is borrowed from: a client-held > credential should never outlive a bounded window even when the upstream token does. We think that is correct. The cap does not bound the provider's token, it bounds the client-held bearer, and its value is that a leaked envelope dies on its own without requiring the principal's access to be revoked wholesale. "The provider says the token does not expire" is not an answer to envelope theft. Nor would dropping the expiry work mechanically, since `exp` is a required claim on open. Give this grant shape the same treatment the 14-day refresh bound already represents: when the upstream returns neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`, mint a refresh envelope sealing the access token, and let the `refresh_token` grant re-mint a fresh 1h access envelope from the sealed grant. This seems to fit the reasoning already documented on `MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS`: > A refresh envelope only renews the short-lived access envelope, and each renewal re-validates the sealed litellm key (revocation gates it) and is re-minted with a fresh window, so the practical bound is idle time, not a fixed session. Both properties hold here. The credential is presented only back to the token endpoint rather than held as a bearer for upstream calls, and each renewal re-validates the sealed identity. The 1h client-held access cap is untouched, revocation still gates every renewal, and hourly interactive re-authorization becomes a 14-day idle bound. One honest caveat: the current refresh path unwraps the sealed refresh token and POSTs `grant_type=refresh_token` upstream, so this needs a distinct arm that re-mints from the sealed grant without an upstream call, not a straight reuse of the existing flow. A per-server override for the access cap would also solve our immediate problem and is a smaller change, since `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is read only by `envelope.py` and has no config field or environment variable today. We suggest it second because it needs an operator to declare provider behavior correctly, and because it weakens the client-held-bearer bound that the docstring above is protecting. If you did prefer this shape, `MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is a same-shaped sibling that an override should probably cover too. Happy to send a PR for either direction. ## User Flow Before this feature (today): - Someone authorizes an MCP server once through the gateway and starts working. - Roughly an hour later the credential is gone. There is no renewal path, so the only way back is the full interactive authorization flow. - That repeats every hour, for as long as they use the integration. After this feature: - Someone authorizes once. Renewal happens against the token endpoint without their involvement. - Interactive re-authorization is needed only after a long idle period, bounded by the existing 14-day refresh window, rather than hourly. ## How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml mcp_servers: example_server: url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp transport: http auth_type: oauth_delegate dcr_bridge: true ``` Version or commit: 1.97.0 Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends: Complete the DCR flow against the server above, against an upstream whose token response includes neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`. The token response returns an access envelope and no `refresh_token` field. There is no further command to run: no refresh grant exists to renew with, so the flow dead-ends at re-authorization once the access envelope reaches its `exp`. What stopped me there: The client has no renewal path and must repeat the interactive `authorization_code` flow roughly every hour. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No

signals.title: [Bug]: Batch spend is permanently lost when a client status poll records the terminal state before the batch cost job's next cycle
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Closest neighbors, neither a duplicate: #37156 covers the cost poller retiring terminal batches unbilled when the poller itself sees the terminal transition (fixed by #37205), and #37153 covered the stale sweep's handling of completed unprocessed rows. This issue is the remaining ordering: the client sees the terminal transition first ### What happened? When a client polls GET /v1/batches/{batch_id} through the proxy while waiting for a cancelled or failed batch to finalize, the proxy records the provider's terminal status the moment the client sees it. The background batch cost job skips batches already recorded as cancelled or failed, so it never revisits that batch and the spend for its completed requests is never written PR #37205 makes the cost job bill any terminal batch with an output file, but only when the job notices the terminal transition itself. A polling client (the normal OpenAI SDK pattern) checks every few seconds while the job's default interval is one hour, so the client effectively always stamps the terminal status first and the spend is still lost. In the reproduction below the job's last look at the batch was 9 seconds before the provider finalized; the client's next poll landed first, and nine subsequent job cycles plus a full proxy restart never billed the 86 completed requests Expected: the completed portion of a cancelled or failed batch is billed regardless of whether the client or the background job sees the terminal status first ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer cancels an in-progress batch and polls it through the gateway until it finalizes; the gateway serves the partial results but never records any spend for them 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds, the way the OpenAI SDK polling helpers do; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and request_counts.completed 86 5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with 86 result lines carrying real token usage 6. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} shows only the $0 batch-creation row and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows spend 0.0, permanently: hours of cost-job cycles and even a gateway restart never bill it After a (hypothetical) fix: the same polled batch is billed for its completed work within one cost-job cycle 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and non-zero request_counts.completed 5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with the completed result lines 6. Within one cost-job cycle GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} gains a batch-retrieval row with the real cost and token counts of those completed requests, and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the matching non-zero spend ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini-batch litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY model_info: mode: batch general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Env: `LITELLM_LICENSE` set (the batch cost job is enterprise), `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=120` (short enough to observe many job cycles; the default 3600 makes the race even more certain), fresh Postgres DB Version or commit: `b34cbb18e2` (the tip of PR #37205's branch, so the #37156 fix is already included; the base branch without #37205 loses the spend on every ordering, not just this one) Commands and their full output (key redacted; live proxy on localhost:49726, real OpenAI batch API): 1. Create a key with a user_id, upload a 2000-request JSONL, create the batch: ```bash KEY=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"lit5663-clobber","user_id":"lit5663-user","models":["gpt-5.4-mini-batch"]}' | jq -r .key) FILE=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -F purpose=batch -F 'target_model_names=gpt-5.4-mini-batch' -F file=@cancelleg2.jsonl | jq -r .id) BATCH=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"input_file_id\":\"$FILE\",\"endpoint\":\"/v1/chat/completions\",\"completion_window\":\"24h\"}" | jq -r .id) ``` 2. Poll `GET /v1/batches/$BATCH` through the proxy every 2-3 s (the SDK pattern). At the first in_progress poll with completed 32, cancel through the proxy: `curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:49726/v1/batches/$BATCH/cancel" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` returns HTTP 200 with status cancelling 3. Keep polling; ~25 min later (provider batch_6a836d8e1c30819090dd7133000d6a6f, cancelled_at 14:08:31 PDT) the first cancelled poll shows `"status": "cancelled"`, a populated output_file_id, `"request_counts": {"total": 2000, "completed": 86, "failed": 0}` 4. `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` returns HTTP 200 with 86 JSONL result lines totaling 1634 prompt + 344 completion = 1978 tokens of real completed work 5. Across six cost-job cycles: `curl -s "http://localhost:49726/spend/logs?request_id=$BATCH" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER"` shows only the $0 `acreate_batch` row, `spend/logs?request_id=${BATCH}_batch_cost` returns `[]`, and `/key/info` reports `"spend": 0.0` 6. Restarting the proxy on the same DB and waiting three more cycles changes nothing: still no `aretrieve_batch` row, key spend still 0.0. The exclusion is durable state, not a warm-cache artifact Timing detail from the proxy log: the cost job examined this batch on every one of its 22 cycles while the batch was non-terminal (last at 14:08:25), the client's poll recorded cancelling -> cancelled at 14:08:34, and none of the nine subsequent cycles examined the batch again ### What a fix PR should look like Two workable shapes, either is fine: - Include provider-terminal statuses in the cost job's pickup so a row stamped cancelled/failed with an output file and not yet billed still gets billed once. This needs an upgrade guard (for example a created_at cutoff) so pre-existing terminal rows from before the fix do not get retroactively billed as one spike on deploy, and it should mind the poll-page slots (MAX_OBJECTS_PER_POLL_CYCLE) so old rows cannot starve new ones - Alternatively, keep the retrieve/cancel path from stamping a terminal status onto a not-yet-billed row (stamp it only once spend has been written, letting the cost job see the transition itself) The regression test belongs in tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py: simulate the retrieve-first ordering (row already carrying the provider's terminal status, batch_processed false, output file present) and assert the job still bills it exactly once ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? litellm_internal_staging @ f04b1dad plus PR #37205 (b34cbb18e2)

signals.title: [Bug]: OAuth2 client_credentials MCP servers never receive client_id/client_secret at runtime — token endpoint always rejects with 400
signals.text: ### What happened? Registering an MCP server with `auth_type: oauth2` / `oauth2_flow: client_credentials` results in `tools/list` failing 100% of the time with: ``` misconfigured: OAuth2 client_credentials grant rejected: token endpoint returned HTTP 400 ``` This happens **regardless of how the server is configured** — via the REST API (`POST /v1/mcp/server` with a nested `credentials: {client_id, client_secret}` object) or via `config.yaml`'s `mcp_servers:` block (with either `os.environ/VAR` or literal values). In every case the token endpoint (a real, independently-verified-working Keycloak `client_credentials` grant) rejects the request, which points to litellm sending an empty or malformed `client_id`/`client_secret`. ### Root cause (traced in source, not guessed) 1. **`LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` (`schema.prisma`) has no `client_id` / `client_secret` columns** — only an encrypted `credentials Json?` blob: ```prisma model LiteLLM_MCPServerTable { server_id String @id @default(uuid()) ... credentials Json? @default("{}") ... } ``` 2. The runtime OAuth2 resolver builds its config from **flat fields on the `MCPServer` Pydantic model**: `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/adapter.py`: ```python config=ClientCredentialsConfig( client_id=server.client_id, client_secret=SecretStr(server.client_secret) if server.client_secret else None, token_url=server.token_url, ... ) ``` 3. **Nothing in the codebase ever copies the decrypted `credentials` blob into `server.client_id` / `server.client_secret`.** Searched the whole `mcp_server` package for any `client_id=<decrypted value>` assignment feeding into an `MCPServer(...)` construction used by the OAuth2 resolver — there is none. `decrypt_credentials()` is only used for master-key rotation (`rotate_mcp_server_credentials_master_key`) and DCR client storage, never to populate the resolver's config. Result: for any server persisted through the database (which is every server registered via the REST API, and — because `general_settings.store_model_in_db: true` is a very common production setting — effectively every `config.yaml`-defined server too), `server.client_id` / `server.client_secret` are **always `None`** at the point the token request is built. Keycloak (or any spec-compliant IdP) correctly returns `400 invalid_request`/`invalid_client` for a `client_credentials` grant with an empty `client_id`. 4. Separately, **`config.yaml`'s `mcp_servers:` loader does not resolve `os.environ/VAR`** for `client_id`/`client_secret`, unlike `model_list.litellm_params`: `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py`: ```python client_id=server_config.get("client_id", None), client_secret=server_config.get("client_secret", None), ``` This is a plain dict `.get()` — no `get_secret()` / env-var indirection. The [MCP OAuth docs](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/mcp_oauth) show `client_id: os.environ/MCP_CLIENT_ID` as the documented pattern, but it is silently taken as a literal string, so the literal text `os.environ/MCP_CLIENT_ID` gets sent to the token endpoint instead of the resolved secret. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Register (via REST API or `config.yaml`) an MCP server: ```yaml mcp_servers: my_server: url: "https://my-mcp-server.example.com/mcp" transport: http auth_type: oauth2 oauth2_flow: client_credentials client_id: "<a real, working client_id>" client_secret: "<its real secret>" token_url: "https://idp.example.com/protocol/openid-connect/token" ``` 2. Independently confirm the same `client_id`/`client_secret`/`token_url` succeed with a plain `curl -d grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=...&client_secret=...` — they do (200, valid token). 3. Call `tools/list` against the proxy's `/mcp/` endpoint for this server. 4. Observe `"status": "internal", "http_status": 500"` in `_meta.litellm.ai/server_outcomes`, and in the proxy logs: ``` Failed to get tools from server my_server: 500: misconfigured: OAuth2 client_credentials grant rejected: token endpoint returned HTTP 400 ``` 5. Confirm the grant mechanics themselves are fine by calling litellm's own `_prepare_grant` / `post_client_credentials_grant` directly with the identical config object (bypassing the server-record load path) — this **succeeds** and returns a valid access token. The bug is specifically in how the persisted/config-loaded `MCPServer` record's credentials reach that function, not in the grant logic itself. ### Expected behavior `client_id`/`client_secret` provided at registration time (via API `credentials` object or `config.yaml`, with or without `os.environ/` indirection) should reach the actual token request unchanged. ### Suggested fix - Add `client_id`/`client_secret` columns to `LiteLLM_MCPServerTable` (or decrypt+unpack the `credentials` blob into the `MCPServer.client_id`/`client_secret` fields at every read path that feeds `_client_credentials_spec`), and/or - Apply the same `get_secret()`/`os.environ/` resolution used for `model_list` to the `mcp_servers:` config.yaml loader for `client_id`, `client_secret`, and any other credential-shaped field. ### Environment - **LiteLLM version**: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:main-stable`, image pulled/deployed 2026-08-10 (prod) — well after the March 2026 fix for #24522, so this is not that issue. - **What part of LiteLLM is this about?**: MCP Gateway / OAuth2 `client_credentials` - Reproduced independently on two separate deployments (Azure Container Apps and an OpenShift-hosted instance with `store_model_in_db: true`), both via REST API registration and via `config.yaml`. ### Related issues Not a duplicate of #24522 (concurrent stateless teardown — different traceback, different mechanism). Possibly related in spirit to #22755 ("Unable to list MCP tools with OAuth through the UI Dashboard", closed `not_planned`) and #15957, which describe the same outward symptom (OAuth-protected MCP tool listing fails) without this root cause having been identified. --- ## Bug 2: `true_passthrough`/`oauth_delegate` MCP sessions time out despite the upstream call itself completing in milliseconds ### What happened? As an alternative to `client_credentials` (see Bug 1), we tested `auth_type: oauth_delegate` (`true_passthrough`), where litellm is supposed to forward the caller's own bearer token verbatim (via the `x-mcp-{alias}-authorization` header) instead of minting its own. `tools/list` against this server times out inside litellm. ### Root cause (traced in source) - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/outbound_credentials/resolver.py`, `_passthrough(self, subject)` (~line 163) forwards `subject.inbound_token` verbatim to the upstream MCP server — this part is correct and matches the caller-supplied-credential design we wanted. - `litellm/proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/mcp_server_manager.py` (~line 4200) wraps the actual `client.list_tools()` call in `anyio.fail_after(MCP_TOOL_LISTING_TIMEOUT)`. In our reproduction, this consistently fires before the upstream ever responds. - We isolated the upstream call from litellm's session/connection handling entirely: a standalone script (`debug_passthrough.py`), running inside the same cluster network as litellm and using the same caller token forwarded the same way, hit the internal MCP URL directly and got back **`HTTP 200` in `0.04s`**. The upstream server, network path, and token are all fine — the timeout is happening somewhere in litellm's own MCP client/session plumbing between accepting the passthrough token and actually completing the `list_tools()` round trip. ### Expected behavior `tools/list` over a `true_passthrough`/`oauth_delegate` MCP server should complete in roughly the same time as a direct call to the upstream (tens of milliseconds in our environment), not hit `MCP_TOOL_LISTING_TIMEOUT`. ### Environment Same as Bug 1 (OpenShift-hosted litellm instance, `store_model_in_db: true`). ### Status This is reported with less certainty than Bug 1 — we have not yet traced the exact point inside litellm's session/connection setup where the delay is introduced (as opposed to Bug 1, which we traced to an exact missing assignment). Flagging it here because it blocks the architecturally-preferred alternative to Bug 1. --- ## Bug 3: `client_credentials` grant requests every scope advertised by the realm's discovery document, instead of only the client's assigned scopes ### What happened? With Bug 1's root cause fixed locally (server record correctly populated with a real, independently-verified-working `client_id`/`client_secret`), the *live* litellm instance's `client_credentials` requests to our IdP (Keycloak) still fail — but with a different, more specific error surfaced in the IdP's own audit log (not visible from litellm's side, only from the token endpoint's server-side logs): ``` error="invalid_request", reason="Invalid scopes: basic uma_protection Custom_Scope a2a-chat-ia-mcp-audience roles phone microprofile-jwt openid web-origins offline_access acr email service_account profile address", grant_type="client_credentials", client_auth_method="client-secret", username="service-account-<client>" ``` Client authentication itself **succeeds** here (Keycloak resolves the service-account user, confirming the secret is valid) — the request fails only because of the `scope` parameter litellm sends. The requested scope list is unusually large and includes scopes that are not, and could never sensibly be, assigned to this specific client (`microprofile-jwt`, `web-origins`, `acr`, several other realm-wide default/optional scopes). This looks like litellm is requesting the full `scopes_supported` list from the IdP's OIDC discovery document (`/.well-known/openid-configuration`) rather than a scope the operator configured (or no `scope` parameter at all, which is valid per RFC 6749 §4.4.2 and lets the IdP apply the client's default scopes). ### Expected behavior The `client_credentials` grant should either omit `scope` entirely (letting the IdP apply the client's configured default scopes, which is spec-compliant and what a plain `curl` grant with no `scope` param does successfully against the same client/IdP), or send only an operator-configured scope list — never every scope advertised by discovery metadata. ### Environment Same as Bug 1/2. ### Related issues Not yet searched for a matching open issue — flagging here since it was discovered as a direct consequence of investigating Bug 1. **Update: Bug 3 also breaks the interactive `authorization_code` flow, not just `client_credentials`** Confirmed this is not specific to `client_credentials`. Registering a second server with `oauth2_flow: authorization_code` (same `client_id`, plus an `issuer` so LiteLLM does RFC 8414 discovery instead of using manually-set `authorization_url`/`token_url`) and hitting LiteLLM's own `/{server_name}/authorize` endpoint produces a `307` redirect to the IdP's `/auth` endpoint whose `scope` query param is the **exact same** full discovery scope list: ``` Invalid scopes: basic uma_protection Custom_Scope a2a-chat-ia-mcp-audience roles phone microprofile-jwt openid web-origins offline_access acr email service_account profile address ``` i.e. once `issuer` is set for discovery, LiteLLM builds this over-broad `scope` value for **every** OAuth2 flow it drives (both the M2M token request and the interactive `/authorize` redirect), not just `client_credentials`. Same root cause, hits both the token-request call site and the `/authorize` redirect builder. This was confirmed via a real interactive login attempt — the actual Keycloak login page itself surfaces `Invalid scopes` (same string as the token-endpoint audit log entry seen with `client_credentials`), which rules out this being a `client_credentials`-only or backend-log-only artifact. Cópialo desde el primer ```markdown hasta el cierre y pégalo directo en el comentario de GitHub — al pegarlo ahí se va a renderizar bien.

signals.title: [Feature]: Bump Granian from 2.7.4 to 2.8.1 in the published proxy
signals.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. There is no open or closed issue/PR for Granian 2.8.x. The last Granian bump was Dependabot [#28538](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/28538) (`2.5.7` → `2.7.4`, closed unmerged) and the security bundle [#29208](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/pull/29208) that landed `2.7.4`. ### The Feature Please evaluate and bump the Granian version shipped with the official proxy images / PyPI package from **2.7.4 to 2.8.1**. `pyproject.toml` already allows `granian>=2.7.4,<3.0`, so 2.8.1 is in range. The published lock and images still ship **2.7.4**. Granian **2.8.1** was released 2026-08-05 ([release](https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian/releases/tag/v2.8.1)). OSV reports no CVEs on 2.7.4 or 2.8.1 — this is not a security fire drill. The last LiteLLM Granian bump *was* CVE-driven (`CVE-2026-42544` / `CVE-2026-42545` in #29208), which is why I am asking here instead of sending a lockfile-only PR. **Please review Granian 2.8.0 breaking changes before bumping** ([2.8.0 notes](https://github.com/emmett-framework/granian/releases/tag/v2.8.0)): - Linux multi-worker + respawn now requires kernel ≥ 5.14 **and** `net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req` enabled. - Non-configurable backpressure on streamed / iterable ASGI responses (can change `/v1/chat/completions` streaming memory vs throughput). - Worker loop / shutdown refactors (relevant if `--max_requests_before_restart` is in use). - WSGI environ priority change (should not affect the ASGI proxy path). 2.8.1 itself is a patch on top of that: ASGI websocket performance regression fix, `PyFutureAwaitable` interface fix, RSGI websocket close, relaxed atomics. I can send a lockfile PR if you want the bump after this review. ### User Flow Before this feature (today): an operator who starts the official proxy with Granian gets 2.7.4 and cannot pick up the 2.8.1 server without rebuilding the image themselves. 1. They deploy `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:1.97.0` (or `pip install litellm==1.97.0`) and start the proxy with `--run_granian` plus TLS. 2. They send `GET https://<litellm-host>/health/liveliness` with HTTP/2. It returns `HTTP/2 200`, `server: granian`, body `"I'm alive!"`. 3. The same URL over HTTP/1.1 also returns `200` and `server: granian`. 4. They have no supported way to run Granian 2.8.1 on that official image. Workaround is a custom image / fork of the lockfile. After this feature (ideal user flow): the same official image ships Granian 2.8.1 after the 2.8.0 behavior is reviewed. 1. They deploy the next official image / PyPI release and start the proxy with the same `--run_granian` plus TLS. 2. They send the same `GET https://<litellm-host>/health/liveliness` with HTTP/2. It still returns `HTTP/2 200`, `server: granian`, body `"I'm alive!"`. 3. The same URL over HTTP/1.1 still returns `200` and `server: granian`. 4. Streamed `POST https://<litellm-host>/v1/chat/completions` with `"stream": true` still completes with SSE `data:` chunks and a normal `[DONE]` (this is the 2.8.0 backpressure check). 5. If they use worker respawn (`--max_requests_before_restart`), workers still recycle without dropping the listener. ### How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with: - Image: `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm-database:1.97.0` - Started with `--run_granian` and in-guest TLS - Public host: `https://llm.kubetee.ai` Version or commit: - LiteLLM `1.97.0` (`stable/1.97.x`) - Granian inside that image: `2.7.4` - Constraint already in tree: `granian>=2.7.4,<3.0` Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends: ``` $ curl -sS -D - --http2 --max-time 15 https://llm.kubetee.ai/health/liveliness HTTP/2 200 content-length: 12 content-type: application/json x-frame-options: DENY content-security-policy: frame-ancestors 'none' x-content-type-options: nosniff server: granian date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 22:24:58 GMT "I'm alive!" ``` ``` $ curl -sS -D - --http1.1 --max-time 15 https://llm.kubetee.ai/health/liveliness HTTP/1.1 200 OK content-length: 12 content-type: application/json x-frame-options: DENY content-security-policy: frame-ancestors 'none' x-content-type-options: nosniff server: granian date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 22:25:00 GMT "I'm alive!" ``` What stopped me there: HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 both work on 2.7.4. The missing piece is only the official 2.8.1 bump. I did not open a lockfile PR because 2.8.0 has breaking changes that need a maintainer look (streaming backpressure + Linux `tcp_migrate_req` / multi-worker respawn), and because `.github/dependabot.yaml` currently watches GitHub Actions only, so Dependabot will not open this. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No

signals.title: fix anthropic structured output 400 error for unsupported schema fields.
signals.text: Relevant issues Fixes - Anthropic doesn't support maxItems/minItems in output_format Related to: Users reporting 400 errors when using structured outputs with constraints on Anthropic models Pre-Submission checklist Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR - I have Added testing in the https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/litellm directory, Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement - https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code - Added 11 comprehensive tests in tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/test_anthropic_structured_output.py - My PR passes all unit tests on https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code - All 231 Anthropic tests passing - My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem - Focused solely on Anthropic structured outputs constraint handling - I have requested a Greptile review by commenting @greptileai and received a Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review CI (LiteLLM team) CI status guideline: - 50-55 passing tests: main is stable with minor issues. - 45-49 passing tests: acceptable but needs attention - <= 40 passing tests: unstable; be careful with your merges and assess the risk. - Branch creation CI run Link: - CI run for the last commit Link: - Merge / cherry-pick CI run Links: Type 🐛 Bug Fix 🆕 New Feature (validation) Changes Problem Anthropic's structured outputs API doesn't support these JSON Schema constraints: - Numerical: minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, multipleOf - String: minLength, maxLength, pattern - Array: maxItems, minItems (except values 0 or 1) When users passed schemas with these constraints, they got 400 BadRequestError from Anthropic. Reference: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs#json-schema-limitations Solution Approach Implemented the same transformation strategy as the official Anthropic SDK: 1. Store Original Schema - Deep copy with all constraints for later validation 2. Add Constraints to Descriptions - Convert constraints to text hints (e.g., "minimum": 0 → "description": "Must be at least 0") 3. Filter Unsupported Constraints - Remove constraints before sending to API 4. Validate Responses - Check Claude's response against original schema to catch violations Implementation Details File: litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py New Methods: - _add_constraint_to_descriptions() - Adds constraint info to descriptions - filter_anthropic_output_schema() - Updated to filter all unsupported constraints - _validate_response_against_schema() - Validates responses using jsonschema - validate_structured_output_response() - Public validation method Updated Methods: - map_response_format_to_anthropic_output_format() - Orchestrates transformation - transform_response() - Integrated validation to check responses before returning What Gets Filtered: unsupported = { "minimum", "maximum", "exclusiveMinimum", "exclusiveMaximum", "multipleOf", "minLength", "maxLength", "pattern", "maxItems" } # Special: minItems preserved if 0 or 1, removed if > 1 # Adds: additionalProperties: false to all objects Recursive Filtering: Handles properties, items, $defs, definitions, anyOf, allOf, oneOf Error Message Compatibility: Uses getattr(e, 'message', getattr(e, 'msg', str(e))) for jsonschema 3.x/4.x Testing 11 comprehensive tests in tests/test_litellm/llms/anthropic/test_anthropic_structured_output.py: 1. ✅ Array constraints filtering (maxItems, minItems) 2. ✅ String/number constraints filtering + description updates 3. ✅ Pattern constraint filtering 4. ✅ Definitions recursion (not just $defs) 5. ✅ oneOf schema filtering 6. ✅ allOf schema filtering 7. ✅ minItems edge cases (0, 1, >1) 8. ✅ additionalProperties automatically added 9. ✅ Nested schema filtering 10. ✅ Response validation error messages 11. ✅ Constraint info in descriptions All 231 Anthropic tests passing ✅ Before/After Before: schema = {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 150} # ❌ 400 BadRequestError from Anthropic After: # Sent to Anthropic: {"type": "integer", "description": "Must be at least 0. Must be at most 150"} # ✅ Success: {"age": 25} # Validated against original schema automatically Production Ready - ✅ End-to-end tested with live API - ✅ All existing tests passing - ✅ Matches official Anthropic SDK behavior - ✅ Error handling for jsonschema compatibility - ✅ Deep copy prevents schema mutation - ✅ Validation catches constraint violations

signals.title: fix(ui): fetch all session logs instead of only first 50
signals.text: ## Summary - The session logs drawer on the `/ui/?page=logs` page only showed 50 results when clicking on a session, even if there were more logs - Root cause: `sessionSpendLogsCall` in `networking.tsx` didn't pass `page` or `page_size` params to the `/spend/logs/session/ui` backend endpoint, which defaults to `page_size=50` - Fix: the function now fetches all pages (using `page_size=100`, the backend max) and merges them into a single response so the session sidebar displays every log entry ## Test plan - [ ] Open the logs page (`/ui/?page=logs`) - [ ] Click on a session that has more than 50 log entries - [ ] Verify all log entries are now displayed in the session drawer sidebar - [ ] Verify sessions with fewer than 50 entries still work correctly 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signals.title: fix(proxy): avoid invalid Prisma JsonFilter in reset_budget_windows
signals.text: ## Summary - stop using `where={"budget_limits": {"not": None}}` in `reset_budget_windows()` for keys and teams - keep filtering in Python with the existing `if not raw: continue` guard and add a regression test for that behavior - avoid periodic `prisma.errors.MissingRequiredValueError` noise from the background budget reset scheduler ## Reproduction This reproduces on the current LiteLLM codepath even when the database contains **zero** rows with `budget_limits` set. Environment used while debugging: - LiteLLM `1.83.10` - `prisma==0.11.0` - `budget_limits` columns present as nullable `jsonb` - `0` rows in both `LiteLLM_VerificationToken` and `LiteLLM_TeamTable` with non-null `budget_limits` Direct reproduction from the running LiteLLM container: ```python rows = await table.find_many(where={"budget_limits": {"not": None}}) ``` This raises: ```text prisma.errors.MissingRequiredValueError: Unable to match input value to any allowed input type for the field. Parse errors: [`where.budget_limits.not`: A value is required but not set, ...] ``` The failure happens before any matching rows are read from Postgres. In this setup, Prisma's generated `JsonFilter.not` expects a JSON value, not Python `None`, so the query itself is invalid. ## Why this change `reset_budget_windows()` already skips empty values in Python: ```python raw = key.budget_limits if not raw: continue ``` So the safest fix is to fetch keys/teams without the invalid Prisma JSON-null filter and preserve the existing Python-side guard. This keeps behavior the same for rows with real window data while avoiding the scheduler log noise for installations that do not use `budget_limits` at all. ## Validation - confirmed the bug against a live LiteLLM container backed by Postgres with no `budget_limits` rows - rebuilt and redeployed the patched image locally - ran `ResetBudgetJob.reset_budget_windows()` successfully in the deployed container with no `MissingRequiredValueError` - verified recent LiteLLM logs no longer contain `MissingRequiredValueError`, `where.budget_limits.not`, or `Failed to reset budget windows` ## Notes I also added a regression test covering the intended behavior: fetch records without a Prisma JSON null filter and only update rows that actually contain `budget_limits`.
signals.author: jibanez-staticduo

signals.title: fix(proxy): paginate reset_budget_windows scans
signals.text: ## Summary - paginate the background `reset_budget_windows()` scans for keys and teams - add a fixed safety batch size plus deterministic ordering for each page - extend the regression tests to cover the paginated behavior ## Why PR #26085 fixes a correctness issue where Prisma rejects `{"budget_limits": {"not": None}}` for nullable JSON fields. That correctness fix intentionally removed the invalid DB filter and relied on the existing Python-side `if not raw: continue` guard. This follow-up addresses the separate scalability concern noted in review by avoiding unbounded `find_many()` scans on every scheduler tick. ## What changed - keys are now fetched in batches with: - `take=500` - `skip=<page offset>` - `order={"token": "asc"}` - teams are now fetched in batches with: - `take=500` - `skip=<page offset>` - `order={"team_id": "asc"}` - existing semantics are preserved: rows without `budget_limits` are still skipped in Python, and rows with changed windows are still updated individually. ## Validation ```bash /home/staticduo/.local/bin/uv run --group dev --extra proxy --extra extra_proxy --extra proxy-runtime python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_reset_budget_job.py -q ``` Result: `20 passed`
