signals.title: feat(proxy): make user_api_key_cache in-memory size configurable
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `user_api_key_cache`'s in-memory tier is hardcoded to 200 entries - 200 is shared across key, team, user and org objects - Proxies with >200 active virtual keys evict on every insert - Every request then falls through to Redis or the DB How it solves it: - Adds `general_settings.user_api_key_cache_max_size` - Sized right where `user_api_key_cache_ttl` is already handled - Rejects values below 1 at startup, rather than breaking the cache - Default behaviour unchanged when the setting is absent ## Relevant issues <!-- none identified --> ## Linear ticket <!-- external contribution --> ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review <!-- Verified locally against litellm_internal_staging @ 24123269cc, in a container provisioned with `uv sync --frozen --all-groups --all-extras`: make lint ................... exit 0, all 8 checks green make test-unit-proxy-core ... 2613 passed, 1 skipped make test-unit-proxy-misc ... the tests added here pass; the remaining failures are pre-existing and flaky. Two consecutive runs of this target on unpatched 24123269cc gave 8 failed / 0 errored and 11 failed / 2 errored respectively, so the failure count varies run-to-run on untouched upstream code (a2a_endpoints, mcp_env_vars, _FakeRedisCache). `make test-unit` is not runnable on a clean checkout, independently of this PR: tests/test_litellm/models/test_models.py and tests/test_litellm/proxy/client/test_models.py both sit in directories without __init__.py, so both import as the bare module `test_models` and collide under pytest's default prepend import mode. CI does not hit this because it runs the scoped test-unit-* matrix targets, which never collect both directories in one session. --> ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real proxy, real postgres, 260 real virtual keys minted and exercised over HTTP, reading the proxy's own `/memory-usage-in-mem-cache`. Both runs use the **same build**, so the only variable is the setting — a before/after across two builds would also differ by the code change itself. Note that endpoint reports `len(cache_dict) + len(ttl_dict)`, i.e. it double-counts each entry (`litellm/proxy/common_utils/debug_utils.py`). Both runs: commit `0c9824abbc`, `litellm --config … --port 4499 --num_workers 1` against a real postgres, 260 virtual keys minted via `POST /key/generate`, each then used against `GET /v1/models`, followed by `GET /memory-usage-in-mem-cache`. ``` BEFORE — general_settings has no user_api_key_cache_max_size (commit 0c9824abbc) minted+used 260 keys {"num_items_in_user_api_key_cache":400, ...} -> ~200 entries # capped, 60 evicted AFTER — general_settings.user_api_key_cache_max_size: 5000 (commit 0c9824abbc) minted+used 260 keys num_items_in_user_api_key_cache=522 -> ~261 entries # all retained ``` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes `user_api_key_cache` is constructed without an `in_memory_cache` argument (`litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py`), so it inherits `InMemoryCache`'s default `max_size_in_memory` of **200** — a general anti-leak default rather than a value chosen for this cache. Those 200 slots are shared across key, team, user, org and object-permission entries, so a proxy with more than ~200 active virtual keys evicts on every insert and falls through to Redis (or the DB) on essentially every request. The TTL of the same cache is already configurable (`general_settings.user_api_key_cache_ttl`); the size is not. Other caches in the codebase size themselves explicitly — the container-ownership caches use `max_size_in_memory=10000`, for example. This adds the missing knob directly beneath the TTL handling it mirrors. ```yaml general_settings: user_api_key_cache_max_size: 5000 ``` This is a tuning knob, not a correctness fix: it is **not** a limit on how many virtual keys work. Keys beyond the bound authenticate fine; they just miss the in-memory tier. Values below 1 are rejected at startup. A negative bound leaves `InMemoryCache.evict_cache()`'s `len(cache_dict) >= max_size_in_memory` permanently true, so the next write pops an already-empty `expiration_heap` and raises `IndexError`; `0` is handled in `set_cache` but silently disables the in-memory tier. Neither is a useful way to express "smaller cache". The field is also declared on `ConfigGeneralSettings`, since the DB-backed config endpoints reject any `general_settings` field not listed there. Note it is *not* added to the `allowed_args` allowlist used to build the admin UI settings page, so this only affects `/config/field/update` — no new UI surface. For transparency: the sibling `user_api_key_cache_ttl` is likewise absent from `ConfigGeneralSettings` today, so it remains settable only through `config.yaml`. Happy to declare it in a follow-up if you'd like the two to match; it is left out here to keep this PR to one change. Declaring the field changes the proxy OpenAPI spec, so `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/lib/http/schema.d.ts` is regenerated to match (`npm run gen:api`). Tests added: - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_server.py` — `load_config` tests covering the new wiring: the setting is applied, its absence leaves the inherited default untouched, an `os.environ/…` value is coerced from `str` to `int`, and `0`/`-1` are rejected without mutating the cache. The applied/coerced tests fail if the `proxy_server.py` change is reverted. Plus a test that the field is a known `ConfigGeneralSettings` field. - `tests/test_litellm/proxy/common_utils/test_user_api_key_cache.py` — records the premise (the cache inherits `InMemoryCache`'s default today) and that an explicitly sized `InMemoryCache` is honoured. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(dashscope): select one pricing tier from request input size
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - DashScope cost tracking applies graduated, income-tax-style slicing to `tiered_pricing`, but Alibaba Model Studio picks one tier from a request's total input tokens and bills every token in that request at that tier's rates. Large Qwen requests are logged well under what the provider actually charges - Each token category was tiered independently from zero, so completion tokens selected their own tier and cached input selected a tier from the cached count alone rather than from the request's input size - The proxy's budget reservation path already uses the request-size model via `select_tier_for_input`, so reservation estimates and post-response spend disagreed with each other on the same request How it solves it: - Resolve the tier once in `dashscope/cost_calculator.py` from `usage.prompt_tokens` using `select_tier_for_input`, the selector budget reservation already uses, and apply that one tier's rates to plain input, cached input, completion and reasoning tokens ## Relevant issues Fixes #34729 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix I do not have DashScope credentials, so this is the repro script from the issue rather than a live proxy run. It makes no provider call; the token counts are synthetic and the rates come straight out of `model_prices_and_context_window.json`. ``` python - <<'PY' from litellm.llms.dashscope.cost_calculator import cost_per_token from litellm.types.utils import Usage from litellm.utils import get_model_info from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.tiered_pricing import ( select_tier_for_input, tier_rate, ) model = "qwen-flash" input_tokens = 300_000 output_tokens = 2_000 usage = Usage( prompt_tokens=input_tokens, completion_tokens=output_tokens, total_tokens=input_tokens + output_tokens, ) actual_input, actual_output = cost_per_token(model, usage) model_info = get_model_info(model=model, custom_llm_provider="dashscope") tier = select_tier_for_input(model_info["tiered_pricing"], input_tokens) expected_input = input_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "input_cost_per_token") expected_output = output_tokens * tier_rate(tier, "output_cost_per_token") print({ "actual_total": actual_input + actual_output, "request_tier_total": expected_input + expected_output, }) PY ``` Before, on `24123269ccb76f36298a2457589f08bd3141072c`: ``` {'actual_total': 0.024599999999999997, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` After: ``` {'actual_total': 0.079, 'request_tier_total': 0.079} ``` `qwen-flash` declares `[0, 256000]` at $0.05/M input and `[256000, 1000000]` at $0.25/M input. A 300,000-token request sits in the second tier, so Model Studio charges all 300,000 input tokens at $0.25/M and the 2,000 completion tokens at that tier's $2/M. The old result charged the first 256,000 input tokens at the cheap rate and put the completion tokens in tier 1 entirely, which is 69% under. Reverting only `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` and keeping the new tests gives the failures below, so the regression coverage is genuinely pinned to this fix: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py -q --tb=line E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0246, 0.079, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:96: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.012800249999999999, (256001 * 2.5e-07), rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:127: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.2488, 0.3, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:281: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0015999999999999999, 0.002, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:259: assert False E assert False + where False = isclose(0.0474, 0.07379999999999999, rel_tol=1e-10) tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py:172: assert False FAILED ...::test_dashscope_cached_tokens_count_toward_tier_selection FAILED ...::test_dashscope_input_above_first_tier_bills_whole_request_at_that_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_output_tokens_do_not_select_their_own_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tier_boundary_is_inclusive_of_range_end FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_string_costs_exceeding_highest_tier FAILED ...::test_dashscope_tiered_pricing_with_caching 7 failed, 3 passed in 1.39s ``` With the fix restored: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_cost_calc/ tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/ -q 193 passed in 23.14s $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_cost_calculator.py -q 80 passed in 4.55s ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `litellm/llms/dashscope/cost_calculator.py` now resolves the tier once per request instead of running four independent graduated calculations. `_calculate_prompt_cost` and `_calculate_completion_cost` take the selected tier rather than the whole `tiered_pricing` list, and read their rates with `tier_rate`, which keeps the existing fallbacks (cached input falls back to the tier's input rate, reasoning falls back to the tier's output rate) and the existing string-cost coercion for YAML-parsed rates. The flat-pricing path for models with no `tiered_pricing` is untouched, as is `calculate_tiered_cost` itself for any caller that wants graduated behaviour. A follow-up commit converts the three annotations the fix touches to PEP 604 / PEP 585 form (`dict | None`, `list[dict] | None`), which keeps the strict-rule budget from moving; the file drops from 8 strict violations to 2. The existing tests in `test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py` asserted the graduated numbers, so they are updated to the request-size expectations. Five cases were added or reworked to cover what the issue asked for: an above-first-tier request billed wholly at that tier, the tier boundary being inclusive of `range_end` (256,000 stays in tier 1, 256,001 moves up), output tokens not selecting their own tier, cached tokens counting toward tier selection, and input beyond the highest declared range falling back to the last tier. The two string-valued-rate regressions from the earlier YAML coercion fix are kept, with expectations recomputed under the new model. ## QA runbook Point a deployment at a DashScope Qwen model with `tiered_pricing` in the cost map (`qwen-flash` or `qwen3-coder-plus`), send one request whose input is comfortably above the first tier's `range_end` and one below it, then compare `spend` on the two `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` rows against the Model Studio console for the same requests. The large request should now be priced entirely at the higher tier rather than partly at the cheap one, and it should match the budget reservation estimate for that request rather than falling short of it. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A live OpenAI Responses API probe using a synthetic search-tool schema reproduced the provider behavior behind this bug: - When `strict` was omitted, Responses normalized the tool to `strict: true`, changed `required` from `["query"]` to `["query", "cursor", "context_channel_id"]`, and generated empty strings for the optional fields. - With `strict: false`, Responses preserved `required: ["query"]` and generated only `{"query":"zz_responses_probe"}`. The patched adapter now emits `strict: false` for ordinary Anthropic tools while preserving an explicit top-level Anthropic `strict: true` request. The sibling Chat Completions adapter also keeps an explicit `strict` value at function level rather than placing it inside the JSON Schema. After rebasing onto `litellm_internal_staging`, focused verification against commit `6dbd305f` passed: ```text ........................................................................ [ 40%] ........................................................................ [ 80%] ................................... [100%] 179 passed, 1 warning in 3.84s ``` The edited modules pass `py_compile`, and `git diff --check` reports no errors. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - Explicitly disable the OpenAI Responses API's strict-by-default normalization when translating ordinary Anthropic tools. - Preserve explicitly requested Anthropic strict tool validation across both Responses and Chat Completions routes. - Add the top-level `strict` field to the Anthropic tool type. - Add regressions proving optional properties stay optional, explicit strict validation remains enabled, and `strict` does not leak into the parameters schema. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): emit sse keepalive comments during slow time-to-first-token
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Streaming responses emit zero bytes during a long time-to-first-token - Idle-timeout hops then abort a connection that is perfectly healthy - Existing keepalive settings act on sockets, not on the response How it solves it: - Optional interval emits an SSE comment whenever the stream is silent - Races the timer alongside the existing first-chunk and disconnect arms - Re-arms past the first token, so mid-stream gaps are covered too - Off by default, so the streaming path stays byte-identical ## Relevant issues Fixes #34819 Related reports of the same symptom from different root causes: #32004, #32491, #24929 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Driving the real `create_response` with a generator that stays silent for 30s before its first frame, printing when each byte reaches the response body. Same command all three times, only the commit and the setting change. **Before, at `daf22ec871` (the base commit).** Nothing reaches the wire for the whole think, so an intermediary watching for idle connections closes a stream that was never unhealthy ``` sse_keepalive_interval_seconds = None model stays silent for 30s before the first token [ 30.002s] data: {"type":"content_block_delta","delta":{"text":"84"}} [ 30.002s] data: [DONE] [ 30.002s] ``` **After, at `6f9557c901`, setting unset.** The default path is unchanged, byte for byte, which is what keeps this safe to ship off by default ``` sse_keepalive_interval_seconds = None model stays silent for 30s before the first token [ 30.002s] data: {"type":"content_block_delta","delta":{"text":"84"}} [ 30.002s] data: [DONE] [ 30.002s] ``` **After, at `6f9557c901`, interval 5s.** Comments fill the silence and stop the moment the real frame lands. The token still arrives at 30s, so nothing was sped up or substituted, the connection was simply kept visible ``` sse_keepalive_interval_seconds = 5.0 model stays silent for 30s before the first token [ 5.001s] : keepalive [ 10.002s] : keepalive [ 15.004s] : keepalive [ 20.005s] : keepalive [ 25.005s] : keepalive [ 30.001s] data: {"type":"content_block_delta","delta":{"text":"84"}} [ 30.001s] data: [DONE] [ 30.012s] ``` Soaked on a live proxy behind an ALB with a 60s idle timeout, three pods, serving extended-thinking traffic with the interval set to 15s. The abort class this fixes stopped occurring; a client that hangs up mid-think still records a 499 and releases its parallel-request slot ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Streaming responses that have connected but not yet produced a token put nothing on the wire. Reasoning and extended-thinking models can stay silent for minutes, and providers that deliver large tool arguments as a trailing burst do the same mid-stream. Any hop between the client and the proxy that watches for idle connections then closes one that is perfectly healthy, and the client sees a truncated stream while the upstream request was still on its way Nothing shipped today can prevent that. `AIOHTTP_KEEPALIVE_TIMEOUT`, `AIOHTTP_SO_KEEPALIVE` and uvicorn's `timeout_keep_alive` all act on sockets, and none of them write a byte to an in-flight response, so a connected but silent stream is invisible to every idle watchdog in the path. This is the same class of problem as #28384, where the proxy was the only component positioned to tell an intermediary how to treat the stream. That fix does not help here: it tells a reverse proxy not to buffer chunks that exist, and during the wait there are none `litellm.sse_keepalive_interval_seconds` (also settable as `litellm_settings: sse_keepalive_interval_seconds`) defaults to unset, which leaves behavior exactly as it is today and is pinned by a test. When an operator sets it, `_buffer_first_chunk_honoring_disconnect` races the keepalive timer alongside the two arms it already had, and returns the still-pending fetch on a genuine stall instead of a chunk. `create_response` then commits to a response whose body emits a comment line until that fetch resolves, yields it, and falls through to plain iteration, so nothing is added to the per-chunk hot path. Comment lines are ignored by conforming SSE parsers per the HTML specification, so nothing a client parses changes The two contracts `create_response` owns are preserved. A disconnect keeps priority over the timer, so the client-disconnect path and the cleanup it drives are untouched, and a chunk that lands inside the interval still reaches the error-only detection and its status-code mapping unchanged One consequence is worth stating plainly, because it is inherent to sending anything at all during the wait rather than incidental to how this is written. Emitting a keepalive commits the status line, so nothing that arrives afterwards can still choose a status code. Two cases follow from that, and both are pinned by tests so they stay decisions rather than surprises. A guardrail that yields `data: {"error": {..., "code": 400}}` later than the interval is delivered as an SSE error frame under a 200 instead of being downgraded to a JSON 400. A guardrail that raises instead of yielding loses its status code entirely and the exception escapes, where with the feature off it would have been mapped. Both are reachable only when the interval is shorter than the time a guardrail needs to reject a request; measured against a request-scanning guardrail that answers in well under a second, an interval in the tens of seconds never reaches either. Anyone setting a sub-second interval on a deployment with slow request-scanning guardrails should know the trade-off exists The timer re-arms for the whole stream rather than stopping once the status line is committed. A stream can start promptly and then go quiet — extended thinking, a long tool-use turn, a provider that delivers large tool arguments as a trailing burst — and those gaps idle out exactly the same watchdogs a slow first token does. Both the buffered-first-chunk and pending-first-chunk paths run the body through the same wrapper, and with the setting unset it forwards the stream unchanged. Two details are load-bearing there: closing a generator does not cascade into one it is iterating, so the nested fetch is released explicitly or the upstream `aclose()` raises "asynchronous generator is already running" and the provider connection survives until garbage collection; and keepalives are protocol filler rather than model output, so they are excluded from the per-chunk spans to keep the chunk count and its latency stats honest Scope is the shared `create_response` return path, which covers `/v1/messages`, `/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` and streaming assistant runs together, gated on `media_type == "text/event-stream"`. `/queue/chat/completions` returned a bare `StreamingResponse` and so was the one streaming route that skipped first-chunk buffering altogether — no keepalive, an error-only stream delivered as 200 + SSE rather than a JSON error carrying the provider status code, and a disconnect during time-to-first-token leaving the upstream call running. It now goes through `create_response` like every other route. Pass-through routes return their own `StreamingResponse` and remain deliberately out of scope Two notes for the reviewer, since both look odd out of context. The done-callback on the pending fetch exists only to consume its outcome so asyncio never reports an unretrieved exception when the response tears the fetch down, and a test asserts that. The `isinstance(interval, bool)` guard is there because `bool` is an `int` subclass, so a config value of `true` would otherwise coerce to a one-second interval instead of being rejected `asyncio.wait` is awaited from two coroutines across the handoff, the pending fetch is cancelled and awaited under a shield in every teardown path, and the response owns the fetch so it cannot be orphaned when the body is never iterated. Each of those is a separate regression test, and each was checked by mutating its guard narrowly and confirming the test fails — including the leak one, which asserts the upstream generator is closed by the time `aclose()` returns and that no task is left pending, rather than relying on garbage collection to reap it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(streaming): track provider-reported cost when caller omits include_usage
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - OpenRouter's cost is dropped from streams without `include_usage` - Provider usage is discarded, so spend logs and budgets show $0 How it solves it: - Keep usage-only chunks in `self.chunks` for accounting - Still never emit them to callers unless `include_usage` is set ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin routing OpenRouter models sees streamed requests logged at $0 even though OpenRouter reports the real cost 1. A developer sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"model": "deepseek-v4-flash"`, `"stream": true`, and no `stream_options` 2. The stream comes back normally: content chunks, a finish chunk, then `data: [DONE]` 3. The admin opens http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs and that request shows $0.00 spend, while OpenRouter's own activity page shows a real charge for it 4. Key and team budgets never count the streamed spend, so budget enforcement drifts from the real bill After: the same streamed request is logged at OpenRouter's own reported cost 1. The developer sends the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with `"stream": true` and no `stream_options` 2. The stream comes back exactly as before: content chunks, a finish chunk, then `data: [DONE]`, still no usage chunk 3. http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs now shows that request at the provider-reported cost, matching OpenRouter's activity page 4. Key and team budgets count the streamed spend ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5656 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live DB-backed proxy hitting real OpenRouter with real spend. Shared config: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: deepseek-v4-flash litellm_params: model: openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash api_key: os.environ/OPENROUTER_API_KEY ``` Every response id below is the OpenRouter generation id, so each logged spend is read back with `GET /spend/logs?request_id=<id>` and cross-checked against OpenRouter's own authoritative number from `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/generation?id=<id>` (`total_cost`, `native_tokens_*`). OpenRouter routes the same model to different backend providers with different pricing per request, so a match is only possible when the provider-reported cost is what got logged, not a static price-map estimate One note for reviewers: since this PR was opened, OpenRouter's edge changed its wire shape. On every model and backend provider probed today (12+, including deepseek-v4-flash from the customer report, and with `stream_options.include_usage` forwarded upstream), `usage` + `cost` now arrive attached to the final choices-bearing chunk instead of the standalone post-finish `choices: []` chunk from the July capture. That chunk was never dropped, so the live Before leg below already logs provider cost; the dropped-chunk regression this PR fixes is replayed byte-exactly by the new unit test, which fails on pre-PR code with `assert None == 0.00025` (verified by mutation: removing the `_record_usage_only_chunk` call). The live run proves the PR holds exact provider-cost parity on all three legs at the tip and leaves client-visible streams untouched ### Before (973329e986) #### streaming, no stream_options 1. `curl -sN -X POST http://localhost:42388/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-...' -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say the word ok"}],"stream":true}'` 2. Stream: content chunks, finish chunk, `data: [DONE]`; 0 usage chunks client-visible; id `gen-1787003115-SxxHg0JOkP5GLEANBmJg` 3. Spend log: `spend=1.44e-06 prompt_tokens=12 completion_tokens=2` 4. OpenRouter generation: `total_cost=1.44e-06`, native tokens 12/2, provider DeepInfra; exact match #### streaming + include_usage 1. Same curl plus `"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}`; exactly 1 usage chunk client-visible; id `gen-1787003116-kRTDb99ateANNx8OAWyq` 2. Spend log: `spend=3.64e-06 prompt_tokens=12 completion_tokens=2` 3. OpenRouter generation: `total_cost=3.64e-06`, native tokens 12/2, provider Azure; exact match #### non-streaming 1. Same curl without `"stream"`; id `gen-1787003117-mcVdnh5acmB2RLkDYCdK` 2. Spend log: `spend=7.56e-05 prompt_tokens=18 completion_tokens=261` 3. OpenRouter generation: `total_cost=7.56e-05`, native tokens 18/261, provider AtlasCloud; exact match ### After (fbc5c1c3d4) #### streaming, no stream_options 1. `curl -sN -X POST http://localhost:48291/v1/chat/completions -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-...' -d '{"model":"deepseek-v4-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say the word ok"}],"stream":true}'` 2. Stream unchanged: content chunks, finish chunk, `data: [DONE]`; 0 usage chunks client-visible, no empty-choices chunk leaked; id `gen-1787003883-GtESJh8LkB0cI2WCnKRk` 3. Spend log: `spend=1.6548e-05 prompt_tokens=91 completion_tokens=53` 4. OpenRouter generation: `total_cost=1.6548e-05`, native tokens 91/53, provider GMICloud; exact match #### streaming + include_usage 1. Same curl plus `"stream_options":{"include_usage":true}`; exactly 1 usage chunk client-visible; id `gen-1787003890-Xm3Q2rWNmhXZKc5qWcXt` 2. Spend log: `spend=1.344e-05 prompt_tokens=18 completion_tokens=39` 3. OpenRouter generation: `total_cost=1.344e-05`, native tokens 18/39, provider AtlasCloud; exact match #### non-streaming 1. Same curl without `"stream"`; id `gen-1787003891-V2QX3ybsk8MEeKwgWCln` 2. Spend log: `spend=0.00014924 prompt_tokens=12 completion_tokens=1019` 3. OpenRouter generation: `total_cost=0.00014924`, native tokens 12/1019, provider Baidu; exact match ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Logged prompt/completion tokens for such streams now come from the provider's usage chunk, not litellm's estimate - OpenRouter's current edge no longer emits the standalone usage-only chunk; the regression test replays the July shape - OpenRouter `/responses` and `/embeddings` never extract provider cost; separate gap, out of scope (LIT-5656) ## Changes `CustomStreamWrapper.chunk_creator` returned early on any chunk with no choices unless the caller had asked for `stream_options.include_usage`. OpenRouter's final chunk is exactly that shape and carries the provider-reported `usage.cost`, so for those streams the chunk never reached `self.chunks`; `stream_chunk_builder` never saw the cost, and cost tracking fell back to the token map (`0.0` for anything unpriced). `include_usage` should govern only what the caller sees, not what gets logged, so the chunk is now recorded for accounting and still withheld from the response stream: ```python else: if self.stream_options is not None and self.stream_options["include_usage"] is True: model_response.choices = [] return model_response self._record_usage_only_chunk(model_response=model_response) return ``` where `_record_usage_only_chunk` appends the usage-bearing chunk to `self.chunks` and returns nothing to the caller. From there the existing `_propagate_usage_cost_to_hidden_params` path lifts `usage.cost` into `_hidden_params["additional_headers"]["llm_provider-x-litellm-response-cost"]`, which `response_cost_calculator` prefers over its own estimate. The regression test registers a `CustomLogger` as the async success callback and asserts on the cost that callback actually receives (`kwargs["response_cost"]` and `standard_logging_object["response_cost"]`), so it covers chunk retention through to callback dispatch rather than rebuilding the response by hand. Dropping the `_record_usage_only_chunk` call makes it fail with `assert None == 0.00025` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/7acbeaa185b949329f06374aa40dd380

signals.title: chore(typing): clear basedpyright Any errors across 6 core files
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - basedpyright reports thousands of `reportAny`/`reportExplicitAny` errors repo-wide, most from typing seams that were never given a real type - untyped seams hide real bugs (e.g. a caller passing the wrong shape) behind `Any`, and make it harder to trust the type checker anywhere it touches these paths How it solves it: - replaces `Any` with concrete types (TypedDicts, Pydantic models validated via `TypeAdapter`, Protocols, precise repository/DB return types) in the six highest-`reportAny`+`reportExplicitAny` production files under `litellm/` - ratchets down the `reportAny`/`reportExplicitAny`/LIT001 budget ceilings in `basedpyright-code-budget.json`, `ruff-strict-budget.json`, and `type-discipline-budget.json` to lock in the reduction - no behavior changes anywhere; every fix is a type annotation change verified against the existing test suite and a whole-tree basedpyright diff ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is a typing-only change with no user-observable behavior, so the proof is the type-checker diff and the full mapped test suite, not a live proxy call. Per-file `reportAny` / `reportExplicitAny` error counts (scoped basedpyright runs, before -> after this branch): | file | reportAny | reportExplicitAny | |---|---|---| | `litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` | 384 -> 311 | 23 -> 20 | | `responses/streaming_iterator.py` | 217 -> 69 | 87 -> 36 | | `proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py` | 321 -> 172 | 27 -> 5 | | `proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py` | 319 -> 239 | 30 -> 14 | | `proxy/utils.py` | 361 -> 322 | 50 -> 28 | | `litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` | 259 -> 153 | 37 -> 27 | Whole-tree basedpyright run (`basedpyright --outputjson` over all of `litellm/`), before this branch vs after, per severity=error rule, confirms zero regressions on any of the 39 rules basedpyright emits in this repo: - `reportAny`: 21518 -> 20921 (-597) - `reportExplicitAny`: 7258 -> 7133 (-125) - every other rule (reportUnknownMemberType, reportUnknownArgumentType, reportUnknownVariableType, reportMissingTypeArgument, reportUnknownParameterType, reportMissingParameterType, reportArgumentType, reportUnnecessaryIsInstance, reportArgumentType, etc) is at or below its baseline count, several improved as a side effect of the same fixes - total error count: 151426 -> 150440 Commands run locally to produce the above and confirm no regressions: ``` uv run basedpyright --outputjson # whole tree, before and after, diffed per rule uv run python scripts/type_discipline_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging uv run python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging cd litellm && uv run ruff check . uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_handler.py tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator.py tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_streaming_iterator.py tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator_error_events.py tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_llm_http_handler.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_endpoints.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_key_management_endpoints.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_utils.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_litellm_logging.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_logging_utils.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_logging_worker.py ``` The mapped test suite above (1024 tests across the touched files and their close neighbors) passes in full, both per-file during development and again on the final merged tree. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes Six files, one commit each, in order: - `litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py`: JSON-boundary helpers (`_require_dict`/`_require_list`/`_require_str`) for the fake-streaming provider chunk parsers, `model_validate` instead of `**` splats for pydantic construction, a narrower return type on the provider chunk early-return dataclass, and a mutation-free rewrite of `model_response_creator`'s chunk merging so its parameters could become `Mapping` instead of `dict` - `responses/streaming_iterator.py`: a `PIIMaskingGuardrail` Protocol for the guardrail callback shapes used by the Responses WebSocket path, `ResponsesAPIResponse`/`ResponsesAPIStreamingResponse` return types throughout the streaming iterators in place of `Any`, and `TypeAdapter`-validated JSON-boundary helpers for the WebSocket forwarding paths - `proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py`: `PrismaClient`/`UserApiKeyCache`/`ProxyLogging` on helper signatures that were bare `Any`, and the existing pydantic mirror models (`LiteLLM_TeamTable`, `LiteLLM_UserTable`, `LiteLLM_OrganizationTable`, etc) on raw Prisma call results - `proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py`: the same typed-repository-model pattern, plus typed `Callable` aliases for the dynamically-loaded custom key-generate/update proxy hooks - `proxy/utils.py`: a `_McpPreCallHookResult` TypedDict for the pre-MCP-call hook response, a `_ConfigRowLike` Protocol for the config-row cache helpers, and prisma's own `DatasourceOverride` TypedDict in `PrismaClient.__init__` in place of an ad-hoc `Dict[str, Any]` kwargs dict - `litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py`: `List[CustomLogger]` for the module-level callback registry (previously `List[Any]`, used in ~90 call sites), a `LoggingCallbackType` alias, and a real union type in place of the nonsensical `Union[Any, BaseModel, dict]` on the standard-logging-payload helpers Where a raw, untyped seam had to stay (a genuinely dynamic third-party SDK shape, a Prisma feature no typed repository helper supports, or a test that mocks the raw Prisma table method directly so a typed helper's `model_validate` would break against a `MagicMock`), it's marked `# any-ok: <reason>` rather than left as a silent `Any`. A handful of `isinstance` checks and one `.dict()` fallback became statically provable once their inputs were typed but stay load-bearing at runtime (mocked test doubles, a pydantic-v1-compat branch that can't execute under this repo's `pydantic>=2.10.0` pin); those are marked `# pyright: ignore[<rule>]` with a reason instead of deleted. `basedpyright-code-budget.json`, `ruff-strict-budget.json`, and `type-discipline-budget.json` are updated (via `make lint-budget-update`) to ratchet their ceilings down by exactly what this branch fixed. ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix: hold references to the background tasks in auth_checks
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Ten `create_task()` results discarded in `auth_checks.py` - One is a **database write**, not telemetry — an SSO binding - The loop only weakly references tasks, so they can vanish mid-flight How it solves it: - Holds each task in a module-level set, drops it in a done callback - Same pattern the repo already uses in three other places - No control flow change ## Relevant issues None found. ## The one that is not telemetry In `get_user_object_from_db_or_cache`, when a user is matched by email during SSO, the `sso_user_id` binding is persisted in the background: ```python if response is not None and sso_user_id is not None: # update sso_user_id asyncio.create_task( # background task to update user with sso id UserRepository(prisma_client).table.update( where={"user_id": response.user_id}, data={"sso_user_id": sso_user_id}, ) ) ``` The task is discarded, and [the event loop only keeps a weak reference](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task): > Important: Save a reference to the result of this function, to avoid a task disappearing mid-execution. The event loop only keeps weak references to tasks. A task that isn't referenced elsewhere may get garbage collected at any time, even before it's done. If it is collected the login still succeeds, so nothing looks wrong — but the binding is never written. The next login falls back to the email lookup again, and the SSO identity never sticks. No exception, no log line; from the outside it reads like a flaky identity provider. ## The other nine Budget alerts — token, soft, max, organization, team and key budgets. A collected alert simply never fires, so a budget event passes unnoticed. Less severe than a lost write, same root cause. | line | task | |---|---| | 1615 | `UserRepository.table.update` — SSO binding | | 3607, 3711, 3802, 3834, 3998 | `budget_alerts` — token / soft / max / team | | 4116, 4160, 4212, 4350 | `budget_alerts` — key / organization | ## The change ```python _background_tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set() # mutable-ok: task registry ... _background_task = asyncio.create_task(...) _background_tasks.add(_background_task) _background_task.add_done_callback(_background_tasks.discard) ``` `discard` rather than `remove` so a double callback cannot raise. The set stays bounded by the number of in-flight tasks. **The repo already does this correctly elsewhere**, which is why I treated it as a bug rather than a style preference — `guardrail_hooks/akto/akto.py:85`, `management_helpers/audit_logs.py:142`, `mcp_server/.../oauth_token_store.py:238`. ## Verification ```console $ ruff check litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py # ruff 0.15.3, pinned in pyproject.toml All checks passed! $ ruff format --check litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py 1 file left unchanged $ python scripts/check_type_discipline.py litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py | grep -c LIT 229 # 229 on main too — zero net new $ python -m py_compile litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py ``` No test: the failure is a garbage-collection race, so a test would have to force a GC at a chosen moment and assert a task did *not* vanish — flaky by construction. Happy to add one if you have a shape in mind. Found with an AST scan for `create_task` / `ensure_future` results discarded as bare expression statements (excluding `TaskGroup.create_task`, which does hold strong references). Companion to #35347, which does the same for `RedisCache`; this one is a different file and they are independent.

signals.title: fix(videos): stop raw-fd uploads crashing filename detection, and drop deprecated .dict() round-trips
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A video opened from a raw fd crashes the character upload - Assistants thread and message round-trips use deprecated `.dict()` - Identical `if`/`else` branches in `add_message` are dead weight How it solves it: - Fall back to the default filename unless `name` is a string - Build the models with `model_validate(model_dump())` instead - Collapse the duplicated branches to a single return ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### The bug, reproduced before and after This is the real transformation code against a real file descriptor, no mocks and no test harness. A video opened from a raw fd reports an `int` as its `name`, and the old expression forwarded that into `mimetypes.guess_type()`. Before, on `litellm_internal_staging`: ``` $ uv run python -c ' import io, os from litellm.llms.openai.videos.transformation import OpenAIVideoConfig from litellm.types.router import GenericLiteLLMParams v = io.open(os.open("/tmp/clip.mp4", os.O_RDONLY), "rb") OpenAIVideoConfig().transform_video_create_character_request( name="hero", video=v, api_base="https://api.openai.com/v1/videos", litellm_params=GenericLiteLLMParams(), headers={})' TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not int ``` After, on this branch, same command with the multipart list printed: ``` video.name is: 3 multipart: [('name', (None, 'hero')), ('video', ('input_video.mp4', 'BufferedReader', 'video/mp4'))] ``` ### Live proxy A proxy was booted off this branch and served real traffic. Every provider credential available to me is out of credit, so the call below reaches the upstream API and comes back with a genuine provider billing error rather than a 200. That still shows the request being routed, transformed, and sent, with a real provider `request_id` coming back. The funded 200-level walkthrough is in the QA runbook rather than captured here; I have not fabricated any provider output. ``` $ python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --use_v2_migration_resolver ... INFO: Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 $ curl -sS http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness "I'm alive!" $ curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","input":"Reply with exactly: typing cleanup e2e ok"}' litellm.BadRequestError: AnthropicException - {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error", "message":"Your credit balance is too low to access the Anthropic API. Please go to Plans & Billing to upgrade or purchase credits."},"request_id":"req_011Ce8gK9MWbdHjk3YqjLt1A"} ``` ### Static checks Whole-tree basedpyright against base `77c8a6452f`, same interpreter and lockfile on both sides: ``` reportUnknownArgumentType: 36732 -> 36689 (-43) reportAny: 14178 -> 14162 (-16) reportDeprecated: 214 -> 198 (-16) TOTAL 142843 -> 142768 (-75) regressions: none ``` `make lint-budget-update` independently ratcheted by the same 75. Mapped tests pass at 1431 passed, 40 skipped. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes The bug is in the OpenAI video transformation. `getattr(video, "name", None) or "input_video.mp4"` assumes `name` is a string, but a file opened from a raw descriptor reports the descriptor number, so an `int` reached `mimetypes.guess_type()` and raised. The filename now falls back to the default unless `name` is a non-empty string. The rest is deprecation and dead-code cleanup in the assistants paths. `llms/openai/openai.py` built threads with `Thread(**response.dict())`, which both relies on the deprecated pydantic v1 `.dict()` alias and re-validates by keyword splat; those four sites now use `Thread.model_validate(response.model_dump())`. Both `llms/openai/openai.py` and `llms/azure/assistants.py` also had an `add_message` whose `if`/`else` branches were character-for-character identical, sync and async alike, so each collapses to a single return and the now-unused `response_obj` declarations go away. `ui_sso.py` gets the same `model_validate` treatment for the one remaining `NewTeamRequest(**...)` site. The tests cover these paths rather than just executing them. The video response transforms are driven through a mock `httpx.Response` and assert the payload parses and the provider id is wrapped so it decodes back to the raw id. The Azure and OpenAI assistants tests use a real SDK client on an `httpx.MockTransport`, so the SDK's own response parsing runs and the handler sees exactly what production would. Both cover the sync and async entry points, pin the message status defaulting to `"completed"` when the provider omits it, and check that `Thread` keeps its declared fields. The SSO default-team helper and the router credential lookup assert their projections directly. Every one of these fails when the line it covers is reverted. This PR started as a broader basedpyright `Any` sweep. `litellm_internal_staging` has since landed overlapping typing and syntax-modernization work that subsumed most of it, so each merge took the base's side on every line it had already fixed. What is left is the bug fix, the deprecation cleanup the base did not reach, and the test coverage. ## QA runbook Run against a proxy with a funded `OPENAI_API_KEY`. 1. Start the proxy off this branch: `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml --detailed_debug --use_v2_migration_resolver 2>&1 | tee litellm.log` 2. `curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/threads -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"metadata":{"origin":"qa"}}'` and expect a 200 with `"object": "thread"` and the metadata echoed; save the `id` as `$THREAD`. This is the `Thread.model_validate` swap in `llms/openai/openai.py` 3. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/threads/$THREAD -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` and expect the same thread back, still carrying `metadata` 4. `curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/threads/$THREAD/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"role":"user","content":"hi"}'` and expect a 200 whose `status` is populated. This is the `OpenAIMessage.model_validate` swap plus the status default 5. For the video fix, with an mp4 at `./clip.mp4`: `curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/videos/characters -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -F "name=hero" -F "video=@./clip.mp4"` and expect a 200 with `"object": "character"` (requires Sora access on the key) 6. The raw-fd case that step 5 cannot reach over HTTP, since FastAPI always supplies a string filename, is the snippet in the Proof of Fix above; run it on this branch and on `litellm_internal_staging` and compare 7. Sanity check: `tail litellm.log` shows the upstream calls for each step with no `TypeError`, no `DeprecationWarning` from `.dict()`, and no validation error ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(rag): resolve vector store registry credentials in rag query
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - /v1/rag/query never resolves the LiteLLM-managed vector store registry, so a vector store registered with a non-OpenAI provider (and its litellm_params such as api_key and api_base) is still queried against api.openai.com. The standalone /v1/vector_stores/{id}/search endpoint already resolves this via _update_request_data_with_litellm_managed_vector_store_registry; rag_query did not How it solves it: - Reuse the shared resolver in rag_query to load the managed vector store for the requested vector_store_id - Set the resolved custom_llm_provider on retrieval_config so _execute_query_pipeline picks it up (it passes custom_llm_provider to asearch explicitly, so it cannot come through request_data kwargs without a duplicate-argument TypeError) - Forward the resolved litellm_params (minus litellm_credential_name) through request_data so they reach the vector store search ## Relevant issues Closes https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35599 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The regression test test_rag_query_resolves_managed_vector_store_registry fails without this change (asserts the registry provider "bedrock" and aws_region_name reach litellm.aquery) and passes with it. The rag endpoint suite (17 tests) and rag/test_main.py (7 tests) pass. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - litellm/proxy/rag_endpoints/endpoints.py: resolve managed vector store registry in rag_query - tests/test_litellm/proxy/rag_endpoints/test_rag_endpoints.py: regression test ## QA runbook Run `python -m pytest tests/test_litellm/proxy/rag_endpoints/test_rag_endpoints.py tests/test_litellm/rag/test_main.py` ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: chore(typing): clear basedpyright Any errors in responses, proxy hooks, and management endpoints
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `Any` hides real shapes in hot production paths - 25752 basedpyright `Any` errors tree-wide - Untyped payload dicts defeat the type checker How it solves it: - TypedDicts and Protocols replace `Any` seams - Precise return types on db/provider helpers - Ratchets the three lint budgets down ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This change is typing-only and has no runtime surface, so there is nothing an end user can curl that behaves differently before and after; the proof that matters is that the type checker sees less `Any` and that runtime behavior is unchanged. Both are reproducible at commit `0db81a60`, with the baseline taken at `491eda31` ```bash uv sync --frozen --group proxy-dev --group e2e-dev uv run --no-sync prisma generate --schema litellm/proxy/schema.prisma (NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=12288 uv run --no-sync basedpyright --outputjson || true) > /tmp/after.json ``` Counting `severity=error` diagnostics under `litellm/`, baseline against this branch: | rule | before | after | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | reportAny | 19234 | 18638 | -596 | | reportExplicitAny | 6518 | 6289 | -229 | | reportUnknownMemberType | 28726 | 28634 | -92 | | reportUnknownVariableType | 22485 | 22400 | -85 | | reportUnknownParameterType | 13865 | 13824 | -41 | | reportMissingTypeArgument | 11036 | 10994 | -42 | | reportUnknownArgumentType | 34754 | 34727 | -27 | | reportArgumentType | 2169 | 2148 | -21 | | all in-repo errors | 149644 | 148492 | -1152 | Combined `reportAny` + `reportExplicitAny` goes from 25752 to 24927. Every other rule is at or below its baseline; nothing was traded for anything ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes The eight files were picked by combined `reportAny` + `reportExplicitAny` count, skipping the handful of multi-thousand-line files at the very top of that ranking (`proxy_server.py` is 16782 lines) where a partial pass churns too much surface area to verify against a zero-regression bar Per file, combined `Any` errors before and after: `responses/streaming_iterator.py` 304 to 132, `proxy/pass_through_endpoints/managed_id_rewriter.py` 163 to 5, `proxy/management_endpoints/model_management_endpoints.py` 151 to 69, `responses/litellm_completion_transformation/transformation.py` 139 to 8, `proxy/hooks/parallel_request_limiter_v3.py` 135 to 10, `litellm_core_utils/streaming_chunk_builder_utils.py` 130 to 34, `llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/handler.py` 128 to 88, and `proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/sampling_handler.py` 122 to 99 The work is the same shape everywhere: payload dicts became TypedDicts, duck-typed record shapes became Protocols, and helpers that returned `Any` or a bare `dict` got their real return types. Where a value is genuinely heterogeneous, it became `object` plus `isinstance` narrowing rather than staying `Any`, since that is behavior-preserving in a way a strict Pydantic validate would not be at boundaries that tolerate malformed input today. New types live next to the existing ones for their area, so `managed_id_rewriter.py` gained `litellm/types/passthrough_endpoints/managed_ids.py` and the rest extended files that were already there Two spots deserve a reviewer's attention. In `streaming_iterator.py`, giving the caching handler and the PII guardrail real types surfaced protected-member reaches that `Any` had been concealing, which basedpyright reports as `reportPrivateUsage`; rather than rename those members, which would be a public API change, the accesses moved into the declaring Protocol behind a public accessor. In `parallel_request_limiter_v3.py`, the batch rate limiter delegate is typed as `CustomLogger` instead of importing the private `_PROXY_BatchRateLimiter`, which is sound because that class subclasses `CustomLogger` and this module only ever uses it through the `async_pre_call_hook` contract No `cast()`, no `# type: ignore`, and no pyright or noqa suppressions were added. Seven `# any-ok:` markers were added where an untyped runtime seam genuinely cannot be typed, matching the existing convention in `litellm/repositories/` `make lint-budget-update` lowered all three ceilings against the final tree: basedpyright by 1140 errors across 48 rules, strict ruff rules by 103, and LIT rules by 36 ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_011ZcQRp2GHHDRhW9SDiPaTp)_

signals.title: feat: add FlexAI as an OpenAI-compatible provider
signals.text: ## Relevant issues New provider registration (no linked issue). Follows [Adding OpenAI-Compatible Providers](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/contributing/adding_openai_compatible_providers) and `litellm/llms/openai_like/README.md`. ## What this adds [FlexAI](https://flex.ai)'s Token Service is an OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint (`https://api.flex.ai/v1`) serving open-weight models — Qwen3.x, DeepSeek-V4, GLM-5.2, gpt-oss, Llama 3.x, Gemma 4, Mistral — plus embedding, image, and speech models. | File | Change | | --- | --- | | `litellm/llms/openai_like/providers.json` | `flexai` entry: `base_url=https://api.flex.ai/v1`, `FLEXAI_API_KEY`, `FLEXAI_API_BASE` override, `base_class=openai_gpt`, `/v1/chat/completions` + `/v1/responses` | | `litellm/constants.py` | `flexai` in `openai_compatible_providers`; `https://api.flex.ai/v1` in `openai_compatible_endpoints` | | `litellm/litellm_core_utils/get_llm_provider_logic.py` | base-URL autodetection — `api_base=https://api.flex.ai/v1` resolves to `flexai`, preferring an explicit `api_key` over the server environment | | `litellm/types/utils.py` | `FLEXAI` in the `LlmProviders` enum | | `model_prices_and_context_window.json` | 21 entries for the served roster | | `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` | same 21 entries (asserted byte-identical by a test — see note below) | | `provider_endpoints_support.json` | endpoint-support block | | `tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/test_flexai_provider.py` | 18 tests | No `param_mappings` needed — verified `max_completion_tokens` is accepted natively. ```python import litellm response = litellm.completion( model="flexai/gpt-oss-120b", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}], ) ``` ## How the pricing entries were produced Generated from FlexAI's **public** model feed — `https://tokens.flex.ai/api/models` (no key required, curl-able by a reviewer) — and then cross-checked field-by-field against authenticated prod `GET /v1/models`. Every entry carries a `source` pointing at that feed. Roster and price agreement, verified **2026-08-04** (FlexAI's served set changes as models are pinned/unpinned, so treat the feed above as the source of truth rather than this snapshot): ``` prod /v1/models : 21 models committed flexai/* : 21 entries in prod, NOT committed : none committed, NOT in prod : none price spot-check (prod pricing.prompt vs committed input_cost_per_token): bge-m3 prod=1e-08 committed=1e-08 MATCH DeepSeek-V4-Flash prod=8.96e-08 committed=8.96e-08 MATCH gemma-4-26B-A4B-it prod=6e-08 committed=6e-08 MATCH GLM-4.5-Air-FP8 prod=1.25e-07 committed=1.25e-07 MATCH GLM-5.2 prod=4.018e-07 committed=4.018e-07 MATCH gpt-oss-120b prod=3.9e-08 committed=3.9e-08 MATCH ``` Both cost-map files were edited by **text splice** rather than a `json.dump` rewrite, so every other entry is byte-identical — the diff is 255 pure insertions per file, zero deletions. Validated against `model_prices_and_context_window.schema.json` (0 errors). ## Live verification from this branch Against prod `https://api.flex.ai/v1`: ``` completion() -> HTTP 200 model=flexai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash tokens=11/2 cost=$0.0000013440 (= 11 x 8.96e-08 + 2 x 1.792e-07, so the cost-map lookup resolves) max_completion_tokens accepted -> yes (no param_mappings needed) responses() -> HTTP 200 ``` ## Checks run - `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/test_flexai_provider.py -q` → **18 passed** - `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/openai_like/ tests/litellm/llms/openai_like/ -q` → **148 passed, 5 skipped** - `python tests/code_coverage_tests/check_provider_folders_documented.py` → passes (`All 27 openai_like providers are documented`) - `python tests/code_coverage_tests/check_get_model_cost_key_performance.py` → passes - `jsonschema` validation of the new entries against `model_prices_and_context_window.schema.json` → 0 errors - `ruff check` on each changed source file → finding count unchanged vs `HEAD` (`constants.py` 201→201, `get_llm_provider_logic.py` 15→15); the new test file has the same 4 findings as the existing `test_pinstripes_provider.py` baseline, and `ruff.toml` excludes `tests/*` from lint ## Two notes for the reviewer **1. The packaged backup copy.** `litellm/model_prices_and_context_window_backup.json` is what `GetModelCostMap.load_local_model_cost_map()` reads, so a provider whose entries land only in the root file gets `"This model isn't mapped yet"` whenever the remote map is unavailable or `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. I hit exactly that, so both files are updated, and `test_flexai_entries_match_packaged_backup` asserts they stay in sync. Happy to drop that test if the backup is meant to be regenerated by tooling instead. **2. Non-chat models are priced but not yet routable.** 5 of the 21 entries are `embedding` / `image_generation` / `audio_transcription` / `audio_speech` for models FlexAI serves. JSON-configured providers currently route only chat completions (`JSONProviderRegistry.exists()` is consulted in `completion()`) and the Responses API, so `provider_endpoints_support.json` honestly declares those endpoints `false`. Their *pricing* is nonetheless correct and calculator-verified — per Greptile's catch, they use the fields the generic calculators actually read (`input_cost_per_image`, `input_cost_per_character`), with tests exercising both calculators. Glad to trim them to chat-only if you'd rather the cost map track routable endpoints exactly. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests — 18 unit tests, all passing - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on the touched paths (`148 passed, 5 skipped` across both `openai_like` test dirs) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] Bot reviews addressed — Greptile's P2 (non-chat pricing fields) and veria-ai's credential-precedence finding are both fixed, each with regression tests 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_013jmFw7fcJTtdTgmkKJa5yr

signals.title: chore(typing): clear basedpyright reportAny errors in proxy, router, and main completion paths
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The 8 files with the most basedpyright reportAny/reportExplicitAny errors carry weak typing - Weak typing hides real bugs and blocks stricter type checking later How it solves it: - Replaces Any-typed dicts and callbacks with TypedDicts, Pydantic TypeAdapter validation, or concrete types - Leaves genuinely heterogeneous boundaries (Prisma rows, dynamically loaded callables) as Any on purpose ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is a typing-only change with no runtime behavior difference, so there is nothing to demonstrate against a live proxy; the verifiable artifact is the whole-tree basedpyright diagnostic count, checked with `basedpyright --outputjson` against the full repo before and after. reportAny: 19292 to 18952 (-340) reportExplicitAny: 6518 to 6422 (-96) Every other basedpyright rule stayed at or below its baseline count repo-wide; several improved as a side effect: reportUnknownArgumentType -8, reportUnknownVariableType -16, reportUnknownMemberType -16. Existing tests were run rather than pytest output pasted here as proof, since this PR's premise is behavior-preservation, not a new capability: the full mapped test suite for every touched file (`tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_litellm_logging.py`, `test_streaming_handler.py`, `tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_llm_http_handler.py`, `tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_lazy_openapi_snapshot.py`, `test_proxy_utils.py`, `test_proxy_server.py`, `tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator.py` and its two sibling files, `tests/test_litellm/test_router.py`) passes: 854 passed, 0 failed (one pre-existing, unrelated failure in `test_main.py::test_openai_env_base` reproduces identically on an unmodified checkout and was excluded). ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes Touches the 8 files with the largest combined reportAny/reportExplicitAny count under `litellm/`: `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py`, `litellm/proxy/utils.py`, `litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py`, `litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py`, `litellm/litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py`, `litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py`, `litellm/main.py`, and `litellm/router.py`, plus a small follow-on fix in `litellm/proxy/_lazy_openapi_snapshot.py` needed to keep that file's own diagnostics from regressing. Representative fixes: `_init_custom_logger_compatible_class`'s `custom_logger_init_args` and several OpenAPI-schema helpers now carry real `JsonValue`/`TypedDict` shapes instead of `Any`; presigned-batch-request dispatch in `llm_http_handler.py` validates its request dict with a Pydantic `TypeAdapter` instead of `cast()`; several previously-Any callback lists and guardrail hooks are now typed against `CustomLogger`/`CustomGuardrail`. A handful of `dict`/`list` annotations that are genuinely mutated in place (accumulators, parsed JSON payloads, provider config dicts) are marked `# mutable-ok` with a one-line reason per the repo's functional-typing convention, since converting them to immutable structures was out of scope for a pure typing pass. Several narrower typings that looked correct in isolation turned out to ripple into other rules once verified against the full repo (a parameter typed against a class whose own base is only partially typed, for instance, turns a silent `Any` into a loud `reportUnknownMemberType` everywhere that parameter's methods get called): those were kept at `Any` rather than forced through, so the net change across every rule is zero or negative, never positive, anywhere in the tree. ## QA runbook ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_011mLr6TWpwQKxf5mj5GsEan)_

signals.title: fix(bedrock): strip client_metadata from converse additionalModelRequestFields
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Codex sends `client_metadata`, Bedrock Converse rejects the call - `drop_params` never removed it, so the route was unusable - Anthropic and Vertex were already fixed in #29489 How it solves it: - Drop `client_metadata` from `additionalModelRequestFields` in Converse - Regression test asserts real passthrough fields still survive ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5232 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Codex is the only client that sends `client_metadata`, so the failure only shows up on Codex -> proxy -> Bedrock. Converse forwards anything it doesn't recognize as `additionalModelRequestFields`, Bedrock hands that to the model verbatim, and Anthropic answers with `client_metadata: Extra inputs are not permitted` Proxy config used for both runs: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-opus-4-8 litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 aws_region_name: us-west-2 litellm_settings: drop_params: true ``` Same curl for both runs, the exact body Codex sends: ```bash curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ -d '{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","input":"say hi","max_output_tokens":16,"client_metadata":{"originator":"codex_cli_rs"}}' ``` Before, at 0659738b3e, the request the proxy builds for Bedrock (from `--detailed_debug`, `drop_params: true` active and not helping): ``` -d '{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "say hi"}]}], "inferenceConfig": {"maxTokens": 16}, "additionalModelRequestFields": {"client_metadata": {"originator": "codex_cli_rs"}}}' ``` After, at cdac5fde0e, same curl, no passthrough field left for Bedrock to reject: ``` -d '{"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"text": "say hi"}]}], "inferenceConfig": {"maxTokens": 16}}' ``` Both runs stopped at Bedrock auth: the AWS credentials I have access to are no longer authorized for `bedrock:InvokeModel` on this account, so I could not get a paid 200 back. The before/after difference is in the request LiteLLM signs and sends, which is exactly the field Bedrock was rejecting, so someone with working Bedrock credentials can confirm the 200 in a minute Until a release ships, `additional_drop_params: ["client_metadata"]` on the model works as a config-only workaround, and it stays a valid escape hatch afterwards ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `AmazonConverseConfig._prepare_request_params` drops `client_metadata` next to where it already drops `parallel_tool_calls`, so it never reaches `additionalModelRequestFields`. `AnthropicConfig.transform_request` does the same thing for the direct Anthropic, Vertex, and Bedrock invoke paths, this closes the one remaining hole Note that `drop_params` is the wrong lever here and always was: it only governs known OpenAI params a provider does not support, while `client_metadata` is not an OpenAI param, so it flows through the provider-specific passthrough instead ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/e57cd0ce775749e595f7da41d0795378
