signals.title: feat(ui): configure the auto router's heuristic scorer from the Admin UI
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Scorer thresholds were config.yaml only, unreachable from the Admin UI - Tuning when the router escalates meant a hand edit plus a restart - The classification panel hardcoded the tier ranges it displayed How it solves it: - Adds an Advanced scoring panel for boundaries, thresholds and weights - Shows it only when the scorer actually runs - The panel's stated ranges now read the configured values ## User Flow Before: an operator who wants short prompts to stop landing in the cheapest tier finds no control for it in the UI, so the router can only be tuned by hand 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints and click Add Auto Router 2. They choose Auto Router, fill the four tier pools, then open Detailed Configuration 3. Under Classification Method they select Heuristic scoring; the only scoring control offered is Custom Technical Keywords 4. The How Classification Works card states the tiers begin at 0.15, 0.35 and 0.60, with nothing on the page able to change any of the three 5. They save, then click Test Routing and send `hi`, which comes back classified Simple 6. To move that threshold they have to edit config.yaml on the proxy host and restart it, which no amount of clicking in the UI can substitute for After: the same operator sets the thresholds in the form, watches the classification change before saving, and can hand the router back to the shipped defaults later 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints and click Add Auto Router 2. They choose Auto Router, fill the four tier pools, then open Detailed Configuration 3. Under Classification Method they select Heuristic scoring, and now also see an Advanced scoring section 4. They expand Advanced scoring and get three groups: Tier boundaries, Token thresholds, and Dimension weights with a slider and a number for each of the seven dimensions, every one prefilled with the value the router uses today 5. They lower the tier boundaries, and the How Classification Works card immediately restates its ranges using the numbers they just typed 6. They click Test Routing and send the same `hi`, which now comes back classified Reasoning rather than Simple, so the change is visible before anything is saved 7. They save, reopen the router from the models page, and Advanced scoring is prefilled with what they saved, with a badge on the collapsed header counting the groups they overrode 8. On a group they never touched, nothing is written at all, so that group keeps following the shipped defaults instead of freezing at the numbers displayed when they happened to open the form 9. Clicking Reset to defaults on a group and saving hands that group back to the shipped behaviour The section is offered whenever the scorer can run, so an LLM classifier that falls back to the heuristic gets it too. An LLM classifier that falls back to the default model never scores anything, so it does not. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Rig: proxy from this branch on `127.0.0.1:4610` against its own Postgres database, Admin UI dev server on `:3000`. Both direct provider keys in `.env` are out of credit (Anthropic returns `credit balance is too low`, OpenAI returns `no credits remaining`), so the tier pools point at an OpenAI-compatible gateway upstream instead. The calls below are real HTTP over the network and real spend, not mocks. Before, at merge base `d0a815d2e1`. This is the config the create form is able to build there, since it has no control that can emit a scoring key. Same prompt in both legs: ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4610/auto_router/test_routing \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"hi","default_model":"t-anth-haiku","complexity_router_config":{ "tiers":{"SIMPLE":["t-anth-haiku"],"MEDIUM":["t-oai-mini"],"COMPLEX":["t-anth-bedrock"],"REASONING":["t-anth-bedrock"]}, "classifier_type":"heuristic","session_affinity":false,"deployment_affinity":true, "escalation_keywords":["LITELLM ESCALATE"]}}' { "tier": "SIMPLE", "score": -0.15, "routed_model": "t-anth-haiku", "tier_boundaries": {"simple_medium": 0.15, "medium_complex": 0.35, "complex_reasoning": 0.6} } ``` After, at `22b8cedf98`, the same call with the boundaries the Advanced scoring panel can now set: ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4610/auto_router/test_routing \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"hi","default_model":"t-anth-haiku","complexity_router_config":{ "tiers":{"SIMPLE":["t-anth-haiku"],"MEDIUM":["t-oai-mini"],"COMPLEX":["t-anth-bedrock"],"REASONING":["t-anth-bedrock"]}, "classifier_type":"heuristic","session_affinity":false,"deployment_affinity":true, "escalation_keywords":["LITELLM ESCALATE"], "tier_boundaries":{"simple_medium":-1.0,"medium_complex":-0.9,"complex_reasoning":-0.8}}}' { "tier": "REASONING", "score": -0.15, "routed_model": "t-anth-bedrock", "tier_boundaries": {"simple_medium": -1.0, "medium_complex": -0.9, "complex_reasoning": -0.8} } ``` The score is identical in both legs, so the boundaries are the only thing that moved the decision. Note that `hi` scores below zero, which is why the boundary fields accept negative values. The same two configs saved as routers, then billed for real: ``` for r in gw-A-default gw-B-tuned; do curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4610/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"$r\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],\"max_tokens\":8}" done gw-A-default -> served by claude-haiku-4-5 | id chatcmpl-fd6ddca4-bf46-4 gw-B-tuned -> served by us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 | id chatcmpl-c853e356-232d-4 ``` Round trip through create, reopen and reset: ``` ### 1. create the router with Advanced scoring filled in POST /model/new -> HTTP 200 ### 2. reopen the edit modal: GET /v1/model/info returns what it prefills {"tier_boundaries": {"simple_medium": 0.22, "medium_complex": 0.44, "complex_reasoning": 0.66}, "token_thresholds": {"simple": 25, "complex": 900}, "dimension_weights": {"tokenCount": 0.05, "codePresence": 0.5, "technicalTerms": 0.15, "reasoningMarkers": 0.2, "simpleIndicators": 0.05, "multiStepPatterns": 0.03, "questionComplexity": 0.02}} ### 3. save again after clicking Reset to defaults on all three groups PATCH /model/02d8c15c-87be-4688-8dfb-62a86fee440c/update -> HTTP 200 {"tier_boundaries": "ABSENT", "token_thresholds": "ABSENT", "dimension_weights": "ABSENT"} ``` Also in this branch, two things the first review round raised: - The dashboard keeps its own copy of the three default sets to prefill the controls. Nothing caught drift from `complexity_router/config.py`, so `TestDashboardScorerDefaultsParity` now pins both copies and the dimension key set. Drifting a value locally fails it. - Boundaries that decrease are now a prominent error rather than amber body text. Saving stays allowed on purpose: a router written that way in `config.yaml` would otherwise be uneditable here for every unrelated change. One unrelated fix rides along, because this PR is what surfaced it. `add_auto_router_tab.test.tsx` has two default-model-pin cases that were already failing on `litellm_internal_staging`: the pinned model is appended after every model the presets contribute, that list has reached 11, and the option fell outside the virtualized dropdown's rendered slice. CI only runs those cases when this file is touched, so nothing caught it. Reverting this branch's diff reproduces both failures at the merge base, and the fix searches the picker instead of trusting option order. It is a separate commit. Step 3 is the case worth calling out. These three keys are now rebuilt from the form on every save rather than carried through from what was stored, which is what makes Reset actually reset. It also makes the prefill in step 2 load bearing, so an absent knob prefills as unset rather than as a copy of the defaults; otherwise an operator who opened the modal and saved without touching scoring would silently pin their router to whatever the defaults happened to be that day. Screenshots to follow. --- > [!NOTE] > [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit cc9ef9204b9ba528a31ee68e02e9dc1c0f0ade38. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

signals.title: fix(batches): price a retrieved batch from its deployment's model and rates (internal copy of #37077)
signals.text: Internal copy of #37077 by @marty-sullivan (head 74ce9bbf73), whose org-owned fork blocks maintainer pushes. All 8 commits are cherry-picked with authorship preserved, plus follow-up commits from review and QA: a fix for an in-place mutation of `get_model_info`'s lru-cached dict, a merge absorbing #37078 and #37205 from staging, and a fix making the enterprise cost poller price from the same deployment rates as the retrieve path ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Retrieving a batch prices it with no model identity - Bedrock batches silently cost $0 with correct tokens - A deployment's own configured rates are ignored - A zero-cost deployment gets billed the public rate - The enterprise cost poller ignored deployment rates too How it solves it: - Price against the deployment's own provider-qualified model - Honor rates the deployment actually declares - Merge published rates onto a copy, never the cached entry - The poller prices through the same shared helper ## User Flow Before: a team running Bedrock batch jobs sees completed batches under-billed: $0.00 on gateways without background batch cost tracking, and a deployment's own configured rates ignored on gateways with it 1. They upload a JSONL file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files (`purpose: batch`, `target_model_names: claude-haiku-4-5`) and get back a gateway file id 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with that `input_file_id` and get back a batch id with `status: validating` 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it returns `status: completed` 4. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs: without background batch cost tracking the batch's entry shows real tokens against $0.00 spend, and with it the entry is priced at the model's public batch rate 5. A team whose gateway administrator configured custom batch rates on a deployment is billed the public rate either way: 0.00242 instead of 0.0052 in the live run below After: the same batch reports the spend those tokens actually cost, at the rates the deployment declares 1. They upload the same JSONL file with POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files and get back a gateway file id 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches and get back a batch id with `status: validating` 3. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} until it returns `status: completed` 4. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows exactly one spend entry for the batch with the same tokens priced at the model's published batch rate 5. The custom-rate deployment's batch is billed exactly the rates declared on that deployment: 0.0052 in the live run below ## Relevant issues Follows #36876 and #37050, which made a batch cost row reach the spend logs at all. With rows now landing, their amounts became auditable, which is how this surfaced ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5666 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Fresh end-to-end run against real Bedrock managed batches at the merged tip, with the enterprise cost poller active (`PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=30`), which is the production-realistic accountant. Before at the current staging base 3f4810b8f2, After at 5a11fe141e (the tip differs from it only by a test-only commit). A broader 23-deployment run of the inline retrieve path (Bedrock + Vertex + zero-cost Vertex) is preserved in #37077's description Shared setup. Two deployments of `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`: `haiku-batch-std` with no custom pricing and `haiku-batch-custom` declaring `input_cost_per_token_batches: 2.0e-06` and `output_cost_per_token_batches: 4.0e-06`. `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`, fresh database per side. One real 100-record batch per deployment: ``` curl -s http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -F purpose=batch -F target_model_names="haiku-batch-std" -F file=@in_std.jsonl curl -s http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"input_file_id":"<unified id>","endpoint":"/v1/chat/completions","completion_window":"24h"}' curl -s http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/batches/<batch id> -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" # poll to completed psql -c 'SELECT model, call_type, spend, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs";' ``` ### Before (3f4810b8f2) 1. Both real Bedrock jobs completed in ~10 minutes; the poller then wrote one `aretrieve_batch` row per batch ``` <std batch id>_batch_cost us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5... aretrieve_batch 0.00242 1400 600 <custom batch id>_batch_cost us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5... aretrieve_batch 0.00242 1400 600 ``` 2. Both rows price at the public batch rate. The custom deployment's declared rates are ignored: it books 0.00242 instead of 1400 x 2.0e-06 + 600 x 4.0e-06 = 0.0052 3. The retrieve path itself still cannot price at all: every client `GET /v1/batches/{id}` logs `response_cost_failure` with "Model is None" (19 occurrences across the two batches), so a proxy without the enterprise poller books $0. The total blackout this causes on the older base, where batches got no priced row at all, is the 973329e986 run in #37077's description ### After (5a11fe141e) 1. Same flow, same tokens; the poller writes exactly one row per batch ``` <std batch id>_batch_cost us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5... aretrieve_batch 0.00242 1400 600 <custom batch id>_batch_cost us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5... aretrieve_batch 0.005200000000000001 1400 600 ``` 2. The std row matches the published batch rate exactly: 1400 x 0.55e-06 + 600 x 2.75e-06 = 0.00242 (the 1.1x `us.` profile rates halved), relative error 1.8e-16 3. The custom row matches the deployment's declared batch rates exactly: 1400 x 2.0e-06 + 600 x 4.0e-06 = 0.0052, relative error 1.7e-16, where the published rates would have given 0.00242 4. Accounting ownership is clean: ~11 client GETs per batch wrote no extra rows (`batch_ignore_default_logging` on the retrieve path), and the spend transactions carry the `LiteLLM Proxy/CheckBatchCost` user agent ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes Retrieving a completed batch computed its cost with no model identity: the call that aggregates a batch's output passed neither the deployment's model nor its pricing For Bedrock that mattered because the cost model then fell back to the provider's own response model, a bare name like `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`, which does not resolve under a bedrock provider prefix. The lookup missed, and a missed lookup returns zero rather than raising, so cost became $0 while usage stayed correct Dropping the deployment's model info mattered independently: rates configured on a deployment are registered by the router under that deployment's id, and never consulting them meant a deployment configured to cost nothing was billed from the global map instead. Standard deployments were unaffected, since their configured rates and the global map agree, which is why this only showed up on Bedrock and on custom-rate deployments Both are fixed at the one call site, by passing the deployment's model and the pricing registered for it. Two details are worth calling out because the obvious implementations of each are wrong: The model comes from `model_call_details`. On this path `self.model` and `litellm_params["model"]` are both None, and `self.model` can otherwise hold the router's `model_group` alias, which no cost map resolves; a live retrieve confirmed `model_call_details` is the only one of the three carrying the provider-qualified deployment model Deployment pricing is decided from the raw registration rather than `get_model_info`. The router registers an entry for every deployment whether or not it declares pricing, and `get_model_info` fills absent costs with 0, so asking it cannot tell "configured as free" apart from "no pricing configured" and would have priced every ordinary deployment's batches at $0. The shared helper therefore returns pricing only when the deployment actually declares one of the batch cost fields, leaving the global map as the default. Ownership is per token direction: the side a deployment leaves unset keeps the published rates, and a declared side is never displaced by them On top of the original PR, this copy merges the published rates onto a copy of `get_model_info`'s return value. That function serves every call from one lru-cached dict, so writing the merge into it poisoned every later `get_model_info` lookup of the deployment id with the published model's rates for the life of the process; the new regression test fails on the in-place version This copy also extends the fix to the enterprise cost poller. #37050 hands accounting ownership to `CheckBatchCost` whenever it is active (`poller_owns_accounting`), but the poller priced from `deployment_info.model_info.model_dump()`, which never carries `litellm_params` pricing, so a custom-rate deployment's batches would have been billed at the public rate on exactly the path that now owns them. The deployment-pricing merge is extracted to a module-level `deployment_pricing_model_info` and the poller calls it with the same deployment id and provider-qualified model as the retrieve path; a regression test asserts the poller passes the declared batch rates through to `calculate_batch_cost_and_usage` One behavior change worth naming: with a model name now reaching this path, a proxy that sets `disable_vertex_batch_output_transformation` will take the Vertex-specific accounting branch on retrieve, which it previously could not reach. That branch exists for exactly that flag, so this makes the flag work on the retrieve path rather than changing what it means ## Caveats - Bedrock InvokeModel usage shapes beyond Anthropic's remain unparsed - They warn and bill $0; parsing them is follow-up work ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: feat(shadow-eval): name the shadowed key in job responses and the UI headline
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Shadow eval cards never say whose traffic they sample - Job responses carry only a 64-char key hash How it solves it: - Responses resolve the hash to key alias and masked name - Card reads "Shadowing X% of \ traffic via \" ## User Flow Before: an admin running shadow evals over several keys cannot tell which key each job samples 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization and the active card says "Shadowing 25% via auto_router1" 2. With two jobs on two different keys, both cards name only the router, so the cards are indistinguishable 3. They send GET http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval and each job carries only `"api_key_id": "64c87d65f785..."`, a hash they must cross-reference against the key list by hand After: every job names the key it samples, on the card and over the API 1. They open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization and the active card says "Shadowing 25% of `prod-batch-alpha` traffic via `auto_router1`" 2. With two jobs on two different keys, each card names its own key; a reverse job reads "Comparing `auto_router1` to `gpt-5` on 10% of `prod-batch-alpha` traffic" 3. They send GET http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval and each job carries `"key_alias": "prod-batch-alpha"` and `"key_name": "sk-...ghYg"` next to the hash; a key with no alias falls back to its masked name, and a deleted key returns null for both while the card falls back to the shortened hash ## Relevant issues ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` [https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code] - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Backend: `ShadowEvalJobResponse` gains nullable `key_alias` and `key_name`, resolved from the key row at read time. The start endpoint reads them off the key row it already fetched for validation; list, detail, and stop resolve through one batched `find_many` over the distinct hashes, so the list path adds a single query rather than one per job. Deleted keys resolve to null UI: the shadow eval card headline names the shadowed key in both directions, falling back from alias to masked key name to a shortened hash. `schema.d.ts` regenerated via `npm run gen:api` Heads up: open PR #36871 moves `api_key_id` into a per-job keys list; these labels rebase onto it as per-key fields ## Proof of fix Live proxy on localhost:4000 backed by a fresh Postgres database, an auto-router (`auto_router1`), and the local stub provider. Same commands at the merge base and at this PR's head Before, at merge base c1fc5983ca, the list response has no key fields: ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" [{"job_id": "cmsxrq5sy0000mgpb0s5hdnqn", "api_key_id": "64c87d65f78523d2d20f1d607ed6a773455a9604c6269b725b4914fa1c20d6e8", "router_name": "auto_router1", "direction": "forward", ...}] ``` After, at this branch, create an aliased key and start a job on it: ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key_alias": "prod-batch-alpha"}' {"token_id": "64c87d65f785...", "key_alias": "prod-batch-alpha", ...} $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"api_key_id": "64c87d65f78523d2d20f1d607ed6a773455a9604c6269b725b4914fa1c20d6e8", "router_name": "auto_router1", "shadow_percentage": 25, "judge_model": "gpt-5-mini", "duration_days": 7, "max_turns": 100}' {"job_id": "cmsxrq5sy0000mgpb0s5hdnqn", "api_key_id": "64c87d65f785...", "key_alias": "prod-batch-alpha", "key_name": "sk-...ghYg", "router_name": "auto_router1", "shadow_percentage": 25.0, "status": "running", ...} ``` List and detail both resolve the labels, and the fallbacks hold: a job on a key generated without an alias reports `"key_alias": null, "key_name": "sk-...EY4A"`, and after `POST /key/delete` on that key the same job lists `"key_alias": null, "key_name": null`: ``` $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" [{"job_id": "cmsxrqngf0001...", "key_alias": null, "key_name": null, "router_name": "auto_router1", "shadow_percentage": 10.0, "status": "running", ...}, {"job_id": "cmsxrq5sy0000...", "key_alias": "prod-batch-alpha", "key_name": "sk-...ghYg", "router_name": "auto_router1", "shadow_percentage": 25.0, "status": "running", ...}] $ curl -s http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/cmsxrq5sy0000mgpb0s5hdnqn -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" {"job_id": "cmsxrq5sy0000...", "key_alias": "prod-batch-alpha", "key_name": "sk-...ghYg", "judged_count": 0, "status": "running", ...} ``` UI screenshots of the card headline to follow in a comment (http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=cost-optimization with the job above running)

signals.title: feat(black_forest_labs): add FLUX 3 video generation
signals.text: Adds `black_forest_labs/flux-3-video` to the video provider surface. Black Forest Labs was already supported for images and edits, but not video. Supports text-to-video, image-to-video, continuation, draft mode, keyframes, duration, resolution, aspect ratio, and audio, and maps the provider's `Reasoning`, `Generating`, and `Ready` states onto LiteLLM's. Black Forest Labs returns a regional `polling_url` per request, for example `api.us7.bfl.ai`, so the transformation follows the returned URL and validates it against the provider domain to permit regional subdomains without opening an SSRF path. The registry entry uses the text-to-video HD rate of $0.17/s. The provider bills six different per-second rates depending on mode and resolution, and the remaining five are recorded in the entry metadata. Tests: 40 provider tests pass, and 101 pass across the existing image and edit suites together with the new video tests. Mutation testing killed 6 of 6 mutants, covering image-to-video misrouting, the HD/FHD boundary, the duration clamp, draft mode prompt handling, progress scaling, and polling URL validation. Verified end to end against the live API rather than mocks: a request submitted through LiteLLM progressed through the real status sequence, returned 30 credits of usage, and downloaded a 6,737,943 byte file that `ffprobe` reports as H.264/AAC, 1280x704, 5.041667s.

signals.title: feat(guardrails): track bedrock guardrail usage units per invocation
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - AWS bills Bedrock guardrail units per request, LiteLLM drops them - Default spend log redaction erases the counters entirely - Blocked requests never reach guardrail usage metrics How it solves it: - Spend logs carry a redaction-proof `guardrail_usage` counter block - New daily table aggregates units by guardrail, date, team, key - `/guardrails/usage` endpoints expose totals and per day/team/key breakdowns - Blocked requests now keep their guardrail info and get counted ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin running Bedrock guardrails pays AWS for guardrail units on every request but can see none of that in LiteLLM, and blocked requests are missing from guardrail metrics entirely 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a benign prompt through a Bedrock-guarded model and get a normal 200 completion 2. They send the same POST with a prompt that violates the guardrail policy and get HTTP 400 "Violated guardrail policy", and AWS charges guardrail units for both invocations 3. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=... for each request: the blocked one has an empty guardrail section, and the passed one shows only "REDACTED_BY_LITELM" with no unit numbers unless prompt storage is switched on 4. They open GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/overview and see request counts only, with the blocked request missing (totalBlocked 0, passRate 100.0) and no unit fields anywhere 5. GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/detail/{guardrail_id} has no unit data either, so the AWS guardrail bill cannot be reconciled per team or key After: the same two requests produce unit counters in the spend logs and aggregated totals on the usage endpoints, blocked call included 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a benign prompt through a Bedrock-guarded model and get a normal 200 completion 2. They send the same POST with a prompt that violates the guardrail policy and get HTTP 400 "Violated guardrail policy", and AWS charges guardrail units for both invocations 3. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=... for each request: both entries, the blocked one included, now carry a `guardrail_usage` object with the AWS counters (topicPolicyUnits, contentPolicyUnits, and the rest) while the guardrail response itself stays redacted 4. GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/overview now returns `usageUnits` on each guardrail row plus a `totalUsageUnits` rollup, and the blocked request is counted (totalBlocked 1) 5. Re-read the first case's spend row for the two fields side by side ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:45365/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-f3474fec-a9f1-4301-bd78-ada4173c4859" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | jq '.[0].metadata.guardrail_information[0] | {guardrail_response, guardrail_usage}' ``` ```json { "guardrail_response": "REDACTED_BY_LITELM", "guardrail_usage": {"topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0} } ``` The raw blob stays redacted while the counters survive as their own field, exactly the constraint the customer setup needs QA observations (none blocks the verdict): - /v1/messages, /v1/responses spend rows use minted chatcmpl ids (pre-existing, unchanged) - usage/logs model mixes alias and upstream id (pre-existing derivation, newly visible) - Overview flags "critical" at 20% failRate on five requests (pre-existing thresholds) - "REDACTED_BY_LITELM" sentinel typo, missing an L (pre-existing, unchanged) - usage/logs reason blob truncates mid-JSON (pre-existing, now redacted anyway) ## Type 🆕 New Feature 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - No unit-to-cost conversion yet, pricing lands in LIT-5651 - Dashboard UI for the new fields lands in LIT-5652 - Zero counters stay in spend logs, skipped in daily aggregates - Aggregates use empty strings, not NULLs, for keyless/teamless traffic - Aggregate rows still failing after 3 backoff retries are logged and dropped, like the sibling daily metrics rollup; the spend log row keeps the counters - Oversized inputs that Bedrock makes LiteLLM re-scan in chunks record only the blocking chunk's units when a later chunk blocks ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR - [x] 5437139b94 passes /live-pr-risk

signals.title: feat(complexity_router): operator-defined tier sets for the LLM classifier
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Auto-router tiers are hardcoded to SIMPLE/MEDIUM/COMPLEX/REASONING - Operators cannot add, remove, or define their own tiers - Extra `tiers` keys are silently accepted and never routable How it solves it: - `tier_definitions` lets operators replace the tier set entirely - Each tier's definition becomes its bullet in the classifier rubric - Built-in tier names may omit the definition and inherit it - Classifier reply schema is built from the defined names - Heuristic scorer is locked out: custom sets require the LLM classifier - `fallback_tier` names where requests land when the classifier fails - Ladder-dependent features (escalation, adaptive, session affinity) rejected at write ## User Flow Before: an operator who wants a SECURITY_REVIEW tier on their auto-router configures it and watches every security request route elsewhere 1. They add `SECURITY_REVIEW: claude-sonnet-5` under `tiers` and a `tier_definitions` entry describing it in `complexity_router_config`, then restart the proxy, which boots without complaint 2. They send POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with model `my-auto-router` and a prompt asking for a security review of a SQL-injectable login handler 3. The response comes back from the COMPLEX tier's model; http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows the routing decision as `tier: COMPLEX`, and the SECURITY_REVIEW model has served zero requests 4. They try pointing a keyword rule at `SECURITY_REVIEW` and the deployment now refuses to load, naming the four built-in tiers as the only legal values After: the same config routes security prompts to the operator's own tier 1. They add the same `tiers` key, `tier_definitions` entry, and a `fallback_tier`, then restart the proxy 2. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions with the same security-review prompt 3. The response comes back from claude-sonnet-5, and http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs shows `tier: SECURITY_REVIEW` with cause `llm_classifier` 4. The keyword rule pointing at `SECURITY_REVIEW` is accepted and routes matching prompts there deterministically ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5214 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Rig: proxy on localhost:4471 backed by Postgres, all tier models and the classifier served through a live gateway upstream (real HTTP, real spend). One config used for both legs, so the diff is the only variable: ```yaml - model_name: my-auto-router litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_config: tiers: SIMPLE: tier-simple # claude-haiku-4-5 MEDIUM: tier-medium # claude-sonnet-4-5 COMPLEX: tier-complex # claude-opus-5 REASONING: tier-reasoning # claude-opus-4-8 SECURITY_REVIEW: tier-security # claude-sonnet-5 tier_definitions: - name: SIMPLE - name: MEDIUM - name: COMPLEX - name: REASONING - name: SECURITY_REVIEW description: requests asking for a security audit, vulnerability review, or exploit analysis of code or systems fallback_tier: MEDIUM classifier_type: llm classifier_llm_config: {model: classifier-model, timeout_ms: 30000} ``` A second router `my-auto-router-flaky` is identical except `timeout_ms: 1`, so its classifier always fails. ### Before (3f4810b8f2) #### /v1/chat/completions routes a security prompt to a built-in tier 1. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4471/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "my-auto-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Do a security review of this login handler and list every vulnerability: def login(u,p): q = \"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name=... + u ...\"; return db.exec(q)"}], "max_tokens": 40}'` 2. Spend log routing decision: `tier: COMPLEX`, `cause: llm_classifier`, served by `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-opus-5`. The `tier_definitions` and `fallback_tier` keys were silently swallowed and SECURITY_REVIEW is unreachable #### /v1/messages, same prompt shape 1. Same security-audit ask through `/v1/messages` 2. Routing decision: `tier: COMPLEX`, served by claude-opus-5 #### /v1/responses, same prompt shape 1. Same security-audit ask through `/v1/responses` 2. Routing decision: `tier: MEDIUM`, served by claude-sonnet-4-5 #### Classifier failure silently runs the heuristic scorer 1. `curl ... -d '{"model": "my-auto-router-flaky", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "audit this handler for vulnerabilities please"}], "max_tokens": 20}'` 2. Routing decision: `cause: heuristic_scorer`, `tier: SIMPLE`; the 1ms-timeout classifier failed and the local scorer decided instead ### After (ae7e562506) #### /v1/chat/completions routes the security prompt to the operator-defined tier 1. Same curl as Before 2. Spend log routing decision: `tier: SECURITY_REVIEW`, `cause: llm_classifier`, served by `bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5` #### /v1/messages, same prompt shape 1. Same curl as Before 2. Routing decision: `tier: SECURITY_REVIEW`, served by claude-sonnet-5 #### /v1/responses, same prompt shape 1. Same curl as Before 2. Routing decision: `tier: SECURITY_REVIEW`, served by claude-sonnet-5 #### Negative control: small talk still routes to a built-in tier 1. `curl ... -d '{"model": "my-auto-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi there, how are you today?"}], "max_tokens": 20}'` 2. Routing decision: `tier: SIMPLE`, served by claude-haiku-4-5 #### Classifier failure routes to fallback_tier, never the heuristic 1. Same flaky-router curl as Before 2. Routing decision: `cause: classifier_fallback`, `tier: MEDIUM`, `signals: ["classifier-fallback:MEDIUM"]`, served by claude-sonnet-4-5 #### Ladder-dependent features are rejected at config write 1. `curl -s -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:4471/model/new -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model_name": "bad-router", "litellm_params": {"model": "auto_router/complexity_router", "complexity_router_config": {..., "tier_definitions": [...], "session_affinity": true}}}'` 2. `400`: "complexity_router_config is invalid at complexity_router_config: Value error, session_affinity cannot be combined with tier_definitions: these features rely on the built-in tier severity order, which a custom tier set does not define" ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Rebuilt from scratch on current staging; supersedes #35915 - Dashboard form controls for tier_definitions are follow-up work - The edit modal carries the new keys through untouched ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit ae7e5625064a2bc212d18e201bb1cc469372c797. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: test(ui): settle the in-flight search before the loading tests end
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `ui-unit-tests` fails on staging while reporting every test passed - Two loading tests end with their mocked search still in flight - The late state update hits a torn-down window and rejects How it solves it: - Both tests now await the search settling before returning - Each keeps its original loading assertion unchanged - Nothing is left pending when the environment tears down ## User Flow Before: a developer watching CI on any dashboard change sees `ui-unit-tests` go red with nothing failing in it 1. They push a branch that touches a UI file and open a PR 2. `ui-unit-tests` reports `Test Files 663 passed`, `Tests 7351 passed`, then `Errors 1 error` 3. The job exits 1 on `ReferenceError: window is not defined`, pointing at a search-tools test that passed 4. They have no failing assertion to act on, so they re-run the job and hope the ordering shifts 5. Because the required check is red, the PR cannot merge After: the same push reports the same passing counts and the job succeeds 1. They push a branch that touches a UI file and open a PR 2. `ui-unit-tests` reports `Test Files 663 passed`, `Tests 7351 passed`, with no error line 3. The job exits 0 and the required check goes green 4. The PR is mergeable without re-running anything ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The observable artifact here is the CI job itself, since the change is confined to test files and alters no runtime behavior. ### Before (67635d832e, staging) 1. `gh run view 32075688331 --log-failed` ``` ⎯⎯⎯⎯ Unhandled Rejection ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ ReferenceError: window is not defined ❯ getCurrentEventPriority node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:10993:22 ❯ requestUpdateLane node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:25495:19 ❯ dispatchSetState node_modules/react-dom/cjs/react-dom.development.js:16648:14 ❯ handleSearch src/app/(dashboard)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.tsx:66:7 66| setIsLoading(false); This error originated in "src/app/(dashboard)/search-tools/_components/SearchToolTester.test.tsx" This error was caught after test environment was torn down. Test Files 663 passed (663) Tests 7351 passed (7351) Errors 1 error ``` 2. `gh run view 32075688331 --json conclusion --jq .conclusion` -> `failure` ### After (3cc16de0d2) 1. `CI=true npm run test -- --run --pool forks --poolOptions.forks.maxForks=14`, the same command the push job runs ``` Test Files 663 passed (663) Tests 7351 passed (7351) ``` 2. Exit code 0, with no `Unhandled` and no `window is not defined` anywhere in the output 3. `ui-unit-tests` on this PR is the equivalent run on CI's own Linux runner ## Type ✅ Test ## Caveats (if any) - The failure is intermittent; local runs on macOS never reproduced it - Diagnosis rests on the stack trace, not on a local red run - Only these two tests leave that promise unsettled at teardown

signals.title: fix(rate_limiter): attach priority rate limit headers on /v1/messages
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `/v1/messages` returned no priority rate limit headers - Its response is a dict, not `ModelResponse` - Both v3 hooks skipped dict responses entirely How it solves it: - Attach headers via `ensure_response_additional_headers`, which handles dicts - Drop the `isinstance(response, ModelResponse)` gate - Regression test covers the dict response shape ## User Flow Before: a developer on a premium key can read their priority rate limit budget on chat completions, but the same call against the Anthropic Messages route tells them nothing 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with their premium key and see `x-ratelimit-priority_model-limit-requests: 75`, `x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-requests: 74`, and `x-litellm-priority: premium` in the response headers 2. They send the same prompt to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same key 3. The response comes back 200 but carries only the upstream provider's `x-ratelimit-limit-requests` and `x-ratelimit-limit-tokens`, with no priority headers and no `x-litellm-priority`, so their client cannot tell how much of its reserved premium capacity is left After: the same Anthropic Messages call reports the priority budget too 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions and see the priority headers as before 2. They send the same prompt to POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the same key 3. The response now carries `x-ratelimit-priority_model-limit-requests`, `x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-requests`, `x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-*`, `x-litellm-priority: premium`, and `x-litellm-rate-limiter-version: v3`, matching what chat completions returns ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5691 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, a live proxy hitting the real Anthropic API with dynamic v3 priority limiting on: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: anthropic-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY rpm: 100 tpm: 100000 litellm_settings: callbacks: ["dynamic_rate_limiter_v3"] priority_reservation: premium: 0.75 standard: 0.25 ``` The key used below was minted with `curl -X POST localhost:4000/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"models": ["anthropic-haiku-4-5"], "metadata": {"priority": "premium"}}'` and exported as `$KEY` ### Before (67635d832e) #### /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":5}' | grep -iE "x-ratelimit|x-litellm-priority|rate-limiter"` 2. Output, priority headers present: ``` x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-remaining-requests: 99 x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-limit-requests: 100 x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-remaining-tokens: 100000 x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-limit-tokens: 100000 x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-requests: 74 x-ratelimit-priority_model-limit-requests: 75 x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 74999 x-ratelimit-priority_model-limit-tokens: 75000 x-litellm-priority: premium x-litellm-rate-limiter-version: v3 ``` #### /v1/messages 1. `curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST localhost:4000/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"anthropic-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"max_tokens":5}' | grep -iE "x-ratelimit|x-litellm-priority|rate-limiter"` 2. Output, only upstream headers, no priority ones: ``` x-ratelimit-remaining-tokens: 99962 x-ratelimit-limit-tokens: 100000 x-ratelimit-remaining-requests: 98 x-ratelimit-limit-requests: 100 ``` ### After (f899d2f1ec) #### /v1/chat/completions 1. Same curl as above 2. Output, unchanged: ``` x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-remaining-requests: 99 x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-limit-requests: 100 x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-remaining-tokens: 100000 x-ratelimit-model_saturation_check-limit-tokens: 100000 x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-requests: 74 x-ratelimit-priority_model-limit-requests: 75 x-ratelimit-priority_model-remaining-tokens: 74999 x-ratelimit-priority_model-limit-tokens: 75000 x-litellm-priority: premium x-litellm-rate-limiter-version: v3 ``` #### /v1/messages 1. signals.title: feat(complexity_router): plan-mode tier floor for coding-agent clients
signals.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Coding agents in plan mode get routed to cheap tiers - Plan-mode signals ride injected prompt text the router strips out - Operators cannot express "plan mode deserves a premium model" How it solves it: - New `plan_mode_min_tier` floor on the complexity router config - Detects Claude Code, Copilot, and Copilot CLI plan-mode sentinels - Floor raises tier, overrides cheap session pins, never lowers - Transient: exiting plan mode auto-routes again, pins untouched - Sentinel turns never pin and never take the default_model exit - Skips the classifier when the floor is the top tier ## User Flow Before: a developer planning a feature in Claude Code through an auto-router gets the cheapest model for the most important turn 1. The proxy admin adds `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX` to the auto-router config and restarts, and the unknown field is silently ignored 2. The developer opens Claude Code pointed at the gateway, presses shift+tab into plan mode, and asks "add a hello endpoint to my server" 3. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the injected "Plan mode is active" system message in the conversation 4. The response comes back from the SIMPLE tier model, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the routing decision as an ordinary heuristic route to the cheap model After: the same plan-mode turn is floored to the premium tier and labeled as such 1. The proxy admin adds `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX` to the auto-router config and restarts 2. The developer opens Claude Code pointed at the gateway, presses shift+tab into plan mode, and asks "add a hello endpoint to my server" 3. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the injected "Plan mode is active" system message in the conversation 4. The response comes back from the COMPLEX tier model, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the routing decision card reading "Plan-mode floor: "Plan mode is active"" 5. When the developer approves the plan and exits plan mode, the next turn classifies normally again instead of staying floored by the old reminder in history ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5643 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a live proxy on localhost:4213 with an auto-router whose tiers are SIMPLE/MEDIUM claude-haiku-4-5 and COMPLEX claude-sonnet-5, `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX`, `session_affinity: true`, and `return_raw_model_name: true` so the response `model` field names the routed deployment. Every provider credential on this machine is out of credit (OpenAI, Anthropic, and Azure all refuse with billing errors), so both tier models point their `api_base` at a local Anthropic-shaped upstream that echoes the requested model id; the routing decision under test happens entirely in the proxy before that hop. A re-run against live providers is owed and the config plus commands below reproduce it as-is by dropping the `api_base` override ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 - model_name: claude-sonnet-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 - model_name: plan-router litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_config: tiers: SIMPLE: claude-haiku-4-5 MEDIUM: claude-haiku-4-5 COMPLEX: claude-sonnet-5 plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX session_affinity: true return_raw_model_name: true ``` ### Before (68d4ba5da5) #### Plain request routes the cheap tier 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}], "max_tokens": 30}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5` #### Claude Code plan-mode shape on /v1/messages 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "system": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are Claude Code."}], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}]}, {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Plan mode is active. The user indicated that they do not want you to execute yet -- you MUST NOT make any edits."}]}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, so the plan-mode turn got the cheap model and the config field was silently ignored #### Copilot plan-mode shape on /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are an expert.
<modeInstructions>
You are currently running in "Plan" mode. Below are your instructions for this mode.
</modeInstructions>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5` ### After (bc52e9cb3d) #### Plain request routes the cheap tier 1. Same curl as Before 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, unchanged #### Claude Code plan-mode shape on /v1/messages 1. Same curl as Before 2. Response model: `claude-sonnet-5`, floored to the COMPLEX tier #### Copilot plan-mode shape on /v1/chat/completions 1. Same curl as Before 2. Response model: `claude-sonnet-5`, floored to the COMPLEX tier #### Exited plan mode no longer floors 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4213/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "plan the hello endpoint"}, {"role": "system", "content": "Plan mode is active. Do not execute."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Here is the plan."}, {"role": "user", "content": "looks good, implement it"}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, because the stale sentinel sits before the newest human ask #### Pinned session floors transiently and reverts on exit 1. Plain request with `"metadata": {"session_id": "qa-sess-1"}` routes and pins `claude-haiku-4-5` 2. Same session with the plan-mode system message appended: response model `claude-sonnet-5`, floored past the pin 3. Same session, next plain turn without the sentinel: response model `claude-haiku-4-5`, back on the session's own pin ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Proof of fix upstream was a local mock; real-provider re-run owed - Adaptive hard floor proven by unit tests; bandit state is not reachable via curl - plugin-filtered-pool signal now checks plugins: only this PR's floored-failure path reaches it without them - Sentinels are client-owned strings that drift with client releases - `plan_mode_patterns` exists so operators can patch drift without upgrading - Sentinels are spoofable by callers; spends up only, within configured pools - Create/edit auto-router UI for the new field is a follow-up - /v1/responses surface not exercised in QA ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit bc52e9cb3d5ae25a6d2848c522240bf7fb260738. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signals.title: fix(shadow_eval): copy messages before router call and raise judge output cap
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Shadow eval turns die with "'tuple' object does not support item assignment" - Long comparisons die with "unparseable judge verdict" at char 0 - Error rows never say where in the stack the shadow call failed How it solves it: - Shadow router call gets a fresh mutable copy of the messages - Judge output cap raised from 500 to 1500 tokens - Shadow call failures lead with exception class and raising code line - Regression test pins that a failed turn never stalls later ones ## User Flow Before: an admin shadow-evaluating an auto-router watches turns burn as error rows instead of verdicts 1. They start a shadow eval on their key via POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start 2. They keep sending their normal traffic, e.g. POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages with tool results and cached system blocks 3. On the dashboard's Auto-Router Shadow Evals tab the banner reads "Last failure: shadow router call failed: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment" and the judged count stalls 4. On long conversations the banner instead reads "Last failure: unparseable judge verdict: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)" because the judge ran out of output room before finishing its verdict After: the same traffic produces judged verdicts 1. They start the same shadow eval via POST http://localhost:4000/auto_router/shadow_eval/start 2. They send the same POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages traffic 3. The dashboard shows the turn as a judged verdict (win, loss, or tie) instead of a failure banner 4. Long conversations get complete verdicts, and if a shadow call ever does fail, the banner names the exception class and the code line that raised it ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: `/tmp/shadowfix_config.yaml` defines `claude-main` (bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0, live AWS Bedrock) and auto-router `tin-shadow-router` whose tiers all point at it. The tuple failure needs production traffic shapes to trigger on demand, so Before is read from a live deployment running the merge-base code ### Before (6a0bd0dffb) #### Shadow call survives in-place message rewrites 1. `select outcome, error from "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalAttempt" where outcome = 'error' order by created_at desc limit 1` 2. Observed: `error | shadow router call failed: 'tuple' object does not support item assignment`, the turn consumed budget and produced no verdict #### Judge verdict fits the output cap 1. `select outcome, judge_cost, error from "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalAttempt" where error like 'unparseable%' limit 1` 2. Observed: `error | 0.008454 | unparseable judge verdict: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)` 3. `select model, completion_tokens, spend from "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" where request_id = 'chatcmpl-75d913f3-ed3a-40f5-89f2-7b5a44b73ef9'` 4. Observed: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 | 500 | 0.008454`, exactly the old 500 token cap and the same spend as the errored attempt's judge_cost, so the verdict was truncated mid-generation ### After (790c209d30) #### Shadow call survives in-place message rewrites 1. `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config /tmp/shadowfix_config.yaml --port 4020 --use_v2_migration_resolver` 2. `curl -X POST http://localhost:4020/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -d '{"key_alias": "shadowfix-proof"}'` returned token_id `c7a6ac...c2ac0` 3. `curl -X POST http://localhost:4020/auto_router/shadow_eval/start -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -d '{"api_key_id": "c7a6ac...c2ac0", "router_name": "tin-shadow-router", "shadow_percentage": 100.0, "judge_model": "claude-main", "duration_days": 1}'` returned job `cmsxtxj9p0000mgjr8275sv5h` 4. `curl -X POST http://localhost:4020/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"` with an agentic-shaped body: system blocks with `cache_control`, a `tools` array, an assistant `tool_use` turn, and a `tool_result` block; Bedrock answered `stop_reason: end_turn`, "The config.yaml file specifies that the application runs on port 4000 and uses the Claude model." 5. `select outcome, tier, real_model, shadow_model, confidence, judge_cost, error from "LiteLLM_ShadowEvalAttempt" order by created_at desc limit 1` 6. Observed: `tie | SIMPLE | bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 | us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 | 0.99 | 0.0006204 | (null)`, the turn was shadowed through the router and judged with no error row #### Judge verdict fits the output cap 1. Same run as above: the judge (also live Bedrock) returned a complete JSON verdict, recorded as `confidence 0.99, judge_cost 0.0006204` in the attempt row from step 6, with no truncation error ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The exact production mutation site is unconfirmed; the new error detail will name it if any path still mutates nested state ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signals.title: fix(proxy): strip callback credentials from the auth object stamped into request metadata
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The proxy stamps the live auth object into request metadata - That object carries team, key, project and org callback credentials - Every integration that logs raw metadata therefore receives them - Legacy rows hold those credentials in plaintext, not ciphertext How it solves it: - Stamp a sanitized copy instead, so all consumers are covered at once - `secret_manager_settings` joins the credential-bearing slot set - Team metadata reaching `user_api_key_auth_metadata` is stripped too ## User Flow Before: an admin gives a team its own Langfuse project, then finds that team's Langfuse secret key sitting inside the traces and spend logs anyone on the team can read 1. The admin creates a team with `POST https://litellm-domain/team/new`, sending `metadata.logging` with the team's `langfuse_public_key` and `langfuse_secret_key` 2. A developer on that team sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and gets a normal 200 back 3. The request is logged to whichever destinations the proxy is configured for, and the payload carries the team's own `langfuse_secret_key` in it 4. The admin opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs`, opens that request, and reads the team's Langfuse secret key out of the stored request 5. Anyone who can read logs for that team can reuse those credentials against the team's Langfuse project After: the same setup logs the same request without the credentials 1. The admin creates the same team the same way 2. The developer sends the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and gets the same 200 back 3. The request is logged to the same destinations, and the payload no longer contains the team's `langfuse_secret_key` 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the same request with the credentials absent, while the team name, key alias and rate limit settings are all still there 5. Reading logs for that team no longer hands over credentials for the team's Langfuse project ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5487 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on a real Postgres, real provider call returning 200 on both legs. The team row holds credentials in both supported shapes plus a non-credential setting, so one run covers the leak and the preservation: ```json {"logging": [{"callback_name": "langfuse", "callback_type": "success", "callback_vars": {"langfuse_host": "http://127.0.0.1:8487", "langfuse_public_key": "pk-lf-LEAKPUB5487", "langfuse_secret_key": "sk-lf-LEAKSEC5487"}}], "callback_settings": {"langfuse": {"callback_vars": {"langfuse_secret_key": "sk-CBSETLEAK5487"}}}, "model_rpm_limit": {"gemini-flash": 100}} ``` Only `logging[].callback_vars` is encrypted at rest. `callback_settings` and `secret_manager_settings` are not, so on a team created through the ordinary `/team/new` API today those two leak as usable plaintext. The Admin UI capture below uses exactly that path, with no direct row writes. ### Before (50e71313b7) #### Credentials reaching a logging destination 1. `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4587/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_KEY" -d '{"model":"gemini-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say the single word: canary"}],"max_tokens":200}'` 2. `http_status=200`, response text `'canary'` 3. Recording what an integration that logs raw request metadata receives: ``` team callback credential (logging shape) reachable: True team callback credential (callback_settings) reachable: True non-credential team config preserved (model_rpm_limit): True stamped object type: UserAPIKeyAuth ``` #### Credentials reaching Postgres 4. `SELECT ... FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" ORDER BY "startTime" DESC LIMIT 1` 5. The row's `proxy_server_request` contains the credentials verbatim: ``` "team_metadata": {"logging": [{"callback_name": "langfuse", "callback_type": "success", "callback_vars": {"langfuse_host": "http://127.0.0.1:8487", "langfuse_public_key": "pk-lf-LEAKPUB5487", "langfuse_secret_key": "sk-lf-LEAKSEC5487"}}], "model_rpm_limit": {"gemini-flash": 100}, "callback_settings": {"langfuse" ... ``` #### Admin UI, what an operator sees on the logs page 6. Open `http://127.0.0.1:4587/ui/?page=logs`, click the newest request for team `payments`, expand Request & Response, switch to JSON, scroll to `team_metadata` 7. The team's own credentials are rendered in the request log: ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr37233/assets/before-team-metadata-leak.png) ### After (dc63988d3c) #### Credentials reaching a logging destination 1. Same curl, same team, same key 2. `http_status=200`, response text `'canary'` 3. Same recording: ``` team callback credential (logging shape) reachable: False team callback credential (callback_settings) reachable: False non-credential team config preserved (model_rpm_limit): True stamped object type: UserAPIKeyAuth team callback still dispatched to destination: ['/api/public/ingestion', '/generic'] ``` #### Credentials reaching Postgres 4. Same query against the row written by this leg 5. `rows_with_canary` is 0, while the before-leg row in the same table still shows 1 #### Prometheus labels still populate 6. `curl -sL http://127.0.0.1:4587/metrics/ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER_KEY"` ``` api_key_alias="lit5487-probe-key" hashed_api_key="6c0cea30689d2a3cfc8e745ba7c7f18dbd7c1ece63c8740b473370e65287bf1b" team_alias="lit5487-canary-team" team="c1375c0f-e643-422d-9f64-dabc4657fa35" ``` Team callbacks still dispatch on both legs, which is the regression that would matter most here: the dispatcher reads the auth object directly rather than the stamped copy, so sanitizing the copy does not disturb it. #### Admin UI, what an operator sees on the logs page 7. Same page, same team, same panel, scrolled to the same `team_metadata` block 8. The credentials are gone and the non-credential team config survives: ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/assets-pr37233/assets/after-team-metadata-clean.png) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Three producers bypass this stamp and still emit raw slots - Widest is the MCP pre-call hook object handed to guardrail vendors - Those stay open, so this says Refs rather than Resolves - Only `logging` is encrypted at rest; the other two leak plaintext - Stamped object is now a copy, so identity comparison would break ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- --- > [!NOTE] > [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 9b881386603dbab0da7497437105c3bf206dc8b2. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

signals.title: fix(proxy): withhold unenumerated credentials from GET /health rows
signals.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `GET /health` copies each deployment's whole config into the response - Only a hand-written list of key names was removed from it - So every credential nobody enumerated came back in plaintext - Unauthenticated on a default install, and to any non-admin key How it solves it: - Classify credentials instead of enumerating them - Source the names from the list `CredentialLiteLLMParams` already drives - Treat auth-header containers as secret whatever the header names are - Scrub at every depth; truncate rather than pass through at the bound ## User Flow Before: any caller who can reach the proxy reads the admin's upstream provider credentials out of a health check 1. The proxy admin puts provider auth in `extra_headers` and `aws_session_token` in `config.yaml`, then starts the proxy on a default install with no master key 2. Any caller sends `GET http://litellm-domain/health` with no `Authorization` header 3. HTTP 200. The healthy row carries the `extra_headers` values in full, plus `aws_session_token`, `azure_ad_token`, `aws_web_identity_token`, `client_secret`, and any bespoke secret field the admin added 4. The same is true whether the deployment is up or down, and whether the caller is anonymous or holds an ordinary key 5. Another user can take those values and call the provider directly, billed to the admin After: the same call still reports health and carries no credentials 1. The proxy admin uses the same `config.yaml` and starts the same proxy 2. The same caller sends `GET http://litellm-domain/health` with no `Authorization` header 3. HTTP 200. The rows still carry the model, the health status, the error text, and the failure status code. No header values, no session token, no AD token, no client secret, no bespoke secret field 4. That holds for a credential name nobody listed, including provider-native spellings like `apiKey` and names nested below the row 5. Another user cannot recover any provider credential from the endpoint ## Relevant issues Fixes #36898 Adopts and completes #37090 by @Siraj637909, whose commit is the first commit on this branch. That change added `extra_headers`, `headers` and `aws_session_token` to the display denylist, which closes the healthy row. This PR keeps the commit and fixes the failure path it does not reach; the enumerated names are now redundant, since the general rule below subsumes them, so the denylist is reduced to the structural keys and the credential names are owned by one mechanism ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5695 Split out of the original single PR. The failure-path echo of the outbound request is LIT-5712, stacked on top of this branch ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup. Canary strings stand in for real provider credentials, so nothing real was exposed. `real-gemini` is a live Gemini call against the real API, so the healthy row in cases 1 and 3 is a real provider response. `dead` points at a closed port so its row lands under `unhealthy_endpoints` ```yaml # leak_full.yaml model_list: - model_name: real-gemini litellm_params: model: gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite api_key: os.environ/GEMINI_API_KEY extra_headers: x-canary-extra-header: CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_VALUE aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_HEALTHY azure_ad_token: CANARY_AZURE_AD_TOKEN_HEALTHY aws_web_identity_token: CANARY_AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_HEALTHY client_secret: CANARY_CLIENT_SECRET_HEALTHY my_custom_upstream_secret: CANARY_CUSTOM_FIELD_HEALTHY litellm_credential_name: CANARY_CREDENTIAL_NAME_HEALTHY - model_name: dead litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-4o-mini api_base: http://127.0.0.1:1 api_key: sk-not-a-real-key extra_headers: Authorization: Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION x-goog-api-key: CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE api-key: CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY headers: X-Custom: CANARY_HEADER_VALUE default_headers: Authorization: Bearer CANARY_DEFAULT_HEADERS_AUTH aws_session_token: CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_VALUE azure_ad_token: CANARY_AZURE_AD_TOKEN_UNHEALTHY aws_web_identity_token: CANARY_AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_UNHEALTHY aws_role_name: CANARY_AWS_ROLE_NAME client_secret: CANARY_CLIENT_SECRET_UNHEALTHY my_custom_upstream_secret: CANARY_CUSTOM_FIELD_UNHEALTHY litellm_credential_name: CANARY_CREDENTIAL_NAME_UNHEALTHY provider_options: apiKey: CANARY_CAMELCASE_APIKEY apikey: CANARY_LOWERCASE_APIKEY secretAccessKey: CANARY_CAMELCASE_SECRET customApiKey_v2: CANARY_MIXEDCASE_APIKEY passphrase: CANARY_PASSPHRASE custom_apikey: CANARY_UNDERSCORE_APIKEY openai_apikey: CANARY_OPENAI_APIKEY customApikey: CANARY_CAMEL_UNSPLIT_APIKEY cost_api_key: CANARY_COST_API_KEY secretKeyRef: CANARY_SECRET_KEY_REF x-api-key-id: CANARY_HYPHEN_KEY_ID # these three must survive: a price, a routing rule, a probe bound input_cost_per_token: 0.0000025 keywords: routing-keyword-must-survive max_tokens: 16 d1: {d2: {d3: {d4: {d5: {d6: {d7: {d8: {d9: {d10: {d11: {d12: api_key: CANARY_BELOW_DEPTH_CAP extra_headers: {api-key: CANARY_HDR_BELOW_DEPTH_CAP} }}}}}}}}}}}} ``` ### Before (3f4810b8f2) #### 1. GET /health, no master key, no auth header 1. `litellm --config leak_full.yaml --port 4190 --host 127.0.0.1` 2. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4190/health` returns HTTP 200 with all 32 canaries present, on both rows ```json "healthy_endpoints": [{ "azure_ad_token": "CANARY_AZURE_AD_TOKEN_HEALTHY", "aws_session_token": "CANARY_AWS_SESSION_TOKEN_HEALTHY", "aws_web_identity_token": "CANARY_AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_HEALTHY", "extra_headers": {"x-canary-extra-header": "CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_VALUE"}, "client_secret": "CANARY_CLIENT_SECRET_HEALTHY", "my_custom_upstream_secret": "CANARY_CUSTOM_FIELD_HEALTHY", ... }] "unhealthy_endpoints": [{ ... "raw_request_typed_dict": { "raw_request_api_base": "http://127.0.0.1:1", "raw_request_body": { "extra_headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer CANARY_EXTRA_HEADERS_AUTHORIZATION", "x-goog-api-key": "CANARY_X_GOOG_API_KEY_VALUE", "api-key": "CANARY_AZURE_STYLE_API_KEY"}, "extra_body": {"azure_ad_token": "CANARY_AZURE_AD_TOKEN_UNHEALTHY", ...}}}}] ``` 3. `api_base` is absent from the top level for this non-admin caller, and `raw_request_typed_dict.raw_request_api_base` returns it anyway ### After (be52dd8e7d) #### 1. GET /health, no master key, no auth header 1. `litellm --config leak_full.yaml --port 4185 --host 127.0.0.1` 2. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4185/health` returns HTTP 200, `healthy_count: 1`, `unhealthy_count: 1`, and 0 of the 32 canaries ```json "healthy_endpoints": [{ "model": "gemini/gemini-3.1-flash-lite", "max_tokens": 16, "cache": {"no-cache": true}, "model_id": "5eed75363b574eb0372b10f61d13a98c33b7f7e3e4229a64ae28c97c348655d1", ... }] "unhealthy_endpoints": [{ "model": "openai/gpt-4o-mini", "max_tokens": 16, "error": "litellm.InternalServerError: ... Connection error.", "provider_options": {"input_cost_per_token": 2.5e-06, "keywords": "routing-keyword-must-survive", "max_tokens": 16, "d1": {"d2": {"d3": {"d4": {"d5": {"d6": {"d7": {"d8": {"d9": {"d10": {"d11": {"d12": "<truncated>"}}}}}}}}}}}, "model_id": "5e511e019008dca3729c2c813eb6d3cd4334ce4fc02d04362b88a52dd411ef6f", "exception_status": 500 }] ``` 3. The rows keep `model`, `model_id`, `error` and `exception_status`. `provider_options` loses all 11 credential spellings and keeps the price, the routing rule and the probe bound, and the branch past the recursion bound reads `<truncated>` rather than the subtree ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `_clean_endpoint_data` no longer decides what to withhold from a hand-written list of names. A key is withheld when it is one of the provider credential fields `_ADMIN_CONFIG_FIELDS_TO_CLEAR_ON_BASE_OVERRIDE` derives from `CredentialLiteLLMParams`, when it is one of the auth-header containers, or when any of its name segments is a credential word or ends with one. Segments split on camelCase as well as `_` and `-`, so `apiKey`, `custom_apikey`, `secretKeyRef` and `sastoken` are all caught while `keywords`, `tokenizer`, `author` and `max_tokens` are not. A `cost` segment excuses the `token` match and nothing else, which is what the 77 `*_cost_per_token` pricing fields need without letting `cost_api_key` through. The rate-limit integers and, at the top level only, the role-gated routing fields are kept Scrubbing is recursive, so a credential nested under a benign key goes too. Values that are neither JSON scalars nor containers are replaced, because the response serializer would otherwise flatten an object into its attributes; that is reachable today through `oci_signer`. Passing the recursion bound truncates instead of returning the subtree, and the bound is a plain constant rather than an env-tunable one, so a knob cannot switch nested scrubbing off `ILLEGAL_DISPLAY_PARAMS` now holds only structural keys, and `raw_request_typed_dict` is one of them. `POST /health/test_connection` re-adds that echo itself, scrubbed and with the target URL's query string removed since some providers carry the key there `_clean_endpoint_data` no longer mutates its argument, which one call site had passing the router's live deployment params. The probe's logging handle is instead cleared where the probe owns it ## QA runbook Not applicable; no `tests/e2e/` changes ## Caveats (if any) - 24 non-secret provider fields also stop appearing, listed below The credential set is derived from the forwarding gate, which is deliberately broad, so these non-secret fields stop appearing in health rows as well: `aws_batch_role_arn`, `aws_bedrock_project_id`, `aws_bedrock_runtime_endpoint`, `aws_external_id`, `aws_profile_name`, `aws_region_name`, `aws_role_name`, `aws_session_name`, `aws_sts_endpoint`, `azure_ad_token`, `bedrock_tags`, `configurable_clientside_auth_params`, `gcs_bucket_name`, `litellm_credential_name`, `organization`, `region_name`, `s3_bucket_name`, `s3_encryption_key_id`, `s3_output_bucket_name`, `s3_region_name`, `vertex_location`, `vertex_project`, `watsonx_region_name`, `aws_web_identity_token`. I swept `litellm/`, `ui/litellm-dashboard/`, `litellm/proxy/client/` and `tests/e2e/` for consumers of health rows: the dashboard reads `unhealthy_count` and `unhealthy_endpoints[0].error` and otherwise renders the row through `JSON.stringify`, the CLI client only calls `/health/readiness`, and nothing reads these fields, so no first-party consumer breaks. Region and bucket names are the ones an operator might miss, and they remain visible on `/model/info` ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR
