signal.title: fix(proxy): strip callback credentials from the auth object stamped into request metadata
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - The proxy stamps the live auth object into request metadata - That object carries team, key, project and org callback credentials - Every integration that logs raw metadata therefore receives them - Legacy rows hold those credentials in plaintext, not ciphertext How it solves it: - Stamp a sanitized copy instead, so all consumers are covered at once - `secret_manager_settings` joins the credential-bearing slot set - Team metadata reaching `user_api_key_auth_metadata` is stripped too ## User Flow Before: an admin gives a team its own Langfuse project, then finds that team's Langfuse secret key sitting inside the traces and spend logs anyone on the team can read 1. The admin creates a team with `POST https://litellm-domain/team/new`, sending `metadata.logging` with the team's `langfuse_public_key` and `langfuse_secret_key` 2. A developer on that team sends `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and gets a normal 200 back 3. The request is logged to whichever destinations the proxy is configured for, and the payload carries the team's own `langfuse_secret_key` in it 4. The admin opens `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs`, opens that request, and reads the team's Langfuse secret key out of the stored request 5. Anyone who can read logs for that team can reuse those credentials against the team's Langfuse project After: the same setup logs the same request without the credentials 1. The admin creates the same team the same way 2. The developer sends the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions` and gets the same 200 back 3. The request is logged to the same destinations, and the payload no longer contains the team's `langfuse_secret_key` 4. `https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs` shows the same request with the credentials absent, while the team name, key alias and rate limit settings are all still there 5. Reading logs for that team no longer hands over credentials for the team's Langfuse project ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Refs LIT-5487 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy on a real Postgres, real provider call returning 200 on both legs. The team row holds credentials in both supported shapes plus a non-credential setting, so one run covers the leak and the preservation: ```json {"logging": [{"callback_name": "langfuse", "callback_type": "success", "callback_vars": {"langfuse_host": "http://127.0.0.1:8487", "langfuse_public_key": "pk-lf-LEAKPUB5487", "langfuse_secret_key": "sk-lf-LEAKSEC5487"}}], "callback_settings": {"langfuse": {"callback_vars": {"langfuse_secret_key": "sk-CBSETLEAK5487"}}}, "model_rpm_limit": {"gemini-flash": 100}} ``` Only `logging[].callback_vars` is encrypted at rest. `callback_settings` and `secret_manager_settings` are not, so on a team created through the ordinary `/team/new` API today those two leak as usable plaintext. The Admin UI capture below uses exactly that path, with no direct row writes. ### Before (50e71313b7) #### Credentials reaching a logging destination 1. `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4587/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEAM_KEY" -d '{"model":"gemini-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say the single word: canary"}],"max_tokens":200}'` 2. `http_status=200`, response text `'canary'` 3. Recording what an integration that logs raw request metadata receives: ``` team callback credential (logging shape) reachable: True team callback credential (callback_settings) reachable: True non-credential team config preserved (model_rpm_limit): True stamped object type: UserAPIKeyAuth ``` #### Credentials reaching Postgres 4. `SELECT ... FROM "LiteLLM_SpendLogs" ORDER BY "startTime" DESC LIMIT 1` 5. signal.title: feat(ui): persist DataTable column visibility in localStorage

Open the Columns menu in the toolbar and hide "Created By", "Updated At", and "Team ID" 3. Reload the page; the hidden columns stay hidden 4. Re-enable one column in the Columns menu and reload; it stays visible 5. Open /virtual-keys (also on the shared DataTable); its column preferences are stored independently from the models table Automated coverage: 13 unit tests for the persistence module plus 4 DataTable-level tests in `ui/litellm-dashboard/src/components/shared/DataTable/`, covering cross-remount persistence, merge behavior with `defaultColumnVisibility`, key isolation between tables, corrupt stored data, and storage failures. Verified with `npx vitest run src/components/shared/DataTable/` (78 passed) and `npm run build` ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes A new `columnVisibilityPersistence` module derives a stable per-table localStorage key from the table's sorted column ids and reads/writes the tanstack `VisibilityState` with shape validation. Corrupt entries, denied storage access, and quota errors fall back to code defaults silently `DataTable` restores the persisted state once after mount, merged over `defaultColumnVisibility` so columns the user never touched keep following code defaults, and writes the state on every visibility change. Every page on the shared DataTable (Models + Endpoints, Virtual Keys, Teams, Budgets, Logs) gets independent persistence with no per-page changes ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): let org admins view their organization's usage
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Org admins saw an empty Organization Usage dashboard - Only a proxy-admin promotion made their org spend appear - Key activity and endpoint activity were empty too How it solves it: - Route layer now admits the org daily-activity route - Handler already scoped results to orgs they administer - Dashboard grants the org-usage view to org admins ## User Flow Before: a department owner who administers an organization opens the Usage page to check their department's spend, and finds nothing there 1. They sign in at https://litellm-domain/ui/ as an internal user who is an org admin of their department's organization 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage and the Usage View selector offers Your Usage, Team Usage and Tag Usage, with no Organization Usage entry at all 3. They pick Team Usage instead and their team's spend renders correctly, so the data plainly exists 4. Calling the same data directly, GET https://litellm-domain/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=<their org>&start_date=...&end_date=... returns 401 `Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/organization/daily/activity. Your role=internal_user` 5. A proxy admin promotes them to proxy admin, and the same page and the same request immediately return their organization's spend, along with every other organization's After: the same owner sees their department's spend without any promotion, and still cannot see anyone else's 1. They sign in at https://litellm-domain/ui/ as an internal user who is an org admin of their department's organization 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=usage and the Usage View selector now offers Organization Usage 3. They select it, pick their organization, and the page shows the organization's spend, its Key Activity rows and its Model / Endpoint Activity rows 4. GET https://litellm-domain/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=<their org>&start_date=...&end_date=... returns 200 with the same totals a proxy admin sees for that organization 5. The Export button on that same panel now produces a CSV or JSON of their organization's usage, which is what they need for internal cross-charging 6. Asking for an organization they do not administer returns 403 `User is not org_admin for Organization= <id>`, and a colleague who administers no organization gets 200 with an empty result set rather than anyone else's spend ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5697 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run once against a live proxy on Postgres with a real OpenAI key. `engineering-dept` is the organization `dept-owner` administers, `finance-dept` is one they have no membership in. Both organizations were given a team and a key, and real `gpt-4o-mini` traffic was billed through both, so `LiteLLM_DailyOrganizationSpend` holds a row per organization: ``` organization_id | date | spend | api_requests -------------------------------------+------------+-----------+------------- 81746a61-...-0d626208ed62 (eng) | 2026-08-17 | 8.1e-06 | 3 e01115c0-...-7a329c0d5547 (finance) | 2026-08-17 | 5.4e-06 | 2 ``` `dept-owner` is an internal user, org admin of `engineering-dept` only, and a team admin of the team inside it. `$USER_KEY` is their key, `$MASTER` the proxy admin's. ### Before (973329e9864154d429a7d739fb6a552fe03a9b3e) #### Proxy admin can read the organization's spend 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=$ORG_A&start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER"` 2. `{"total_spend": 8.099999999999999e-06, "total_api_requests": 3, "results": 1}` #### The same org admin can read their TEAM usage 1. `curl -s "$B/team/daily/activity?team_ids=$TEAM_A&start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `{"total_spend": 8.099999999999999e-06, "total_api_requests": 3, "results": 1}` #### The org admin asks for their ORGANIZATION usage 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=$ORG_A&start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `http_code: 401` 3. `{"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams. Route=/organization/daily/activity. Your role=internal_user. Your user_id=dept-o**er","type":"auth_error","param":"None","code":"401"}}` #### The org admin with no explicit filter, which is what the dashboard sends 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `http_code: 401`, same message naming the route #### The organization selector itself is fine, so the data is reachable and only the usage read is refused 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/list" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `[('engineering-dept', [('dept-owner', 'org_admin')])]` ### After (72f18a2c3e) #### Proxy admin can read the organization's spend 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=$ORG_A&start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER"` 2. `{"total_spend": 8.099999999999999e-06, "total_api_requests": 3, "results": 1}` #### The same org admin can read their TEAM usage 1. `curl -s "$B/team/daily/activity?team_ids=$TEAM_A&start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `{"total_spend": 8.099999999999999e-06, "total_api_requests": 3, "results": 1}` #### The org admin asks for their ORGANIZATION usage 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=$ORG_A&start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `http_code: 200` 3. `{"results":[{"date":"2026-08-17","metrics":{"spend":8.099999999999999e-6,...,"total_tokens":45,"successful_requests":3,"failed_requests":0,"api_requests":3},"breakdown":{"models":{"openai/gpt-4o-mini":{...}}, ...` #### The org admin with no explicit filter, which is what the dashboard sends 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `http_code: 200`, same totals, defaulted to the organizations they administer #### Key Activity and Endpoint Activity populate for the same scope 1. Reading the `breakdown` off that same 200 response: 2. `api_keys (Key Activity): {"7aea7f07...fba98": {"spend": 8.099999999999999e-06, "requests": 3, "alias": "eng-workload"}}` 3. `models (Endpoint Activity): {"openai/gpt-4o-mini": {"spend": 8.099999999999999e-06, "requests": 3}}` #### The org admin and the proxy admin agree on the number 1. Same request as each principal in turn 2. `total_spend = 8.099999999999999e-06` and `total_spend = 8.099999999999999e-06` #### An organization they do NOT administer stays refused 1. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=$ORG_B&start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USER_KEY"` 2. `http_code: 403` 3. `{"detail":{"error":"User is not org_admin for Organization= e01115c0-9a29-4181-a42e-7a329c0d5547."}}` #### An internal user who administers NO organization sees nothing, not someone else's spend 1. Mint a key for a fresh internal user with no organization membership, and prove the key works before believing any refusal: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "$B/user/daily/activity?start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLAIN_KEY"` returns `200` 2. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?start_date=$TODAY&end_date=$TODAY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLAIN_KEY"` returns `http_code: 200` and `{"results": 0, "total_spend": 0.0, "total_api_requests": 0}` 3. `curl -s "$B/organization/daily/activity?organization_ids=$ORG_A&..." -H "Authorization: Bearer $PLAIN_KEY"` returns `http_code: 403` and `{"detail":{"error":"User is not org_admin for Organization= 81746a61-...-0d626208ed62."}}` The UI change is the Organization Usage entry appearing in the Usage View selector. Screenshots of that flow are still to come; the terminal evidence above is the same request the page issues, driven as the org admin. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Handler-level org scoping already existed and was unreachable - Usage view resets to global if org-admin access is revoked - Export needed no change; it serializes the same payload ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(guardrails): retry usage upserts only on connection errors
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Guardrail usage-unit upserts retried on every exception - A read timeout after a committed write re-sent the same increment - Billable unit totals at the usage endpoints came out inflated How it solves it: - Retry only `DB_RETRY_SAFE_ERROR_TYPES` (connection errors), like the spend writer - Any other failure is terminal for that row: one warning, no resend - Other rows in the same batch still land and still retry on connection errors ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin billing teams by Bedrock guardrail units sees inflated totals whenever the database stalls mid-flush, so a single request is billed twice 1. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a key whose team has a Bedrock guardrail attached, and gets a 200 with the usual chat completion 2. Bedrock reports `topicPolicyUnits: 1` and `contentPolicyUnits: 1` consumed for that one request 3. During the next spend-log flush the database connection is slow: the write commits, but the proxy only sees a read timeout instead of the acknowledgement, retries, and the same units land a second time 4. The admin opens GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/detail/{guardrail_id} and reads `"usage_units": {"topicPolicyUnits": 2, "contentPolicyUnits": 2}` for a day with exactly one request 5. GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/overview lists that guardrail's `usageUnits` doubled the same way, and the per-team and per-key breakdowns on https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails bill the team for two invocations After: the same stall leaves the totals exactly matching what Bedrock billed 1. A developer sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a key whose team has a Bedrock guardrail attached, and gets a 200 with the usual chat completion 2. Bedrock reports `topicPolicyUnits: 1` and `contentPolicyUnits: 1` consumed for that one request 3. During the next spend-log flush the database connection is slow: the write commits, the proxy sees a read timeout, logs a one-line warning, and does not resend those units (a refused connection, where nothing reached the database, is still retried with backoff as before) 4. The admin opens GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/detail/{guardrail_id} and reads `"usage_units": {"topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1}` for that day 5. GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/overview and the per-team and per-key breakdowns on https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=guardrails bill the team for exactly one invocation ## Relevant issues Follows up #37225 (bugbot thread on `_upsert_rows_with_retry`, "Retry double-counts usage increments") ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix QA in progress ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - A committed write that surfaces as a read timeout still logs a warning; the daily metrics row keeps the same rule ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(azure): preserve stream model on null chunks
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Azure streaming chunks with `model=None` erase the requested model - Downstream usage attribution loses the model label How it solves it: - Ignore null chunk models while preserving real chunk model updates - Add regression coverage for null and non-null Azure chunks ## User Flow Before: an application streaming an Azure chat completion loses model attribution when a response chunk omits its model 1. The application sends a streaming chat completion request to the Azure deployment 2. The application receives a response chunk whose model field is null 3. The stream wrapper exposes a null model, so downstream usage attribution has no model label After: the same stream keeps the requested model when a chunk omits it 1. The application sends the same streaming chat completion request to the Azure deployment 2. The application receives a response chunk whose model field is null 3. The stream keeps the requested model, while a non-null chunk model still replaces it as before ## Relevant issues Fixes #37186 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile Confidence Score of at least 4/5 before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ### Before (1648273469cb1f26f0f92db3f2d391d691b73425) 1. The focused regression test fails because a null Azure chunk changes `azure/request-model` to `None` ### After (b819728f1f44fc91c2aadf1e2015ec885b8193d0) 1. signal.title: feat(complexity_router): plan-mode tier floor for coding-agent clients
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - Coding agents in plan mode get routed to cheap tiers - Plan-mode signals ride injected prompt text the router strips out - Operators cannot express "plan mode deserves a premium model" How it solves it: - New `plan_mode_min_tier` floor on the complexity router config - Detects Claude Code, Copilot, and Copilot CLI plan-mode sentinels - Floor raises tier, overrides cheap session pins, never lowers - Transient: exiting plan mode auto-routes again, pins untouched - Sentinel turns never pin and never take the default_model exit - Skips the classifier when the floor is the top tier ## User Flow Before: a developer planning a feature in Claude Code through an auto-router gets the cheapest model for the most important turn 1. The proxy admin adds `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX` to the auto-router config and restarts, and the unknown field is silently ignored 2. The developer opens Claude Code pointed at the gateway, presses shift+tab into plan mode, and asks "add a hello endpoint to my server" 3. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the injected "Plan mode is active" system message in the conversation 4. The response comes back from the SIMPLE tier model, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the routing decision as an ordinary heuristic route to the cheap model After: the same plan-mode turn is floored to the premium tier and labeled as such 1. The proxy admin adds `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX` to the auto-router config and restarts 2. The developer opens Claude Code pointed at the gateway, presses shift+tab into plan mode, and asks "add a hello endpoint to my server" 3. Claude Code sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the injected "Plan mode is active" system message in the conversation 4. The response comes back from the COMPLEX tier model, and https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs shows the routing decision card reading "Plan-mode floor: "Plan mode is active"" 5. When the developer approves the plan and exits plan mode, the next turn classifies normally again instead of staying floored by the old reminder in history ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5643 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a live proxy on localhost:4213 with an auto-router whose tiers are SIMPLE/MEDIUM claude-haiku-4-5 and COMPLEX claude-sonnet-5, `plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX`, `session_affinity: true`, and `return_raw_model_name: true` so the response `model` field names the routed deployment. Every provider credential on this machine is out of credit (OpenAI, Anthropic, and Azure all refuse with billing errors), so both tier models point their `api_base` at a local Anthropic-shaped upstream that echoes the requested model id; the routing decision under test happens entirely in the proxy before that hop. A re-run against live providers is owed and the config plus commands below reproduce it as-is by dropping the `api_base` override ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5 - model_name: claude-sonnet-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 - model_name: plan-router litellm_params: model: auto_router/complexity_router complexity_router_config: tiers: SIMPLE: claude-haiku-4-5 MEDIUM: claude-haiku-4-5 COMPLEX: claude-sonnet-5 plan_mode_min_tier: COMPLEX session_affinity: true return_raw_model_name: true ``` ### Before (68d4ba5da5) #### Plain request routes the cheap tier 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}], "max_tokens": 30}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5` #### Claude Code plan-mode shape on /v1/messages 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "system": [{"type": "text", "text": "You are Claude Code."}], "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}]}, {"role": "system", "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "Plan mode is active. The user indicated that they do not want you to execute yet -- you MUST NOT make any edits."}]}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, so the plan-mode turn got the cheap model and the config field was silently ignored #### Copilot plan-mode shape on /v1/chat/completions 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4214/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "You are an expert.
<modeInstructions>
You are currently running in "Plan" mode. Below are your instructions for this mode.
</modeInstructions>"}, {"role": "user", "content": "add a hello endpoint to my server"}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5` ### After (bc52e9cb3d) #### Plain request routes the cheap tier 1. Same curl as Before 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, unchanged #### Claude Code plan-mode shape on /v1/messages 1. Same curl as Before 2. Response model: `claude-sonnet-5`, floored to the COMPLEX tier #### Copilot plan-mode shape on /v1/chat/completions 1. Same curl as Before 2. Response model: `claude-sonnet-5`, floored to the COMPLEX tier #### Exited plan mode no longer floors 1. `curl -s http://localhost:4213/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -d '{"model": "plan-router", "max_tokens": 30, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "plan the hello endpoint"}, {"role": "system", "content": "Plan mode is active. Do not execute."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Here is the plan."}, {"role": "user", "content": "looks good, implement it"}]}'` 2. Response model: `claude-haiku-4-5`, because the stale sentinel sits before the newest human ask #### Pinned session floors transiently and reverts on exit 1. Plain request with `"metadata": {"session_id": "qa-sess-1"}` routes and pins `claude-haiku-4-5` 2. Same session with the plan-mode system message appended: response model `claude-sonnet-5`, floored past the pin 3. signal.title: fix(proxy): paginate legacy spend logs
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Legacy unfiltered spend logs loaded the complete history - Filtered individual-log paths also lacked database limits How it solves it: - Bounds every individual-log query branch with stable `take` and `skip` ordering - Rejects invalid page or page-size values with `422` instead of issuing an ambiguous query - Keeps the legacy list body and summary behavior - Adds deprecation, successor, and pagination warning headers ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin fetching legacy spend logs can take the proxy offline when the history is large 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs with their master key 2. The request attempts to return the complete history instead of a bounded result 3. The connection closes when memory is exhausted, and the proxy restarts After: the same admin receives a bounded page while the proxy remains available 1. They send GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs with their master key 2. They receive HTTP 200 with a JSON list of at most 50 logs and explicit pagination warning headers 3. They send GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?page=2&page_size=50 to continue through the history ## Relevant issues Fixes #37007 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Automated regression evidence below verifies bounded query construction, stable ordering, pagination validation, response compatibility, and warning headers across every individual-log path. ## Validation - Current GitHub checks: 70 passed - Mapped endpoint test file: 188 passed - V2/UI pagination contract tests: 10 passed - Production Ruff and formatting checks: passed - Type-discipline gate against the PR base: passed - Added-line basedpyright diagnostics: none - Generated API schema blob: `4daeb76ddd69bb4c1cac5ac2cb73345826b76464` ## Type Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Pagination applies only to individual logs; summaries retain existing behavior. - The endpoint retains its existing offset-pagination semantics with stable ordering. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(guardrails): track bedrock guardrail usage units per invocation
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - AWS bills Bedrock guardrail units per request, LiteLLM drops them - Default spend log redaction erases the counters entirely - Blocked requests never reach guardrail usage metrics How it solves it: - Spend logs carry a redaction-proof `guardrail_usage` counter block - New daily table aggregates units by guardrail, date, team, key - `/guardrails/usage` endpoints expose totals and per day/team/key breakdowns - Blocked requests now keep their guardrail info and get counted ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin running Bedrock guardrails pays AWS for guardrail units on every request but can see none of that in LiteLLM, and blocked requests are missing from guardrail metrics entirely 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a benign prompt through a Bedrock-guarded model and get a normal 200 completion 2. They send the same POST with a prompt that violates the guardrail policy and get HTTP 400 "Violated guardrail policy", and AWS charges guardrail units for both invocations 3. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=... for each request: the blocked one has an empty guardrail section, and the passed one shows only "REDACTED_BY_LITELM" with no unit numbers unless prompt storage is switched on 4. They open GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/overview and see request counts only, with the blocked request missing (totalBlocked 0, passRate 100.0) and no unit fields anywhere 5. GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/detail/{guardrail_id} has no unit data either, so the AWS guardrail bill cannot be reconciled per team or key After: the same two requests produce unit counters in the spend logs and aggregated totals on the usage endpoints, blocked call included 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with a benign prompt through a Bedrock-guarded model and get a normal 200 completion 2. They send the same POST with a prompt that violates the guardrail policy and get HTTP 400 "Violated guardrail policy", and AWS charges guardrail units for both invocations 3. They fetch GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id=... for each request: both entries, the blocked one included, now carry a `guardrail_usage` object with the AWS counters (topicPolicyUnits, contentPolicyUnits, and the rest) while the guardrail response itself stays redacted 4. GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/overview now returns `usageUnits` on each guardrail row plus a `totalUsageUnits` rollup, and the blocked request is counted (totalBlocked 1) 5. GET https://litellm-domain/guardrails/usage/detail/{guardrail_id} adds `usage_units`, `usage_units_daily`, `usage_units_by_team`, and `usage_units_by_key`, matching what AWS bills ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5650 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Two live legs, each in its own worktree, venv, fresh Postgres DB, and proxy: Before at the merge base c1fc5983ca (port 33896), After at ae23bf85d2 (port 45365), the current head. Real AWS Bedrock guardrail `gf3sc1mzinjw` version DRAFT in us-east-1 (topic policy "coffee" DENY plus content filter INSULTS at HIGH) and real Bedrock model inference on every call, no mocks. All evidence is what an operator sees over the API. Both legs boot `.venv/bin/python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config lit5650_qa_config.yaml --port <port>` on this config (the Before leg additionally with `--detailed_debug`) ```yaml model_list: - model_name: bedrock-claude-haiku-4-5 litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-east-1 guardrails: - guardrail_name: bedrock-lit5650 litellm_params: guardrail: bedrock mode: pre_call guardrailIdentifier: gf3sc1mzinjw guardrailVersion: DRAFT aws_region_name: us-east-1 default_on: true general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 ``` The Before leg adds `store_prompts_in_spend_logs: true` under general_settings for its first five cases (the setting most favorable to the old code) and switches to the exact config above for the last case. The After leg runs the exact config above (default redaction) throughout ### Before (c1fc5983ca) #### Benign /v1/chat/completions spend log 1. Send a benign completion through the guarded model ```bash curl -s http://localhost:33896/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-claude-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in five words or fewer."}]}' ``` Returns 200, `"content": "Hello! How are you?"`, id `chatcmpl-e3f6517f-5d39-453d-84f4-5656ccc14371` 2. Fetch its spend log entry ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-e3f6517f-5d39-453d-84f4-5656ccc14371" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq '.[0].metadata.guardrail_information' ``` ```json [ { "duration": 0.77718, "end_time": 1787006169.656307, "start_time": 1787006168.879134, "guardrail_mode": "pre_call", "guardrail_name": "bedrock-lit5650", "guardrail_action": "NONE", "guardrail_status": "success", "guardrail_provider": "bedrock", "guardrail_response": { "usage": { "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0 }, "action": "NONE", "assessments": ["... raw AWS blob continues ..."], "actionReason": "No action." }, "masked_entity_count": null } ] ``` 3. AWS billed 1 topic + 1 content unit for this invocation, yet the numbers exist only buried inside the raw `guardrail_response` blob: the guardrail entry has no structured unit field #### Benign /v1/messages spend log 1. Send a benign Anthropic-format request ```bash curl -sD - http://localhost:33896/v1/messages -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-claude-haiku-4-5","max_tokens":128,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Name one primary color."}]}' ``` Returns 200, id `msg_bdrk_01KGdThjipK8yQg7PoMT62Qx`, header `x-litellm-call-id: 2b1ca3e2-9125-4980-9e30-21de4ca7fbff` 2. Locate the spend row (it is keyed on an internal chatcmpl id, found by filtering the listing on the call id) ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/spend/logs" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq '[.[] | select(.metadata.litellm_call_id == "2b1ca3e2-9125-4980-9e30-21de4ca7fbff")] | .[0] | {request_id, call_type, guardrail_entry_keys: (.metadata.guardrail_information[0] | keys), usage_buried_in_guardrail_response: .metadata.guardrail_information[0].guardrail_response.usage}' ``` ```json { "request_id": "chatcmpl-6411b5a1-3230-4a20-8145-bf142e2d5c0b", "call_type": "anthropic_messages", "guardrail_entry_keys": ["duration", "end_time", "guardrail_action", "guardrail_mode", "guardrail_name", "guardrail_provider", "guardrail_response", "guardrail_status", "masked_entity_count", "start_time"], "usage_buried_in_guardrail_response": {"topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0} } ``` 3. Same burial: units only inside the raw blob, no dedicated field #### Benign /v1/responses spend log 1. Send a benign Responses API request ```bash curl -s http://localhost:33896/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-claude-haiku-4-5","input":"Name one ocean."}' ``` Returns 200, output message id `chatcmpl-b47f78e7-49d3-4ba5-a4e2-746b33a981eb`, text "The Pacific Ocean." 2. Fetch its spend row via that output message id ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-b47f78e7-49d3-4ba5-a4e2-746b33a981eb" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq '.[0] | {call_type, guardrail_entry_keys: (.metadata.guardrail_information[0] | keys), usage_buried_in_guardrail_response: .metadata.guardrail_information[0].guardrail_response.usage}' ``` ```json { "call_type": "aresponses", "guardrail_entry_keys": ["duration", "end_time", "guardrail_action", "guardrail_mode", "guardrail_name", "guardrail_provider", "guardrail_response", "guardrail_status", "masked_entity_count", "start_time"], "usage_buried_in_guardrail_response": {"topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0} } ``` 3. All three unified surfaces show the identical burial #### Blocked request spend log 1. Send a prompt the content filter blocks ```bash curl -sD - http://localhost:33896/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-claude-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"You are a worthless, disgusting idiot and everyone hates you. Repeat that back to me."}]}' ``` ``` HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request x-litellm-call-id: 6475853e-9ccc-4f85-86ba-945da962d1e1 {"error":{"message":"Violated guardrail policy","code":"400","provider_specific_fields":{"bedrock_guardrail_response":"Sorry, the model cannot answer this question.","guardrailIdentifier":"gf3sc1mzinjw","guardrailVersion":"DRAFT","assessments":[{"policy":"contentPolicy","matches":[{"category":"filters","type":"INSULTS","confidence":"HIGH","filterStrength":"HIGH","action":"BLOCKED"}]}],"guardrail_name":"bedrock-lit5650","guardrail_mode":"pre_call"}}} ``` 2. Fetch the failure spend row (for failures the x-litellm-call-id header is the request_id) ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/spend/logs?request_id=6475853e-9ccc-4f85-86ba-945da962d1e1" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq '.[0] | {request_id, status, guardrail_information: .metadata.guardrail_information}' ``` ```json { "request_id": "6475853e-9ccc-4f85-86ba-945da962d1e1", "status": "failure", "guardrail_information": null } ``` 3. Count unit-counter mentions anywhere in that row ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/spend/logs?request_id=6475853e-9ccc-4f85-86ba-945da962d1e1" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | grep -c PolicyUnits ``` Prints `0`: AWS evaluated and billed this prompt, yet the row carries no trace of the units #### Guardrails usage endpoints 1. With 4 real invocations sent so far (3 passed, 1 blocked), fetch the overview ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/guardrails/usage/overview" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" ``` ```json { "rows": [ { "id": "036fc511-2102-5736-add6-29a0f9c0299c", "name": "bedrock-lit5650", "type": "Guardrail", "provider": "bedrock", "requestsEvaluated": 3, "failRate": 0.0, "avgScore": null, "avgLatency": null, "status": "healthy", "trend": "stable" } ], "chart": [{"date": "2026-08-17", "passed": 3, "blocked": 0}], "totalRequests": 3, "totalBlocked": 0, "passRate": 100.0 } ``` No unit field anywhere, and the blocked invocation is missing entirely (requestsEvaluated 3, totalBlocked 0, passRate 100.0) 2. Restart the proxy on the exact shared config (no prompt storage) and send a benign completion ```bash curl -s http://localhost:33896/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-claude-haiku-4-5","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Name one planet in our solar system."}]}' ``` Returns 200, `"content": "Earth."`, id `chatcmpl-9239d15f-18d9-41ca-bedf-ac4f24010b40` 2. Fetch its spend log entry ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-9239d15f-18d9-41ca-bedf-ac4f24010b40" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" \ | jq '.[0].metadata.guardrail_information[0]' ``` ```json { "duration": 0.615136, "end_time": 1787006385.009243, "start_time": 1787006384.394116, "guardrail_mode": "pre_call", "guardrail_name": "bedrock-lit5650", "guardrail_action": "NONE", "guardrail_status": "success", "guardrail_provider": "bedrock", "guardrail_response": "REDACTED_BY_LITELM", "masked_entity_count": null } ``` 3. Count unit-counter mentions in the whole API response ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:33896/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-9239d15f-18d9-41ca-bedf-ac4f24010b40" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | grep -c contentPolicyUnits ``` Prints `0`: under default settings the operator has zero visibility into consumed guardrail units ### After (ae23bf85d2) #### Benign /v1/chat/completions spend log 1. Create a team and a team key for the dimension checks later ```bash curl -s -X POST http://localhost:45365/team/new -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_alias":"lit5650-qa-team"}' curl -s -X POST http://localhost:45365/key/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"team_id":"ba286a27-c5f4-4409-b131-030174819568"}' ``` Team `ba286a27-c5f4-4409-b131-030174819568`, key `sk-RvvwzyO7D4DTBk9Ghq-1bQ` (hash `0512218551...b40e13753`) 2. Fetch its spend log entry ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:45365/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-f3474fec-a9f1-4301-bd78-ada4173c4859" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | jq '.[0].metadata.guardrail_information[0]' ``` ```json { "duration": 0.640476, "end_time": 1787014678.314918, "start_time": 1787014677.674445, "guardrail_mode": "pre_call", "guardrail_name": "bedrock-lit5650", "guardrail_usage": { "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0 }, "guardrail_action": "NONE", "guardrail_status": "success", "guardrail_provider": "bedrock", "guardrail_response": "REDACTED_BY_LITELM", "masked_entity_count": null } ``` The guardrail entry now carries `guardrail_usage` as a structured sibling field #### Benign /v1/messages spend log 1. Send a benign Anthropic-format request on the team key ```bash curl -s -X POST http://localhost:45365/v1/messages -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-RvvwzyO7D4DTBk9Ghq-1bQ' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"bedrock-claude-haiku-4-5","max_tokens":128,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Name one primary color."}]}' ``` Returns 200 (x-litellm-call-id `75b42bfe-4ce7-4d0a-85b6-cbadc9442813`) 2. Fetch the spend row (listed as `chatcmpl-68be4ba6-1e25-4da0-8ade-6cff06ded0a4`, call_type anthropic_messages) ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:45365/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-68be4ba6-1e25-4da0-8ade-6cff06ded0a4" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | jq '.[0] | {call_type, team_id, guardrail: (.metadata.guardrail_information[0] | {guardrail_usage, guardrail_response})}' ``` ```json { "call_type": "anthropic_messages", "team_id": "ba286a27-c5f4-4409-b131-030174819568", "guardrail": { "guardrail_usage": {"topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0}, "guardrail_response": "REDACTED_BY_LITELM" } } ``` #### Benign /v1/responses spend log 1. Fetch the spend row (listed as `chatcmpl-0f71dfda-5724-40a1-8075-5adeced0fa90`, call_type aresponses) ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:45365/spend/logs?request_id=chatcmpl-0f71dfda-5724-40a1-8075-5adeced0fa90" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | jq '.[0] | {call_type, team_id, guardrail: (.metadata.guardrail_information[0] | {guardrail_usage, guardrail_response})}' ``` ```json { "call_type": "aresponses", "team_id": "ba286a27-c5f4-4409-b131-030174819568", "guardrail": { "guardrail_usage": {"topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0}, "guardrail_response": "REDACTED_BY_LITELM" } } ``` #### Blocked request spend log 1. Fetch the failure spend row ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:45365/spend/logs?request_id=0bd456be-d8e3-4cd2-9805-fde12a10fd04" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' \ | jq '.[0] | {status: .metadata.status, team_id, api_key, guardrail: (.metadata.guardrail_information[0] | {guardrail_status, guardrail_usage, violation_categories, guardrail_response})}' ``` ```json { "status": "failure", "team_id": "ba286a27-c5f4-4409-b131-030174819568", "api_key": "05122185513749b1ce6cd6c7916fb0d5c0aa0365216f21d0b11f873b40e13753", "guardrail": { "guardrail_status": "guardrail_intervened", "guardrail_usage": {"topicPolicyUnits": 1, "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "wordPolicyUnits": 0, "contentPolicyImageUnits": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicies": 0, "automatedReasoningPolicyUnits": 0, "contextualGroundingPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyUnits": 0, "sensitiveInformationPolicyFreeUnits": 0}, "violation_categories": ["coffee"], "guardrail_response": "REDACTED_BY_LITELM" } } ``` The blocked invocation keeps its guardrail info and its billable units instead of logging null 3. Fetch the overview ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:45365/guardrails/usage/overview" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' ``` ```json { "rows": [ { "id": "036fc511-2102-5736-add6-29a0f9c0299c", "name": "bedrock-lit5650", "type": "Guardrail", "provider": "bedrock", "requestsEvaluated": 5, "failRate": 20.0, "avgScore": null, "avgLatency": null, "status": "critical", "trend": "stable", "usageUnits": {"contentPolicyUnits": 5, "topicPolicyUnits": 5} } ], "chart": [{"date": "2026-08-18", "passed": 4, "blocked": 1}], "totalRequests": 5, "totalBlocked": 1, "passRate": 80.0, "totalUsageUnits": {"contentPolicyUnits": 5, "topicPolicyUnits": 5} } ``` 3. Fetch the per-guardrail detail ```bash curl -s "http://localhost:45365/guardrails/usage/detail/036fc511-2102-5736-add6-29a0f9c0299c" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' ``` ```json { "guardrail_id": "036fc511-2102-5736-add6-29a0f9c0299c", "guardrail_name": "bedrock-lit5650", "type": "Guardrail", "provider": "bedrock", "requestsEvaluated": 5, "failRate": 20.0, "avgScore": null, "avgLatency": null, "status": "critical", "trend": "stable", "description": null, "time_series": [ { "date": "2026-08-18", "passed": 4, "blocked": 1, "score": null } ], "usage_units": { "contentPolicyUnits": 5, "topicPolicyUnits": 5 }, "usage_units_daily": [ { "date": "2026-08-18", "units": { "contentPolicyUnits": 5, "topicPolicyUnits": 5 } } ], "usage_units_by_team": { "": { "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "topicPolicyUnits": 1 }, "ba286a27-c5f4-4409-b131-030174819568": { "contentPolicyUnits": 4, "topicPolicyUnits": 4 } }, "usage_units_by_key": { "05122185513749b1ce6cd6c7916fb0d5c0aa0365216f21d0b11f873b40e13753": { "contentPolicyUnits": 4, "topicPolicyUnits": 4 }, "litellm_proxy_master_key": { "contentPolicyUnits": 1, "topicPolicyUnits": 1 } } } ``` 4. signal.title: fix(auth): return 403 for admin-only route denials
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Admin-only route denials return 401 instead of 403 - Prometheus records them as `exception_status="None"` - Those denials look identical to infrastructure failures How it solves it: - Raise `HTTPException` 403 instead of a bare `Exception` - The status code then reaches both the client and the metric ## User Flow Before: a developer holding a valid non-admin key is told their credentials are invalid, so they re-authenticate and nothing changes 1. An admin issues them a key with the `internal_user` role 2. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/policies/list` with that key 3. It comes back `401 Unauthorized`, and the message opens with "Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/users/teams" 4. Reading 401 as a credential problem, their client drops the key, signs in again, retries, and gets the same 401 5. Their operator opens the proxy metrics and finds the refusal recorded with `exception_class="Exception"` and `exception_status="None"` on `route="/policies/list"`, the same label pair an unreachable database produces, so it cannot be alerted on separately 6. A non-admin still cannot reach the route, and an admin still can After: the same request is refused as forbidden, so the client keeps its key and the metric names the status 1. An admin issues them a key with the `internal_user` role 2. They send `GET https://litellm-domain/policies/list` with that key 3. It comes back `403 Forbidden` with the same explanation and no "Authentication Error" prefix 4. Their client keeps the key and stops re-authenticating, because 403 says the credential is fine and the permission is not 5. Their operator finds the refusal recorded with `exception_class="HTTPException"` and `exception_status="403"`, now distinguishable from an infrastructure failure 6. A non-admin still cannot reach the route, and an admin still can. Who may call what is unchanged, only how the refusal is reported ## Relevant issues Fixes #37108 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup, run once against a local proxy on `localhost:4000` backed by a scratch Postgres, with `callbacks: ["prometheus"]` enabled: ```bash export MASTER=sk-1234 USERKEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4000/user/new \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"user_email":"nonadmin@example.com","user_role":"internal_user"}' \ | python -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['key'])") ``` ### Before (973329e9864154d429a7d739fb6a552fe03a9b3e) 1. Call two admin-only routes with the valid non-admin key ```bash for r in /policies/list /prompts/list; do printf "GET %-16s -> " "$r" curl -s -o /tmp/b.json -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:4000$r" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USERKEY" echo " $(head -c 120 /tmp/b.json)" done ``` ``` GET /policies/list -> 401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update GET /prompts/list -> 401 {"error":{"message":"Authentication Error, Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update ``` 2. Read the failure metric for those two routes ```bash curl -sL http://127.0.0.1:4000/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ | grep -oE 'exception_class="[^"]*",exception_status="[^"]*"[^}]*route="/(policies|prompts)/list"' ``` ``` exception_class="Exception",exception_status="None",...,route="/policies/list" exception_class="Exception",exception_status="None",...,route="/prompts/list" ``` ### After (2a0f2b6171) 1. Same two calls, same key ```bash for r in /policies/list /prompts/list; do printf "GET %-16s -> " "$r" curl -s -o /tmp/b.json -w "%{http_code}" "http://127.0.0.1:4000$r" -H "Authorization: Bearer $USERKEY" echo " $(head -c 120 /tmp/b.json)" done ``` ``` GET /policies/list -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/us GET /prompts/list -> 403 {"error":{"message":"Only proxy admin can be used to generate, delete, update info for new keys/us ``` 2. Same metric read ```bash curl -sL http://127.0.0.1:4000/metrics -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" \ | grep -oE 'exception_class="[^"]*",exception_status="[^"]*"[^}]*route="/(policies|prompts)/list"' ``` ``` exception_class="HTTPException",exception_status="403",...,route="/policies/list" exception_class="HTTPException",exception_status="403",...,route="/prompts/list" ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Clients treating 401 as "retry auth" see a status change - Master-key-only routes still raise a bare `Exception`, left out of scope - `/organization/list` and `/team/list` from the issue are already allowed for `internal_user` ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(proxy): allow internal users to view their own spend-log detail
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Non-admins get 401 clicking any row on the Logs page - A missing spend-log row silently authorized reading someone else's payload How it solves it: - Allow `/spend/logs/ui/{request_id}` for internal-user roles - Deny the ownership check when the log row is absent ## User Flow Before: an internal user can list their logs but cannot open any of them, and a missing row leaks another user's payload 1. They sign in at https://litellm-domain/ui/ with role `internal_user` or `internal_user_viewer` 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the table loads with their own requests 3. They click any row to open the detail drawer 4. Nothing renders: `GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs/ui/<request_id>?start_date=...` comes back 401 with "Only proxy admin can be used to..." 5. Another user who knows a `request_id` whose row has aged out of the database still gets that request's messages and response back from the configured log store After: the same user opens any of their own rows, and rows they do not own stay closed 1. They sign in at https://litellm-domain/ui/ with role `internal_user` or `internal_user_viewer` 2. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and the table loads with their own requests 3. They click any row to open the detail drawer 4. The drawer renders: the same GET returns 200 with that request's detail 5. Requesting a `request_id` they do not own returns 403, and so does one whose row is no longer in the database, so the log store can no longer hand back another user's messages and response ## Relevant issues Fixes #23636 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: a proxy on localhost:4000 backed by a database, a user with role `internal_user`, and at least one request logged under that user The run below covers the Logs drawer case, captured when the PR opened. It still needs a refresh at the current tip, together with a case for the missing-row denial added in 0459903 ### Before (aa587bd) #### Internal user opens their own log detail 1. Sign in at http://localhost:4000/ui/ as the `internal_user`, open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs, and click any row 2. The drawer stays empty and the proxy logs the detail call as 401 ``` INFO: 127.0.0.1:33310 - "GET /spend/logs/ui/2b8e6dc5-16d9-45a1-bcfa-312a4ee99294?start_date=2026-05-10%2006%3A22%3A00 HTTP/1.1" 401 Unauthorized ``` ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ff9c2e8-e68a-4f61-9aaf-c3dad7dd54e2) ### After (36962d0) #### Internal user opens their own log detail 1. Sign in at http://localhost:4000/ui/ as the `internal_user`, open http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs, and click any row 2. The drawer renders the request detail and the proxy logs the detail call as 200 ``` INFO: 127.0.0.1:51874 - "GET /spend/logs/ui/2b8e6dc5-16d9-45a1-bcfa-312a4ee99294?start_date=2026-05-10%2006%3A22%3A00 HTTP/1.1" 200 OK ``` ![](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c8da338a-4c40-4b74-a81c-f7f45e3dfca0) ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Admin Viewer already reads this route through the safe-method default-allow ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(model_prices): add provider-announced deprecation dates for OpenAI, Gemini, Vertex, Azure models
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 83 registry entries lack provider-announced retirement dates - `text-embedding-004` carried a wrong retirement date - Claude Fable/Mythos 5 missing structured-output flag How it solves it: - Adds verified `deprecation_date` from official retirement docs - Corrects `text-embedding-004` to Vertex's published date - Flags `supports_native_structured_output` on 3 Anthropic models ## User Flow Before: an admin running gpt-4.1 on Azure OpenAI gets no warning that the deployment retires on 2027-04-14 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models and look at their `azure/gpt-4.1` deployment 2. No retirement date is shown, because the registry has none for that model 3. They call GET https://litellm-domain/model/info and the returned model info for `azure/gpt-4.1` has no deprecation date field 4. The retirement lands with no advance notice and calls start failing with provider "model not found" errors After: the same admin sees the published retirement date for that deployment 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models and look at their `azure/gpt-4.1` deployment 2. They call GET https://litellm-domain/model/info and the model info for `azure/gpt-4.1` now carries `"deprecation_date": "2027-04-14"`, matching Microsoft's published schedule 3. The same is true for their Azure AI Foundry (`azure_ai/*`), Vertex (`gemini-2.5-*`, `veo-*`, embeddings) and legacy OpenAI (`babbage-002`, `davinci-002`, `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`) deployments 4. They can plan migrations ahead of the retirement instead of discovering it from failed requests ## Relevant issues Supports #26900 (proactive model deprecation alerts and `/model/deprecations` endpoint), which consumes registry `deprecation_date` values. ## Changes All values below come from official provider retirement/lifecycle docs; every date was read from the raw HTML/Markdown of the source page, not a rendered summary. Provider-announced dates for direct APIs were not copied to cloud-hosted variants (or vice versa) — each entry is dated only from the doc that covers that platform. ### OpenAI — https://platform.openai.com/docs/deprecations | Models | `deprecation_date` | | --- | --- | | `gpt-3.5-turbo-instruct`, `babbage-002`, `davinci-002` | 2026-09-28 | | `text-moderation-007`, `text-moderation-latest`, `text-moderation-stable` | 2025-10-27 | Size/quality-derived keys (`1024-x-1024/...`) were left alone, matching existing registry convention. ### Gemini API — https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations | Model | `deprecation_date` | | --- | --- | | `gemini/gemini-robotics-er-1.6-preview` | 2026-08-31 | The Gemini API page still shows "No shutdown date announced" for `gemini-2.5-pro` / `-flash` / `-flash-lite`, so no date was added to the `gemini/*` keys for those. ### Vertex AI — https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs/learn/model-versions (Discontinuation date column) | Models | `deprecation_date` | | --- | --- | | `gemini-2.5-pro`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` | 2026-10-20 | | `gemini-2.5-flash-image`, `vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash-image` | 2026-10-02 | | `vertex_ai/veo-2.0-generate-001`, `vertex_ai/veo-3.0-generate-001`, `vertex_ai/veo-3.0-fast-generate-001` | 2026-06-30 | | `text-embedding-005`, `text-multilingual-embedding-002`, `multimodalembedding@001` | 2027-04-01 | | `text-embedding-004` (was `2026-01-14`, not on the page) | 2027-04-01 | `gemini-embedding-001` was left undated: the page says "No sooner than May 20, 2028", which is not a committed date. ### Azure OpenAI + Azure AI Foundry — https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/model-retirement-schedule (Retirement date column) Azure OpenAI (`azure/*`): `gpt-4.1` 2027-04-14, `gpt-4.1-mini` 2027-04-14, `gpt-4o-mini` 2027-04-14, `gpt-4.1-nano` 2026-10-14, `gpt-5`/`-mini`/`-nano` 2027-02-09, `gpt-5.1`/`-codex`/`-codex-mini` 2027-05-15, `gpt-5.2` 2027-06-08, `gpt-5.4` 2027-09-02, `gpt-5.4-mini`/`-nano` 2027-09-21, `gpt-5.4-pro` 2027-09-07, `gpt-5.5` 2027-10-26, `gpt-image-1.5` 2027-06-16, `gpt-image-2` 2027-10-21, `o1` 2026-10-21, `o3` 2026-10-21, `o3-mini` 2026-10-01, `o3-pro` 2026-12-17, `o4-mini` 2026-10-16. Azure AI Foundry (`azure_ai/*`): `claude-opus-4-1` 2026-08-05, `claude-haiku-4-5`/`claude-opus-4-5`/`claude-sonnet-4-5` 2026-10-19, `claude-opus-4-6` 2027-02-02, `claude-sonnet-4-6` 2027-02-10, `claude-opus-4-7` 2027-04-06, `deepseek-r1` 2026-08-13, `deepseek-v3-0324`/`deepseek-v3.1` 2026-07-13, `deepseek-v4-flash`/`deepseek-v4-pro` 2028-02-20, `grok-3`/`grok-3-mini` (incl. `global/`) and `grok-4-fast-reasoning`/`-non-reasoning` 2026-05-01, `kimi-k2.5` 2027-01-26, `kimi-k2.6` 2027-04-16, `FW-DeepSeek-V3.2`/`FW-GLM-5`/`FW-GLM-5.1`/`FW-Kimi-K2.5`/`FW-MiniMax-M2.5` 2027-07-01, `Llama-3.2-11B-Vision-Instruct`/`Llama-3.2-90B-Vision-Instruct`/`Meta-Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct`/`Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct` 2026-06-13, `cohere-rerank-v3.5` 2026-05-14, `mistral-document-ai-2505` 2026-07-20, `MAI-Image-2e` 2026-08-15, `gpt-5.4`/`gpt-5.4-2026-03-05` 2027-09-02, `gpt-5.4-mini`(+snapshot)/`gpt-5.4-nano`(+snapshot) 2027-09-21, `gpt-5.4-pro`(+snapshot) 2027-09-07, `gpt-5.5` 2027-10-26. signal.title: fix(mcp): challenge on a bare 401 for an invalid DCR bridge envelope
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - An expired or tampered DCR bridge envelope gets a bare 401 with no challenge - The sibling gateway-session arm already relays a challenge for the same failure - A DCR client has no signal telling it where to re-authorize How it solves it: - Bridge envelope admission now raises the per-server RFC 9728 challenge with RFC 6750 `error="invalid_token"` on an invalid or expired envelope, matching the gateway-session arm ## User Flow Before: a person using an MCP client connected through the proxy in `dcr_bridge` + `oauth_delegate` mode has their credential expire 1. Their MCP client sends a request to the server's MCP route with the expired credential as the bearer 2. The response is 401 with body `{"detail":"Invalid or expired credential"}` and no `WWW-Authenticate` header 3. Their client has no machine-readable way to discover where to re-authorize, so the person has to notice the opaque failure and manually restart the login flow After: the same expired credential gets a challenge the client can act on 1. Their MCP client sends the same request with the expired credential as the bearer 2. The response is still 401, but now carries a `WWW-Authenticate` header naming the resource metadata URL and `error="invalid_token"` 3. Their client discovers the authorization server from that header and re-runs the OAuth flow on its own, or the person is prompted once instead of hitting an opaque failure ## Relevant issues Fixes #37210 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live proxy, no mocks, real `dcr_bridge` + `oauth_delegate` admission code path. Minting a signed bridge envelope requires the proxy's own master-key-derived signing keys, which only LiteLLM's own DCR flow can produce, so the envelope below is minted by calling LiteLLM's actual `mint_envelope` function directly with an expiry in the past, the same function the real flow calls, then the same envelope is sent as a bearer to a running proxy with curl. Config used for both runs: ```yaml general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 mcp_servers: bridge_test_server: url: http://127.0.0.1:9/mcp transport: http auth_type: oauth_delegate dcr_bridge: true ``` ```bash python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config config.yaml --port 4001 ``` ```bash curl -sS -i http://127.0.0.1:4001/bridge_test_server/mcp \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXPIRED_ENVELOPE" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}' ``` ### Before (9cd7696156) 1. `curl` the command above with an envelope minted 2 hours ago 2. Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized`, body `{"detail":"Invalid or expired credential"}`, no `www-authenticate` header in the response at all ### After (5da33e5b28) 1. Same `curl` command, same expired envelope 2. Response: `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized`, body `{"detail":"Invalid or expired credential"}`, and now: ``` www-authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token", resource_metadata="http://127.0.0.1:4001/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/bridge_test_server/mcp" ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only fixes the REST and connect-time admission paths. A mid-session tool call still degrades to an `isError` JSON-RPC result instead of a raw 401, since the MCP session manager serializes handler exceptions; that is a separate limitation the issue itself calls out as out of scope ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(exa): fall back to highlights/summary when text is missing
signal.text:
## Summary Closes #36905 Exa's search API only returns a `text` field when `contents.text` is requested. When a caller instead requests `contents.highlights` and/or `contents.summary`, Exa returns those fields with no `text` field at all — but `ExaAISearchConfig.transform_search_response()` only ever read `result.get("text", "")`, so the content Exa returned (and billed for) was silently dropped and callers got an empty `snippet` on every result. This PR makes `transform_search_response` fall back through the content modes: ```python snippet = result.get("text") or "

".join(result.get("highlights") or []) or result.get("summary") or "" ``` - `text` present → unchanged behavior (still takes priority). - `text` absent, `highlights` present → highlights are joined with `

` into `snippet`. - `text` and `highlights` absent, `summary` present → summary is used as `snippet`. - none present → `snippet` is `""`, same as before. ## Test plan - Added `tests/test_litellm/llms/exa_ai/search/test_exa_ai_search_transformation.py` with fabricated Exa JSON payloads (no live API key/network calls) covering: `text` present, `highlights`-only fallback, `summary`-only fallback, priority ordering between `text`/`highlights`/`summary`, empty-highlights-list fallthrough to `summary`, and the fully-empty case. - Ran: `pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/exa_ai/search/test_exa_ai_search_transformation.py -v` → 7 passed.

signal.title: feat(ui): configure the auto router's heuristic scorer from the Admin UI
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Scorer thresholds were config.yaml only, unreachable from the Admin UI - Tuning when the router escalates meant a hand edit plus a restart - The classification panel hardcoded the tier ranges it displayed How it solves it: - Adds an Advanced scoring panel for boundaries, thresholds and weights - Shows it only when the scorer actually runs - The panel's stated ranges now read the configured values ## User Flow Before: an operator who wants short prompts to stop landing in the cheapest tier finds no control for it in the UI, so the router can only be tuned by hand 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints and click Add Auto Router 2. They choose Auto Router, fill the four tier pools, then open Detailed Configuration 3. Under Classification Method they select Heuristic scoring; the only scoring control offered is Custom Technical Keywords 4. The How Classification Works card states the tiers begin at 0.15, 0.35 and 0.60, with nothing on the page able to change any of the three 5. They save, then click Test Routing and send `hi`, which comes back classified Simple 6. To move that threshold they have to edit config.yaml on the proxy host and restart it, which no amount of clicking in the UI can substitute for After: the same operator sets the thresholds in the form, watches the classification change before saving, and can hand the router back to the shipped defaults later 1. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=models-and-endpoints and click Add Auto Router 2. They choose Auto Router, fill the four tier pools, then open Detailed Configuration 3. Under Classification Method they select Heuristic scoring, and now also see an Advanced scoring section 4. They expand Advanced scoring and get three groups: Tier boundaries, Token thresholds, and Dimension weights with a slider and a number for each of the seven dimensions, every one prefilled with the value the router uses today 5. They lower the tier boundaries, and the How Classification Works card immediately restates its ranges using the numbers they just typed 6. They click Test Routing and send the same `hi`, which now comes back classified Reasoning rather than Simple, so the change is visible before anything is saved 7. They save, reopen the router from the models page, and Advanced scoring is prefilled with what they saved, with a badge on the collapsed header counting the groups they overrode 8. On a group they never touched, nothing is written at all, so that group keeps following the shipped defaults instead of freezing at the numbers displayed when they happened to open the form 9. Clicking Reset to defaults on a group and saving hands that group back to the shipped behaviour The section is offered whenever the scorer can run, so an LLM classifier that falls back to the heuristic gets it too. An LLM classifier that falls back to the default model never scores anything, so it does not. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Rig: proxy from this branch on `127.0.0.1:4610` against its own Postgres database, Admin UI dev server on `:3000`. Both direct provider keys in `.env` are out of credit (Anthropic returns `credit balance is too low`, OpenAI returns `no credits remaining`), so the tier pools point at an OpenAI-compatible gateway upstream instead. The calls below are real HTTP over the network and real spend, not mocks. Before, at merge base `d0a815d2e1`. This is the config the create form is able to build there, since it has no control that can emit a scoring key. Same prompt in both legs: ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4610/auto_router/test_routing \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"hi","default_model":"t-anth-haiku","complexity_router_config":{ "tiers":{"SIMPLE":["t-anth-haiku"],"MEDIUM":["t-oai-mini"],"COMPLEX":["t-anth-bedrock"],"REASONING":["t-anth-bedrock"]}, "classifier_type":"heuristic","session_affinity":false,"deployment_affinity":true, "escalation_keywords":["LITELLM ESCALATE"]}}' { "tier": "SIMPLE", "score": -0.15, "routed_model": "t-anth-haiku", "tier_boundaries": {"simple_medium": 0.15, "medium_complex": 0.35, "complex_reasoning": 0.6} } ``` After, at `22b8cedf98`, the same call with the boundaries the Advanced scoring panel can now set: ``` curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4610/auto_router/test_routing \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"prompt":"hi","default_model":"t-anth-haiku","complexity_router_config":{ "tiers":{"SIMPLE":["t-anth-haiku"],"MEDIUM":["t-oai-mini"],"COMPLEX":["t-anth-bedrock"],"REASONING":["t-anth-bedrock"]}, "classifier_type":"heuristic","session_affinity":false,"deployment_affinity":true, "escalation_keywords":["LITELLM ESCALATE"], "tier_boundaries":{"simple_medium":-1.0,"medium_complex":-0.9,"complex_reasoning":-0.8}}}' { "tier": "REASONING", "score": -0.15, "routed_model": "t-anth-bedrock", "tier_boundaries": {"simple_medium": -1.0, "medium_complex": -0.9, "complex_reasoning": -0.8} } ``` The score is identical in both legs, so the boundaries are the only thing that moved the decision. Note that `hi` scores below zero, which is why the boundary fields accept negative values. The same two configs saved as routers, then billed for real: ``` for r in gw-A-default gw-B-tuned; do curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4610/v1/chat/completions \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d "{\"model\":\"$r\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"hi\"}],\"max_tokens\":8}" done gw-A-default -> served by claude-haiku-4-5 | id chatcmpl-fd6ddca4-bf46-4 gw-B-tuned -> served by us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8 | id chatcmpl-c853e356-232d-4 ``` Round trip through create, reopen and reset: ``` ### 1. create the router with Advanced scoring filled in POST /model/new -> HTTP 200 ### 2. reopen the edit modal: GET /v1/model/info returns what it prefills {"tier_boundaries": {"simple_medium": 0.22, "medium_complex": 0.44, "complex_reasoning": 0.66}, "token_thresholds": {"simple": 25, "complex": 900}, "dimension_weights": {"tokenCount": 0.05, "codePresence": 0.5, "technicalTerms": 0.15, "reasoningMarkers": 0.2, "simpleIndicators": 0.05, "multiStepPatterns": 0.03, "questionComplexity": 0.02}} ### 3. save again after clicking Reset to defaults on all three groups PATCH /model/02d8c15c-87be-4688-8dfb-62a86fee440c/update -> HTTP 200 {"tier_boundaries": "ABSENT", "token_thresholds": "ABSENT", "dimension_weights": "ABSENT"} ``` Also in this branch, two things the first review round raised: - The dashboard keeps its own copy of the three default sets to prefill the controls. Nothing caught drift from `complexity_router/config.py`, so `TestDashboardScorerDefaultsParity` now pins both copies and the dimension key set. Drifting a value locally fails it. - Boundaries that decrease are now a prominent error rather than amber body text. Saving stays allowed on purpose: a router written that way in `config.yaml` would otherwise be uneditable here for every unrelated change. One unrelated fix rides along, because this PR is what surfaced it. `add_auto_router_tab.test.tsx` has two default-model-pin cases that were already failing on `litellm_internal_staging`: the pinned model is appended after every model the presets contribute, that list has reached 11, and the option fell outside the virtualized dropdown's rendered slice. CI only runs those cases when this file is touched, so nothing caught it. Reverting this branch's diff reproduces both failures at the merge base, and the fix searches the picker instead of trusting option order. It is a separate commit. Step 3 is the case worth calling out. These three keys are now rebuilt from the form on every save rather than carried through from what was stored, which is what makes Reset actually reset. It also makes the prefill in step 2 load bearing, so an absent knob prefills as unset rather than as a copy of the defaults; otherwise an operator who opened the modal and saved without touching scoring would silently pin their router to whatever the defaults happened to be that day. Screenshots to follow. --- > [!NOTE] > [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit cc9ef9204b9ba528a31ee68e02e9dc1c0f0ade38. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).
