signal.title: fix(responses): unwrap object-form tool_choice before calling the Responses API
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `tool_choice: {"type": "auto"}` reaches OpenAI verbatim - OpenAI rejects it on `tool_choice.type` with a 400 - Breaks every tool call, web search included - Cursor and Claude Code both send this shape How it solves it: - Unwrap the object to the bare string - Fixed at the validation site and the Responses bridge - Function and custom tool_choice keep existing behavior ## User Flow Before: a developer whose IDE sends the object form of `tool_choice` cannot make any tool-backed request through a model routed to OpenAI's Responses API 1. They point Cursor at the gateway and pick `gpt-5.6-responses`, a model group the admin routed to OpenAI's Responses API 2. Cursor sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with their prompt, a `tools` list, and `"tool_choice": {"type": "auto"}` 3. Back comes `400` with `OpenAIException - Invalid value: 'auto'. Supported values are: 'none', 'auto', and 'required'. ... param: tool_choice.type` 4. Claude Code pointed at the same gateway sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"tool_choice": {"type": "auto"}` and gets the same `400` 5. Every request that names tools fails this way, so tool calling and web search are unusable from both editors After: the same requests return normal completions 1. They point Cursor at the gateway and pick `gpt-5.6-responses`, a model group the admin routed to OpenAI's Responses API 2. Cursor sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with their prompt, a `tools` list, and `"tool_choice": {"type": "auto"}` 3. Back comes `200` with a normal completion, and follow-up turns can carry real tool calls 4. Claude Code pointed at the same gateway sends POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"tool_choice": {"type": "auto"}` and also gets a `200` 5. Requests that arrive natively on POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses behave exactly as they did before ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Both runs hit a live proxy against real OpenAI, model group `gpt-5.6-responses` routed to `openai/responses/gpt-5.6`, no mocks ### Before (973329e986) #### /v1/chat/completions 1. ```bash curl -s http://localhost:52741/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.6-responses", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the DJIA at today?"}], "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_quote", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"symbol": {"type": "string"}}}}}], "tool_choice": {"type": "auto"} }' ``` 2. Returns HTTP 400: `litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - ... "message": "Invalid value: 'auto'. Supported values are: 'code_interpreter', ... 'apply_patch'.", "param": "tool_choice.type", "code": "invalid_value"` #### /v1/messages 1. Same payload shape via `curl -s http://localhost:52741/v1/messages` with Anthropic-style `tools` and `"tool_choice": {"type": "auto"}` 2. Returns HTTP 400 `model_not_found`: `The requested model 'responses/gpt-5.6' does not exist`, an unrelated pre-existing gap in the /v1/messages path for responses-routed models that fires before `tool_choice` is ever validated ### After (98bfbb99d2) #### /v1/chat/completions 1. Same request as Before 2. Returns HTTP 200 with a real tool call: `"finish_reason": "tool_calls", ... "function": {"arguments": "{\"symbol\":\"^DJI\"}", "name": "get_quote"}` #### /v1/messages 1. Same request as Before 2. Returns the same pre-existing HTTP 400 `model_not_found`, unchanged by this PR: that path fails before `tool_choice` handling on both sides, so this endpoint cannot demonstrate the fix either way today ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `validate_chat_completion_tool_choice` in `litellm/utils.py` returned `{"type": "auto"}` unchanged, with a comment describing it as the Cursor IDE format. No OpenAI surface accepts the object form of `auto`, `none`, or `required`; chat completions and the Responses API both reject it on `tool_choice.type`. It now unwraps the object to the bare string, which is the shape both surfaces do accept. Two imports the function never used were dropped at the same time `_normalize_tool_choice_for_responses_api` in the chat-to-Responses bridge owns the last mile of the Responses `tool_choice` contract, and it only rewrote the `function` and `custom` forms. It now unwraps the three bare-string values as well, so a caller that reaches the bridge without passing through the validation site cannot leak the object either Tests cover both sites. `tests/litellm_utils_tests/test_validate_tool_choice.py` asserts the unwrap directly, the bridge's parametrized normalization cases now expect bare strings for the three string values while the `function` and `custom` cases are untouched, and a new on-the-wire test in the bridge's mapped test file asserts what actually lands in the request body sent to `/v1/responses`, including that the function form still serializes to `{"type": "function", "name": ...}`. With the two source changes reverted, 7 of these fail ## Caveats (if any) The proof drives curl with the exact wire payload the reporting IDE sends rather than the IDE itself; the payload is replicated byte for byte, so a GUI-driven rerun would add no signal /v1/messages and native /v1/responses with `openai/responses/*` models 400 with model_not_found on both legs, a pre-existing routing gap on the base branch that is unrelated to this change and masks those surfaces for any PR An object form carrying extra keys, such as Anthropic's `{"type": "auto", "disable_parallel_tool_use": true}`, now unwraps to the bare string and drops the extra key. That shape was never valid on the chat completions surface and previously failed upstream, so nothing working regresses ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: Batch spend is permanently lost when a client status poll records the terminal state before the batch cost job's next cycle
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Closest neighbors, neither a duplicate: #37156 covers the cost poller retiring terminal batches unbilled when the poller itself sees the terminal transition (fixed by #37205), and #37153 covered the stale sweep's handling of completed unprocessed rows. This issue is the remaining ordering: the client sees the terminal transition first ### What happened? When a client polls GET /v1/batches/{batch_id} through the proxy while waiting for a cancelled or failed batch to finalize, the proxy records the provider's terminal status the moment the client sees it. The background batch cost job skips batches already recorded as cancelled or failed, so it never revisits that batch and the spend for its completed requests is never written PR #37205 makes the cost job bill any terminal batch with an output file, but only when the job notices the terminal transition itself. A polling client (the normal OpenAI SDK pattern) checks every few seconds while the job's default interval is one hour, so the client effectively always stamps the terminal status first and the spend is still lost. In the reproduction below the job's last look at the batch was 9 seconds before the provider finalized; the client's next poll landed first, and nine subsequent job cycles plus a full proxy restart never billed the 86 completed requests Expected: the completed portion of a cancelled or failed batch is billed regardless of whether the client or the background job sees the terminal status first ### User Flow Before a (hypothetical) fix: a developer cancels an in-progress batch and polls it through the gateway until it finalizes; the gateway serves the partial results but never records any spend for them 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds, the way the OpenAI SDK polling helpers do; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and request_counts.completed 86 5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with 86 result lines carrying real token usage 6. GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} shows only the $0 batch-creation row and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows spend 0.0, permanently: hours of cost-job cycles and even a gateway restart never bill it After a (hypothetical) fix: the same polled batch is billed for its completed work within one cost-job cycle 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/files with purpose=batch and target_model_names to upload their requests JSONL 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches with the returned input_file_id and the batch starts at the provider 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id}/cancel and get HTTP 200; the batch shows status cancelling while in-flight requests keep completing 4. They poll GET https://litellm-domain/v1/batches/{batch_id} every few seconds; about 25 minutes later a poll returns status cancelled with a populated output_file_id and non-zero request_counts.completed 5. GET https://litellm-domain/v1/files/{output_file_id}/content returns HTTP 200 with the completed result lines 6. Within one cost-job cycle GET https://litellm-domain/spend/logs?request_id={batch_id} gains a batch-retrieval row with the real cost and token counts of those completed requests, and GET https://litellm-domain/key/info shows the matching non-zero spend ### Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.4-mini-batch litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.4-mini api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY model_info: mode: batch general_settings: master_key: os.environ/LITELLM_MASTER_KEY database_url: os.environ/DATABASE_URL ``` Env: `LITELLM_LICENSE` set (the batch cost job is enterprise), `PROXY_BATCH_POLLING_INTERVAL=120` (short enough to observe many job cycles; the default 3600 makes the race even more certain), fresh Postgres DB Version or commit: `b34cbb18e2` (the tip of PR #37205's branch, so the #37156 fix is already included; the base branch without #37205 loses the spend on every ordering, not just this one) Commands and their full output (key redacted; live proxy on localhost:49726, real OpenAI batch API): 1. Create a key with a user_id, upload a 2000-request JSONL, create the batch: ```bash KEY=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"key_alias":"lit5663-clobber","user_id":"lit5663-user","models":["gpt-5.4-mini-batch"]}' | jq -r .key) FILE=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/files -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -F purpose=batch -F 'target_model_names=gpt-5.4-mini-batch' -F file=@cancelleg2.jsonl | jq -r .id) BATCH=$(curl -s http://localhost:49726/v1/batches -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "{\"input_file_id\":\"$FILE\",\"endpoint\":\"/v1/chat/completions\",\"completion_window\":\"24h\"}" | jq -r .id) ``` 2. Poll `GET /v1/batches/$BATCH` through the proxy every 2-3 s (the SDK pattern). At the first in_progress poll with completed 32, cancel through the proxy: `curl -s -X POST "http://localhost:49726/v1/batches/$BATCH/cancel" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"` returns HTTP 200 with status cancelling 3. Keep polling; ~25 min later (provider batch_6a836d8e1c30819090dd7133000d6a6f, cancelled_at 14:08:31 PDT) the first cancelled poll shows `"status": "cancelled"`, a populated output_file_id, `"request_counts": {"total": 2000, "completed": 86, "failed": 0}` 4. `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` returns HTTP 200 with 86 JSONL result lines totaling 1634 prompt + 344 completion = 1978 tokens of real completed work 5. Across six cost-job cycles: `curl -s "http://localhost:49726/spend/logs?request_id=$BATCH" -H "Authorization: Bearer $MASTER"` shows only the $0 `acreate_batch` row, `spend/logs?request_id=${BATCH}_batch_cost` returns `[]`, and `/key/info` reports `"spend": 0.0` 6. Restarting the proxy on the same DB and waiting three more cycles changes nothing: still no `aretrieve_batch` row, key spend still 0.0. The exclusion is durable state, not a warm-cache artifact Timing detail from the proxy log: the cost job examined this batch on every one of its 22 cycles while the batch was non-terminal (last at 14:08:25), the client's poll recorded cancelling -> cancelled at 14:08:34, and none of the nine subsequent cycles examined the batch again ### What a fix PR should look like Two workable shapes, either is fine: - Include provider-terminal statuses in the cost job's pickup so a row stamped cancelled/failed with an output file and not yet billed still gets billed once. This needs an upgrade guard (for example a created_at cutoff) so pre-existing terminal rows from before the fix do not get retroactively billed as one spike on deploy, and it should mind the poll-page slots (MAX_OBJECTS_PER_POLL_CYCLE) so old rows cannot starve new ones - Alternatively, keep the retrieve/cancel path from stamping a terminal status onto a not-yet-billed row (stamp it only once spend has been written, letting the cost job see the transition itself) The regression test belongs in tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py: simulate the retrieve-first ordering (row already carrying the provider's terminal status, batch_processed false, output file present) and assert the job still bills it exactly once ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? litellm_internal_staging @ f04b1dad plus PR #37205 (b34cbb18e2)

signal.title: [Bug]: Named MCP authorization-server issuer mismatches protected-resource metadata
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? For a named OAuth2 MCP server, LiteLLM's protected-resource metadata advertises a scoped authorization-server identifier: ```json { "authorization_servers": [ "https://proxy.example.com/example-server" ] } ``` However, the corresponding authorization-server metadata returns the bare proxy origin: ``` { "issuer": "https://proxy.example.com" } ``` RFC 8414 requires the returned issuer to exactly match the authorization-server identifier represented by that metadata. OAuth clients that validate issuer matching therefore reject discovery before authorization can begin. Expected behavior: ``` { "issuer": "https://proxy.example.com/example-server" } ``` The issuer should match authorization_servers[0] from the protected-resource metadata. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Configure an OAuth2 MCP server named `example-server` behind LiteLLM Proxy. 2. Request its protected-resource metadata: ```bash curl https://proxy.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/example-server 3. Observe that the response advertises the scoped authorization-server identifier: ``` { "authorization_servers": [ "https://proxy.example.com/example-server" ] } ``` 4. Request the corresponding authorization-server metadata: `curl https://proxy.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/example-server` 5. Observe that its issuer is the unscoped proxy origin: ``` { "issuer": "https://proxy.example.com" } ``` 6. Compare the values and observe that issuer does not equal authorization_servers[0]. An OAuth client that enforces RFC 8414 issuer validation rejects discovery before authorization begins. ### Relevant log output ```shell ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(mcp): scope authorization server issuer
signal.text: Generated with AI ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Named MCP OAuth metadata returns an unscoped issuer - Strict RFC 8414 clients reject the issuer mismatch How it solves it: - Scope named-server issuers to the advertised server identifier - Keep root discovery behavior unchanged ## User Flow Before: an OAuth client configured with a per-server authorization server identifier rejects discovery before authorization begins 1. The client is configured to reach MCP server `example_server` through its per-server authorization server identifier `https://proxy.example.com/example_server` 2. It sends `GET https://proxy.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/example_server` 3. It receives `issuer: "https://proxy.example.com"`, which does not match the identifier it requested, so strict RFC 8414 validation rejects the metadata and authorization never starts After: the same client receives a matching issuer and continues authorization 1. The client is configured with the same per-server identifier `https://proxy.example.com/example_server` 2. It sends `GET https://proxy.example.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/example_server` 3. It receives `issuer: "https://proxy.example.com/example_server"`, which matches the identifier it requested, so it proceeds to the authorization endpoint ## Relevant issues Fixes #36479 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5681 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Config used for both legs (`qa36482_config.yaml`, booted with `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config qa36482_config.yaml --port <port>`): ```yaml mcp_servers: example_server: url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp auth_type: oauth2 oauth2_flow: authorization_code client_id: qa-client client_secret: qa-secret authorization_url: https://idp.example.com/authorize token_url: https://idp.example.com/token ``` ### Before (973329e986) 1. Fetch named-server authorization server metadata ```bash curl -s http://localhost:24817/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/example_server | jq '{issuer}' ``` ```json {"issuer": "http://localhost:24817"} ``` 2. The path-inserted variant returns the same unscoped issuer ```bash curl -s http://localhost:24817/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/example_server | jq '{issuer}' ``` ```json {"issuer": "http://localhost:24817"} ``` A client that resolved this server through its per-server identifier `http://localhost:24817/example_server` sees a mismatched issuer and rejects the metadata ### After (5ddff616dc) 1. Named-server authorization server metadata now scopes the issuer ```bash curl -s http://localhost:27461/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/example_server | jq '{issuer}' ``` ```json {"issuer": "http://localhost:27461/example_server"} ``` 2. The path-inserted variant matches ```bash curl -s http://localhost:27461/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/mcp/example_server | jq '{issuer}' ``` ```json {"issuer": "http://localhost:27461/example_server"} ``` 3. Root discovery with no server name is unchanged ```bash curl -s http://localhost:27461/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server | jq '{issuer}' ``` ```json {"issuer": "http://localhost:27461"} ``` 4. The openid-configuration alias keeps the origin issuer for JWT-verifying gateways, even with a single OAuth2 server resolved ```bash curl -s http://localhost:27461/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq '{issuer, authorization_endpoint}' ``` ```json {"issuer": "http://localhost:27461", "authorization_endpoint": "http://localhost:27461/example_server/authorize"} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - None ### Final Attestation - [x] The test asserts that the authorization-server `issuer` matches the protected-resource metadata's `authorization_servers` entry. *- Irosh via Claude* <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 5ddff616dcba8382a4b5d1692c7552f71586950b. signal.title: feat(proxy): let USE_V2_MIGRATION_RESOLVER select the v2 migration resolver
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Helm deployments cannot reach the v2 migration resolver How it solves it: - Add `USE_V2_MIGRATION_RESOLVER` env var to the existing flag ## User Flow Before: an operator wants the v2 resolver on a Helm install and has no way to turn it on 1. They read that `--use_v2_migration_resolver` avoids schema thrashing during rolling deploys and decide to adopt it 2. They add `USE_V2_MIGRATION_RESOLVER: "true"` under `envVars` in their values file and run `helm upgrade` 3. `kubectl logs job/litellm-migrations` still shows the default resolver warning, so nothing changed 4. They try passing the flag instead, and find the migration job's command takes no arguments, so there is nowhere to put it 5. Their only remaining option is a custom image or a patched chart After: the env var turns it on 1. They add `USE_V2_MIGRATION_RESOLVER: "true"` under `envVars` and run `helm upgrade` 2. `kubectl logs job/litellm-migrations` shows `Using v2 migration resolver (--use_v2_migration_resolver)` 3. The default resolver warning is gone 4. Removing the env var, or setting it to `"false"`, returns them to the v1 resolver ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes `--use_v2_migration_resolver` gains `envvar="USE_V2_MIGRATION_RESOLVER"`. Nothing else changes: the flag, its default, and both resolvers are untouched, so a deployment that sets nothing keeps the v1 resolver exactly as before. The gap this closes is that the flag was unreachable from a deployment. The Helm migrations job's container command is `python litellm/proxy/prisma_migration.py`, and that script calls `run_server` with a fixed argv, so there is no place to append a CLI flag. Every other migration-related knob on that path is already an env var, and this one was not. Worth knowing before adopting it: the v2 resolver raises on unrecoverable migration failures, where v1 returns a bool that startup ignores unless `ENFORCE_PRISMA_MIGRATION_CHECK` is set. Turning this on therefore makes a failing migration fail the job instead of passing quietly, which is the intended behavior but will be visible as new job failures wherever a migration was already failing unnoticed. ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(helm): bound the migrations Job so a blocked migration cannot stall the release
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - A blocked schema migration hangs the release forever - `backoffLimit` never fires: the pod never terminates - Operators must delete the Job by hand to recover - Unrelated gateway, backend and UI changes silently stop shipping How it solves it: - Add `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds` to both charts - Default 1800s, so a stuck Job fails instead of hanging - Guarded by `with`, so `null` restores the old behaviour ## User Flow Before: an operator upgrading the chart, whose migration blocks on the database, gets an upgrade that never returns 1. They run `helm upgrade litellm ./helm/litellm -f values.yaml` 2. The migration Job starts and its container blocks talking to the database 3. The command sits waiting on the pre-upgrade hook and never returns 4. `kubectl get job litellm-migrations` still reads `Running 0/1` hours later, with no conditions set 5. Nothing else in the release rolls out, so unrelated gateway, backend and UI changes never reach the cluster 6. The only way out is `kubectl delete job litellm-migrations` by hand After: the same upgrade gives up on its own, so the operator gets a failure they can act on instead of a hang 1. They run the same `helm upgrade litellm ./helm/litellm -f values.yaml` 2. The migration Job starts and blocks on the database exactly as before 3. After `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds` (1800 by default) the Job reports `Failed`, reason `DeadlineExceeded` 4. `helm upgrade` returns non-zero naming the failed hook rather than waiting forever 5. The rest of the release is no longer pinned behind a Job that cannot finish, so the next attempt can proceed once the database issue is addressed 6. An operator who wants the old unbounded behaviour sets `migrationJob.activeDeadlineSeconds: null` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix There is no HTTP route to exercise here, so the proof is the rendered manifest plus a live Kubernetes cluster showing the two Jobs behave differently. **1. The field renders, in both charts.** Captured at `ae3e19a83f` ``` $ helm template t helm/litellm -f helm/litellm/tests/values/required.yaml | grep -A1 ttlSecondsAfterFinished ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 120 activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800 $ helm template t helm/litellm-helm | grep -B1 -A1 activeDeadlineSeconds ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 120 backoffLimit: 4 activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800 ``` **2. A blocked migration now terminates.** Live `kind` cluster, two Jobs identical except for the new field, each running a container that starts and then blocks the way a migration waiting on an unreachable database does. The 30s deadline stands in for the 1800s default so the run is observable ``` $ kubectl apply -f before.yaml -f after.yaml job.batch/mig-no-deadline-v2 created job.batch/mig-with-deadline-v2 created $ kubectl logs job/mig-no-deadline-v2 connecting to database... $ for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do sleep 15; echo "t=$((i*15))s"; kubectl get jobs --no-headers; done t=15s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 20s mig-with-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 20s t=30s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 35s mig-with-deadline-v2 FailureTarget 0/1 35s t=60s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 65s mig-with-deadline-v2 Failed 0/1 65s t=75s mig-no-deadline-v2 Running 0/1 80s mig-with-deadline-v2 Failed 0/1 80s ``` Terminal state of each: ``` $ kubectl get job mig-with-deadline-v2 -o jsonpath='{range .status.conditions[*]}type={.type} reason={.reason} message={.message}{"\n"}{end}' type=FailureTarget reason=DeadlineExceeded message=Job was active longer than specified deadline type=Failed reason=DeadlineExceeded message=Job was active longer than specified deadline $ kubectl get job mig-no-deadline-v2 -o jsonpath='conditions={.status.conditions} active={.status.active}' conditions= active=1 ``` The Job without the field never reaches a terminal state, which is what leaves a release waiting on it. The Job with the field fails on its own. **3. The tests fail without the change.** Reverting only the two templates and the two values files, keeping the new tests, at base `f03df1bb42` ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm FAIL test migrations Job ServiceAccount resolution and pod hardening - bounds the Job with a deadline by default, so a blocked migration cannot stall the release forever - honours an operator-supplied deadline Tests: 2 failed, 72 passed, 74 total ``` The third new test asserts the field is absent when nulled, which passes either way, so it was mutation-tested separately: dropping the `with` guard so the field always renders makes it fail. ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/migration_job_tests.yaml' helm/litellm FAIL - omits the deadline entirely when it is nulled out, restoring the unbounded behaviour Tests: 1 failed, 15 passed, 16 total ``` Restored, both suites are green at `ae3e19a83f` ``` $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm Tests: 74 passed, 74 total $ helm unittest -f 'tests/*.yaml' helm/litellm-helm Tests: 97 passed, 97 total ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - The container blocking was simulated, not a genuinely wedged database connection - Default changes behaviour: migrations running past 1800s now fail - Measured healthy runs finish in about 30s, so headroom is roughly 60x - The budget is shared across all `backoffLimit` retries, not per attempt - A killed migration can leave a partially applied entry needing manual resolution - `Chart.yaml` untouched, matching recent template-only changes to litellm-helm ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(logging): preserve uvicorn color_message args during secret redaction
signal.text: ## TLDR fixes #37121 Problem this solves: - Proxy startup can print literal `%s://%s:%d` instead of the real URL - Only shows in a real TTY (colors on), so it's easy to miss in CI/Docker How it solves it: - Preserve record.args long enough to also substitute uvicorn's color_message - Redaction filter now fixes up color_message before clearing args ## User Flow Before: an admin starting the proxy in an interactive terminal can't tell what port it's listening on 1. They run `litellm --config config.yaml --port 4000` directly in a terminal (no piping) 2. The startup banner prints `INFO: Uvicorn running on %s://%s:%d (Press CTRL+C to quit)` 3. They have to already know the port from their own `--port` flag; the log line is useless After: the same startup banner shows the real address 1. They run the same command in the same terminal 2. The startup banner prints `INFO: Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 (Press CTRL+C to quit)` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix before: after: Reproduced by running the real proxy (`python -m litellm.proxy.proxy_cli --config litellm/proxy/dev_config.yaml`) under a real TTY, at the merge base before this fix: ``` INFO: Started server process [%d] INFO: Uvicorn running on %s://%s:%d (Press CTRL+C to quit) ``` With this fix applied, the same startup path prints: ``` INFO: Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:4000 (Press CTRL+C to quit) ``` Two regression tests in `tests/test_litellm/test_secret_redaction.py` cover this. `test_filter_preserves_uvicorn_color_message_args` drives uvicorn's actual `DefaultFormatter` in color mode and fails without the fix, reproducing this exact output. `test_filter_redacts_secrets_substituted_into_color_message` pins the ordering that keeps the substitution safe: it runs before args are cleared, which puts it ahead of the extra-field redaction loop, so a secret arriving through `record.args` is still scrubbed out of `color_message`. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Only reproduces when stderr is a real TTY (colors on); piping through `tee` or running without a TTY (e.g. most Docker/CI setups) masks it ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(batches): aggregate reasoning tokens and per-line pass/fail counts
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Completed batch cost/usage silently drops reasoning tokens even when the provider reports them - Nothing counts or logs how many requests inside a batch succeeded vs failed - Failures reported only in a batch's separate error file are invisible to cost tracking How it solves it: - Aggregates `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` across successful batch output lines - Counts successful/failed requests in the same single pass over the output file - Also fetches the batch's `error_file_id` (when present) and folds its failures into the count - Surfaces both new counts on the SpendLogs row the same way `batch_models` already does ## User Flow Before: a developer running a batch with a reasoning model and a mix of good/bad requests gets no reasoning-token accounting and no idea how many requests actually failed 1. They submit a 2-line batch to `POST /v1/batches` (one valid request, one with an invalid `temperature`) against a reasoning model 2. Once the batch reaches `completed`, they check their SpendLogs entry for that batch's retrieve call 3. The entry shows a real dollar cost and total token count, but nothing about reasoning tokens, and no way to tell that 1 of the 2 requests actually failed After: the same batch's SpendLogs entry tells the full story 1. They submit the same 2-line batch to `POST /v1/batches` 2. Once the batch reaches `completed`, they check their SpendLogs entry for that batch's retrieve call 3. The entry's usage now includes `reasoning_tokens` for the reasoning model's actual thinking tokens, and `metadata.batch_successful_requests` / `metadata.batch_failed_requests` correctly show 1 and 1 ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real batch submitted against OpenAI (`gpt-5-mini`, reasoning model), 2 input lines: one valid request, one with an invalid `temperature: 999` to force a genuine per-request failure. No mocks; real batch job, real $ cost. Verified at the SDK layer (`litellm.aretrieve_batch` / `_handle_completed_batch`), which is where this fix lives and where both the proxy and SDK batch-cost paths converge. ### Before (973329e986) 1. Ran the completed batch through the pre-fix `_handle_completed_batch`: ``` cost: 0.00011 models: ['gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07'] usage: Usage(completion_tokens=107, prompt_tokens=24, total_tokens=131, completion_tokens_details=None, prompt_tokens_details=None) (no successful_requests/failed_requests field exists on this return shape at all) ``` 2. `completion_tokens_details` is `None` even though the completion actually used 64 reasoning tokens, and there is no way to know 1 of the 2 requests failed ### After (02cf319b48) 1. Ran the same completed batch through the fixed `_handle_completed_batch`: ``` cost: 0.00011 successful_requests: 1 failed_requests: 1 reasoning_tokens: 64 ``` 2. `reasoning_tokens` now correctly reports 64, and `failed_requests: 1` matches OpenAI's own `request_counts` (`completed=1, failed=1, total=2`) exactly - the failed line lives only in the batch's `error_file_id`, which the fix now also reads ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Anthropic/Bedrock extended-thinking batches do not get reasoning-token estimates in this PR; that requires plumbing the raw thinking-block text through a separate code path and is left as follow-up - Vertex's raw (non-default `disable_vertex_batch_output_transformation`) response shape treats a null `response` field as the only failure signal, since no distinct error shape is established for that path ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(anthropic): preserve optional Responses tool properties
signal.text: Base branch: `litellm_internal_staging` This is a from-scratch reimplementation of Eugene Yao's #34784 on top of current staging, opened while he is out of office. Same bug and same fix in spirit, but the code and tests here were rewritten against today's `litellm_internal_staging` rather than rebased ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Optional Anthropic tool arguments come back filled with empty values - OpenAI-backed `/v1/messages` silently ignored the caller's `required` list - A tool-level `strict` landed inside the JSON schema, not on the function How it solves it: - Always send `strict` on Responses function tools, `false` when unset - Map Anthropic tool `strict` onto `function.strict` for chat/completions - Stop merging `strict` into the caller's `input_schema` ## User Flow Before: a developer whose Anthropic-style app calls an OpenAI model through the gateway gets every optional tool argument back as an empty string, so their handler branches on values the user never asked for 1. They point their Anthropic SDK at the gateway and send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with `"model"` set to an OpenAI-backed deployment 2. The request carries one tool, `get_weather`, whose schema has `properties` of `city`, `unit` and `include_forecast`, and `"required": ["city"]` 3. The model answers with a `tool_use` block whose `input` contains all three keys: `city` filled in, plus `unit: ""` and `include_forecast: ""` 4. Their tool handler sees `unit` and `include_forecast` as present-but-blank, so it either fetches a forecast nobody wanted or throws on an empty enum value 5. Sending the same tool with an explicit `"strict": false` changes nothing, because the gateway never forwarded that field After: the caller's `strict` choice now reaches the provider, so optional-argument handling follows the documented modes 1. They send the identical POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages with the identical tool 2. The gateway now sends the tool with an explicit `"strict": false`, the documented way to keep non-strict behavior, so any optional keys in the reply are the model's own choice rather than strict-mode filler 3. A caller who genuinely wants strict structured-output validation sends `"strict": true` and has it forwarded: the provider applies strict mode to their schema, and a strict-incompatible schema now gets a clear 400 naming the missing required key instead of being silently normalized ## Relevant issues Reimplements #34784 ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5676 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real-provider e2e run against OpenAI `gpt-5.6` through a live proxy, replacing the earlier stub-provider wire capture. Only `/v1/messages` inbound is affected; both of its outbound translations are covered as cases. The probe is one curl, varying only the tool's `strict` field: ```bash curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:<port>/v1/messages \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'x-api-key: sk-1234' \ -H 'anthropic-version: 2023-06-01' \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-real", "max_tokens": 256, "tool_choice": {"type": "tool", "name": "get_weather"}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Boston?"}], "tools": [{ "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get the current weather in a given location", "input_schema": { "type": "object", "properties": { "city": {"type": "string", "description": "City name"}, "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius", "fahrenheit"], "description": "Optional temperature unit"}, "include_forecast": {"type": "boolean", "description": "Optional 3-day forecast"} }, "required": ["city"], "additionalProperties": false } }] }' ``` Config: `model_name: gpt-real` -> `model: openai/gpt-5.6`, `api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY`. The chat/completions case adds `use_chat_completions_url_for_anthropic_messages: true` under `litellm_settings` ### Before (973329e986) #### /v1/messages over the Responses API 1. Probe with no `strict`, with `"strict": false`, and with `"strict": true`: all three return the identical `tool_use` input `{"city": "Boston", "unit": "fahrenheit", "include_forecast": false}`, optional keys filled every time, because the caller's `strict` never leaves the gateway 2. The outbound function tool in the proxy debug log carries no `strict` key at all: `'type': 'function', 'name': 'get_weather', 'description': ..., 'parameters': {...}` #### /v1/messages over chat/completions, tool with "strict": true 1. The call succeeds with `{"city": "Boston"}`, the provider having silently ignored the strict request 2. The debug log shows the caller's `strict` merged inside the schema, mutating it: `'required': ['city'], 'additionalProperties': False, 'strict': True}` inside `parameters`, with `'strict': None` on the function ### After (3cdf041827) #### /v1/messages over the Responses API 1. Probe with no `strict`: the outbound tool now carries `'strict': False` explicitly, the documented way to pin non-strict behavior on the Responses API; the reply's optional keys are the model's own choice 2. Probe with `"strict": false`: same explicit `'strict': False` on the wire 3. Probe with `"strict": true`: the strict request finally reaches OpenAI, which enforces it and returns 400 `invalid_function_parameters` naming exactly what strict mode needs: `'required' is required to be supplied and to be an array including every key in properties. Missing 'unit'` #### /v1/messages over chat/completions, tool with "strict": true 1. The debug log shows `strict` where the provider reads it, `'additionalProperties': False}, 'strict': True, 'type': 'function'`, on the function and no longer inside `parameters`, which goes out exactly as the caller wrote it 2. The provider now enforces the strict request, returning the same 400 for a strict-incompatible schema where Before silently ignored it ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Responses always sends `strict`; chat/completions omits it when unset - That asymmetry is deliberate: each API's own default differs - The OpenAI to Anthropic direction still drops `function.strict` On the asymmetry, so no reviewer has to go find it: the Responses adapter now emits `strict` unconditionally, while the chat/completions adapter emits it only when the caller supplied it. Sending `strict: false` explicitly to Chat Completions would be harmless but pointless, since that is already its documented default, and it would add a key to every outbound tool for providers behind the OpenAI-compatible surface that may not accept it. Responses needs the explicit value precisely because its default is the opposite ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes only affect Anthropic `/v1/messages` pass-through tool translation to OpenAI, but alter provider-facing tool payloads and can change which tool arguments models return. > > **Overview** > Fixes **optional tool arguments showing up as empty strings** when Anthropic-style `/v1/messages` calls are routed to OpenAI backends, by correctly handling **`strict`** on outbound tool definitions. > > For the **Responses API** path, every converted function tool now includes **`strict: false`** when the caller omits it, so OpenAI does not default to strict mode and rewrite **`required`** to include every property. Explicit **`strict: true`** is still forwarded. > > For the **chat/completions** path, **`strict`** is mapped onto **`function.strict`** when provided and is **excluded from the generic merge into `parameters`**, which previously polluted the caller's **`input_schema`** and was ignored by the provider. When **`strict`** is unset, it stays omitted (Chat Completions' non-strict default). > > **`AnthropicMessagesTool`** typing adds a read-only **`strict`** field, with regression tests for both adapters. > > <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3cdf041827c32b6b56e349156866edc465b33240. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup> <!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

signal.title: fix(anthropic): stop emitting empty thinking blocks on the Responses adapter
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Reasoning turns without a summary emit empty thinking blocks - Clients persist them and replay them next turn - Anthropic then 400s: "each thinking block must contain thinking" - Resuming a Claude Code session fails How it solves it: - Open the thinking block on first non-empty summary delta - Stop opening it when the reasoning item appears - Only close blocks that were actually opened ## User Flow Before: a Claude Code session that ran on an OpenAI reasoning model cannot be resumed on an Anthropic model 1. A user points Claude Code at the proxy (`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=gpt-5.6-responses`) and asks a question; the client streams the answer over POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages and renders it 2. The streamed turn carried an empty thinking block, so the client records `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "signature": ""}` in its session transcript alongside the answer 3. They reopen the session on the default Anthropic model (`claude --continue` with `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5`) and ask a follow-up 4. The client replays the transcript over POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages and shows `API Error: 400 ... messages.2.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking`; every further message in the session keeps failing the same way After: the same resume works 1. The user runs the same first turn; the streamed answer carries no thinking block and the transcript records none 2. They reopen the session with `claude --continue` on the Anthropic model and ask the follow-up 3. The client replays the transcript over POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages and renders the answer, and the session continues normally 4. A turn that explicitly requests a reasoning summary still streams its thinking block with real content first ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This only affects `/v1/messages` with a model that routes through the Responses bridge, since the empty block is produced by the Responses-to-Anthropic streaming adapter. `/v1/chat/completions` and native `/v1/responses` never build Anthropic content blocks, so there is no equivalent surface to prove on them Shared setup: live proxy against real OpenAI and Anthropic (real provider spend, no mocks), config ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-responses litellm_params: model: openai/gpt-5.6 api_key: os.environ/OPENAI_API_KEY - model_name: claude-opus-5 litellm_params: model: anthropic/claude-opus-5 api_key: os.environ/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY ``` The Before proxy runs from the merge base f04b1dadfb on port 32333, the After proxy from this PR's tip 5295da055c on port 23112. Both sides drive the real Claude Code CLI (2.1.233) interactively through the identical flow; `--strict-mcp-config` only keeps this machine's local MCP servers out of the session ### Before (f04b1dadfb) #### Claude Code session resumed on an Anthropic model 1. Commands: ```bash export ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:32333 ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=sk-1234 ANTHROPIC_MODEL=gpt-5.6-responses claude --strict-mcp-config # ask, then /exit ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-opus-5 claude --strict-mcp-config --continue # follow up ``` 2. What the resumed session shows: ``` ❯ In one word, what is 17 times 23? ⏺ 391 ❯ And 18 times 23? ⏺ API Error: 400 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"messages.2.content.0.thinking: each thinking block must contain thinking"},"request_id":"req_011Ce8x1wgBXiMuKQh62Xx3y"}. Received Model Group=claude-opus-5 ``` 3. The session file Claude Code recorded for turn 1 contains `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": "", "signature": ""}`, which is what the resumed turn replays; the session stays broken on every retry #### Wire: summary-less reasoning stream 1. Command: ```bash curl -sN http://localhost:32333/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-5.6-responses", "max_tokens": 512, "stream": true, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "In one word, what is 17 times 23?"}]}' \ | grep -A1 content_block_start ``` 2. Observed output: the empty thinking block opens at index 0 ``` event: content_block_start data: {"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0, "content_block": {"type": "thinking", "thinking": ""}} -- event: content_block_start data: {"type": "content_block_start", "index": 1, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}} ``` #### Wire: summary-producing reasoning stream 1. Command: ```bash curl -sN http://localhost:32333/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "gpt-5.6-responses", "max_tokens": 4096, "stream": true, "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 2048, "summary": "detailed"}, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "A farmer has chickens and rabbits, 35 heads and 94 legs total. How many of each? Think it through."}]}' ``` 2. Observed output: thinking block at index 0 followed by 100 `thinking_delta` events with real summary text, then the text block at index 1 ### After (5295da055c) #### Claude Code session resumed on an Anthropic model 1. Same commands, with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:23112` 2. What the resumed session shows: ``` ❯ In one word, what is 17 times 23? ⏺ 391 ❯ And 18 times 23? ⏺ 414 ``` 3. The session file contains no thinking block at all, and the session keeps working on further turns #### Wire: summary-less reasoning stream 1. Same command against port 23112 2. Observed output: no thinking block at all, the text block opens at index 0 ``` event: content_block_start data: {"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}} ``` #### Wire: summary-producing reasoning stream 1. Same command against port 23112 2. Observed output: thinking block at index 0 followed by 98 `thinking_delta` events with real summary text (`"**Solving the equations**\n\nI"...`), then the text block at index 1 QA observations, all pre-existing and untouched by this PR: - OpenAI rejects MCP tool schemas containing regex lookaround patterns - `openai/responses/`-prefixed models are unroutable via `/v1/messages` - Transcripts already carrying an empty block still fail replay ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `AnthropicResponsesStreamWrapper._process_event` opened an Anthropic `thinking` content block as soon as `response.output_item.added` reported a `reasoning` item. OpenAI emits that item on every reasoning turn, but only emits `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` when a summary was requested and produced, so a summary-less turn was surfaced to the client as `{"type": "thinking", "thinking": ""}`. Anthropic's own API rejects that block as input, so any client that persists the assistant turn and replays it, which is what Claude Code does on resume, breaks on the next request The block is now opened lazily by the summary-delta handler on the first non-empty delta, so a reasoning turn that never produces summary text produces no block at all. `response.output_item.done` no longer falls back to the current block index when the item has no block open, since with the eager open gone that fallback would emit `content_block_stop` for somebody else's block A small `_open_block` helper absorbs the allocate-index, register-item-id, queue-`content_block_start` sequence that the message, tool-use, and text-delta paths were each repeating inline, which is what makes the lazy open a two-line change rather than a fourth copy. It takes the content block as a `Mapping` to satisfy the repo's mutable-annotation budget Three test cases in the adapter's mapped test file cover a reasoning turn with no summary events, a reasoning turn whose only summary deltas are empty, and a reasoning turn that does produce summary text and must still emit the block. With the source change reverted, the first two fail. One existing case, `test_process_event_unregistered_item_id_opens_new_text_block`, now drives a summary delta to open its block, since a bare `output_item.added` no longer opens one ## Caveats (if any) - Transcripts already recorded with an empty block keep failing until they age out ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: feat(ui): add user ID request log filter
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Request Logs cannot be narrowed to one authenticated internal user - End User often appears as an opaque JSON blob containing a device ID, so it is not a usable way to find an internal user - Using the global user directory would exclude team admins and expose users outside the caller's Request Logs scope How it solves it: - Adds a **User ID** picker between Key Alias and End User - Populates it from a bounded, paginated spend-log facet containing only users from rows the caller can already read - Makes an explicit `user_id` filter intersect with the existing own-user/permitted-team authorization scope - Reuses the existing `user_id` Request Logs query parameter; no database migration or new index is required ## User Flow Before: a user with Request Logs access cannot narrow the table to one internal user 1. They open `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs` 2. They open the Request Logs filter drawer 3. They see Key Alias followed directly by End User 4. They must scan the Internal User column manually After: the same user can select an internal user from the logs they are authorized to read 1. They open `http://localhost:4000/ui/?page=logs` 2. They open the Request Logs filter drawer 3. They see User ID between Key Alias and End User 4. They search for an exact internal ID or email and see only that user's requests Proxy admins can choose users from all visible logs. Team admins and users with team spend-log permission can choose members appearing in their permitted teams. Other users only receive options from their own visible rows. Server-side authorization remains authoritative, and selecting a user can only narrow the result set. ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket Resolves LIT-5679 ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Shared setup: two live proxies against one fresh Postgres database. The After proxy runs this PR's tip and serves its dashboard build on `http://localhost:41883`; the Before proxy runs the pre-PR base on `http://localhost:41887`. Config has one model (`openai/gpt-5.4-mini`) and master key `sk-qa-36781-master`. Spend logs were seeded with three real `/v1/chat/completions` calls billed to OpenAI: two as `user_alice_36781` and one as `user_bob_36781`, both created as `internal_user` via `/user/new`. A non-admin key for bob (`$BOB_KEY` below) came from `curl -X POST http://localhost:41883/key/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-36781-master" -d '{"user_id": "user_bob_36781"}'`. Focused suites also pass locally: 65 dashboard Vitest tests, 34 backend facet pytest tests, and 5 authorization intersection pytest tests ### Before (973329e986) #### User ID facet endpoint 1. `curl -s -w '\nHTTP %{http_code}' -G 'http://localhost:41887/management/v1/spend_logs/users' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-36781-master' --data-urlencode 'filter[startTime][gte]=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z' --data-urlencode 'filter[startTime][lte]=2026-08-17T23:59:59Z'` 2. `{"detail":"Not Found"}` with HTTP 404, so the UI has nothing to populate a user picker from #### Facet with a non-admin key 1. The same request with `Authorization: Bearer $BOB_KEY` 2. The same 404 #### Logs filtered by user_id with the master key 1. `curl -s -G 'http://localhost:41887/spend/logs/ui' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-qa-36781-master' --data-urlencode 'start_date=2026-08-17 00:00:00' --data-urlencode 'end_date=2026-08-17 23:59:59' --data-urlencode 'user_id=user_alice_36781'` 2. `{"total":2}` with both rows belonging to `user_alice_36781`: the query parameter itself predates this PR #### Explicit user_id from a scoped caller 1. signal.title: No renewal path when an upstream grant has neither expires_in nor refresh_token
signal.text: ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## The Feature When an upstream token response carries neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`: - the access envelope gets `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` (3600), since `_envelope_ttl_seconds(None)` returns the cap, and - no refresh envelope is minted, because `discoverable_endpoints.py` skips that step when the response has no `refresh_token`. The result is that the client has no renewal path at all. Recovery is a full interactive `authorization_code` flow, roughly every hour, for the lifetime of the integration. Some providers issue access tokens that do not expire, and signal that by omitting `expires_in`. Nothing on the wire distinguishes this from "expires, lifetime unstated", so the gateway assumes the latter. We are not asking it to assume otherwise. The problem is what happens next: for this shape of grant there is no bounded renewal mechanism, only re-authorization. Two mechanisms already exist and neither reaches this case. **The upstream 401 relay.** For `is_oauth_delegate` servers, `mcp_server_manager` relays an upstream 401 as `MCPUpstreamAuthError` so callers turn it into a 401 with the upstream's own `WWW-Authenticate` and re-run the OAuth flow. The comment states the intent: only a 401 is a re-auth signal, and it is the caller's to resolve. That is the right design, but the access envelope's own `exp` fires first, so the upstream is never asked and the relay never runs. The gateway's locally chosen expiry pre-empts the provider's own answer. **The refresh envelope.** #32980 added refresh envelopes and scoped them to grants returning a `refresh_token`: > A new refresh envelope is re-issued only when the upstream returns a new refresh token, so the design mirrors the upstream authorization server's own rotation policy rather than reinventing it: against a rotating upstream the client rotates and the upstream detects reuse of a retired token; against a non-rotating upstream the original refresh envelope stands until its bounded TTL. That covers a non-rotating upstream, which keeps its refresh envelope for the 14-day bound. It does not cover an upstream that returns no refresh token at all, which gets no envelope and therefore no bound other than the 1h access cap. We are not asking for the access cap to be raised or removed. The constant's own docstring anticipates that argument and rejects it: > Hard ceiling on ACCESS envelope lifetime [...] matching the 1h lifetime of the > BYOK session bearer this module's signing approach is borrowed from: a client-held > credential should never outlive a bounded window even when the upstream token does. We think that is correct. The cap does not bound the provider's token, it bounds the client-held bearer, and its value is that a leaked envelope dies on its own without requiring the principal's access to be revoked wholesale. "The provider says the token does not expire" is not an answer to envelope theft. Nor would dropping the expiry work mechanically, since `exp` is a required claim on open. Give this grant shape the same treatment the 14-day refresh bound already represents: when the upstream returns neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`, mint a refresh envelope sealing the access token, and let the `refresh_token` grant re-mint a fresh 1h access envelope from the sealed grant. This seems to fit the reasoning already documented on `MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS`: > A refresh envelope only renews the short-lived access envelope, and each renewal re-validates the sealed litellm key (revocation gates it) and is re-minted with a fresh window, so the practical bound is idle time, not a fixed session. Both properties hold here. The credential is presented only back to the token endpoint rather than held as a bearer for upstream calls, and each renewal re-validates the sealed identity. The 1h client-held access cap is untouched, revocation still gates every renewal, and hourly interactive re-authorization becomes a 14-day idle bound. One honest caveat: the current refresh path unwraps the sealed refresh token and POSTs `grant_type=refresh_token` upstream, so this needs a distinct arm that re-mints from the sealed grant without an upstream call, not a straight reuse of the existing flow. A per-server override for the access cap would also solve our immediate problem and is a smaller change, since `MAX_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is read only by `envelope.py` and has no config field or environment variable today. We suggest it second because it needs an operator to declare provider behavior correctly, and because it weakens the client-held-bearer bound that the docstring above is protecting. If you did prefer this shape, `MAX_REFRESH_ENVELOPE_TTL_SECONDS` is a same-shaped sibling that an override should probably cover too. Happy to send a PR for either direction. ## User Flow Before this feature (today): - Someone authorizes an MCP server once through the gateway and starts working. - Roughly an hour later the credential is gone. There is no renewal path, so the only way back is the full interactive authorization flow. - That repeats every hour, for as long as they use the integration. After this feature: - Someone authorizes once. Renewal happens against the token endpoint without their involvement. - Interactive re-authorization is needed only after a long idle period, bounded by the existing 14-day refresh window, rather than hourly. ## How far you got Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml mcp_servers: example_server: url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp transport: http auth_type: oauth_delegate dcr_bridge: true ``` Version or commit: 1.97.0 Commands and their full output, up to the step that dead-ends: Complete the DCR flow against the server above, against an upstream whose token response includes neither `expires_in` nor `refresh_token`. The token response returns an access envelope and no `refresh_token` field. There is no further command to run: no refresh grant exists to renew with, so the flow dead-ends at re-authorization once the access envelope reaches its `exp`. What stopped me there: The client has no renewal path and must repeat the interactive `authorization_code` flow roughly every hour. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## LiteLLM is hiring a founding backend engineer, are you interested in joining us and shipping to all our users? No

signal.title: Bridge envelope admission returns a bare 401 where the gateway session path returns an invalid_token challenge
signal.text: ## Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ## What happened? `MCPRequestHandler` has two admission arms for a cryptographically valid credential that can no longer be admitted, for example because it has expired. They handle the same condition differently. `_admit_gateway_session` fails closed with an RFC 9728 challenge via `_gateway_dcr_challenge`, including RFC 6750 `error="invalid_token"` when a bearer was presented. Its own comment explains why: > A cryptographically valid bearer whose referenced user is now missing or SCIM-deactivated is an invalid_token at the requested scope: relay the RFC 9728 challenge so the DCR client re-authorizes, matching the SessionBearerInvalid arm, instead of a bare 401 with no WWW-Authenticate. `_admit_dcr_bridge_delegate`, in the same class, raises `HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid or expired credential")` on its `BridgeEnvelopeInvalid() | NotBridgeEnvelope()` arm. No `WWW-Authenticate` header, so it never reaches the challenge helper that the sibling arm uses. Without a challenge a client has no machine-readable signal telling it where to re-authorize, so recovery has to be driven by hand even though the client is capable of re-running the flow. This also seems inconsistent with the mode's own intent. For `is_oauth_delegate` servers, `mcp_server_manager` already relays an upstream 401 as `MCPUpstreamAuthError` specifically so callers can turn it into a 401 with the upstream's `WWW-Authenticate` and re-run the OAuth flow, and `server.py` converts that to a 401 preserving the challenge. So challenge-driven re-authorization is the intended recovery path for this mode. The envelope admission arm is the one place in that chain that drops it. Three merged PRs have closed the same kind of gap in neighboring paths: #30124 (surface upstream challenges for delegated OAuth), #31921 (surface `tools/list` auth failures as a 401 challenge on single-server routes), and #32741 (surface rejected delegate-auth upstream tokens as a connect-time 401, whose verification output shows the `error="invalid_token"` challenge being relayed). The bridge envelope arm arrived with #32824 and did not get the same treatment, so this looks like an oversight rather than a deliberate exception. Related but distinct: #36358 reports a different defect in the same bridge mode, where the injected upstream credential is discarded on tool calls. That one is about egress after a successful admission. This one is about the response when admission fails. ## User Flow Before: - Someone uses an MCP client that connects through the proxy. Their credential eventually reaches its expiry. - The next request fails with a 401 that carries no challenge, so the client has no way to discover where to re-authorize. It surfaces a generic failure instead. - The person has to work out for themselves that re-authorization is what is needed, then re-run the login by hand. After: - The 401 carries a challenge, so the client discovers the authorization server and re-runs the flow. - The person either keeps working or is prompted once by their client, rather than diagnosing an opaque error. ## Proof the bug occurs Config / setup the proxy ran with: ```yaml mcp_servers: example_server: url: https://mcp.example.com/mcp transport: http auth_type: oauth_delegate dcr_bridge: true ``` Version or commit: 1.97.0 Commands and their full output: 1. Configure an MCP server in `dcr_bridge` + `oauth_delegate` mode and complete the DCR flow so the client holds an access envelope. 2. Wait for the envelope to pass its `exp`, or tamper with it. 3. Send any request to the server's MCP route with that envelope as the bearer. Observed: `401` with body `{"detail":"Invalid or expired credential"}` and no `WWW-Authenticate` response header. Expected: `401` carrying a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, as the gateway session path returns for the equivalent condition. Concretely, `_admit_dcr_bridge_delegate` would emit an `invalid_token` challenge on an expired or otherwise unusable envelope, matching `_admit_gateway_session`. Scope note: this would fix the REST and connect-time paths. It would not by itself help a tool call that fails mid-session, because as `server.py` notes, the MCP session manager serializes handler exceptions as JSON-RPC errors, so a mid-session tool call cannot emit a raw 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate` header and degrades to an `isError` result instead. That looks like a separate limitation rather than part of this inconsistency. Happy to send a PR if the direction is agreeable. ## What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ## What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.97.0

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex and Anthropic each copy the whole SSE-fragment buffer on every chunk, O(n^2) in payload size - Anthropic also has no parse-deferral heuristic and can wedge forever on two concatenated JSON envelopes How it solves it: - Add a shared JSONFragmentAccumulator in litellm_core_utils/, an O(1)-append buffer with a peel-one-value primitive - Migrate both providers' ModelResponseIterator onto it instead of fixing Vertex alone ## User Flow Before: a developer streaming a large tool-call response from Gemini sees latency that grows with the size of the response 1. They send a streaming chat completion to a Gemini model with a tool whose output is a large (multi-KB to multi-MB) JSON payload 2. The response streams back correctly, but time-to-completion grows faster than the payload size does, and profiling the proxy process shows most of the time inside the JSON-reassembly step of the SSE parser After: the same request streams back in time proportional to the payload size, not proportional to its square 1. They send the same streaming chat completion 2. The response streams back with latency that scales linearly with payload size 3. The same fix applies to Anthropic tool-call and structured-output streaming, which had the identical buffer-copy cost plus no parse-deferral at all ## Relevant issues Fixes #31861 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix To be added: a live proxy run showing MCP tool guardrail evaluations and a blocked call both counted in the Guardrails Monitor, where before the fix Total Evaluations and Total Blocked stayed at 0 for MCP tool calls ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes MCP tool calls reached the guardrail hooks without a `litellm_logging_obj` on the synthetic request, so guardrail evaluations were never serialized into the standard logging object and the Guardrails Monitor reported Total Evaluations 0 for MCP traffic. Separately, a pre-call guardrail block raised before any failure handler ran, so the failure spend-log row written by `post_call_failure_hook -> get_logging_payload` persisted with `guardrail_information` None and the block was never counted, leaving Total Blocked at 0 `call_mcp_tool` is already `@client`-decorated, so the wrapper builds a `litellm_logging_obj` and injects it into kwargs; rather than hand-rolling a second `function_setup` in the raw handler, `server.py` now threads that same object through `execute_mcp_tool -> pre_call_tool_check` and into the inner `call_mcp_tool` call. `MCPServerManager` carries it (and its metadata dict) onto the synthetic LLM-shaped request passed to `pre_call_hook` and `during_call_hook`, so the guardrail bridge and success/failure logging serialize one completed record. On the Responses path, `_execute_tool_calls` in `litellm_proxy_mcp_handler.py` passes the logging object it already builds via `function_setup` into `call_tool` For a blocked call, the `except` in `call_mcp_tool` now runs `failure_handler` / `async_failure_handler` before `post_call_failure_hook`, so `guardrail_information` is populated on the standard logging object before the failure row is written. Running the failure handlers there also flips `has_logged_sync_failure` / `has_logged_async_failure`, so the `@client` wrapper's own post-raise failure logging short-circuits on `should_run_logging` and does not double-count the same logging object The source change also surfaced config-defined guardrails in the monitor endpoints; that part is intentionally omitted here because this base branch already implements it via `IN_MEMORY_GUARDRAIL_HANDLER.list_config_guardrails` and `get_config_guardrail_by_id` wired into the overview, detail, and logs endpoints, so backporting it would duplicate existing code
