signal.text: ## Relevant issues N/A ## Linear ticket https://linear.app/litellm-ai/issue/LIT-3930/clean-up-repo-root-src-layout-migration ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests (n/a: repo layout change with no new runtime surface; every move is verified behavior-identical below, and the one script touched, check_licenses.py, is itself a CI gate that was run end to end) - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (5/5) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Tracked root items drop from 70 to 63 ``` $ git ls-tree litellm_internal_staging --name-only | wc -l 70 $ git ls-tree HEAD --name-only | wc -l 63 ``` Ruff behavior is byte-identical after folding ruff.toml into pyproject.toml. The CI-gated scope passes exactly as before, and the format check reports the same single pre-existing file as the base branch ``` $ cd litellm && uv run --no-sync ruff check . All checks passed! $ uv run --no-sync ruff format --check --exclude '/enterprise/' . 1 file would be reformatted, 2082 files already formatted ``` Root-level `ruff check .` (not gated in CI) reports the same 1014 pre-existing findings in scripts/ and cookbook/ before and after; a diff of the per-file finding sets is empty The strict-rule config chain is also proven identical: `ruff check litellm --config ruff-strict.toml` reports the same 60481 findings with the same per-rule distribution on the base branch (extending the old ruff.toml) and on this branch (extending pyproject.toml), and the CI gate passes ``` $ uv run --no-sync python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging OK: every strict rule is within its codebase ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) ``` The license gate passes with the relocated cache, both from the repo root and from a subdirectory (the script is now CWD-independent) ``` $ python tests/code_coverage_tests/check_licenses.py ... ✅ All dependencies have acceptable licenses. $ cd docker && python ../tests/code_coverage_tests/check_licenses.py ... ✅ All dependencies have acceptable licenses. ``` The prometheus move is a one-line volume path swap in docker-compose.yml (`./prometheus.yml` -> `./docker/prometheus.yml`); the in-container path is unchanged ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes This takes the safe slice of LIT-3930. It deletes root files that should never have been there: a stale litellm 1.79.1 sdist checked in under `dist/` (the repo is at 1.92.0; `/dist/` is now gitignored), `qa_sticky_session.sh` which leaked in alongside an unrelated commit, the dead flake8 toolchain (`.flake8` config plus the `flake8` dev dependency; nothing in the Makefile, workflows, CircleCI, or hooks invokes it since ruff replaced it) and the vestigial `[tool.isort]` section (isort is not installed anywhere) It also consolidates configs that are provably safe to move: `ruff.toml` folds into `pyproject.toml` `[tool.ruff]` (ruff resolves both identically, proven above), with `ruff-strict.toml` now extending `pyproject.toml` instead of the removed file (same per-rule findings, proven above); `codecov.yaml` moves to `.github/` (a codecov-supported location; both the Action and the CircleCI orb auto-discover it); and `prometheus.yml` moves next to the other Docker assets in `docker/`. Separately, the repo carried two divergent tracked copies of `license_cache.json` (root and `tests/code_coverage_tests/`, disjoint key sets, zero conflicts) because `check_licenses.py` resolved the cache against the CWD; the copies are merged into the tests location and the script now anchors all of its default paths (cache, liccheck.ini, pyproject.toml, uv.lock) to its own location, so it runs from any directory and the duplicate cannot come back Just as important is what this deliberately does not touch, because the rest of the ticket as specced would break external contracts. `model_prices_and_context_window.json` and `policy_templates.json` are fetched at runtime from `raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/main/...` by every deployed release (see `litellm/__init__.py` and the policy endpoints), so those files can never move; the same fetch list pins `litellm/anthropic_beta_headers_config.json`, which means moving `litellm/` under `src/` would also break every shipped version at runtime, on top of invalidating path filters in 20+ workflows, the 3100-line CircleCI config, the Dockerfiles and every open community PR. "Embed all configs in pyproject.toml" is only partially possible: flake8 could not read pyproject (deleted instead), `ruff-strict.toml` must stay a standalone file because ruff supports only one config per pyproject and the strict gate passes it via `--config`, `pyrightconfig.json` is copied into bare worktrees by `scripts/type_check_gate.py` so embedding it needs that gate reworked first, and the budget JSONs are data consumed by the delta gates, not tool configs. `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` are auto-discovered at the root by their respective tools so an `.ai/` folder would break them, and `render.yaml` must sit at the root for Render's deploy flow. `mcp_servers.json` is unreferenced in-repo but may have external raw-URL consumers, so it stays put pending a decision on the ticket

signal.title: feat(proxy): add per-model use_local_token_counter to skip provider CountTokens API
signal.text: ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Configure two Bedrock deployments, one with the new flag and one without, then hit the token counter with `call_endpoint=true` and compare `tokenizer_type`. `dev_config.yaml`: ```yaml model_list: - model_name: claude-remote-count litellm_params: model: bedrock/anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-west-2 - model_name: claude-local-count litellm_params: model: bedrock/anthropic.claude-3-5-haiku-20241022-v1:0 aws_region_name: us-west-2 model_info: use_local_token_counter: true ``` Run the proxy, then: ```bash # no flag -> hits Bedrock's remote CountTokens API curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:4000/utils/token_counter?call_endpoint=true' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-remote-count","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello Claude, how are you today?"}]}' # flag set -> stays local, no AWS call curl -sS -X POST 'http://localhost:4000/utils/token_counter?call_endpoint=true' \ -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-1234' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -d '{"model":"claude-local-count","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello Claude, how are you today?"}]}' ``` Expected: the first response reports `"tokenizer_type":"bedrock_api"` (remote count), the second reports a local tokenizer type (e.g. the anthropic/tiktoken tokenizer) and never calls Bedrock. ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Changes Previously there was no way to keep token counting local for a specific deployment. Anthropic-format `/v1/messages/count_tokens` and `/utils/token_counter?call_endpoint=true` always dispatch to the provider's remote CountTokens API (for Bedrock, Anthropic, Vertex, etc.), and the only existing switch, `litellm.disable_token_counter`, disables counting entirely instead of falling back to the local tokenizer. This adds a per-model `model_info.use_local_token_counter` flag. When set, `_get_provider_token_counter` resolves no provider counter for that deployment, so both endpoints fall through to the local tokenizer (tiktoken/HF/anthropic-local depending on the model) and no remote CountTokens request is made. It lives next to the existing `model_info.custom_tokenizer` field, which is the other token-counting knob on `model_info`. Tests in `tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_proxy_token_counter.py` cover the gate directly (`_get_provider_token_counter` returns no counter when the flag is set, and still returns `BedrockTokenCounter` when it is not) and end-to-end through the `token_counter` endpoint (flag on -> Bedrock handler never called and `tokenizer_type` is local; flag off -> remote API used). Removing the gate makes the flag-on cases fail.

signal.title: feat: restore Agent Shin on safe triggers with staged rollout mechanics
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Follow-up to #30784, which removed these two workflows because they ran on `pull_request_target` (see also #30433, where they were introduced) ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix zizmor audit of the three Agent Shin workflows at commit 13f34623, confirming the dangerous trigger stays gone: ``` $ uvx zizmor --offline .github/workflows/triage_pr_with_llm.yml .github/workflows/review_gate.yml .github/workflows/triage_reconsider.yml INFO zizmor: zizmor v1.26.1 INFO audit: zizmor: completed .github/workflows/review_gate.yml INFO audit: zizmor: completed .github/workflows/triage_pr_with_llm.yml INFO audit: zizmor: completed .github/workflows/triage_reconsider.yml No findings to report. Good job! (27 suppressed) ``` Workflow files are only dispatchable once they exist on the default branch, so the live end-to-end proof runs after merge. Reviewer steps, all dry-run and side-effect free while `AGENT_SHIN_ENABLED` is unset: 1. `gh workflow run "Agent Shin — PR triage" -f pr_number=<open external PR> -f close=false` 2. `gh workflow run "Agent Shin — review gate" -f pr_number=<same PR> -f close=false` 3. Open each run in the Actions tab and check the step summary contains the judge's verdict for that PR, with a `::notice::` line confirming dry-run mode and no comment/label/close on the PR itself 4. Set repo variable `AGENT_SHIN_MODE=lite`, re-run step 2, and check the step summary shows `would-notify-lite` (the one-time 7-day notice preview) instead of `would-close` for a failing PR; unset the variable afterwards 5. Comment `@agent-shin reconsider` on a bot-closed PR that has no Greptile score and check the run summary shows `would-reconsider-needs-greptile` pointing the author at `@greptileai` ## Type 🚄 Infrastructure ## Changes Restores `triage_pr_with_llm.yml` and `review_gate.yml`, which #30784 deleted because they ran on `pull_request_target`. The bodies are the same as the deleted versions except for the trigger surface and the lines that depended on it `triage_pr_with_llm.yml` now runs only on `workflow_dispatch`. `review_gate.yml` runs on `workflow_dispatch` plus its original daily 09:30 UTC schedule sweep, which #30784 also deleted and which this PR brings back. Neither workflow can be fired by a fork author: `workflow_dispatch` requires `actions:write`, so only maintainers and the agent-shin bridge app can trigger them. The `pull_request_target`-specific plumbing (`EVENT_PR`, the force-dry-run branch for automatic PR events, and the conditional `OPENAI_API_KEY` expression keyed on event name) is removed, with the close/dry-run gating on `AGENT_SHIN_ENABLED` kept identical Instant reaction to fork PR events, the one thing `pull_request_target` provided that these triggers cannot, is restored by a separate Cloudflare Worker (private repo agent-shin). It receives GitHub App `pull_request` webhooks, verifies the HMAC signature, and dispatches these two workflows with the PR number. It refuses to dispatch unless the repo variable `AGENT_SHIN_ENABLED` is exactly `true`, preserving the old guarantee that an external user cannot force paid LLM calls by churning fork PRs while the bot is in dry-run. The bridge's GitHub App carries only `actions:write`, `variables:read`, and `metadata:read`, so the privileged triage logic keeps running exclusively as base-repo code inside Actions On top of the restore, this PR adds the mechanics for the staged public rollout: The review gate now maintains a label pair instead of a single label: `ready for review` on pass, `not ready` on fail, reconciled idempotently on every run so the pair always shows the current verdict Lite mode: while repo variable `AGENT_SHIN_MODE` is the exact string `lite`, the review gate never closes anything and instead posts a one-time notice that closes start in 7 days, linking the policy blog post from `AGENT_SHIN_POLICY_URL` and deduped via a hidden HTML marker. Labels still reconcile and regression comments quote the 7-day window instead of the 24h grace. Any other value of the variable, including unset, gives full behavior, mirroring the fail-safe exact-string convention used for `AGENT_SHIN_ENABLED` Reconsider on a closed PR is now held to the full reopen bar: the PR must carry a Greptile confidence score of at least 4/5 (a missing score fails fast, before any LLM spend, with a comment walking the author through `@greptileai` and the QA evidence requirements), and the linked-issue short-circuit is bypassed so the rubric's end-to-end QA evidence check always applies. A pass reopens the PR and swaps the label pair to `ready for review`. Reconsider on an open PR now runs the review gate for that PR, so an author who just fixed their description gets the tag flipped immediately instead of waiting for the daily sweep The PR rubric is tightened to match the rollout policy: bug-fix proof must show the failure before the change and the fix after, and command-based proof produced by a custom script only counts when the script source is visible in the body (a collapsible section is fine) or a linked gist The default triage model moves to `gpt-5.6-luna` Tests: 247 passing across the Agent Shin suites, including new coverage for the label pair lifecycle, every lite-mode branch (one-time notice, dedup, dry-run, regression wording, never-closes-even-past-grace), the Greptile reconsider gate (missing score, low score, dry-run, PR-only), the linked-issue bypass in reconsider mode, the model default, and static workflow guardrails pinning the exact-string `lite` comparison and the open-PR-to-review-gate routing ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

The deployment `gpt-5.6-sol-e2e` is a real custom-named `gpt-5.6-sol` deployment on the e2e suite Azure resource; the after run reaches Azure and costs real $ Before, captured on `litellm==1.86.7` from PyPI (the fix first shipped in v1.87.0; it entered release branches as a cherry-pick, so `git tag --contains` on the staging commit misleadingly points at v1.91.0): ```bash $ python - <<'EOF' import os import litellm litellm.completion( model="azure/gpt-5.6-sol-e2e", base_model="azure/gpt-5.6-sol", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "A farmer has 17 sheep, all but 9 run away, then he buys twice as many as remain minus 3. How many sheep? Reply with just the number."}], max_completion_tokens=2000, reasoning_effort="none", api_base=os.environ["AZURE_API_BASE"], api_key=os.environ["AZURE_API_KEY"], ) EOF UnsupportedParamsError: litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: Azure OpenAI does not support reasoning_effort='none' for this model. Supported values are: 'low', 'medium', and 'high'. To drop this parameter, set `litellm.drop_params=True` or for proxy: `litellm_settings: drop_params: true` Issue: https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/16704 ``` The error is raised before any network call, which is exactly why the e2e row in #33468 cannot see it: the proxy's config-file registration resolves capabilities via `base_model` on its own, so a live proxy passes this shape even on images whose SDK path is broken (verified on the v1.86.2 image) After, captured at commit 2df2c6c165 (same call, printing the response): ```bash $ python - <<'EOF' import os import litellm r = litellm.completion( model="azure/gpt-5.6-sol-e2e", base_model="azure/gpt-5.6-sol", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "A farmer has 17 sheep, all but 9 run away, then he buys twice as many as remain minus 3. How many sheep? Reply with just the number."}], max_completion_tokens=2000, reasoning_effort="none", api_base=os.environ["AZURE_API_BASE"], api_key=os.environ["AZURE_API_KEY"], ) print(f"content={r.choices[0].message.content!r} reasoning_tokens={r.usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens}") EOF content='24' reasoning_tokens=0 ``` ## Type ✅ Test ## Changes Adds four tests to `tests/test_litellm/llms/azure/chat/test_azure_base_model_routing.py` (the test file PR #28490 introduced) pinning the exact GH #31243 shape at the SDK layer: `reasoning_effort='none'` against a custom-named Azure deployment whose true model is supplied via `base_model` Two tests pin `get_optional_params`: with `base_model="azure/gpt-5.6-sol"` the param survives mapping as `reasoning_effort='none'`, and without `base_model` the gate fails closed with `UnsupportedParamsError`, so the positive test cannot pass vacuously. A `cast` is an unchecked assertion, so these move the `Any` out of the checker's view rather than proving it away; they deserve a closer read than the rest of the diff. Several `# mutable-ok:` uses were forced: the row-dump TypedDicts are splatted into pydantic models whose fields are declared `List`/`Dict`, and widening those to `Sequence`/`Mapping` introduced hundreds of `reportArgumentType` errors. signal.title: fix(vector-stores): paginate managed resource list by unified_resource_id cursor
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Managed resource listing paginated on the wrong column - `after` compared a base64 id against uuid primary keys - Pages looped and dropped resources - `build_list_page` raised AttributeError on dict items How it solves it: - Cursor on `unified_resource_id`, the id clients hold - `unified_resource_id` added as a total-order tie-breaker - Unresolvable `after` returns 400, not an empty page - List page ids read from dicts and objects alike ## Relevant issues Same bug class as #34192, in the sibling paginator ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix A note on how this is proven: `list_user_resources` has no HTTP surface today. `GET /v1/vector_stores` routes through `ProxyBaseLLMRequestProcessing` to `avector_store_list` on the router, so it never consults the managed vector store hook the way `GET /v1/batches` consults the managed files hook. There is therefore no curl that reaches this code. The runs below drive `alist_vector_stores`, the exact method that endpoint would call once it is wired up, against the real local Postgres through Prisma, with four managed vector stores seeded into `LiteLLM_ManagedVectorStoreTable` (`vs_000` oldest -> `vs_003` newest, random uuid primary keys as `@default(uuid())` produces) and a caller scoped to `user_id=lit-vs-proof-user`. A client walks with `limit=2`, feeding each response's `last_id` back as `after`. Labels are decoded from the base64 `unified_resource_id` returned as each item's `id`. Before, at `7b019cf152` (the base commit): ``` page 1: after=none -> raised AttributeError detail='dict' object has no attribute 'id' RESULT: 0/4 unique vector stores in 0 call(s) ``` Every non-empty page raised, because this listing builds plain dicts and `build_list_page` sourced `first_id` / `last_id` through attribute access. Before, at `7b019cf152` with only the `build_list_page` part of this PR applied, so the cursor behaviour is observable: ``` page 1: after=none -> ['vs_003', 'vs_002'] last_id=vs_002 has_more=True page 2: after=vs_002 -> ['vs_002'] last_id=vs_002 has_more=False RESULT: 2/4 unique vector stores in 2 call(s), duplicates=1 -> last_id did not advance, vs_002 came back twice, vs_001 and vs_000 were never returned unresolvable cursor: returned {"object": "list", "data": [], "first_id": null, "last_id": null, "has_more": false} ``` After, at `f913d42abb`: ``` page 1: after=none -> ['vs_003', 'vs_002'] last_id=vs_002 has_more=True page 2: after=vs_002 -> ['vs_001', 'vs_000'] last_id=vs_000 has_more=False RESULT: 4/4 unique vector stores in 2 call(s), duplicates=0 unresolvable cursor: raised HTTPException status=400 detail=Invalid 'after' cursor: no vector_store found with id 'does-not-exist-xyz'. ``` The second page is also proof that Postgres accepts the new query shape: Prisma really does take a `cursor` on `unified_resource_id` together with `skip=1` and a two-key `order`, and returns the four rows in reverse-chronological order across exactly two round trips. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `list_user_resources` on `BaseManagedResource` backs the managed vector store listing (`alist_vector_stores`). It carried the same broken cursor that #34192 fixes for managed batches: ```python if after: where_clause["id"] = {"gt": after} # id is a random uuid() PK ... order={"created_at": "desc"} # desc order, but gt cursor ``` The `after` value a client sends back is a resource's `unified_resource_id`, because that is what the listing returns as each item's `id` and as `last_id`. Comparing that base64 string against unrelated random uuids either re-selects the rows the previous page returned or excludes rows that should have come next, and ordering by `created_at desc` while filtering with `gt` points the two in opposite directions. The live run above shows both symptoms at once: a `last_id` that never advances and two of four resources that are never returned. The fix is the same as #34192: a Prisma cursor on the unique `unified_resource_id` with `skip=1`, plus `unified_resource_id` as a secondary sort key so the ordering is total. A cursor is only well-defined when the ordering fully determines row order; `created_at` alone is not unique, so rows sharing a timestamp can come back in an order that shifts between requests and slip through the seam between pages. Two related truncations are fixed with it. An `after` that does not resolve to a resource the caller can list returned an empty page, which a client cannot distinguish from the end of the list; it now returns 400 naming the cursor. The lookup runs against the caller's own rows, so the cursor cannot be anchored to a resource the caller cannot see: a Prisma cursor resolves by unique column regardless of the `where` filter. And `has_more` came from whether the page was full rather than whether another row exists, so an exact multiple of `limit` cost an extra empty request and a page shortened by an unparseable row looked like the end of the list. The listing now fetches `limit + 1` rows and reports `has_more` from the extra row. Separately, `build_list_page` read `first_id` and `last_id` through attribute access only. The file and batch listings pass pydantic objects so they were fine, but this listing passes plain dicts, so every non-empty page raised AttributeError. It now reads the id from either shape. Tests, all of which fail on the base commit and pass here: `test_list_resources_pagination_uses_unified_resource_id_cursor` pins the cursor, the `skip`, and the two-key order, and asserts no `id` filter leaks into the where clause; `test_list_resources_pagination_walks_all_pages_without_loops_or_gaps` walks every page the way a client does and asserts each resource comes back exactly once, newest first; `test_list_resources_has_more_false_on_exactly_full_final_page` covers the extra empty request; `test_list_resources_rejects_unknown_after_cursor` and `test_list_resources_cursor_lookup_is_scoped_to_the_caller` cover the 400 and the owner-scoped lookup; `test_list_page_reads_ids_from_dict_items` covers the AttributeError, alongside object-item and empty-page cases. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: chore(typing): clear basedpyright Any errors across 6 core files
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - basedpyright reports thousands of `reportAny`/`reportExplicitAny` errors repo-wide, most from typing seams that were never given a real type - untyped seams hide real bugs (e.g. a caller passing the wrong shape) behind `Any`, and make it harder to trust the type checker anywhere it touches these paths How it solves it: - replaces `Any` with concrete types (TypedDicts, Pydantic models validated via `TypeAdapter`, Protocols, precise repository/DB return types) in the six highest-`reportAny`+`reportExplicitAny` production files under `litellm/` - ratchets down the `reportAny`/`reportExplicitAny`/LIT001 budget ceilings in `basedpyright-code-budget.json`, `ruff-strict-budget.json`, and `type-discipline-budget.json` to lock in the reduction - no behavior changes anywhere; every fix is a type annotation change verified against the existing test suite and a whole-tree basedpyright diff ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [ ] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix This is a typing-only change with no user-observable behavior, so the proof is the type-checker diff and the full mapped test suite, not a live proxy call. Per-file `reportAny` / `reportExplicitAny` error counts (scoped basedpyright runs, before -> after this branch): | file | reportAny | reportExplicitAny | |---|---|---| | `litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py` | 384 -> 311 | 23 -> 20 | | `responses/streaming_iterator.py` | 217 -> 69 | 87 -> 36 | | `proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py` | 321 -> 172 | 27 -> 5 | | `proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py` | 319 -> 239 | 30 -> 14 | | `proxy/utils.py` | 361 -> 322 | 50 -> 28 | | `litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py` | 259 -> 153 | 37 -> 27 | Whole-tree basedpyright run (`basedpyright --outputjson` over all of `litellm/`), before this branch vs after, per severity=error rule, confirms zero regressions on any of the 39 rules basedpyright emits in this repo: - `reportAny`: 21518 -> 20921 (-597) - `reportExplicitAny`: 7258 -> 7133 (-125) - every other rule (reportUnknownMemberType, reportUnknownArgumentType, reportUnknownVariableType, reportMissingTypeArgument, reportUnknownParameterType, reportMissingParameterType, reportArgumentType, reportUnnecessaryIsInstance, reportArgumentType, etc) is at or below its baseline count, several improved as a side effect of the same fixes - total error count: 151426 -> 150440 Commands run locally to produce the above and confirm no regressions: ``` uv run basedpyright --outputjson # whole tree, before and after, diffed per rule uv run python scripts/type_discipline_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging uv run python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging cd litellm && uv run ruff check . uv run pytest tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_streaming_handler.py tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator.py tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_streaming_iterator.py tests/test_litellm/responses/test_streaming_iterator_error_events.py tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_llm_http_handler.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_team_endpoints.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/test_key_management_endpoints.py tests/test_litellm/proxy/test_proxy_utils.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_litellm_logging.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_logging_utils.py tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_logging_worker.py ``` The mapped test suite above (1024 tests across the touched files and their close neighbors) passes in full, both per-file during development and again on the final merged tree. ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes Six files, one commit each, in order: - `litellm_core_utils/streaming_handler.py`: JSON-boundary helpers (`_require_dict`/`_require_list`/`_require_str`) for the fake-streaming provider chunk parsers, `model_validate` instead of `**` splats for pydantic construction, a narrower return type on the provider chunk early-return dataclass, and a mutation-free rewrite of `model_response_creator`'s chunk merging so its parameters could become `Mapping` instead of `dict` - `responses/streaming_iterator.py`: a `PIIMaskingGuardrail` Protocol for the guardrail callback shapes used by the Responses WebSocket path, `ResponsesAPIResponse`/`ResponsesAPIStreamingResponse` return types throughout the streaming iterators in place of `Any`, and `TypeAdapter`-validated JSON-boundary helpers for the WebSocket forwarding paths - `proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py`: `PrismaClient`/`UserApiKeyCache`/`ProxyLogging` on helper signatures that were bare `Any`, and the existing pydantic mirror models (`LiteLLM_TeamTable`, `LiteLLM_UserTable`, `LiteLLM_OrganizationTable`, etc) on raw Prisma call results - `proxy/management_endpoints/key_management_endpoints.py`: the same typed-repository-model pattern, plus typed `Callable` aliases for the dynamically-loaded custom key-generate/update proxy hooks - `proxy/utils.py`: a `_McpPreCallHookResult` TypedDict for the pre-MCP-call hook response, a `_ConfigRowLike` Protocol for the config-row cache helpers, and prisma's own `DatasourceOverride` TypedDict in `PrismaClient.__init__` in place of an ad-hoc `Dict[str, Any]` kwargs dict - `litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py`: `List[CustomLogger]` for the module-level callback registry (previously `List[Any]`, used in ~90 call sites), a `LoggingCallbackType` alias, and a real union type in place of the nonsensical `Union[Any, BaseModel, dict]` on the standard-logging-payload helpers Where a raw, untyped seam had to stay (a genuinely dynamic third-party SDK shape, a Prisma feature no typed repository helper supports, or a test that mocks the raw Prisma table method directly so a typed helper's `model_validate` would break against a `MagicMock`), it's marked `# any-ok: <reason>` rather than left as a silent `Any`. A handful of `isinstance` checks and one `.dict()` fallback became statically provable once their inputs were typed but stay load-bearing at runtime (mocked test doubles, a pydantic-v1-compat branch that can't execute under this repo's `pydantic>=2.10.0` pin); those are marked `# pyright: ignore[<rule>]` with a reason instead of deleted. `basedpyright-code-budget.json`, `ruff-strict-budget.json`, and `type-discipline-budget.json` are updated (via `make lint-budget-update`) to ratchet their ceilings down by exactly what this branch fixed. ### Final Attestation - [ ] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(anthropic): buffer streamed responses carrying server-fulfilled tools so retrieval tool calls never reach the client
signal.text: ## Description ## TLDR Problem this solves: - When the Headroom guardrail (or compression interception) compresses a streaming `/v1/messages` request and injects its retrieval tool, the model's `headroom_retrieve` tool_use streams straight to the client. Claude Code fails the turn with `Error: No such tool available: headroom_retrieve` because the tool only exists server-side - The server-side retrieval rerun does happen, but its answer is appended as a second `message_start ... message_stop` after the first message's `message_stop`, a spot no Anthropic SSE client ever reads. The user pays for an upstream call whose output is thrown away How it solves it: - `CustomLogger` gains `server_fulfilled_tool_names`; the Headroom guardrail declares `headroom_retrieve` and compression interception declares `litellm_content_retrieve` - When a streaming Anthropic Messages request carries one of those tools, `AgenticAnthropicStreamingIterator` buffers the upstream message instead of forwarding it live, emitting SSE `ping` events every 15s (through both the upstream message and the retrieval rerun) so client stall watchdogs stay quiet. If the agentic loop replaces the message, only the follow-up response is streamed and the buffered tool_use message is dropped; if no interception fires, the buffer replays byte-identical - If retrieval never replaces a message that does hold a server-fulfilled tool_use, the turn ends on an SSE `error` event rather than replaying the tool call, so the unknown-tool failure cannot come back through the fallback path - Requests without a server-fulfilled tool keep true live streaming, and the websearch interception stream-conversion path is untouched ## User Flow Before: the flow fails at step 4, where the session errors on a tool the user never configured 1. A Claude Code user points `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at a LiteLLM gateway that has the Headroom compression guardrail enabled; every turn is `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with `"stream": true` 2. Once the conversation grows, the gateway compresses older history into markers; turns keep streaming normally 3. On a later turn the assistant says it will recover compressed context, and the stream ends with `stop_reason: "tool_use"` naming `headroom_retrieve` 4. The session shows `Error: No such tool available: headroom_retrieve`, the turn is wasted, and the model re-derives the lost context by re-reading files 5. The user is also billed for a follow-up model call whose corrected answer never appears anywhere in their session After: the flow succeeds at step 3 with one clean streamed answer 1. A Claude Code user points `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at a LiteLLM gateway that has the Headroom compression guardrail enabled; every turn is `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/messages` with `"stream": true` 2. Once the conversation grows, the gateway compresses older history into markers; turns keep streaming normally 3. On a later turn the connection carries only `ping` events for a few seconds while the gateway recovers the compressed content server-side 4. The reply arrives as a single normal message that already incorporates the recovered context; no unknown-tool error and nothing billed that the user cannot see ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live local proxy, real Anthropic API (claude-haiku-4-5), Headroom compression service stubbed at `127.0.0.1:47311` because the real one is a private deployment; the stub replaces the first user turn with a marker carrying `hash=a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2` and serves `/v1/retrieve/{hash}` back ```bash curl -sS -N http://127.0.0.1:<proxy-port>/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-local-headroom-test" \ -H "content-type: application/json" \ -H "anthropic-version: 2023-06-01" \ -d '{ "model": "claude-haiku-4-5", "max_tokens": 300, "stream": true, "system": "You are a helpful assistant.", "messages": [ {"role": "user", "content": "Remember this: the launch code is OCTOPUS-7734."}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Noted."}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is the launch code? If you see a compression marker instead of the original text, use the headroom_retrieve tool with its hash to recover the original content first, then answer with just the code."} ] }' ``` Before (proxy at `litellm_internal_staging` 1bafdb3c93): the client receives the `headroom_retrieve` tool_use message, then an illegal second message after `message_stop` ``` 0.96s event: content_block_start 0.96s data: {"type":"content_block_start","index":0,"content_block":{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Tm...","name":"headroom_retrieve","input":{}}} 1.15s event: message_delta 1.15s data: {"type":"message_delta","delta":{"stop_reason":"tool_use",...}} 1.15s event: message_stop 1.59s event: message_start <- second message the client never reads 1.59s data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"text_delta","text":"The launch code is **OCTOP"}} 1.63s event: message_stop ``` This is exactly what a real Claude Code session shows as `Error: No such tool available: headroom_retrieve` right after the model says it will retrieve compressed context After (proxy at this branch, e4c2ad4627, whose hold-back happy path is unchanged by the later commits): pings while the retrieval loop runs, then one clean message with the recovered answer ``` 1.32s event: ping 1.97s event: ping 2.00s event: message_start 2.00s event: content_block_start 2.00s data: {"type":"content_block_delta","index":0,"delta":{"type":"text_delta","text":"OCTOPUS-7734"}} 2.00s event: message_delta {"stop_reason":"end_turn"} 2.00s event: message_stop ``` Control (same request with `x-headroom-bypass: true`, so no tool is injected): first byte at 0.50s with text deltas spread over the stream, proving untouched requests keep true live streaming ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/integrations/custom_logger.py`: new `server_fulfilled_tool_names` class attribute (default empty) so any interception callback can declare tools it answers server-side - `litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/headroom/headroom.py`: declares `headroom_retrieve` - `litellm/integrations/compression_interception/handler.py`: declares `litellm_content_retrieve` - `litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py`: `_server_fulfilled_tools_in_request` intersects the request tools with registered callbacks' declared names and passes `hold_back` plus those names to the agentic streaming iterator - `litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/messages/agentic_streaming_iterator.py`: hold-back mode drains upstream in a background task, runs the hooks in a second one, and awaits each follow-up chunk in a third, emitting `ping` SSE events every 15s (below common 20s zero-byte client watchdogs) whenever none of them has produced a byte yet, then streams only the follow-up response, replays the buffer verbatim, or emits an SSE `error` when the buffer still holds a server-fulfilled tool_use; `aclose` cancels all three tasks - `litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py`: a keepalive ping no longer counts as a delivered chunk, so a client that disconnects after only pings still gets its budget reservation reconciled instead of holding the worst-case reservation until the counter expires, unless the hold-back buffer already holds provider output that the client paid for but never saw - `litellm/constants.py`: the ping frame lives in one place now, shared by the iterator, the proxy generator, and the existing SSE keepalive wrapper - Tests: hold-back leak regression, verbatim replay, ping keepalive timing across upstream, hooks, and a slow follow-up stream, upstream and follow-up error propagation, error-instead-of-replay on hook crash and on no-op hooks, client-owned tool_use still replayed, task cancellation on close, budget reconciliation after a ping-only disconnect, plus gate unit tests and declaration wiring checks Nested reruns are safe by construction: the retrieval rerun re-enters the same handler, so if its tools still carry the retrieval tool the follow-up stream is held back too, and if the loop's depth or fingerprint guard trips instead, the outer buffer takes the SSE `error` path ## QA runbook 1. Write a stub compression service that answers `POST /v1/compress` by replacing message content with `[COMPRESSED by Headroom. Recover the original text by calling the headroom_retrieve tool with hash=a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2]` (same row count) and `GET /v1/retrieve/a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2` with `{"original_content": "The launch code is OCTOPUS-7734."}`; run it on a free port 2. Proxy config: one `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` model plus `guardrails: [{guardrail_name: headroom-compress, litellm_params: {guardrail: headroom, mode: pre_call, default_on: true, api_base: http://127.0.0.1:<stub-port>}}]` 3. Boot `python litellm/proxy/proxy_cli.py --config <config> --port <port> --detailed_debug` on this branch and run the curl above 4. Expect only `ping` events followed by a single message whose text contains `OCTOPUS-7734`; fail the QA if any `tool_use` block or a second `message_start` appears 5. Re-run with `-H "x-headroom-bypass: true"` and expect an ordinary live stream with no injected pings before `message_start` beyond upstream's own ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/a11f814e7c18431fad858ea4e7953f0f Requested by: @mateo-berri

signal.title: chore(typing): clear basedpyright Any errors across proxy, rag and mcp modules
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - 17311 `reportAny` errors hide real type bugs - Untyped Prisma seams leak `Any` into every caller - JSON and SSE payloads carry no declared shape How it solves it: - Protocols for the untyped Prisma table actions - TypedDicts for JSON, SSE and provider payloads - Precise parameter and return types on helpers - 453 fewer `reportAny`, 27 fewer `reportExplicitAny` ## User Flow This is a typing-only change, so there is no user-visible flow difference. Runtime behavior is identical before and after: same requests, same responses, same status codes, same logs. The two verification lenses described under Changes were run specifically to confirm that ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [ ] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) No new tests are added on purpose. Nothing here changes behavior, so a test that passes after this PR would have passed before it, and the repo's guidance is that a test which cannot fail is worse than no test. The mapped suites for all eight files were run instead, and they are the regression net: 1011 passing tests across the MCP server, memory, cache settings, CLI auth, RAG and websearch interception suites ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured at commit `1ac37000` The gate is the proof that matters for a typing change, and it is reproducible in one command against the whole tree: ``` $ make check ... uv run --no-sync python scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging OK: every strict rule is within its codebase ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) uv run --no-sync python scripts/type_discipline_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging OK: every LIT rule is within its codebase ceiling (base origin/litellm_internal_staging) uv run --no-sync python scripts/type_check_gate.py --base origin/litellm_internal_staging OK: every rule is within its basedpyright limit or no higher than base (147151 errors total) uv run --no-sync basedpyright tests/e2e 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes cd litellm && uv run --no-sync ruff check . All checks passed! [from litellm import *] OK! no issues! ``` For the behavior side I did not stand up a live proxy, since spending real provider credit was not something this change needed and none of it should move. If you want end to end confirmation before merging, these hit the four surfaces the diff actually touches, against a proxy on `localhost:4000`: 1. `curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model": "gpt-5", "input": "say hi", "background": true}'` then poll the returned id with `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/responses/<id> -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` until it reports `completed`, which exercises the background streaming path 2. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/cache/settings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` and then `curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/cache/settings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type": "redis", "ttl": 600}'`, expecting the saved settings echoed back 3. `curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:4000/memory -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key": "k1", "value": "v1"}'` followed by `curl -sS "http://localhost:4000/memory?key=k1" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"`, expecting the row back with its id 4. `curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/mcp/server -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234"` for the MCP server list, which is the largest of the retyped db call sites ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Changes Eight files under `litellm/` were picked by combined `reportAny` plus `reportExplicitAny` count and retyped at the seam rather than at the call site, so the type flows outward instead of being asserted repeatedly. The four biggest offenders in the tree, `proxy_server.py`, `proxy/utils.py`, `litellm_logging.py` and `main.py`, were deliberately left alone: they are god objects in the five to fifteen thousand line range where a typing sweep cannot be made safe in a single pass, and a clean zero regression result was worth more than a bigger number Per rule, repo-wide, counting only in-tree `severity=error` diagnostics: | rule | before | after | delta | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | reportAny | 17311 | 16858 | -453 | | reportExplicitAny | 5892 | 5865 | -27 | | reportUnknownVariableType | 22386 | 22357 | -29 | | reportUnknownParameterType | 13813 | 13795 | -18 | | reportUnknownMemberType | 28725 | 28708 | -17 | | reportMissingParameterType | 3905 | 3892 | -13 | | reportMissingTypeArgument | 10999 | 10987 | -12 | | reportUnknownArgumentType | 35720 | 35712 | -8 | | total errors | 147728 | 147151 | -577 | Every other rule is unchanged, and no rule anywhere in the tree went up. Both passes were measured with the same command in the same frozen environment, since installed packages change what basedpyright can prove and counts from two differently provisioned venvs are not comparable Per file, `reportAny` and `reportExplicitAny`: | file | reportAny | reportExplicitAny | | --- | --- | --- | | `proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/sampling_handler.py` | 93 to 2 | 3 to 1 | | `rag/ingestion/s3_vectors_ingestion.py` | 86 to 2 | 3 to 0 | | `proxy/response_polling/background_streaming.py` | 79 to 2 | 1 to 0 | | `proxy/memory/memory_endpoints.py` | 71 to 4 | 8 to 0 | | `proxy/_experimental/mcp_server/db.py` | 79 to 34 | 1 to 1 | | `proxy/client/cli/commands/auth.py` | 67 to 19 | 14 to 6 | | `proxy/management_endpoints/cache_settings_endpoints.py` | 72 to 44 | 2 to 1 | | `integrations/websearch_interception/handler.py` | 88 to 75 | 10 to 6 | The shape of the work differs by file. In `mcp_server/db.py` the whole file was reading Prisma rows through an untyped client, so seven Protocols now describe the table actions the module actually calls and one accessor per table is the single place the untyped client is touched; every read and write site downstream holds a real row. `memory_endpoints.py` and `cache_settings_endpoints.py` got the same treatment on a smaller scale. In `background_streaming.py` the SSE event, output item and terminal response payloads became TypedDicts, which let every previously bare parameter take a real annotation and made an existing `cast` unnecessary. `s3_vectors_ingestion.py` gained TypedDicts for the S3 Vectors request and response bodies plus declared types for the config derived attributes. `sampling_handler.py` had one root cause behind 91 of its errors: a `dict[str, Any]` payload splatted into `acompletion` at three call sites, so each of roughly 45 keyword parameters was fed an `Any`. `auth.py` got TypedDicts for the CLI SSO payloads Some `Any` was left in place on purpose, which is why three files are not near zero. In `cache_settings_endpoints.py` the settings dict is unpacked into `Cache(**settings)`, and typing it as `dict[str, object]` trades 43 `reportAny` for 43 `reportArgumentType` while validating it into a model would silently drop the extra keys that flow into `Cache`'s kwargs today, a real behavior change. The remaining cases in `websearch_interception/handler.py` and `db.py` are the same pattern or genuine untyped boundaries. Trading one error class for another, or buying a lower count with a behavior change, is not worth it Two things a reviewer should look at. First, `litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py` is not in the diff but gains four `reportUnknownArgumentType` diagnostics, because giving `background_streaming_task` real parameter types makes arguments checkable that an untyped signature had been masking. Those four point at a real pre-existing problem, the untyped `proxy_server` module globals, and the rule is still down 8 across the tree. I tried absorbing them with typed locals at the call site and it made that file worse, since `Unknown` propagates differently from `Any`; reverting the annotations instead would cost roughly 20 errors in `background_streaming.py` to hide 4 here. Second, `s3_vectors_ingestion.py` now raises if the signed request helper returns `None`. That branch is unreachable today and exists because `AsyncHTTPHandler.put/post/get` infer `httpx.Response | None`, an artifact of `_raise_masked_async_error` being annotated `-> None` when it always raises. Fixing that annotation to `NoReturn` is the right root fix and is deliberately out of scope here, since it re-infers the return type of every async HTTP call in the codebase No `cast()`, no `# type: ignore`, no `# pyright: ignore`, no `# noqa`, no `# any-ok`, and no new `Any` appear on any added line. Three files dropped their `Any` import entirely and one dropped `cast`. Budgets were ratcheted with `make lint-budget-update`: basedpyright by 577 errors across 48 rules, ruff strict by 38 and the LIT rules by 30 The diff was also reviewed by two independent adversarial passes, one hunting banned constructs and mutable-collection annotations and one hunting runtime behavior changes at every altered line and call site. The first found real issues, all fixed in this branch before the commit; the second came back clean ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01NwfMWk97UM4pWnpdzX2zMZ)_

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Backend Any counts keep drifting toward their basedpyright ceilings - 16 hotspot files carried 1,328 reportAny/reportExplicitAny errors How it solves it: - Real types at each Any seam: TypedDicts, Protocols, precise annotations - Zero casts, zero ignores, zero new Anys; the only suppression comments are five `writable-ok` reasons on log-payload fields the logging integration overwrites by design, required by the LIT012 rule that landed on staging mid-review - Ratchets all three lint budgets down so the headroom cannot grow back ## User Flow This PR has no end-user symptom: it is a typing-only refactor with byte-identical runtime behavior, so Before and After are the same flow. The risk it removes is latent and lands on contributors, where Any-typed seams in these 16 files let the type checker approve real mistakes unchecked. Before: a proxy admin manages keys and users with no visible problem 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate with a team id and get back a `sk-...` key 2. They send GET https://litellm-domain/user/info?user_id=their-user and see that user's keys and teams 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"tags": ["free"]` and the request routes to the tagged deployment After: the same admin does the same three steps and sees byte-identical responses 1. They send POST https://litellm-domain/key/generate with a team id and get back a `sk-...` key 2. They send GET https://litellm-domain/user/info?user_id=their-user and see that user's keys and teams 3. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with `"tags": ["free"]` and the request routes to the tagged deployment ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Whole-tree basedpyright at cb65bf08b8 versus its merge base 0ca0fa22b8, measured with the exact command the CI gate runs, counting severity=error diagnostics in-tree: ``` rule before after delta reportAny 15,496 14,523 -973 reportExplicitAny 5,356 5,102 -254 all rules combined 145,547 143,989 -1,558 ``` No basedpyright rule increased, repo-wide or in any individual file. `make lint-budget-update` output after merging litellm_internal_staging (fdd72b5b23) into the branch, confirming the fixes are real and the ceilings now hold them: ``` Ratcheted basedpyright limits down by 1548 errors this branch fixed across 48 rules Ratcheted strict-rule limits down by 75 violations this branch fixed Ratcheted LIT-rule limits down by 240 violations this branch fixed ``` The staging merge also adopts the LIT012 rule that landed upstream mid-review: all 183 TypedDict fields this PR introduced are now `ReadOnly[...]`, and the handful of post-construction writes that rule surfaced were rewritten as one-shot construction with no behavior change. `make check` is green end to end, both at cb65bf08b8 and at the merge commit: ruff, ruff-strict gate, type-discipline gate, basedpyright gate, `from litellm import *` safety, circular import check, and dashboard type sync. The mapped test suites for every touched module pass: 1,720 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failures pre-merge, and the suites for every module re-touched during the merge (runwayml videos, the logging integration, google_genai adapters, context management editors, guardrail translation, tag routing) pass post-merge: 465 tests, 0 failures ## Type 🧹 Refactoring ## Caveats (if any) - Roughly 200 target errors remain in the touched files: each needs cast or ignore, which this PR bans - A few laundering helpers annotate raw Prisma/SQL rows; schema changes could stale them silently - Five log-payload TypedDict fields opt out of `ReadOnly` via `writable-ok`: the logging integration overwrites them on deep-copied payloads by design, and making those flows fully functional is out of scope here ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit 6ab6e4fa7a3284b498d36311cd4a587901bc6e66. signal.title: fix(responses): stop the chat completions bridge from leaking unknown request fields
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Codex CLI against a chat-completions-only backend 400s on every turn - The /v1/responses bridge forwards unknown client fields (client_metadata, custom_metadata) verbatim - Spec-valid params like prompt_cache_key and text.verbosity were silently lost instead How it solves it: - The bridge now only forwards litellm params and valid chat completion params - Unknown client-only fields are dropped and logged, matching the native responses path - prompt_cache_key, prompt_cache_retention, safety_identifier, service_tier, metadata and text.verbosity are now mapped through - store, prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention now reach the wire on plain /v1/chat/completions too ## User Flow Before: a Codex CLI user pointing at a proxy whose model is a chat-completions-only backend gets a 400 on every turn 1. They set `base_url = "http://localhost:4000/v1"` and `wire_api = "responses"` for their provider in `~/.codex/config.toml` and run `codex exec "Create hello.txt containing 'bridge works'"` 2. Codex sends POST http://localhost:4000/v1/responses with its usual payload, which includes a `client_metadata` field 3. The turn fails with `400: Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "client_metadata": Cannot find field.` and Codex prints an ERROR instead of doing the task 4. Retrying never helps because every Codex request carries that field After: the same Codex run completes because client-only fields never reach the backend 1. They set `base_url = "http://localhost:4000/v1"` and `wire_api = "responses"` for their provider in `~/.codex/config.toml` and run `codex exec "Create hello.txt containing 'bridge works'"` 2. Note: current litellm_internal_staging HEAD cannot boot the proxy under the locked fastapi 0.141.1 (missing `get_flat_dependant`); both runs had the one-file boot fix from the unmerged branch `litellm_fix_management_v1_flat_dependant` applied locally, which is unrelated to request handling Config used (a chat-completions-only deployment, `drop_params: True` on, exactly as an affected user would have): ```yaml model_list: - model_name: codex-bridge litellm_params: model: openai/google/gemini-2.5-flash api_base: https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>/locations/global/endpoints/openapi api_key: os.environ/VERTEX_OPENAI_TOKEN use_chat_completions_api: true additional_drop_params: ["prompt_cache_key", "prompt_cache_retention", "safety_identifier"] general_settings: master_key: sk-1234 litellm_settings: drop_params: True ``` **Before, at commit cb211b5f7c** (base of this branch), the exact request the latest Codex (0.135.0) shape produces, against Google's strict Generative Language OpenAI-compat endpoint: ``` curl -sS http://localhost:4000/v1/responses \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "User-Agent: codex_cli_rs/0.135.0" \ -d '{"model": "codex-bridge", "instructions": "You are Codex, a coding agent.", "input": [{"type": "message", "role": "user", "content": [{"type": "input_text", "text": "Reply with exactly: bridge-ok"}]}], "tool_choice": "auto", "parallel_tool_calls": false, "store": false, "stream": false, "include": ["reasoning.encrypted_content"], "prompt_cache_key": "codex-qa-session-1", "text": {"verbosity": "low"}, "client_metadata": {"x-codex-turn-metadata": "{\"turn\":1}"}, "custom_metadata": {"team": "qa"}}' ``` ``` {"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - Error code: 400 - [{'error': {'code': 400, 'message': 'Invalid JSON payload received. HTTP_STATUS:400 ``` Same commit against the more tolerant Vertex AI OpenAI-compat endpoint returns 200 but the debug log proves the leak still goes over the wire: ``` 'extra_body': {'client_metadata': {'x-codex-turn-metadata': '{"turn":1}'}, 'custom_metadata': {'team': 'qa'}, ... ``` **After, at commit 31a40571e1**, the identical curl returns 200 with the model reply: ``` {"id":"resp_...","object":"response","output":[{"type":"message","id":"...","status":"completed","role":"assistant", "content":[{"type":"output_text","text":"bridge-ok","annotations":[]}],...}],"status":"completed",...} HTTP_STATUS:200 ``` and the debug log shows the guard working instead of the leak: ``` Responses API to chat completion bridge dropped unsupported params: ('client_metadata', 'custom_metadata') ``` **Real Codex CLI end to end, at commit 31a40571e1** (`CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codex-qa-home LITELLM_API_KEY=sk-1234 codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox workspace-write "Create a file named hello.txt containing the single line 'bridge works', then read it back and tell me its contents."`): ``` OpenAI Codex v0.135.0 model: codex-bridge / provider: litellm codex Okay, I'll create `hello.txt` and then read its contents. exec /bin/zsh -lc "echo 'bridge works' > hello.txt" succeeded exec /bin/zsh -lc 'cat hello.txt' succeeded: bridge works codex The file `hello.txt` contains the line "bridge works". tokens used: 138 ``` The proxy log for that session shows Codex really sent the field on every turn and the bridge dropped it every time: ``` $ grep -o "dropped unsupported params: ([^)]*)" litellm.log | sort | uniq -c 3 dropped unsupported params: ('client_metadata',) ``` One caveat surfaced during QA: Google's Generative Language compat endpoint also rejects the spec-valid `prompt_cache_key` this PR now forwards. Backends that reject valid OpenAI chat params can opt out per deployment with `additional_drop_params`, as in the config above; tolerant spec-compliant backends need nothing ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes - `litellm/responses/litellm_completion_transformation/handler.py`: residual kwargs are filtered against litellm params + `OPENAI_CHAT_COMPLETION_PARAMS` + provider credential keys (plus `extra_body`, `drop_params`, `additional_drop_params` and friends) before being splatted into `litellm.completion`; anything else is dropped with a debug log. `allowed_openai_params` entries always survive, and `extra_body` remains the verbatim escape hatch. signal.title: fix: let s3_bucket_name reach litellm_params
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `s3_bucket_name` in a model's `litellm_params` is silently dropped - Bedrock batch output cannot be downloaded without an env var - `gcs_bucket_name` works, so Vertex users never hit this How it solves it: - Adds `s3_bucket_name` to `OPTIONAL_KWARGS_KEYS` - One-line change, plus a regression test ## User Flow Before: someone running Claude batch jobs on Bedrock configures the bucket on the model, submits a job that completes, and then cannot fetch the results 1. They set `s3_bucket_name` on their Bedrock deployment in `config.yaml` and start the proxy with no `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` in the environment 2. They `POST /v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and a JSONL of requests, and get a file ID back 3. They `POST /v1/batches` with that file ID, and get a batch ID back 4. They poll `GET /v1/batches/{id}` until it reports `completed`, with an empty failure message and no error file 5. They `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and get `500 {"error":{"message":"S3 bucket_name is required. Set 's3_bucket_name' in proxy config or AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME for Bedrock file content retrieval."}}` 6. The results are unreachable through the gateway even though the job succeeded and was billed, and the only way out is to restart the proxy with the environment variable set After: the same configuration works, and the results come back 1. They set `s3_bucket_name` on their Bedrock deployment in `config.yaml` and start the proxy with no `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` in the environment 2. They `POST /v1/files` with `purpose=batch` and a JSONL of requests, and get a file ID back 3. They `POST /v1/batches` with that file ID, and get a batch ID back 4. They poll `GET /v1/batches/{id}` until it reports `completed`, with an empty failure message and no error file 5. They `GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content` and get `200` with one JSONL line per record 6. They read the results, matching each line back to their input by ID ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Captured against a deployed proxy on `v1.91.3`, which carries the same allowlist as the merge base, rather than against the two commit hashes. The reproduction is a real Bedrock batch job in `eu-west-1` billed to a real account, and the download is the exact call an end user makes. A run at the merge base and at the PR tip is still worth doing before merge; I could not stand up managed files locally because that path needs a database and the migration step did not complete under emulation on my machine. Shared setup: one Bedrock deployment whose `litellm_params` carry `model`, `aws_access_key_id`, `aws_secret_access_key`, `aws_region_name` and `s3_bucket_name`, with `AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME` absent from the process environment. Input is a 100 record JSONL, which is Bedrock's minimum. ### Before (allowlist without `s3_bucket_name`) 1. Upload the input ``` POST /v1/files purpose=batch, target_model_names=bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 200 status=uploaded ``` 2. Create the batch ``` POST /v1/batches 200 status=validating ``` 3. Poll until terminal ``` GET /v1/batches/{id} 200 status=completed failure_message '' error_file_id null job: arn:aws:bedrock:eu-west-1:...:model-invocation-job/kpiid5uv6b9l ``` 4. Download the output, which is where it breaks ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content 500 {"error":{"message":"S3 bucket_name is required. Set 's3_bucket_name' in proxy config or AWS_S3_BUCKET_NAME for Bedrock file content retrieval.","code":"500"}} ``` 5. Repeat step 4 passing the model explicitly, since a caller would try that next, and get the same result ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content?model=bedrock/global.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 500 same error GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content with header x-litellm-model 500 same error ``` ### After (`070320e94c`, and equivalently with the env var set) 1. Upload the input ``` POST /v1/files 200 status=uploaded ``` 2. Create the batch ``` POST /v1/batches 200 status=validating ``` 3. Poll until terminal ``` GET /v1/batches/{id} 200 status=completed failure_message '' error_file_id null ``` 4. Download the output ``` GET /v1/files/{output_file_id}/content 200 59400 bytes, 100 JSONL records ``` 5. Confirm every submitted record came back, keyed by ID ``` matched 100/100 ticket-0000 -> DELIVERY ticket-0001 -> BILLING ticket-0002 -> PROMO ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - `s3_region_name` is likely dropped the same way, untested - Proof captured on `v1.91.3`, not at the two hashes

signal.title: fix(anthropic_messages): drain upstream in a detached pump so client …
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Interrupted Bedrock `/v1/messages` streams undercount output tokens vs AWS - Client disconnect cancels the upstream read before the terminal usage event is seen - litellm bills the few chunks the client drained, not the full response How it solves it: - Move the upstream read into a detached background pump task that outlives the client connection - Pump drains to the terminal usage event and bills there; client-facing generator only relays chunks from a bounded queue - Queue is bounded so a slow client still throttles the upstream read instead of buffering the full response in memory - Concurrent detached drains are capped so that many simultaneous disconnecting clients can't each hold an open upstream connection and accumulate in-memory buffers indefinitely; when the cap is full the pump bills partial and calls `aclose()` to stop the client-side read (cap and queue size are tunable via env vars) - Provider-side stream errors are forwarded through the queue to a still-connected client unchanged, preserving the original status ## Relevant issues Fixes https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/issues/35958 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reproduction against a live proxy with a Bedrock Claude model configured. Start a streaming `/v1/messages` request that produces a long completion, read a few SSE chunks, then disconnect, then read the spend log back and compare completion tokens against the AWS Bedrock invocation logs for the same request. ```bash # 1. fresh key so spend is isolated KEY=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:4000/key/generate \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"models": []}' | python -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["key"])') # 2. stream, read ~5 chunks, then disconnect (curl killed by head) curl -sN -X POST http://localhost:4000/v1/messages \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model":"us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0","max_tokens":3000,"stream":true, "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write several detailed paragraphs (at least 500 words) about the history of the Roman Empire"}]}' \ | head -c 2000 ; echo # 3. wait for the async spend pipeline to flush, then read the row back sleep 15 curl -s "http://localhost:4000/spend/logs?api_key=$KEY" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234" | python -m json.tool # 4. pull the matching AWS Bedrock invocation log and compare outputTokenCount aws logs filter-log-events \ --log-group-name "/aws/bedrock/model-invocations" \ --start-time $(($(date +%s) * 1000 - 600000)) \ --profile saml-pub ``` Before (commit `6d604d27a6`): the spend row records `completion_tokens` reflecting only the few chunks drained before disconnect (roughly 1 to 15), far below the `outputTokenCount` AWS billed. After (commit `a85a9e1186`): the spend row records `completion_tokens` matching the full response AWS generated and billed. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes On the `/v1/messages` to `bedrock/` invoke streaming path, a client disconnect raises `CancelledError` inside the httpx socket read. That cancellation unwinds the entire upstream generator chain before any `finally` can run, so trying to drain the same upstream generator afterward reads zero remaining chunks. Bedrock keeps generating server-side and bills the full response, so litellm logged only the truncated partial the client drained and undercounted output tokens against the AWS invocation logs. Input tokens were already correct; the gap was output side. `async_sse_wrapper` now runs the upstream read in a detached background task (`_pump_upstream_to_queue`, rooted in a module-level set so asyncio does not garbage-collect it). The pump fully drains the provider stream to its terminal `message_delta` / `message_stop` and bills there, so spend tracking always sees the real terminal usage. The client-facing generator only relays chunks off a bounded `asyncio.Queue`, so a client disconnect tears down the relay without cancelling the pump. A `client_detached` event stops the pump from enqueueing after disconnect, and the queue bound limits how far ahead the pump can run while a slow client is attached. When `client_detached` fires mid-stream, the pump claims a slot in a bounded set (`_DETACHED_STREAM_DRAINS`) before continuing to drain for billing. Without a cap, a spike of disconnecting clients could each leave a background task holding an open connection and accumulating the full response in memory, so the proxy's per-process memory and file-descriptor usage would scale with abandoned requests rather than active ones. If the cap is already full, the pump bills what it has and calls `aclose()` to stop the client-side read; the provider may still generate and bill server-side, but the proxy stops accumulating. Both the cap and the relay queue size are tunable via env vars. When the upstream raises while the client is still connected, the exception is forwarded through the queue and re-raised in the client-facing generator so the proxy's failure handling keeps the original provider status. If the upstream raises after the client has already disconnected, the pump salvages partial spend rather than dropping the row. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(caching): guard disconnect() against None async_redis_conn_pool in cluster mode
signal.text: ## Relevant issues Fixes #31206 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [ ] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Reproduce before the fix: ```python import asyncio from unittest.mock import patch async def repro(): with patch("asyncio.get_running_loop", side_effect=RuntimeError): from litellm.caching.redis_cache import RedisCache cache = RedisCache(host="localhost", port=6379, password="x") cache.async_redis_conn_pool = None # what get_redis_connection_pool returns for cluster await cache.disconnect() # AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'disconnect' asyncio.run(repro()) ``` After the fix the call returns cleanly with no exception. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `get_redis_connection_pool()` returns `None` when `REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES` is set because the cluster client manages its own internal connection pool. `RedisCache.__init__` assigns that `None` directly to `self.async_redis_conn_pool`. `disconnect()` then called `self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(...)` unconditionally, raising `AttributeError` and crashing proxy shutdown on every Redis Cluster deployment. The fix is a single early-return guard at the top of `disconnect()`: if `async_redis_conn_pool` is `None` there is nothing to disconnect, so we return immediately. A regression test in `tests/test_litellm/caching/test_redis_cache.py` covers this path.
