signal.title: fix(guardrails): timeout-protect custom guardrail exec to prevent hang
signal.text: Fixes #28259 ### Summary `TestCustomCodeGuardrail` (`/guardrails/test` endpoint) executes user-supplied Python code with `exec()` on the request thread. RestrictedPython blocks imports and `eval`, but **not infinite loops** — so a top-level `while True: pass` in otherwise-valid custom code hangs the handler thread forever and eventually exhausts the proxy's worker pool. ### Changes - Compile only at the call site; module-level `exec` now runs inside the same timeout-protected `ThreadPoolExecutor` scope as `apply_fn` (5s `EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`). - Use `executor.shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True)` instead of a context manager: `__exit__` calls `shutdown(wait=True)`, which would block forever on a worker stuck in an infinite loop even after `future.result()` timed out. - Code that doesn't define `apply_guardrail` now reports a proper `compilation` error via `_MissingGuardrailError` (previously the check ran before exec and returned a generic error). - Keep the detailed error in the server log; client gets a fixed message. ### Tests New `tests/proxy/guardrails/test_guardrail_exec_timeout.py`: - top-level infinite loop hits the execution timeout (does not hang) - valid code still runs and returns `success: true` - missing `apply_guardrail` reports `error_type: compilation` - non-admin caller rejected with 403 before any code runs `4 passed` locally (Python 3.13, litellm @ main + proxy extras).

signal.title: [Bug]: Non-streaming requests never cancel upstream work when the client disconnects
signal.text: # [Bug]: Non-streaming requests never cancel upstream work when the client disconnects ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related but distinct: - #30244 / #30245 — fixed the **streaming** `/chat/completions` path (confirmed working, see below). - #36123 — streaming `/v1/responses` and `/v1/messages` still leak. Open. - #3341 — the original feature request for this behaviour. Closed as "done" in 2024, then reverted. Details below. This report is about the **non-streaming** path, which none of the above covers. ### What happened? When a client disconnects from a non-streaming request, the proxy never tells the upstream provider to stop. The backend keeps generating to completion, holding GPU memory and a scheduler slot for a response nobody will read. If the user retries after their own timeout, the orphaned work stacks up. ### History `check_request_disconnection()` was added for #3341 and wired into the `chat_completion` and `completion` routes. It was then removed in [`498bfa9`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/commit/498bfa9a4cc7eeb00eec31af8be50689a68b4835) ("fix - revert check_request_disconnection"). A user asked on #3341 why the revert happened and never received an answer. On `v1.89.5` the function definition survives at `litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py:1936` with **zero call sites** anywhere in the package. On current `main` the function is gone entirely, and `proxy_server.py` contains no `is_disconnected` reference at all. So the streaming path was repaired by #30245 while the non-streaming path has been without cancellation since 2024. ### Reproduction Backend: a local OpenAI-compatible server that *does* implement disconnect cancellation (polls `Request.is_disconnected()` and aborts the generation task), so the backend is not the variable here. **Through the proxy, non-streaming** — client killed at 20 s: ``` 08:52:35 client disconnects 08:53:55 backend log: Chat completion: 1 tokens in 87.06s, prompt: 11213 ``` The backend ran for a further 67 s after the client was gone. **Direct to the same backend, non-streaming** — client killed at 15 s: ``` backend log: Request b6b64dc4-... cancelled, aborting ``` Cancelled immediately. **Through the proxy, streaming** — client killed at 18 s: ``` 09:00:36 client disconnects 09:00:36 backend log: Aborting request dba57122-... ``` Cancelled in the same second — #30245 works. The only variable across the three runs is proxy-vs-direct and stream-vs-non-stream. ### Expected A client disconnect on a non-streaming request should cancel the upstream call, the same way it now does for streaming `/chat/completions`. ### Questions 1. Was the 2024 revert of `check_request_disconnection` due to a specific problem (false positives from `is_disconnected()`, interaction with spend logging, event-loop cost of the polling task)? #3341 never got an answer, and knowing the reason would shape any fix. 2. Is a `poll`-based approach still the intended design, or should non-streaming reuse the response-closing mechanism that #30245 introduced for streaming? ### Relevant log output See reproduction section above. ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on? v1.89.5 (behaviour also expected on `main`, where the function no longer exists at all)

signal.text: Hi LiteLLM team 👋 — I'm Hassieb from the Langfuse team. Langfuse Cloud's [Fast Preview](<https://langfuse.com/docs/v4>) uses the new observations-first ingestion path. For real-time data there, Python integrations should use SDK v4.7.0+ or send compatible OpenTelemetry spans with the v4 ingestion header. I reviewed LiteLLM's two Langfuse callback paths. signal.title: fix(http_handler): dispose aiohttp session when AsyncHTTPHandler is finalized without a running loop
signal.text: ## Title fix(http_handler): dispose aiohttp session when `AsyncHTTPHandler` is finalized without a running loop ## Relevant issues Follow-up to the recycle-time disposal fix (#33428 / #32003). That fix covers sessions replaced by `_get_valid_client_session()`; this PR covers the clients that are **never recycled** and still leak. ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/test_litellm/` directory - [x] Test output pasted below (new tests passing locally) ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_http_handler.py -q -k "finalizer or sync_close" 5 passed, 55 deselected $ pytest tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_http_handler.py \ tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_aiohttp_transport.py \ tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_async_client_cleanup.py \ tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_gemini_session_leak.py -q 98 passed in 14.41s ``` - [x] My PR passes all unit tests on `make test-unit` - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes **Problem.** `AsyncHTTPHandler.__del__` can only schedule an async close when a running event loop exists at finalization time: ```python def __del__(self) -> None: try: if not _handler_may_close_client(...): return asyncio.get_running_loop().create_task(self._client.aclose()) except Exception: pass ``` In any loop-less context — worker threads whose event loop has already closed, sync code paths, interpreter/worker shutdown — `get_running_loop()` raises, the exception is swallowed, and the underlying aiohttp `ClientSession` is abandoned to GC, emitting `Unclosed client session` / `Unclosed connector` warnings. This is exactly the lifecycle of clients minted for short-lived event loops: `LLMClientCache` keys clients by `id(running_loop)`, so each ephemeral loop gets its own handler; those handlers live and die with their loop and are only ever finalized loop-lessly. Measured in production (FastAPI service running background eval workers with per-task event loops): a steady residual of these warnings survives the recycle-time fix, because these sessions never reach `_get_valid_client_session()` again. **Fix** (all inside `AsyncHTTPHandler`): 1. **No running loop:** fall back to the connector's synchronous teardown via `LiteLLMAiohttpTransport._mark_connector_closed` — the same finalizer-safe path the transport already uses for dead-loop recycles. It releases pooled connections and flips the closed flags that `ClientSession.__del__` / connector `__del__` check, so no warnings fire at GC. The fallback honors `_owns_session`, so a shared session (e.g. the proxy's) is never closed by a handler. 2. **Running loop:** keep the async close, but hold a strong reference to the scheduled task until it completes — a bare `create_task()` result may be garbage-collected before it runs. Mirrors `LiteLLMAiohttpTransport._background_close_tasks`. **Tests** (`tests/test_litellm/llms/custom_httpx/test_http_handler.py`): - `test_finalizer_without_running_loop_closes_dead_loop_session` — a handler whose session was created on a since-closed loop is finalized with no running loop; the session must end up closed. - `test_finalizer_with_running_loop_schedules_close_and_holds_task_ref` — the close task is registered, retained, and drains the registry on completion. - `test_sync_close_helper_respects_session_ownership` — owned session closed; shared session untouched. All three fail without the fix and pass with it. Existing `custom_httpx` suites (`test_http_handler.py`, `test_aiohttp_transport.py`, `test_async_client_cleanup.py`, `test_gemini_session_leak.py`) pass: 98/98. Behavioral A/B on the repro (5 clients used on ephemeral loops, refs dropped with no loop running, forced GC): **10 unclosed-session warnings before → 0 after**.

signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? With Redis **cluster mode** enabled, every proxy shutdown ends in an unhandled `AttributeError`, and uvicorn reports `Application shutdown failed. Exiting.` ``` AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'disconnect' File "litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 1232, in <lifespan> await proxy_shutdown_event() File "litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py", line 843, in proxy_shutdown_event await litellm.cache.disconnect() File "litellm/caching/caching.py", line 913, in disconnect await self.cache.disconnect() File "litellm/caching/redis_cache.py", line 1356, in disconnect await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True) ``` This is deterministic, not intermittent — it fires on every shutdown. ### User Flow ### Suggested fix Two parts: 1. Guard the base class — `redis_cache.py`: ```python async def disconnect(self): if self.async_redis_conn_pool is not None: await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True) ``` 2. Give `RedisClusterCache` a real teardown, since the guard alone leaks the cluster client: ```python async def disconnect(self): if self.redis_async_redis_cluster_client is not None: await self.redis_async_redis_cluster_client.aclose() await super().disconnect() ``` `aclose()` is already the primitive used in `test_connection()` in that same file. Wrapping the `litellm.cache.disconnect()` call in `proxy_shutdown_event()` in a try/except would also stop one cache failure from aborting the rest of shutdown, independent of this bug. ### Proof the bug occurs ### Root cause `get_redis_connection_pool()` returns `None` by design in cluster mode, because a `RedisCluster` builds its own per-node pools rather than taking a shared `BlockingConnectionPool` — `litellm/_redis.py:691-692`: ```python if "startup_nodes" in redis_kwargs: return None ``` `RedisCache.__init__` stores that `None` unconditionally (`redis_cache.py:309`), and `RedisCache.disconnect()` then dereferences it with no guard (`redis_cache.py:1355-1356`): ```python async def disconnect(self): await self.async_redis_conn_pool.disconnect(inuse_connections=True) ``` `RedisClusterCache` overrides `init_async_client`, the two mget paths and `test_connection` — but **not** `disconnect()` — so the base-class dereference is always reached. ### Impact The exception propagates out of `proxy_shutdown_event()`, so everything ordered after `litellm.cache.disconnect()` is skipped: | line | step | outcome | |---|---|---| | 838-840 | `flush_gateway_requests()`, `prisma_client.disconnect()` | ✅ run before the crash | | 843 | `litellm.cache.disconnect()` | 💥 raises | | 845 | `jwt_handler.close()` | ❌ skipped | | 848 | `db_writer_client.close()` | ❌ skipped | | 852 | `shutdown_billing_metrics_recorder()` | ❌ skipped | | 856 | langfuse flush | ❌ skipped | | 868 | `cleanup_router_config_variables()` | ❌ skipped | Prisma closing first bounds the damage, but the skipped billing flush is data loss by your own comment at `proxy_server.py:851-852`: *"final flush of billable-request counts: without it, up to one export interval of enterprise billing data is dropped on every restart."* Anyone running cluster mode with enterprise billing or langfuse loses that on every restart. ### Reproduce 1. Point the proxy at any cluster-mode Redis (e.g. ElastiCache Serverless, which is always cluster-mode) and set `REDIS_CLUSTER_NODES`. 2. Start the proxy, then send SIGTERM. 3. Shutdown raises instead of completing. ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? 1.97.0 (also reproduces on 1.96.2 — same code, only a Final annotation differs) ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_

signal.title: fix(core): stop get_image_dimensions crashing on bare base64 and unfetchable URLs
signal.text: Replaces #37111 — its head branch was accidentally deleted during a force-push, which detached the PR from further updates. Same change, full commit history preserved (plus the two CI-budget follow-ups). ## Bug `get_image_dimensions` documents `"The URL or base64 encoded string of the image."` as valid input, but two documented-or-implied inputs crash it: ```py >>> get_image_dimensions(data="<bare base64 png>") # docstring says this is supported ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1) # data.split(",", 1) >>> get_image_dimensions(data="https://host/x.png") # host unreachable / times out ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1) # falls into the base64 branch ``` The final fallback comment — *"return sensible default image dimensions if unable to get dimensions"* — was unreachable for these paths: the unconditional `_header, encoded = data.split(",", 1)` raised before format detection, and a failed URL fetch dropped straight into that same branch. This matters for `calculate_img_tokens(..., mode="high")`, which is exported public API: a temporarily-unreachable image URL or a bare-base64 payload turns token counting into an exception instead of an estimate. ## Fix - The base64 path is extracted into `_decode_base64_image`, accepting both data-URL form and bare base64; decode errors return `None` (debug-logged). - An unfetchable URL no longer falls into the base64 branch; with no image data an early return yields `DEFAULT_IMAGE_WIDTH/DEFAULT_IMAGE_HEIGHT`, as the fallback comment intended. - `img_data` is explicitly `bytes | None` and narrowed before format detection, keeping the basedpyright `reportOptionalSubscript` budget at zero delta; the extraction keeps the C901 total at the upstream baseline (one point below, in fact). ## Verification Three hermetic tests next to the existing mocked-fetch ones (no network): bare base64 parses real PNG dimensions (100×200); a mocked failed fetch returns the defaults; undecodable input returns the defaults.`tests/test_litellm/litellm_core_utils/test_token_counter.py`: 81 passed, 1 skipped locally (only the tokenizer-download tests deselected — they need network/model downloads and run in CI).

signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex requests fail with a raw `No module named 'google'` - The install hint exists here, but four imports skipped it - Those four are the only ones the async path reaches How it solves it: - All four now route through one guarded import helper - Reuses the existing message; adds no dependency ## User Flow Before: a developer pointing the proxy at a Vertex model gets an error naming nothing they can install 1. They `pip install "litellm[proxy]"` and configure `model: vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash` 2. They start the proxy on port 4000; it comes up clean, no warning 3. They POST `http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with that model 4. A 500 comes back reading `litellm.APIConnectionError: No module named 'google'` 5. No package is named, so they guess at what to install After: the same request names the package 1. They `pip install "litellm[proxy]"` and configure `model: vertex_ai/gemini-2.5-flash` 2. They start the proxy on port 4000; it comes up clean, no warning 3. They POST `http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions` with that model 4. A 500 comes back reading `Google Cloud SDK not found. Install it with: pip install 'litellm[google]'` 5. They run that command and the request reaches real credential checks ## Relevant issues Relates to #30320 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Built from this repo's `uv.lock` with exactly `--extra proxy`: 110 packages, no `google-auth`. Only the patch differs between the two runs. ``` === 2. google-auth must be ABSENT; this is the packaging gap the issue reports === google-auth NOT INSTALLED (expected) packages in closure: 110 === 4. BEFORE: base version of the file, google-auth absent === # 6704a105ee APIConnectionError: litellm.APIConnectionError: No module named 'google' === 5. AFTER: the patch, google-auth still absent === # b461a67d97 APIConnectionError: litellm.APIConnectionError: Google Cloud SDK not found. Install it with: pip install 'litellm[google]' or pip install google-cloud-aiplatform ``` Installing `google-auth` makes the guard transparent; the request then fails on credentials: ``` === 6. install google-auth; the guard must become transparent === google-auth: 2.56.3 File ".../vertex_llm_base.py", line 265, in _credentials_from_default_auth return google_auth.default(scopes=scopes) google.auth.exceptions.DefaultCredentialsError: Your default credentials were not found. ``` A real billed Gemini call, unaffected: ``` {"model": "gemini-2.5-flash", "content": "proxy healthy", "usage": {"completion_tokens": 26, "prompt_tokens": 7, "total_tokens": 33}} ``` ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `GOOGLE_IMPORT_ERROR_MESSAGE` was already raised at seven import sites here. Four `TokenState` imports were not, and all four sit only on the async path, so proxy requests got a bare `ModuleNotFoundError` while sync callers got the hint. Sharing one helper also keeps `get_access_token_async` under its complexity ceiling. Both new tests fail on unpatched code. ## Caveats (if any) - Does not add `google-auth` to the `proxy` extra - The issue's startup-validation ask stays open - A too-old `google-auth` now also reports "not found" - Matches the seven guarded sites already here ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR <!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY --> --- > [!NOTE] > <sup>[Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) is generating a summary for commit b461a67d97b1559669bb149389a2163d44d9bc6f. signal.title: [Bug]: chat->responses bridge emits output_text input items without required 'annotations' field (strict providers like Azure reject with 400)
signal.text: ### What happened? When a `/chat/completions` request for a gpt-5.x model contains **both `tools` and `reasoning_effort`**, LiteLLM correctly bridges the request to the Responses API (the upstream chat endpoint rejects that combination with *"Function tools with reasoning_effort are not supported ... Please use /v1/responses instead"*). However, the bridge converts assistant **history** messages into `output_text` content blocks **without the `annotations` field**: ```python # litellm/completion_extras/litellm_responses_transformation/transformation.py def _convert_content_str_to_input_text(self, content: str, role: str) -> Dict[str, Any]: if role == "user" or role == "system" or role == "tool": return {"type": "input_text", "text": content} else: return {"type": "output_text", "text": content} # <-- no "annotations" ``` Per the OpenAI spec, `annotations` is **required** on `output_text` items passed as input. See the official openai-python SDK type ([response_output_text_param.py](https://github.com/openai/openai-python/blob/main/src/openai/types/responses/response_output_text_param.py)): ```python class ResponseOutputTextParam(TypedDict, total=False): annotations: Required[Iterable[Annotation]] # Required text: Required[str] type: Required[Literal["output_text"]] ``` OpenAI's own endpoint is lenient about the missing field, but stricter spec-conformant providers (e.g. **Azure AI Foundry `/openai/v1`**) reject the bridged request with 400: ```json { "error": { "code": "invalid_payload", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations", "type": "invalid_request_error" } } ``` Every odd `input[N]` index in the error corresponds to an assistant history message, so any multi-turn conversation (2nd request onward) fails. First requests succeed because there is no assistant history yet. This breaks agentic clients (OpenCode, etc.) that always send `tools` + `reasoning_effort`. ### Reproduction Proxy config: `openai/gpt-5.x` model with `api_base` pointing to an Azure AI Foundry v1 endpoint (`https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/<proj>/openai/v1`). ```bash curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "model": "gpt-5.x-deployment", "reasoning_effort": "medium", "tools": [{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_time","description":"get time","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{}}}}], "messages": [ {"role":"user","content":"say ok"}, {"role":"assistant","content":"ok"}, {"role":"user","content":"again"} ] }' ``` Matrix (all against the same deployment): | payload | result | |---|---| | multi-turn only | 200 OK (no bridge) | | multi-turn + `reasoning_effort` | 200 OK (no bridge) | | multi-turn + `tools` | 200 OK (no bridge) | | multi-turn + `tools` + `reasoning_effort` | **400 annotations error** (bridged) | The value of `reasoning_effort` doesn't matter (`minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high` all fail). ### Proposed fix One line — always emit the field, empty array when there are no annotations: ```python return {"type": "output_text", "text": content, "annotations": []} ``` (The list-content path `_convert_content_to_responses_format` should likewise preserve/emit `annotations` on `output_text` items.) Related (opposite direction, already fixed): #18378 / #18754 handled responses→chat annotation preservation; this issue is about the chat→responses **request** direction. ### Relevant log output ``` litellm.BadRequestError: OpenAIException - { "error": { "code": "invalid_payload", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations", "type": "invalid_request_error", "details": [ {"code": "ValidationError", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[1].content[0].annotations", "type": "error"}, {"code": "ValidationError", "message": "Required property 'annotations' is missing", "param": "input[3].content[0].annotations", "type": "error"} ] } } ``` ### Are you a ML Ops Team? No ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.88.1

signal.title: [Bug]: Bedrock OpenAI GPT-5.6 (us.openai.*) — Responses routing hang + missing chat/stream transforms
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. Related (not duplicates — different symptoms / code paths): - #36922 — FastAPI `get_flat_dependant` startup crash (same root as Bug 1 below) - #36016 — `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*` metadata `mode: responses` (related to Bug 2 fuzzy match / routing) This issue covers end-to-end failures when calling **Bedrock Invoke** models via `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-{sol,terra,luna}` (Chat Completions / Anthropic Messages proxy), which are not covered by the above. --- ### What happened? On **litellm 1.97.0** with FastAPI **0.141.1**, proxying AWS Bedrock OpenAI GPT-5.6 models (`bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol|terra|luna` in `us-east-1`) fails in four stacked ways: 1. **Proxy may not start** with recent FastAPI (`ImportError: cannot import name 'get_flat_dependant'`). 2. **Requests hang forever** unless the model is forced to chat mode — routing incorrectly treats these as Responses API models (fuzzy match against `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*` with `mode: responses`), leading to an infinite completion ↔ responses bridge loop. 3. **Non-streaming** returns `BadRequestError` / `'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` when parsing the Bedrock OpenAI Chat Completions JSON (no OpenAI provider branch in the Invoke response transform; falls through to Titan `results[0].outputText`). 4. **Streaming** returns valid SSE / event structure but **empty text** on every delta (no OpenAI `choices[].delta.content` branch in the event-stream chunk parser). **Expected:** `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-*` work as chat models for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` (stream + non-stream), same as other Bedrock chat providers. **Workaround that unblocks after local patches:** set `model_info.mode: chat` on each model, plus add OpenAI cases to Invoke `transform_response` and stream `_chunk_parser` (see Technical notes). --- ### User Flow **Before a (hypothetical) fix:** a developer who configured Bedrock GPT-5.6 on the proxy never gets usable completions (hang, parse error, or empty stream). 1. They add `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` to the proxy `model_list` and start the proxy (or hit startup ImportError on FastAPI ≥0.115). 2. They send `POST /v1/chat/completions` (or `/v1/messages`) with a short user message to that model alias. 3. Without `model_info.mode: chat`, the request never returns (proxy hangs / retries forever). 4. With `mode: chat` forced, non-stream returns HTTP 400-class LiteLLM error mentioning BedrockException / `'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` while the raw body still contains OpenAI-shaped `choices[].message.content`. 5. With non-stream patched locally, stream returns SSE / Anthropic event frames but every `content_block_delta` / delta has empty text — client UI shows a finished stream with no tokens. **After a (hypothetical) fix:** the same Bedrock GPT-5.6 alias works for chat and messages, stream and non-stream, without hanging or empty deltas. 1. Admin configures `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` (no special `mode` workaround required). 2. Developer sends the same `POST /v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages`. 3. Non-stream returns assistant text + usage in the normal OpenAI / Anthropic response shape. 4. Stream returns incremental text deltas with a normal finish reason. --- ### Proof the bug occurs **Config / setup the proxy ran with:** ```yaml model_list: - model_name: gpt-5.6-sol-bedrock # Without this, requests hang (Bug 2). With it, Bugs 3–4 still reproduce. model_info: mode: chat litellm_params: model: bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol aws_profile_name: your-profile aws_region_name: us-east-1 drop_params: true general_settings: master_key: "sk-litellm-local" ``` Same pattern for `us.openai.gpt-5.6-terra` and `us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna`. **Version or commit:** litellm **1.97.0**, FastAPI **0.141.1**, Python **3.11**, macOS aarch64, AWS region **us-east-1**. **Observed errors / symptoms:** Bug 1 — startup: ```text ImportError: cannot import name 'get_flat_dependant' from 'fastapi.dependencies.utils' ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'proxy_server' ``` Bug 2 — without `model_info.mode: chat`: request hangs indefinitely; debug shows recursive `acompletion` via Responses bridge after fuzzy-matching `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-sol` (`mode: responses`). Bug 3 — non-streaming (with `mode: chat`): ```text litellm.BadRequestError: BedrockException - Error processing={"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","index":0,"message":{"annotations":[],"content":"ok","role":"assistant"}}],...}, Received error='NoneType' object is not subscriptable ``` (Note: payload already contains valid OpenAI `choices[].message.content` — parse path is wrong.) Bug 4 — streaming (after Bug 3 fixed locally): SSE / `/v1/messages` event stream structure is valid, but all content deltas are empty strings. Non-stream works; stream does not (separate code path). **Models tested:** `us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol`, `us.openai.gpt-5.6-terra`, `us.openai.gpt-5.6-luna`. --- ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy (Also reproducible via SDK completion paths that use Bedrock Invoke transforms.) ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.97.0 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details _No response_ --- ### Technical notes (for maintainers) **Bug 1** — `litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/management_v1/common.py` still imports `get_flat_dependant` (removed FastAPI 0.115+). See also #36922. **Bug 2** — Built-in `model_cost` has `bedrock_mantle/openai.gpt-5.6-*` with `mode: responses`. Resolving `bedrock/us.openai.gpt-5.6-sol` fuzzy-matches that entry → `responses_api_bridge` → infinite loop. Prefer `mode: chat` (+ keep `/v1/responses` in endpoints if needed) **or** stop cross-matching `bedrock/us.openai.*` → `bedrock_mantle/openai.*`. Overlaps #36016 metadata discussion; hang is the user-visible failure here. **Bug 3** — `litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/invoke_transformations/base_invoke_transformation.py`: `transform_request` already has an `openai` branch; `transform_response` does not — falls through to Titan `results[0]`. Suggested: handle `provider == "openai"` via `choices[0].message.content` + usage; also strip Anthropic-only optional params before Invoke for OpenAI models. **Bug 4** — `litellm/llms/bedrock/chat/invoke_handler.py` `AWSEventStreamDecoder._chunk_parser`: add branch for OpenAI stream chunks `choices[0].delta.content` / `finish_reason`. Happy to open a PR with the local patches if useful.

signal.title: fix(cost): honour deployment custom pricing for OCR calls
signal.text: ## Title fix(cost): honour deployment custom pricing for OCR calls ## Relevant issues Fixes #36608 ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have Added testing in the `tests/litellm/` directory - [x] I have added a screenshot of my new test passing locally - [x] My PR passes all unit tests - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `ocr_cost()` resolved pricing only through `litellm.get_model_info()` — a cost map lookup keyed by model name. Custom pricing for a router deployment is registered under the **deployment id**, and `_register_custom_pricing_for_request()` deliberately strips pricing fields from the shared `{provider}/{model}` key so siblings don't clobber each other. So the key `ocr_cost()` looked up was exactly the one guaranteed not to carry the pricing. Result: an OCR model absent from the cost map billed **$0** regardless of configuration, even though `ocr_cost_per_page` / `ocr_cost_per_credit` are declared `CustomPricingLiteLLMParams` fields and are accepted without error. This mirrors the existing **video generation** path rather than inventing a mechanism. That path already had the same problem — pricing that isn't token-based can't travel via `custom_cost_per_token` — and solves it by pulling deployment `model_info` off the logging object: ```python if custom_pricing and litellm_logging_obj is not None: _litellm_params = getattr(litellm_logging_obj, "litellm_params", None) if _litellm_params is not None: _metadata = _litellm_params.get("metadata", {}) or {} _video_model_info = _metadata.get("model_info", None) ``` So: - `ocr_cost()` takes an optional `model_info` and prefers it over the map **only when it actually carries OCR pricing**; otherwise the existing map lookup runs unchanged. - `cost_per_token()` gains an optional `custom_model_info` passthrough. - `completion_cost()` extracts it the same way the video branch does. Backwards compatible — every new parameter defaults to `None`, and with nothing configured the behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was, including still returning `0.0` for a genuinely unpriced model. ## Testing New file `tests/test_litellm/test_ocr_custom_pricing.py`, 8 tests. **6 of them fail on the base branch and pass with this change**; the other 2 are controls that must pass either way (the premise guard that the test model really is absent from the map, and the unchanged-$0 behaviour when nothing is configured). ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/test_ocr_custom_pricing.py -q ........ [100%] 8 passed in 0.29s # with the fix reverted: 6 failed, 2 passed in 0.45s ``` Wider cost suite, no regressions (`test_cost_calculator.py`, `test_gpt_image_cost_calculator.py`, `test_register_model_zero_cost_persistence.py`, `test_router_model_cost_isolation.py`): ``` 1 failed, 133 passed ``` The single failure is `test_router_model_cost_isolation.py::test_custom_pricing_isolated_from_sibling_via_proxy_model_info_path`, which fails **identically on a clean checkout** of this base branch — a `ModuleNotFoundError` from an optional proxy dependency in my environment, unrelated to this change. ## Field report Found on a production proxy: two Azure AI OCR deployments on the same account, same document, both HTTP 200 with identical correct text extraction — one billed $0.003/page (in the map), the other $0.00 (not in the map). Nothing in the response distinguishes them, which is what makes this quietly expensive. ## A separate defect noticed while writing the tests Not fixed here, to keep this PR isolated — but worth a look, because it currently breaks OCR tests on this branch: `OCRResponse` (`litellm/llms/base_llm/ocr/transformation.py`) declares a field `object: str = "ocr"` **after** two fields annotated `list[dict[str, object]] | None` (`tables`, `keyValuePairs`). The field named `object` shadows the builtin in the class namespace, so pydantic resolves the annotation to the string `"ocr"` and treats it as a forward-referenced type: ``` pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `OCRResponse` is not fully defined; you should define `ocr`, then call `OCRResponse.model_rebuild()`. ``` This reproduces on a clean checkout — `tests/test_litellm/llms/mistral/ocr/test_mistral_ocr_cost.py` currently fails this way (9 failed, 5 passed) with no changes applied. My tests use `model_construct()` to route around it, with a comment saying why. Happy to open a separate issue/PR if useful; annotating those two fields `Any` looks sufficient.

signal.title: feat(opencode): add opencode_go and opencode_zen first-class providers
signal.text: ## TLDR Add OpenCode as a first-class LiteLLM provider with two surface variants, opencode_go and opencode_zen, supporting three wire formats: Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, and OpenAI Responses. Problem this solves: - OpenCode has an API but no first-class LiteLLM provider support, so users must rely on fragile custom_llm_provider workarounds. How it solves it: - Registers both surfaces as first-class providers with transformation classes, cost-map entries, wildcard model expansion, surface-aware auth key resolution, and dashboard placeholder support. ## User Flow Before: a user cannot reach the OpenCode models through LiteLLM because the providers are not wired into the dispatch mapping or the cost map. 1. They send a request with model opencode_zen/grok-4.5 and no custom_llm_provider. 2. The request fails with a model-not-found error. After: the same request succeeds because the providers are registered. 1. LiteLLM routes opencode_zen/grok-4.5 through the new OpenCode provider transformation class. 2. The request is forwarded to the OpenCode gateway with the correct Bearer token resolved from the OPENCODE_ZEN_API_KEY env var. 3. signal.title: [Bug]: project budgets missing from atomic pre-call budget reservation
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate ### What happened? Project max budgets are checked at read time and can alert, but they are never part of the atomic pre-call reservation path that teams, orgs, keys, users, end-users, tags, and team members already use Related #33871 covers the missing DB spend write for `LiteLLM_ProjectTable.spend` (open PR #33883). This issue is the complementary gap: even after spend is written, concurrent requests can still overshoot a project budget because `reserve_budget_for_request` never builds a `spend:project:{project_id}` counter ### Current behavior `_get_budget_counters` in `litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/budget_reservation.py` builds counters for Key, Team, TeamMember, User, EndUser, Tag, and Organization. `"Project"` is absent from `_COUNTER_ENTITY_TYPES`, and there is no `_get_project_budget_counter` `user_api_key_auth` already loads `project_object` for `common_checks` / `_project_max_budget_check`, but `_reserve_budget_after_common_checks` does not pass it into `reserve_budget_for_request` `increment_spend_counters` and `SpendCounterReseed.from_db` also have no `spend:project:` branch, so a reserved project counter would not be incremented or reseeded after the call `_project_max_budget_check` still compares `project_object.spend` from cache/DB instead of `get_current_spend(counter_key=f"spend:project:...")` the way `_team_max_budget_check` does ### Expected behavior When a virtual key has a `project_id` and that project has `litellm_budget_table.max_budget > 0`: 1. Pre-call reservation includes `spend:project:{project_id}` (same atomic admission hold as org/team) 2. Post-call `increment_spend_counters` updates that counter when it was not already reserved, or reconciles the reservation 3. `SpendCounterReseed.from_db` can reseed `spend:project:{id}` from `LiteLLM_ProjectTable` 4. `_project_max_budget_check` uses `get_current_spend` against the project counter ### Steps / references 1. Create a project with `max_budget` and attach a virtual key via `project_id` 2. Fire concurrent `/chat/completions` requests whose combined estimated cost exceeds the project budget 3. Observe that reservation never holds a project counter; overspend is possible under concurrency even if #33871 is fixed Code anchors: - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/litellm_internal_staging/litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/budget_reservation.py ( `_COUNTER_ENTITY_TYPES`, `_get_budget_counters` ) - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/litellm_internal_staging/litellm/proxy/auth/user_api_key_auth.py ( `_reserve_budget_after_common_checks` ) - https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/litellm_internal_staging/litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py ( `_project_max_budget_check` ) ### Proposed solution Mirror the Organization counter pattern for Project: - Add `_get_project_budget_counter(project_object)` and wire it through `reserve_budget_for_request` / `_get_budget_counters` - Pass `project_object` from auth into reservation - Add `_increment_project_spend_counter` and thread `project_id` from `user_api_key_project_id` metadata in the cost callback - Extend `SpendCounterReseed.from_db` for `spend:project:` - Switch `_project_max_budget_check` to `get_current_spend` ### Alternatives considered Folding this into #33871 / PR #33883. That PR correctly focuses on DB spend persistence. Reservation + counter-backed read-time enforcement is a separate concern and is easier to review on its own once the spend write path exists (or in parallel, using `fallback_spend` from the cached project object) ### Scope In scope: atomic reservation, post-call counter increment, reseed, counter-backed project max-budget check, regression tests Out of scope: DB spend writer (#33871), project soft-budget counter migration, project budget windows / multi-window limits ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] A project with `max_budget` participates in `reserve_budget_for_request` when `project_object` is present - [ ] Concurrent overshoot against the project budget is blocked the same way as team/org - [ ] `increment_spend_counters` and `SpendCounterReseed.from_db` understand `spend:project:{id}` - [ ] `_project_max_budget_check` reads via `get_current_spend` - [ ] Focused unit tests cover reserve / release / skip-when-no-budget ### Backward compatibility No API or schema change. Keys and projects without a project max budget stay on the current no-op path (single find / early return) ### Risks Until #33871 lands, DB reseed for `spend:project:` may return `0.0` / missing spend while the table is never incremented. Reservation still protects in-flight concurrency using `fallback_spend` from the cached project object. Full end-to-end accuracy needs both this fix and #33871 ### Relevant log output ```shell N/A (logic gap; no exception today because project is simply omitted from reservation) ```

signal.title: feat(cost): support time-based off-peak pricing in cost calculation
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Some providers discount per-token rates during a daily window - The cost map only modeled one static rate per model - Logged spend therefore overstates cost inside that window How it solves it: - A model entry can carry an `off_peak_pricing` block - `hours_utc` takes one `"HH:MM-HH:MM"` window or a list - Windows may wrap past midnight; unset rates fall back - An off-peak rate replaces the tier or threshold rate - Timezone-aware timestamps are normalized to UTC before comparing ## User Flow Before: a proxy admin serving a provider that discounts by time of day sees the same spend logged around the clock, so their cost dashboard overstates what the provider actually invoices 1. They add the deployment to their config with a single `input_cost_per_token` and `output_cost_per_token` 2. They send POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions with that model at 18:00 UTC, inside the provider's published discount window 3. They open https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs and see the request billed at the full daytime rate 4. They send the same request again at 12:00 UTC and see an identical spend figure, so the discount never shows up anywhere After: the same two requests bill differently, so logged spend tracks the provider invoice 1. They add `off_peak_pricing` to the deployment, giving `hours_utc` plus the discounted per-token rates 2. They send the same POST https://litellm-domain/v1/chat/completions at 18:00 UTC 3. https://litellm-domain/ui/?page=logs now shows that request at the discounted rate 4. They send it again at 12:00 UTC and see the standard rate, so the two windows are visibly different ## Relevant issues Fixes #31606 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix The feature is time-gated, so the only thing that changes between two otherwise identical calls is the clock. Captured at 7621e0df4e, asking the cost calculator for the same usage at four different times: ```python from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone import litellm from litellm.litellm_core_utils.llm_cost_calc.utils import _get_token_base_cost from litellm.types.utils import Usage litellm.register_model( { "offpeak-demo": { "litellm_provider": "openai", "mode": "chat", "input_cost_per_token": 1e-6, "output_cost_per_token": 2e-6, "off_peak_pricing": { "hours_utc": "16:30-00:30", "input_cost_per_token": 5e-7, "output_cost_per_token": 1e-6, }, } } ) info = litellm.get_model_info(model="offpeak-demo") usage = Usage(prompt_tokens=100, completion_tokens=50, total_tokens=150) for label, when in [ ("18:00 UTC (inside window)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 18, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("12:00 UTC (outside window)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("00:15 UTC (past midnight wrap)", datetime(2026, 1, 1, 0, 15, tzinfo=timezone.utc)), ("02:00 UTC+8 (same instant as 18:00 UTC)", datetime(2026, 1, 2, 2, 0, tzinfo=timezone(timedelta(hours=8)))), ]: print(label, _get_token_base_cost(info, usage, current_time=when)[:2]) ``` ``` 18:00 UTC (inside window) (5e-07, 1e-06) 12:00 UTC (outside window) (1e-06, 2e-06) 00:15 UTC (past midnight wrap) (5e-07, 1e-06) 02:00 UTC+8 (same instant as 18:00 UTC) (5e-07, 1e-06) ``` The last row is the timezone case: an aware timestamp in UTC+8 lands on the same instant as 18:00 UTC and gets the discount, rather than being compared as a bare 02:00 wall clock and missing the window To see it end to end, put the same `off_peak_pricing` block on a deployment in your proxy config, set `hours_utc` so it covers the current UTC time, send a real request to /v1/chat/completions, and check the spend on /ui/?page=logs against the same request made outside the window ## Type 🆕 New Feature ## Caveats (if any) - Windows are UTC only, no named timezones - Naive timestamps are treated as already being UTC - Not exposed yet on deployment-level custom pricing params - Boundary-crossing requests bill at completion time, not request start - Off-peak replaces tier rates rather than discounting them proportionally ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(gemini-realtime): keep the client's voice on Vertex AI native-audio Live
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - Vertex AI Live silently discards the voice a client asks for - The strip was justified by a rejection Vertex does not actually do How it solves it: - Keep `speechConfig` on Vertex, still strip it for Google AI Studio - Overridable predicate, matching the existing `_include_function_response_id` ## Relevant issues ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist **Please complete all items before asking a LiteLLM maintainer to review your PR** - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review (Greptile reviews automatically once the PR is opened; only comment `@greptileai` to re-request a review after pushing changes) ## Delays in PR merge? If you're seeing a delay in your PR being merged, ping the LiteLLM Team on [Slack (#pr-review)](https://join.slack.com/t/litellmossslack/shared_invite/zt-3o7nkuyfr-p_kbNJj8taRfXGgQI1~YyA). ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix `_finalize_gemini_live_setup` pops `speechConfig` for any model flagged `gemini_native_audio`. The constant that introduced it says those models "reject a `speechConfig` on `setup` with a 1007 invalid-argument error". That premise does not hold on Vertex AI. **Vertex's own answer, before the fix**, talking straight to `BidiGenerateContent` so no LiteLLM code is in the path. Same socket, same setup, only `speechConfig` varies: ``` direct to Vertex, valid voice Aoede -> setupComplete direct to Vertex, bogus voice -> closed code=1000 direct to Vertex, no speechConfig -> setupComplete ``` Vertex accepts a valid voice and rejects an invalid one, which means it reads the field rather than refusing it. That is the opposite of what the strip assumes, and it is also what makes the invalid voice a usable probe: if `speechConfig` reaches Vertex, a bogus voice cannot succeed. **Before**, dev gateway at `53cec79d55`, a real Live session over `/v1/realtime` on `gemini-live-2.5-flash-native-audio`: ``` A real voice name (Aoede) -> ok, 10 audio deltas A bogus voice name (NotARealVoice1) -> ok, 10 audio deltas ``` The bogus voice sails through, so the voice never left the proxy. **After**, dev gateway at `ec9d9abfa2`, same request shape: ``` voice=Aoede -> OK, 10 audio deltas voice=Puck -> OK, 10 audio deltas voice=None -> OK, 9 audio deltas voice=NotARealVoice1 -> TIMEOUT (no response.done) ``` Valid voices work and only the invalid one fails, so the client's `speechConfig` is now reaching Vertex. Two things worth stating plainly rather than leaving for a reviewer to trip over. First, these captures were taken with `gemini_live_defer_setup` enabled, because with the default auto-setup LiteLLM sends its own `setup` on connect and the client's later `session.update` is dropped before it can carry a voice at all, so the strip is unreachable on that path. Second, Vertex's rejection of the invalid voice surfaces to the client as a timeout rather than an error, because the backend close is not propagated. Both are separate problems from this one and neither is introduced here. Google AI Studio was never verified to accept `speechConfig`, so its behaviour is deliberately unchanged and a test pins that. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Changes `GeminiRealtimeConfig` gains `_strip_native_audio_speech_config`, returning `True` so Google AI Studio keeps today's behaviour. `VertexAIRealtimeConfig` overrides it to `False`. `_finalize_gemini_live_setup` becomes an instance method so the override applies; both call sites already used `self`. The `responseModalities` TEXT to AUDIO coercion is untouched, since Vertex genuinely does reject TEXT on these models. ### Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: fix(responses): map response_format onto text.format instead of silently dropping it
signal.text: ## TLDR Problem this solves: - `responses(response_format=...)` was accepted and silently ignored - No mapping, no `UnsupportedParamsError`, no warning — schema unenforced - Caller reasonably concludes structured output is unsupported; it isn't - Same call works on `anthropic/*`, silently does nothing on `openai/*` How it solves it: - Map `response_format` onto `text.format`, the responses API spelling - Reuse the conversion already written for `text_format=` - Precedence `text` > `text_format` > `response_format`; existing spellings unchanged - Also fixes `KeyError` on `{"type": "json_object"}` and on a missing `strict` - A format with no readable `type` now raises rather than being dropped ## User Flow Before: a developer asking for a JSON schema the way they do everywhere else in litellm gets unconstrained prose back, and nothing tells them why. 1. They already call `/v1/chat/completions` with `"response_format": {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {...}}` and get conforming JSON, so they reach for the same field on `/v1/responses`. 2. They send `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"model": "xai/grok-4.3"`, their prompt, and that same `response_format` block. 3. They get `200 OK`. `output_text` is prose — `**Findings:** This sentence is textbook AI-speak...` — not the `{"flags": [...]}` object they asked for. No error, no warning names `response_format`. 4. They try the same request against `"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"` and it *does* return `{"flags": [...]}`, so it looks like a model capability difference rather than anything to do with the field. 5. They conclude `/v1/responses` has no structured output and either drop it or hand-roll JSON parsing with retries. After: the same request returns the object they asked for, on every provider. 1. They send the same `POST https://litellm-domain/v1/responses` with `"model": "xai/grok-4.3"` and the same `response_format` block. 2. They get `200 OK` and `output_text` is `{"flags": [...]}` — the requested schema. 3. `"model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-5"` returns the same shape, as before. 4. A request sending `text` (or `text_format`) instead is unaffected; if both are sent, `text` wins. ## Relevant issues Fixes #37125 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) — see Caveats for what I could run locally - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [x] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review — 5/5 on `c5d0800004`, after its P1 was fixed in `da207f1f4c` ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Real calls against xAI, no mocks. `xai/grok-4.3` is used because it has a native `XAIResponsesAPIConfig`, so it takes the native responses path where the bug lives. `anthropic/*` and `gemini/*` have no responses config, route through the chat-completions bridge, and were never affected — testing there hides the bug. Shared script (`probe.py`), unchanged between the two runs: ```python import json, os import litellm SCHEMA = {"type": "object", "properties": {"flags": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}}, "required": ["flags"], "additionalProperties": False} PROMPT = ("Review this sentence for AI-speak: 'We leverage synergies to unlock value.' " "Reply with your findings.") def run(label, **kw): try: r = litellm.responses(model="xai/grok-4.3", input=PROMPT, max_output_tokens=400, api_key=os.environ["XAI_API_KEY"], **kw) txt = (r.output_text or "").strip().replace("\n", " ") try: result = sorted(json.loads(txt).keys()) except Exception: result = f"<not JSON: {txt[:60]!r}>" except Exception as e: result = f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:80]}" print(f" {label:22} -> {result}") run("no format") run("text=", text={"format": {"type": "json_schema", "name": "Flags", "strict": True, "schema": SCHEMA}}) run("response_format=", response_format={"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "Flags", "strict": True, "schema": SCHEMA}}) run("response_format no type", response_format={"json_schema": {"name": "Flags", "schema": SCHEMA}}) ``` ### Before (973329e986) 1. `python probe.py` 2. Observed: ``` no format -> <not JSON: '**Findings:** This sentence is textbook AI-speak (or corpora'> text= -> ['flags'] response_format= -> <not JSON: '**Findings:** This sentence is textbook AI-speak / corporat'> response_format no type -> <not JSON: '**Findings:** This sentence is textbook AI-speak / corporate'> ``` Row 3 is the bug: the call succeeded and the schema was not applied. Row 2 shows the capability is present and reachable under the other spelling. Row 4 is the same silent drop for a malformed format. ### After (da207f1f4c) Captured at `da207f1f4c`. The tip is now `c5d0800004`, whose only change is trimming a source comment per review — no behaviour difference, so this run stands. 1. `python probe.py` 2. Observed: ``` no format -> <not JSON: 'The sentence is classic AI-speak / corporate jargon: vague, '> text= -> ['flags'] response_format= -> ['flags'] response_format no type -> BadRequestError: litellm.BadRequestError: Could not read a `type` from the supplied response form ``` Row 3 now returns the requested schema. Row 2 is unchanged. Row 4 now reports the malformed format instead of silently sending the request unconstrained. Unit tests, same tree: ``` $ pytest tests/test_litellm/responses/test_response_format_conversion.py -q ............ [100%] 12 passed ``` and against `973329e986` with only the new test file applied, 5 of the 12 fail with `KeyError: 'text'` — the params carried no format at all. That is deliberate: the broken version returns `200`, so a test asserting only a successful call passes against it. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Behaviour change: `response_format` now reaches the provider - A caller relying on it being ignored would newly get a constrained response - OpenAI/Azure share the native path; verified on xAI only (no OpenAI credit) - `tests/test_litellm/responses/` has 12 failures on staging, unrelated and pre-existing - Ran ruff check, ruff format, and that test dir locally; not the full CI matrix - Second commit is lint-only: `Final` on four locals to clear the LIT010 gate - Third commit addresses the P1 review finding (malformed format now raises) ## Final Attestation - [x] The tests check the right things, including the edge cases, and regressions in the respective real-world customer use-cases are not possible after this PR

signal.title: [Bug]: Global max_budget_limiter instantiated but never registered (Budget Bypass)
signal.text: ### Check for existing issues - [x] I have searched the existing issues and checked that my issue is not a duplicate. ### What happened? The global proxy budget enforcement is completely bypassed. Even when a max_budget is set for a user or globally, LiteLLM continues to process requests and spend money after the limit is reached. The root cause is in utils.py: The _PROXY_MaxBudgetLimiter is instantiated, but it is never registered as a callback. Therefore, the async_pre_call_hook (which should block the request) is never triggered. What I expected: The proxy should trigger a BudgetExceededError and return a 429 status code once the defined budget limit is exceeded. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Set a very low budget (e.g., max_budget: 0.0001) in your config.yaml or for a specific user. 2. Start the LiteLLM Proxy. 3. Send multiple requests that exceed this budget. ### Relevant log output ```shell # The limiter is instantiated here: self.max_budget_limiter = _PROXY_MaxBudgetLimiter() # However, a grep for the instance variable shows it is NEVER registered: grep -n "max_budget_limiter\." litellm/utils.py ``` ### What part of LiteLLM is this about? Proxy ### What LiteLLM version are you on ? v1.83.10 ### Twitter / LinkedIn details https://www.linkedin.com/in/kai-beuker-206775399/

signal.title: test(dashscope): cover tier-selection boundaries not currently exercised
signal.text: ## What this is Tests only. No behaviour change. The tiered-pricing work landed independently while #34760 was open, and it landed in better shape than what I had proposed there: selection reads `breakdown.total_input_tokens` rather than `usage.prompt_tokens`, and tier application is all-or-nothing. I have closed #34760 accordingly. What is left is that four behaviours the shipped implementation depends on are not covered by the eighteen tests currently in this file. All four pass on `litellm_internal_staging` as it stands, so these are guards on what shipped, not a request to change it. ## The four **`cached_tokens_count_toward_tier_selection`** is the one I would most want kept. Selecting on `breakdown.total_input_tokens` rather than `usage.prompt_tokens` is a deliberate choice, and it is observable: a request of 40k tokens where 30k are cached sits in the first tier by plain input and in the second by total. Nothing currently fails if that choice is reverted. **`input_above_first_tier_bills_whole_request_at_that_tier`** pins the all-or-nothing semantic, as opposed to billing each band separately. **`output_tokens_do_not_select_their_own_tier`** pins that completion tokens never influence which tier is chosen. **`tier_boundary_is_inclusive_of_range_end`** pins the boundary: exactly `range_end` stays in the tier, one token more moves the whole request up. This is the off-by-one that would be easiest to introduce and hardest to notice, since both sides produce a plausible number. ## Verification ``` tests/test_litellm/llms/dashscope/test_dashscope_cost_calculator.py 22 passed ``` 18 existing plus these 4, run against `litellm_internal_staging` at `973329e`. Each test asserts against rates read from the model cost map rather than hard-coded figures, so they follow a pricing change instead of breaking on one.

signal.title: fix(xai): stop rejecting `instructions` on the Responses API (unblocks web search + system prompt)
signal.text:
## TLDR Problem this solves: - xAI web search + a system prompt fails: `UnsupportedParamsError` on `instructions` - The premise is wrong — xAI does support `instructions` - `drop_params=True` "fixes" it by silently discarding the system prompt How it solves it: - Stop removing `instructions` from xAI's supported Responses params - Drop the matching unreachable `params.pop("instructions")` - Invert two stale assertions, add a regression test on the bridge path ## User Flow Before: a developer whose app asks Grok questions needing current web results cannot use a system prompt at all — the request is rejected before it leaves their process. 1. They call `litellm.completion(model="xai/grok-4.3", ...)` with a `system` message ("You must answer with the bare version number and nothing else."), a `user` question, and `web_search_options={"search_context_size": "medium"}` 2. Nothing reaches xAI. They get `litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: LlmProviders.XAI does not support parameters: {'instructions': 'You must answer with the bare version number and nothing else.'}` 3. They follow the error's own advice and set `drop_params=True`. The call returns 200 with a correct, web-sourced answer — but their system prompt was thrown away, so instead of `1.97.0` they get ``**1.97.0** (as shown on the official PyPI project page).[[1]](https://pypi.org/project/litellm/)`` followed by install instructions. Nothing in the response says the instructions were dropped 4. They delete the system message to get the call working, losing output-format control on every web-search request After: the same request succeeds with the system prompt honored. 1. They call `litellm.completion(model="xai/grok-4.3", ...)` with the same `system` message, `user` question, and `web_search_options` 2. The request reaches xAI, which runs the web search and applies the system prompt 3. They get back `1.97.0` — current, search-sourced, formatted exactly as asked 4. Setting `drop_params=True` changes nothing; the system prompt is preserved either way ## Relevant issues Fixes #37127 ## Linear ticket ## Pre-Submission checklist - [x] I have added meaningful tests - [x] My PR passes all CI/CD checks (e.g., lint, format, unit tests) - [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible; it only solves 1 specific problem - [ ] I have received a Greptile **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review ## Screenshots / Proof of Fix Live xAI, no mocks. Shared setup for every case below: ```python import litellm, os SYSTEM = "You must answer with the bare version number and nothing else." MSGS = [ {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM}, {"role": "user", "content": "What is the newest litellm version on PyPI?"}, ] litellm.completion( model="xai/grok-4.3", messages=MSGS, web_search_options={"search_context_size": "medium"}, api_key=os.environ["GROK_API_KEY"], max_tokens=4000, # drop_params=True # case 2 only ) ``` The question is chosen so the answer is only reachable via live search, and the system prompt is chosen so it is visible in the output whether it survived. ### Before (973329e98) #### Case 1: default 1. Run the snippet above. 2. Observed: ``` UnsupportedParamsError: litellm.UnsupportedParamsError: LlmProviders.XAI does not support parameters: {'instructions': 'You must answer with the bare version number and nothing else.'}, for model=grok-4.3. To drop these, set `litellm.drop_params=True` ``` #### Case 2: `drop_params=True` 1. Run the same snippet with `drop_params=True`. 2. Observed — call succeeds, system prompt silently gone: ``` content: '**1.97.0** (as shown on the official PyPI project page).[[1]](https://pypi.org/project/litellm/)

You can install it with:
```
pip install litellm
```' obeyed system prompt (bare version only): False usage: 7435 in / 294 out ``` ### After (7d26d0b9) #### Case 1: default 1. Run the snippet above. 2. Observed: ``` content: '1.97.0' obeyed system prompt (bare version only): True usage: 7498 in / 325 out ``` #### Case 2: `drop_params=True` 1. Run the same snippet with `drop_params=True`. 2. Observed — identical, no longer sensitive to `drop_params`: ``` content: '1.97.0' obeyed system prompt (bare version only): True usage: 7467 in / 278 out ``` The ~7.5k input tokens are the injected live search results, so search is genuinely running in every passing case. ### Evidence that xAI accepts `instructions` Three direct `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/responses` calls, no litellm in the path: ``` === 1. instructions only === HTTP 200 output_text: BANANA <- instructions were "Always answer with exactly the word BANANA." echoed instructions: 'Always answer with exactly the word BANANA.' === 2. instructions + web_search tool === HTTP 200 output_text: **1.97.0** echoed instructions: 'Answer in exactly one short sentence.' === 3. system role in input + web_search === HTTP 200 output_text: **1.97.0** ``` xAI accepts `instructions`, honors it, and echoes it back — including alongside a server-side `web_search` tool. It is also listed in [their API reference](https://docs.x.ai/docs/api-reference#create-new-response). ### Unit tests ``` tests/test_litellm/llms/xai/ tests/test_litellm/test_xai_responses_auto_routing.py tests/test_litellm/responses/ tests/test_litellm/completion_extras/ ``` 596 passed on the merge base, 597 on this branch (the one new regression test), with an identical set of 13 pre-existing failures on both sides — all Windows-environment issues in unrelated files (POSIX file modes, websocket URL construction), untouched by this PR. `scripts/check_type_discipline.py` on the changed test file reports LIT010 at 51, identical to the merge base, so this PR adds nothing to that ceiling-pinned rule. ## Type 🐛 Bug Fix ## Caveats (if any) - Two near-duplicate xAI Responses test files exist; both updated - Did not touch the shared bridge's system→`instructions` hoist — unnecessary once xAI accepts it - Regression test injects a mocked `client=` rather than patching `HTTPHandler.post`
